# Part 244 — PEM Key Loader

## Aim of the code

Convert configured PEM key material into Java cryptographic keys.

## Code

package com.gsir.auth.infrastructure;

import java.security.PrivateKey;

import java.security.PublicKey;

public interface JwtKeyLoader {

    PrivateKey loadPrivateKey(String pem);

    PublicKey loadPublicKey(String pem);

}

Implementation:

package com.gsir.auth.infrastructure;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.security.KeyFactory;

import java.security.PrivateKey;

import java.security.PublicKey;

import java.security.spec.PKCS8EncodedKeySpec;

import java.security.spec.X509EncodedKeySpec;

import java.util.Base64;

@Component

public class RsaJwtKeyLoader implements JwtKeyLoader {

    private static final String BEGIN_PRIVATE =

            "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----";

    private static final String END_PRIVATE =

            "-----END PRIVATE KEY-----";

    private static final String BEGIN_PUBLIC =

            "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----";

    private static final String END_PUBLIC =

            "-----END PUBLIC KEY-----";

    @Override

    public PrivateKey loadPrivateKey(String pem) {

        try {

            String normalized = pem

                    .replace(BEGIN_PRIVATE, "")

                    .replace(END_PRIVATE, "")

                    .replaceAll("\\s", "");

            byte[] decoded =

                    Base64.getDecoder().decode(normalized);

            PKCS8EncodedKeySpec specification =

                    new PKCS8EncodedKeySpec(decoded);

            return KeyFactory

                    .getInstance("RSA")

                    .generatePrivate(specification);

        } catch (Exception exception) {

            throw new IllegalStateException(

                    "Unable to load JWT private key",

                    exception

            );

        }

    }

    @Override

    public PublicKey loadPublicKey(String pem) {

        try {

            String normalized = pem

                    .replace(BEGIN_PUBLIC, "")

                    .replace(END_PUBLIC, "")

                    .replaceAll("\\s", "");

            byte[] decoded =

                    Base64.getDecoder().decode(normalized);

            X509EncodedKeySpec specification =

                    new X509EncodedKeySpec(decoded);

            return KeyFactory

                    .getInstance("RSA")

                    .generatePublic(specification);

        } catch (Exception exception) {

            throw new IllegalStateException(

                    "Unable to load JWT public key",

                    exception

            );

        }

    }

}

The final implementation must additionally validate key size according to the production cryptographic policy.

# Part 246 — JWT Claim Consistency Validation

## Aim of the code

Prevent contradictory claims from being accepted.

For example, sub and uid must not identify different users.

## Code

package com.gsir.auth.infrastructure;

import java.util.UUID;

public final class JwtClaimValidator {

    private JwtClaimValidator() {

    }

    public static UUID requireSame(

            UUID first,

            UUID second,

            String claimName) {

        if (first == null || second == null) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException(

                    "Required claim missing: " + claimName

            );

        }

        if (!first.equals(second)) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException(

                    "JWT claim mismatch"

            );

        }

        return first;

    }

}

The verifier should enforce:

sub == uid

and independently validate:

uid != null

oid != null

wid != null

sid != null

This reduces ambiguity at the security boundary.

package com.gsir.security;

import com.gsir.auth.infrastructure.InvalidJwtException;

import com.gsir.auth.infrastructure.JwtClaims;

import com.gsir.auth.infrastructure.JwtSigner;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service

public class AccessTokenVerifierImpl

        implements AccessTokenVerifier {

    private final JwtSigner jwtSigner;

    public AccessTokenVerifierImpl(

            JwtSigner jwtSigner) {

        this.jwtSigner = jwtSigner;

    }

    @Override

    public VerifiedAccessToken verify(

            String rawToken) {

        if (rawToken == null ||

                rawToken.isBlank()) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException(

                    "Missing access token"

            );

        }

        JwtClaims claims =

                jwtSigner.verify(rawToken);

        SecurityPrincipal principal =

                new SecurityPrincipal(

                        claims.userId(),

                        claims.organizationId(),

                        claims.workspaceId(),

                        claims.sessionId()

                );

        return new VerifiedAccessToken(

                principal

        );

    }

}

The resulting SecurityPrincipal is still only an authenticated identity.

Authorization has not yet occurred.

## Critical security rule

A valid JWT does not by itself mean:

user has access to project

user has access to workspace

user is organization administrator

user can execute a tool

user can execute scientific computation

user can invoke an AI model

user can modify research data

Those decisions belong to the authorization and application layers.

# Part 252 — Session Existence and Revocation Validation

## Aim of the Code

After JWT cryptographic and claim validation succeeds, GSIR must verify that the authenticated session is still valid.

A validly signed JWT must not automatically grant access if its corresponding server-side session has been revoked, expired, or otherwise invalidated.

This creates the authentication chain:

JWT → claims → session → user → tenant/membership authorization

The session check must occur before protected application access is granted.

## Code

### SessionValidationResult.java

package com.gsir.security.auth;

import java.util.UUID;

public record SessionValidationResult(

        boolean valid,

        UUID sessionId,

        UUID userId,

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId,

        String reason

) {

    public static SessionValidationResult valid(

            UUID sessionId,

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    ) {

        return new SessionValidationResult(

                true,

                sessionId,

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                null

        );

    }

    public static SessionValidationResult invalid(String reason) {

        return new SessionValidationResult(

                false,

                null,

                null,

                null,

                null,

                reason

        );

    }

}

### SessionValidationService.java

package com.gsir.security.auth;

import java.util.UUID;

public interface SessionValidationService {

    SessionValidationResult validate(

            UUID sessionId,

            UUID userId

    );

}

### SessionValidationServiceImpl.java

package com.gsir.security.auth;

import com.gsir.security.exception.InvalidJwtException;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.time.Clock;

import java.time.Instant;

import java.util.UUID;

@Service

public class SessionValidationServiceImpl

        implements SessionValidationService {

    private final SessionRepositoryPort sessionRepository;

    private final Clock clock;

    public SessionValidationServiceImpl(

            SessionRepositoryPort sessionRepository,

            Clock clock

    ) {

        this.sessionRepository = sessionRepository;

        this.clock = clock;

    }

    @Override

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)

    public SessionValidationResult validate(

            UUID sessionId,

            UUID userId

    ) {

        if (sessionId == null || userId == null) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException();

        }

        SessionRecord session = sessionRepository

                .findById(sessionId)

                .orElseThrow(InvalidJwtException::new);

        if (!session.userId().equals(userId)) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException();

        }

        Instant now = clock.instant();

        if (session.revokedAt() != null) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException();

        }

        if (!session.expiresAt().isAfter(now)) {

            throw new InvalidJwtException();

        }

        return SessionValidationResult.valid(

                session.id(),

                session.userId(),

                session.organizationId(),

                session.workspaceId()

        );

    }

}

### Security Rule

The JWT must contain the session identifier required to perform this validation.

Recommended claim:

sid = session UUID

The authenticated request therefore follows:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT>

        │

        ▼

JWT signature verification

        │

        ▼

JWT claim validation

        │

        ├── sub/user identity

        ├── sid/session identity

        ├── issuer

        ├── audience

        ├── expiration

        └── time validity

        │

        ▼

SessionValidationService

        │

        ├── session exists?

        ├── belongs to user?

        ├── revoked?

        └── expired?

        │

        ▼

Authenticated SecurityPrincipal

### Important Boundary

Do not store complete authorization state inside the JWT.

The JWT establishes a cryptographically authenticated identity.

The database remains authoritative for:

- session revocation;

- session expiration;

- organization membership;

- workspace membership;

- project access;

- account status;

- other mutable authorization state.

This permits immediate server-side invalidation without waiting for a long-lived access token to expire.

# Part 253 — Complete JWT → Session Authentication Pipeline

## Aim of the Code

Connect the JWT verification layer from Parts 242–251 with the server-side session validation from Part 252.

The security filter must:

- Extract the Bearer token.

- Verify the JWT cryptographically.

- Validate required claims.

- Extract sub and sid.

- Validate the corresponding server-side session.

- Construct the authenticated SecurityPrincipal.

- Place the authenticated principal into Spring Security's SecurityContext.

- Reject invalid authentication without exposing sensitive internal details.

No controller should independently repeat JWT or session validation.

## Code

### 1. Extend JWT Claims

}

The JWT must contain:

sub = user ID

sid = session ID

iss = issuer

aud = audience

iat = issued-at timestamp

exp = expiration timestamp

sub and sid are identifiers only. They must not contain sensitive personal information.

### 3. Authentication Pipeline Service

package com.gsir.security.auth;

import com.gsir.security.jwt.AccessTokenVerifier;

import com.gsir.security.jwt.JwtClaims;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service

public class AccessAuthenticationService {

    private final AccessTokenVerifier accessTokenVerifier;

    private final SessionValidationService sessionValidationService;

    public AccessAuthenticationService(

            AccessTokenVerifier accessTokenVerifier,

            SessionValidationService sessionValidationService

    ) {

        this.accessTokenVerifier = accessTokenVerifier;

        this.sessionValidationService = sessionValidationService;

    }

    public SecurityPrincipal authenticate(String token) {

        JwtClaims claims = accessTokenVerifier.verify(token);

        SessionValidationResult session =

                sessionValidationService.validate(

                        claims.userId(),

                        claims.sessionId()

                );

        return new SecurityPrincipal(

                session.userId(),

                session.sessionId(),

                session.organizationId(),

                session.workspaceId()

        );

    }

}

The exact argument order must match the final SessionValidationService contract established in Part 252.

### 4. Bearer Token Resolver

package com.gsir.security.web;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component

public class BearerTokenResolver {

    public String resolve(HttpServletRequest request) {

        String authorization =

                request.getHeader("Authorization");

        if (authorization == null ||

                authorization.isBlank()) {

            return null;

        }

        if (!authorization.regionMatches(

                true,

                0,

                "Bearer ",

                0,

                7

        )) {

            return null;

        }

        String token =

                authorization.substring(7).trim();

        return token.isEmpty() ? null : token;

    }

}

Only the standard HTTP Authorization: Bearer <token> form is accepted.

### 5. Authentication Filter

package com.gsir.security.web;

import com.gsir.security.auth.AccessAuthenticationService;

import com.gsir.security.exception.InvalidJwtException;

import jakarta.servlet.FilterChain;

import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;

import org.springframework.security.authentication.UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken;

import org.springframework.security.core.context.SecurityContextHolder;

import org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter;

import java.io.IOException;

public class JwtAuthenticationFilter

        extends OncePerRequestFilter {

    private final BearerTokenResolver bearerTokenResolver;

    private final AccessAuthenticationService authenticationService;

    public JwtAuthenticationFilter(

            BearerTokenResolver bearerTokenResolver,

            AccessAuthenticationService authenticationService

    ) {

        this.bearerTokenResolver = bearerTokenResolver;

        this.authenticationService = authenticationService;

    }

    @Override

    protected void doFilterInternal(

            HttpServletRequest request,

            HttpServletResponse response,

            FilterChain filterChain

    ) throws ServletException, IOException {

        String token =

                bearerTokenResolver.resolve(request);

        if (token == null) {

            filterChain.doFilter(request, response);

            return;

        }

        try {

            SecurityPrincipal principal =

                    authenticationService.authenticate(token);

            UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken authentication =

                    UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken.authenticated(

                            principal,

                            null,

                            java.util.Collections.emptyList()

                    );

            SecurityContextHolder

                    .getContext()

                    .setAuthentication(authentication);

            filterChain.doFilter(request, response);

        } catch (InvalidJwtException ex) {

            SecurityContextHolder.clearContext();

            response.setStatus(

                    HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED

            );

            response.setContentType("application/json");

            response.getWriter().write(

                    "{\"error\":\"UNAUTHORIZED\"}"

            );

        }

    }

}

### 6. Authentication Context Rule

The filter must never place an unverified identity into the security context.

The only valid sequence is:

HTTP Request

     │

     ▼

Bearer token extraction

     │

     ▼

JWT cryptographic verification

     │

     ▼

JWT claim validation

     │

     ▼

Session validation

     │

     ▼

SecurityPrincipal

     │

     ▼

Spring SecurityContext

     │

     ▼

Authorization

     │

     ▼

Controller

If any stage fails:

Request

  │

  ▼

Failure

  │

  ▼

401 Unauthorized

### 7. Anonymous Request Rule

Absence of a Bearer token is not itself a JWT error.

Public endpoints may continue without authentication.

Protected endpoints must subsequently be rejected by Spring Security authorization rules.

Therefore:

No token

   │

   ├── public endpoint → continue

   │

   └── protected endpoint → 401

This keeps authentication and endpoint authorization as separate responsibilities.

### 8. SecurityContext Cleanup

The application must not accidentally reuse authentication between requests.

Spring Security's request security context lifecycle should be used rather than maintaining a custom static authentication store.

Never implement:

static SecurityPrincipal currentUser;

or any equivalent global mutable authentication state.

## Required Tests

### Valid authentication

valid JWT

+ valid session

+ matching user

= authenticated request

### Revoked session

valid JWT

+ revoked session

= 401

### Expired session

valid JWT

+ expired session

= 401

### Wrong session owner

JWT user A

+ session belonging to user B

= 401

### Invalid JWT

invalid signature

= 401

### Missing token

no Authorization header

+ protected endpoint

= 401

### Public endpoint

no Authorization header

+ public endpoint

= request continues

## Security Invariant

A cryptographically valid JWT is necessary but not sufficient for access.

The effective authentication condition is:

[ Authenticated = JWT_{valid} \land Claims_{valid} \land Session_{valid} \land User_{match} ]

Authorization is a separate condition:

[ Authorized = Authenticated \land Membership_{valid} \land Permission_{sufficient} ]

This prevents the JWT layer from becoming the sole source of mutable authorization truth.

Part 254 — Membership-based RBAC and organization/workspace authorization.

# Part 255 — Membership Persistence Adapters and Database Tenant Integrity

## Aim of the Code

Connect the organization/workspace authorization ports to the persistence layer without allowing authorization logic to bypass tenant boundaries.

The persistence layer must enforce:

- organization membership lookup by (user_id, organization_id);

- workspace membership lookup by (user_id, organization_id, workspace_id);

- uniqueness of memberships;

- foreign-key integrity;

- organization/workspace ownership boundaries;

- no cross-tenant membership resolution.

The application authorization layer remains responsible for permission decisions.

The database remains responsible for structural integrity.

## Code

### 1. Organization Membership Entity

package com.gsir.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.*;

import java.util.UUID;

@Entity

@Table(

        name = "organization_memberships",

        uniqueConstraints = {

                @UniqueConstraint(

                        name = "uk_org_membership_user_org",

                        columnNames = {

                                "user_id",

                                "organization_id"

                        }

                )

        },

        indexes = {

                @Index(

                        name = "idx_org_membership_user_org",

                        columnList = "user_id,organization_id"

                )

        }

)

public class OrganizationMembershipEntity {

    @Id

    @Column(nullable = false)

    private UUID id;

    @Column(name = "user_id", nullable = false)

    private UUID userId;

    @Column(name = "organization_id", nullable = false)

    private UUID organizationId;

    @Column(nullable = false, length = 32)

    private String role;

    protected OrganizationMembershipEntity() {

    }

    public UUID getId() {

        return id;

    }

    public UUID getUserId() {

        return userId;

    }

    public UUID getOrganizationId() {

        return organizationId;

    }

    public String getRole() {

        return role;

    }

}

The exact column definitions must match the approved Flyway schema.

If the existing migration uses different names, types, indexes, or constraints, this mapping must be adjusted to the migration rather than modifying the database silently.

## 5. Organization Membership Adapter

package com.gsir.persistence.adapter;

import com.gsir.persistence.repository.OrganizationMembershipJpaRepository;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.OrganizationMembershipPort;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.OrganizationMembershipRecord;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.OrganizationRole;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

@Component

public class OrganizationMembershipPersistenceAdapter

        implements OrganizationMembershipPort {

    private final OrganizationMembershipJpaRepository repository;

    public OrganizationMembershipPersistenceAdapter(

            OrganizationMembershipJpaRepository repository

    ) {

        this.repository = repository;

    }

    @Override

    public Optional<OrganizationMembershipRecord> findMembership(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId

    ) {

        return repository

                .findByUserIdAndOrganizationId(

                        userId,

                        organizationId

                )

                .map(entity ->

                        new OrganizationMembershipRecord(

                                entity.getUserId(),

                                entity.getOrganizationId(),

                                OrganizationRole.valueOf(

                                        entity.getRole()

                                )

                        )

                );

    }

}

## 6. Workspace Membership Adapter

package com.gsir.persistence.adapter;

import com.gsir.persistence.repository.WorkspaceMembershipJpaRepository;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.WorkspaceMembershipPort;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.WorkspaceMembershipRecord;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.WorkspaceRole;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

@Component

public class WorkspaceMembershipPersistenceAdapter

        implements WorkspaceMembershipPort {

    private final WorkspaceMembershipJpaRepository repository;

    public WorkspaceMembershipPersistenceAdapter(

            WorkspaceMembershipJpaRepository repository

    ) {

        this.repository = repository;

    }

    @Override

    public Optional<WorkspaceMembershipRecord> findMembership(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    ) {

        return repository

                .findByUserIdAndOrganizationIdAndWorkspaceId(

                        userId,

                        organizationId,

                        workspaceId

                )

                .map(entity ->

                        new WorkspaceMembershipRecord(

                                entity.getUserId(),

                                entity.getWorkspaceId(),

                                entity.getOrganizationId(),

                                WorkspaceRole.valueOf(

                                        entity.getRole()

                                )

                        )

                );

    }

}

## 7. Do Not Trust the Membership Row Alone

A workspace membership row containing:

user_id = U

organization_id = A

workspace_id = W

must not automatically be considered structurally valid.

The database must ensure:

[ W.organization_id = A ]

The preferred design is therefore a composite foreign-key relationship where the schema supports it.

Conceptually:

organizations

      │

      │ (id)

      ▼

workspaces

      │

      │ (id, organization_id)

      ▼

workspace_memberships

This prevents a workspace membership from referencing a workspace under a different organization.

## 8. Composite Tenant Integrity

For tenant-scoped tables, preserve the previously established integrity pattern:

workspaces:

(id, organization_id)

projects:

(id, workspace_id)

The database should support references such as:

workspace_memberships

    (workspace_id, organization_id)

            │

            ▼

workspaces

    (id, organization_id)

and, where appropriate:

projects

    (workspace_id)

            │

            ▼

workspaces

The purpose is structural prevention of cross-tenant relationships.

## 9. Role Conversion Safety

Avoid silently converting malformed database values into a valid role.

This is unsafe:

try {

    return OrganizationRole.valueOf(entity.getRole());

} catch (Exception ignored) {

    return OrganizationRole.MEMBER;

}

An invalid role must fail closed.

Correct behavior:

invalid persisted role

        ↓

persistence/domain error

        ↓

request denied

        ↓

security event recorded

Never downgrade an invalid authorization state to a weaker or stronger role automatically.

## 10. Database Constraints

The corresponding Flyway migration must provide, as applicable:

UNIQUE (user_id, organization_id)

for organization memberships.

And:

UNIQUE (user_id, workspace_id)

for workspace memberships.

Role values must also be constrained to the approved role set.

For example:

CHECK (

    role IN ('OWNER', 'ADMIN', 'MEMBER')

)

and:

CHECK (

    role IN ('OWNER', 'ADMIN', 'MEMBER', 'VIEWER')

)

These exact role sets remain subject to the approved GSIR schema contract.

Do not create a new migration merely because this document proposes an example constraint.

## 11. Authorization Lookup Invariant

Every workspace authorization lookup must contain:

userId

organizationId

workspaceId

Never replace it with:

workspaceId only

when the tenant boundary requires organization verification.

The intended query semantics are:

[ M = M(user,\ organization,\ workspace) ]

not:

[ M = M(workspace) ]

## 12. Persistence Security Tests

The persistence layer must test:

### Correct tenant

User U

Organization A

Workspace W-A

Membership U/A/W-A

lookup(U,A,W-A)

→ found

### Wrong organization

lookup(U,B,W-A)

→ empty

### Wrong user

lookup(U2,A,W-A)

→ empty

### Cross-tenant database relationship

Attempt:

workspace.organization_id = A

membership.organization_id = B

membership.workspace_id = workspace

Expected:

database constraint violation

### Duplicate membership

Attempting:

same user

same organization

second membership

must fail through the unique constraint.

## 13. No Authorization Cache Yet

Do not introduce Redis authorization caching at this stage.

Membership changes must take effect immediately.

The initial production-safe path is:

Request

  ↓

Authentication

  ↓

Database membership lookup

  ↓

Authorization

Caching can be evaluated later using measured latency and consistency requirements.

Premature caching would create additional invalidation and security complexity.

## Security Invariants

### Invariant 1

A user cannot authorize against an organization in which they have no membership.

### Invariant 2

A workspace membership must belong to the same organization as the referenced workspace.

### Invariant 3

Duplicate memberships are prohibited.

### Invariant 4

Invalid persisted roles fail closed.

### Invariant 5

Authorization code cannot bypass the persistence port.

### Invariant 6

Database integrity and application authorization provide separate layers of protection.

# Part 256 — Resource-Level Authorization

## Aim of the Code

Extend authorization from organization/workspace membership to the concrete GSIR resources users operate on.

The authorization layer must protect resources including:

- projects;

- notes;

- web links;

- conversations;

- files;

- document-related resources.

The rule is:

Authenticated User

       ↓

Organization Membership

       ↓

Workspace Membership

       ↓

Resource Tenant Ownership

       ↓

Resource Permission

       ↓

Operation

Resource authorization must be performed in the service/application layer rather than duplicated across controllers.

## Code

### 1. Resource Scope

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

public enum ResourceScope {

    ORGANIZATION,

    WORKSPACE,

    PROJECT

}

This represents the authorization boundary, not a database entity.

### 2. Resource Access Port

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

public interface ResourceAccessPort {

    Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> findProject(

            UUID projectId

    );

    Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> findNote(

            UUID noteId

    );

    Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> findWebLink(

            UUID webLinkId

    );

    Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> findConversation(

            UUID conversationId

    );

    Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> findFile(

            UUID fileId

    );

}

The port exposes only the minimum tenant information required for authorization.

It must not return complete resource entities.

### 3. Resource Access Record

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import java.util.UUID;

public record ResourceAccessRecord(

        UUID resourceId,

        ResourceScope scope,

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId,

        UUID projectId

) {

}

Nullable fields depend on the resource's actual tenancy level.

For example:

Organization resource:

organizationId != null

workspaceId     = null

projectId       = null

Workspace resource:

organizationId != null

workspaceId     != null

projectId       = null

Project resource:

organizationId != null

workspaceId     != null

projectId       != null

## 4. Resource Permission

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

public enum ResourcePermission {

    READ,

    CREATE,

    UPDATE,

    DELETE

}

This is intentionally small.

Additional permissions should only be introduced when a real GSIR workflow requires them.

## 5. Project Authorization

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import com.gsir.security.exception.AccessDeniedException;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.util.UUID;

@Service

public class ProjectAuthorizationService {

    private final ResourceAccessPort resourceAccess;

    private final AuthorizationService authorizationService;

    public ProjectAuthorizationService(

            ResourceAccessPort resourceAccess,

            AuthorizationService authorizationService

    ) {

        this.resourceAccess = resourceAccess;

        this.authorizationService = authorizationService;

    }

    public void requireProjectAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID projectId

    ) {

        ResourceAccessRecord resource =

                resourceAccess.findProject(projectId)

                        .orElseThrow(

                                AccessDeniedException::new

                        );

        if (!organizationId.equals(

                resource.organizationId()

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        if (!workspaceId.equals(

                resource.workspaceId()

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        if (!projectId.equals(

                resource.projectId()

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        authorizationService.requireWorkspaceMembership(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId

        );

    }

}

The resource's persisted tenant relationship is verified before access is granted.

## 6. Generic Workspace Resource Authorization

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import com.gsir.security.exception.AccessDeniedException;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.util.UUID;

@Service

public class WorkspaceResourceAuthorizationService {

    private final ResourceAccessPort resourceAccess;

    private final AuthorizationService authorizationService;

    public WorkspaceResourceAuthorizationService(

            ResourceAccessPort resourceAccess,

            AuthorizationService authorizationService

    ) {

        this.resourceAccess = resourceAccess;

        this.authorizationService = authorizationService;

    }

    public void requireNoteAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID noteId

    ) {

        requireWorkspaceResource(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                resourceAccess.findNote(noteId)

        );

    }

    public void requireWebLinkAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID webLinkId

    ) {

        requireWorkspaceResource(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                resourceAccess.findWebLink(webLinkId)

        );

    }

    public void requireConversationAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID conversationId

    ) {

        requireWorkspaceResource(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                resourceAccess.findConversation(

                        conversationId

                )

        );

    }

    public void requireFileAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID fileId

    ) {

        requireWorkspaceResource(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                resourceAccess.findFile(fileId)

        );

    }

    private void requireWorkspaceResource(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            java.util.Optional<ResourceAccessRecord> result

    ) {

        ResourceAccessRecord resource =

                result.orElseThrow(

                        AccessDeniedException::new

                );

        if (resource.scope()

                != ResourceScope.WORKSPACE) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        if (!organizationId.equals(

                resource.organizationId()

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        if (!workspaceId.equals(

                resource.workspaceId()

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        authorizationService.requireWorkspaceMembership(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId

        );

    }

}

The exact scope of each existing GSIR table must follow the approved schema rather than being inferred from this example.

## 7. Project-Scoped Resources

If a resource belongs to a project, authorization must include the complete hierarchy:

Organization

     │

     ▼

Workspace

     │

     ▼

Project

     │

     ▼

Resource

The resource must never be authorized by checking only:

projectId

The authorization contract should verify:

[ Resource.projectId = RequestedProject ]

and:

[ Project.workspaceId = RequestedWorkspace ]

and:

[ Workspace.organizationId = RequestedOrganization ]

This creates defense in depth against malformed or inconsistent resource relationships.

## 8. Resource Authorization Must Precede Mutation

For an update:

authorizationService

    .requireWorkspaceMembership(

        principal.userId(),

        organizationId,

        workspaceId

    );

resourceAuthorization

    .requireNoteAccess(

        principal.userId(),

        organizationId,

        workspaceId,

        noteId

    );

noteService.update(...);

Never perform the mutation first and check authorization afterward.

## 9. Controller Boundary

Controllers should obtain the authenticated principal and delegate authorization.

Example:

@PutMapping("/workspaces/{workspaceId}/notes/{noteId}")

public NoteResponse updateNote(

        @AuthenticationPrincipal SecurityPrincipal principal,

        @PathVariable UUID workspaceId,

        @PathVariable UUID noteId,

        @Valid @RequestBody UpdateNoteRequest request

) {

    noteAuthorization.requireNoteAccess(

            principal.userId(),

            principal.organizationId(),

            workspaceId,

            noteId

    );

    return noteService.update(

            principal.userId(),

            workspaceId,

            noteId,

            request

    );

}

The controller does not implement membership logic itself.

## 10. Query-Level Tenant Filtering

Authorization checks alone are not enough for collection endpoints.

For example:

GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/notes

must query notes using the authorized workspace:

SELECT ...

FROM notes

WHERE workspace_id = :workspaceId;

Never load all notes and filter them in Java afterward.

For project collections:

SELECT ...

FROM projects

WHERE workspace_id = :workspaceId;

The tenant predicate belongs as close to persistence as practical.

## 11. Resource Existence Leakage

An unauthorized caller should not receive different responses such as:

404 → resource exists but belongs to another tenant

403 → resource exists and belongs to another tenant

unless that distinction is an explicitly approved product/security policy.

The default security boundary should fail closed without revealing cross-tenant resource existence.

## 12. Authorization Matrix

| **Resource** | **Minimum Scope** | **Required Boundary** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Organization data | Organization | Organization membership |
| Workspace | Organization | Organization membership |
| Project | Workspace | Workspace membership |
| Note | Workspace/project as defined by schema | Matching tenant scope |
| Web link | Workspace/project as defined by schema | Matching tenant scope |
| Conversation | Workspace/project as defined by schema | Matching tenant scope |
| File | Workspace/project as defined by schema | Matching tenant scope |

This table is an implementation contract only after reconciliation with the approved database schema.

## 13. Required Tests

### Cross-organization project

User → Organization A

Project → Organization B

→ DENY

### Cross-workspace project

User → Workspace A

Project → Workspace B

→ DENY

### Cross-tenant note

User → Organization A

Note → Organization B

→ DENY

### Correct resource

authenticated user

+ valid membership

+ matching tenant

+ matching resource

→ ALLOW

### Collection isolation

User belongs to Workspace A

GET /workspaces/A/notes

→ only Workspace A notes

No resource from Workspace B may appear.

## 14. Security Invariant

For a resource R:

[ Access(R)= Authenticated \land TenantMatch(R) \land Membership \land Permission ]

For hierarchical resources:

[ Organization \rightarrow Workspace \rightarrow Project \rightarrow Resource ]

must remain internally consistent.

## 15. Architecture Rule

Do not create separate authorization agents.

Do not introduce an authorization microservice.

Do not give the AI/AGI layer direct authorization authority.

The authorization path remains deterministic:

Request

   ↓

Spring Security

   ↓

SecurityPrincipal

   ↓

AuthorizationService

   ↓

Persistence

   ↓

Deterministic decision

The future AGI system can request an action, but the authorization layer independently determines whether that action is permitted.

This preserves the controlled Action + Tool/API boundary.

Part 257 — Implement authorization-aware project/resource persistence queries and prevent IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) access.

# Part 257 — Authorization-Aware Persistence and IDOR Protection

## Aim of the Code

Prevent Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) and equivalent tenant-isolation failures at the persistence boundary.

A user must not gain access to another tenant's resource merely by changing an identifier such as:

/project/{projectId}

/notes/{noteId}

/files/{fileId}

/conversations/{conversationId}

Authorization must therefore be enforced through both:

- application-level authorization;

- tenant-scoped persistence queries.

The persistence layer must never provide a convenient unrestricted lookup that allows a protected service to accidentally bypass its authorization boundary.

## Code

### 1. Tenant-Scoped Project Query Port

package com.gsir.project;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

public interface ProjectQueryPort {

    Optional<ProjectAccessRecord> findForAccess(

            UUID projectId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    );

}

### 2. Project Access Record

package com.gsir.project;

import java.util.UUID;

public record ProjectAccessRecord(

        UUID projectId,

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId

) {

}

Only the fields required to establish the tenant boundary are exposed.

The authorization layer does not need the complete JPA entity.

### 3. JPA Repository

package com.gsir.persistence.repository;

import com.gsir.persistence.entity.ProjectEntity;

import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

public interface ProjectJpaRepository

        extends JpaRepository<ProjectEntity, UUID> {

    Optional<ProjectEntity>

    findByIdAndOrganizationIdAndWorkspaceId(

            UUID projectId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    );

}

The exact derived-query property names must match the actual ProjectEntity.

If the final entity does not contain organizationId directly, the query must instead enforce the organization boundary through the workspace relationship.

## 4. Persistence Adapter

package com.gsir.persistence.adapter;

import com.gsir.persistence.repository.ProjectJpaRepository;

import com.gsir.project.ProjectAccessRecord;

import com.gsir.project.ProjectQueryPort;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.Optional;

import java.util.UUID;

@Component

public class ProjectQueryPersistenceAdapter

        implements ProjectQueryPort {

    private final ProjectJpaRepository repository;

    public ProjectQueryPersistenceAdapter(

            ProjectJpaRepository repository

    ) {

        this.repository = repository;

    }

    @Override

    public Optional<ProjectAccessRecord> findForAccess(

            UUID projectId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    ) {

        return repository

                .findByIdAndOrganizationIdAndWorkspaceId(

                        projectId,

                        organizationId,

                        workspaceId

                )

                .map(entity ->

                        new ProjectAccessRecord(

                                entity.getId(),

                                entity.getOrganizationId(),

                                entity.getWorkspaceId()

                        )

                );

    }

}

## 5. Never Authorize by ID Alone

This pattern is prohibited for protected tenant resources:

projectRepository.findById(projectId);

followed by:

if (project != null) {

    // allow

}

The resource identifier is supplied by the caller and therefore cannot establish ownership.

The secure pattern is:

projectQueryPort.findForAccess(

        projectId,

        organizationId,

        workspaceId

);

The query itself verifies the expected tenant relationship.

## 6. Generic Tenant Query Pattern

For a workspace-scoped resource:

SELECT *

FROM resource

WHERE id = :resourceId

  AND organization_id = :organizationId

  AND workspace_id = :workspaceId;

For a project-scoped resource:

SELECT *

FROM resource

WHERE id = :resourceId

  AND organization_id = :organizationId

  AND workspace_id = :workspaceId

  AND project_id = :projectId;

The actual predicates must match each table's approved schema.

## 7. Secure Resource Loading

Create a single application-level pattern:

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import com.gsir.security.exception.AccessDeniedException;

import java.util.UUID;

public final class TenantAccess {

    private TenantAccess() {

    }

    public static void requireMatch(

            UUID expectedOrganizationId,

            UUID actualOrganizationId,

            UUID expectedWorkspaceId,

            UUID actualWorkspaceId

    ) {

        if (!expectedOrganizationId.equals(

                actualOrganizationId

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        if (!expectedWorkspaceId.equals(

                actualWorkspaceId

        )) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

    }

}

This is a defensive application check.

It does not replace tenant-scoped database queries.

## 8. Project Service

package com.gsir.project;

import com.gsir.security.authorization.AuthorizationService;

import com.gsir.security.exception.AccessDeniedException;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.util.UUID;

@Service

public class ProjectAccessService {

    private final ProjectQueryPort projectQuery;

    private final AuthorizationService authorizationService;

    public ProjectAccessService(

            ProjectQueryPort projectQuery,

            AuthorizationService authorizationService

    ) {

        this.projectQuery = projectQuery;

        this.authorizationService = authorizationService;

    }

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)

    public ProjectAccessRecord requireAccess(

            UUID userId,

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId,

            UUID projectId

    ) {

        authorizationService.requireWorkspaceMembership(

                userId,

                organizationId,

                workspaceId

        );

        ProjectAccessRecord project =

                projectQuery.findForAccess(

                        projectId,

                        organizationId,

                        workspaceId

                ).orElseThrow(

                        AccessDeniedException::new

                );

        TenantAccess.requireMatch(

                organizationId,

                project.organizationId(),

                workspaceId,

                project.workspaceId()

        );

        return project;

    }

}

## 9. Collection Queries

IDOR protection also applies to collection endpoints.

Unsafe:

List<ProjectEntity> findAll();

for a tenant-facing endpoint.

Preferred:

List<ProjectEntity>

findAllByOrganizationIdAndWorkspaceId(

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId

);

Example:

package com.gsir.persistence.repository;

import com.gsir.persistence.entity.ProjectEntity;

import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;

import java.util.List;

import java.util.UUID;

public interface ProjectCollectionRepository

        extends JpaRepository<ProjectEntity, UUID> {

    List<ProjectEntity>

    findAllByOrganizationIdAndWorkspaceId(

            UUID organizationId,

            UUID workspaceId

    );

}

This ensures the database performs the tenant restriction.

## 10. Prevent Accidental Unscoped Access

For protected application services, establish the rule:

findById()

may only be used when:

- the resource is not tenant-scoped; or

- a higher-level invariant has already established ownership and the usage is deliberately documented.

For normal tenant operations, prefer:

findByIdAndTenant(...)

or an equivalent scoped query.

This is a code-review rule as much as a technical rule.

## 11. IDOR Test Matrix

### Same tenant

User → Organization A

Workspace → A1

Project → A1/P1

request(P1)

→ 200 / allowed

### Different workspace

User → Workspace A1

request(Project P2)

Project P2 → Workspace A2

→ 403

### Different organization

User → Organization A

request(Project P3)

Project P3 → Organization B

→ 403

### Random UUID

request(nonexistent UUID)

→ denied

The application must not expose whether a random identifier corresponds to another tenant's resource.

### Enumeration attempt

P1

P2

P3

P4

...

must not allow discovery of resources belonging to other tenants.

## 12. Mutation Protection

Every mutation must use the same tenant-aware lookup.

Unsafe:

projectRepository.findById(projectId)

        .ifPresent(project -> project.update(...));

Secure:

ProjectAccessRecord project =

        projectAccessService.requireAccess(

                principal.userId(),

                principal.organizationId(),

                workspaceId,

                projectId

        );

projectService.updateAuthorized(

        project,

        request

);

Authorization occurs before the state transition.

## 13. Delete Protection

Deletion requires exactly the same tenant boundary.

DELETE /projects/{projectId}

must not mean:

delete(projectId)

It means:

authenticate

→ authorize organization

→ authorize workspace

→ verify project tenant

→ verify DELETE permission

→ delete

## 14. Defense-in-Depth Model

GSIR now has multiple independent protections:

              Request

                 │

                 ▼

        JWT Authentication

                 │

                 ▼

          Session Validation

                 │

                 ▼

       Organization Membership

                 │

                 ▼

         Workspace Membership

                 │

                 ▼

        Tenant-Scoped Query

                 │

                 ▼

       Resource Ownership Check

                 │

                 ▼

          Permission Check

                 │

                 ▼

             Mutation

A failure at any stage prevents the operation.

## 15. AGI/Tool Boundary

The future GSIR AGI layer must use exactly the same authorization boundary.

An AI-generated action such as:

update project

delete note

read document

send message

execute computation

must become a controlled tool request.

Conceptually:

AGI

 ↓

Action Request

 ↓

Tool Gateway

 ↓

Authenticated User Context

 ↓

Authorization Service

 ↓

Tenant-Scoped Persistence

 ↓

Operation

The AGI must never receive a bypass such as:

repository.findById(id)

repository.deleteById(id)

as an unrestricted tool.

This is a core safety property of the integrated AGI architecture.

## 16. Security Invariants

### Invariant 1

A resource UUID does not establish authorization.

### Invariant 2

Tenant predicates must be applied at persistence/query boundaries.

### Invariant 3

Collection queries must also be tenant-scoped.

### Invariant 4

Mutation requires authorization before state change.

### Invariant 5

AI/AGI tool execution cannot bypass authorization.

### Invariant 6

Cross-tenant access must fail closed.

## Percentage of Progress

Authentication/Security Foundation: ~62%

Completed:

- authentication;

- JWT/session validation;

- organization/workspace authorization;

- membership persistence;

- tenant-integrity design;

- resource authorization;

- tenant-scoped persistence contracts;

- IDOR protection;

- collection isolation;

- mutation/delete authorization boundary;

- AGI tool authorization boundary.

Part 258 — Implement centralized permission evaluation and method-level authorization without duplicating security logic in controllers.

# Part 258 — Centralized Permission Evaluation and Method-Level Authorization

## Aim of the Code

Create one deterministic permission-evaluation boundary for GSIR.

The system must avoid repeating authorization rules throughout controllers and services.

The authorization model becomes:

Authentication

      ↓

Tenant Membership

      ↓

Resource Scope

      ↓

Permission Evaluation

      ↓

Application Operation

The permission evaluator must be reusable by:

- REST controllers;

- application services;

- background jobs;

- workflow execution;

- AI/AGI tool execution.

It must never grant access merely because a request originates from an internal service.

## Code

### 1. Permission Context

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import java.util.UUID;

public record PermissionContext(

        UUID userId,

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId,

        UUID resourceId,

        ResourceScope resourceScope

) {

}

The context contains only information required for the authorization decision.

### 2. Permission Decision

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

public record PermissionDecision(

        boolean allowed

) {

    public static PermissionDecision allow() {

        return new PermissionDecision(true);

    }

    public static PermissionDecision deny() {

        return new PermissionDecision(false);

    }

}

The external API must not expose internal authorization reasoning.

### 3. Permission Evaluator

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

public interface PermissionEvaluator {

    PermissionDecision evaluate(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    );

    void require(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    );

}

### 4. Centralized Evaluator Implementation

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import com.gsir.security.exception.AccessDeniedException;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service

public class PermissionEvaluatorImpl

        implements PermissionEvaluator {

    private final AuthorizationService authorizationService;

    public PermissionEvaluatorImpl(

            AuthorizationService authorizationService

    ) {

        this.authorizationService = authorizationService;

    }

    @Override

    public PermissionDecision evaluate(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    ) {

        try {

            evaluateInternal(context, permission);

            return PermissionDecision.allow();

        } catch (AccessDeniedException ex) {

            return PermissionDecision.deny();

        }

    }

    @Override

    public void require(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    ) {

        evaluateInternal(context, permission);

    }

    private void evaluateInternal(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    ) {

        if (context == null ||

                context.userId() == null ||

                context.organizationId() == null) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        switch (context.resourceScope()) {

            case ORGANIZATION ->

                    authorizationService

                            .requireOrganizationMembership(

                                    context.userId(),

                                    context.organizationId()

                            );

            case WORKSPACE ->

                    requireWorkspace(

                            context

                    );

            case PROJECT ->

                    requireProject(

                            context

                    );

        }

        evaluateRolePermission(

                context,

                permission

        );

    }

    private void requireWorkspace(

            PermissionContext context

    ) {

        if (context.workspaceId() == null) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        authorizationService

                .requireWorkspaceMembership(

                        context.userId(),

                        context.organizationId(),

                        context.workspaceId()

                );

    }

    private void requireProject(

            PermissionContext context

    ) {

        if (context.workspaceId() == null ||

                context.resourceId() == null) {

            throw new AccessDeniedException();

        }

        authorizationService

                .requireWorkspaceMembership(

                        context.userId(),

                        context.organizationId(),

                        context.workspaceId()

                );

    }

    private void evaluateRolePermission(

            PermissionContext context,

            ResourcePermission permission

    ) {

        /*

         * The exact permission-to-role matrix must follow

         * the approved GSIR authorization policy.

         *

         * Until that policy is formally approved, fail closed

         * rather than inventing permissions.

         */

        throw new UnsupportedOperationException(

                "Permission matrix is not yet approved"

        );

    }

}

### Important

The final evaluateRolePermission() implementation must not invent business permissions.

The role hierarchy introduced previously provides the mechanism, but the exact mapping:

ROLE → RESOURCE → OPERATION

must be an approved GSIR policy before production authorization decisions depend on it.

Until then, an unsupported permission must fail closed.

## 5. Method-Level Authorization Boundary

Create a small application annotation:

package com.gsir.security.authorization;

import java.lang.annotation.*;

@Target(ElementType.METHOD)

@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)

@Documented

public @interface RequirePermission {

    ResourcePermission value();

}

Example:

@RequirePermission(ResourcePermission.READ)

public NoteResponse getNote(...) {

    ...

}

This annotation describes the required operation.

It does not itself perform authorization.

## 6. Why the Annotation Is Not Sufficient

Avoid implementing security as:

@RequirePermission(READ)

with an interceptor that guesses:

- organization;

- workspace;

- project;

- resource ID;

- user identity.

Parameter-name inference is fragile and can become a security vulnerability.

The authorization context must be explicitly constructed.

Preferred:

PermissionContext context =

        new PermissionContext(

                principal.userId(),

                principal.organizationId(),

                workspaceId,

                noteId,

                ResourceScope.WORKSPACE

        );

permissionEvaluator.require(

        context,

        ResourcePermission.READ

);

## 7. Application-Service Pattern

A protected application service should follow:

@Transactional(readOnly = true)

public NoteResponse getNote(

        SecurityPrincipal principal,

        UUID workspaceId,

        UUID noteId

) {

    PermissionContext context =

            new PermissionContext(

                    principal.userId(),

                    principal.organizationId(),

                    workspaceId,

                    noteId,

                    ResourceScope.WORKSPACE

            );

    permissionEvaluator.require(

            context,

            ResourcePermission.READ

    );

    return noteQueryService.getAuthorized(

            principal.organizationId(),

            workspaceId,

            noteId

    );

}

The service therefore has explicit security inputs.

## 8. Write Operations

For updates:

permissionEvaluator.require(

        context,

        ResourcePermission.UPDATE

);

Only after successful authorization:

authorize

   ↓

load tenant-scoped resource

   ↓

validate business rules

   ↓

mutate

   ↓

persist

   ↓

outbox event

Never:

load

   ↓

mutate

   ↓

authorize

## 9. Delete Operations

Deletion requires its own permission:

permissionEvaluator.require(

        context,

        ResourcePermission.DELETE

);

Then:

authorized delete

      ↓

transaction

      ↓

database mutation

      ↓

audit/outbox processing

The delete operation must not be exposed through an unrestricted repository method.

## 10. Background Jobs

Background execution must carry an explicit security context.

Unsafe:

jobRunner.execute(

        () -> projectRepository.deleteById(id)

);

Preferred conceptual contract:

jobRunner.execute(

        new AuthorizedJobContext(

                organizationId,

                workspaceId,

                initiatingUserId

        ),

        () -> projectService.performAuthorizedOperation(...)

);

A system job may have a separate trusted-service identity, but that identity must be explicit and policy-controlled.

Internal execution must not automatically imply unlimited tenant access.

## 11. AI/AGI Tool Execution

The same evaluator must sit behind the Tool Gateway.

AGI

 │

 ▼

Tool Request

 │

 ▼

Tool Gateway

 │

 ▼

PermissionContext

 │

 ▼

PermissionEvaluator

 │

 ├── DENY → stop

 │

 └── ALLOW

       │

       ▼

Tenant-scoped operation

The model cannot choose its own permission.

For example, an AI-generated request:

DELETE project P

does not mean:

AI says delete → delete

It means:

AI proposes action

        ↓

Tool validates request

        ↓

User/session context

        ↓

Tenant authorization

        ↓

DELETE permission

        ↓

business validation

        ↓

execution

## 12. Fail-Closed Permission Handling

Unsupported combinations must never default to allow.

Forbidden pattern:

default:

    return PermissionDecision.allow();

Required pattern:

default:

    return PermissionDecision.deny();

Likewise, malformed authorization context must result in denial.

## 13. Permission Matrix Contract

Before production implementation, GSIR must explicitly approve a matrix similar to:

| **Scope** | **Role** | **READ** | **CREATE** | **UPDATE** | **DELETE** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization | OWNER | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Organization | ADMIN | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | policy |
| Organization | MEMBER | ✓ | policy | policy | ✗ |
| Workspace | OWNER | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Workspace | ADMIN | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | policy |
| Workspace | MEMBER | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Workspace | VIEWER | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

This table is a policy placeholder, not an architectural approval.

The exact values must be finalized through the project's governance/decision process.

## 14. Tests

### Deny without authentication

no SecurityPrincipal

→ DENY

### Deny without organization membership

authenticated

+ no organization membership

→ DENY

### Deny without workspace membership

authenticated

+ organization member

+ no workspace membership

→ DENY

### Unsupported permission

permission matrix unresolved

→ DENY

### Cross-tenant context

user → organization A

context → organization B

→ DENY

### AGI tool

AI proposes DELETE

+ user lacks DELETE

→ tool execution blocked

### Authorized operation

authenticated

+ valid membership

+ valid tenant

+ approved permission

→ ALLOW

## 15. Security Architecture Rule

There must be one authoritative permission-evaluation mechanism.

Avoid:

Controller authorization

Service authorization

AI authorization

Job authorization

with subtly different rules.

Prefer:

                  PermissionEvaluator

                         │

        ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐

        ▼                ▼                ▼

    REST API          Jobs/Workflows    AI Tools

        │                │                │

        └────────────────┼────────────────┘

                         ▼

                 Tenant-scoped service

This reduces authorization drift.

## 16. Important Implementation Gate

At this point, the mechanism for centralized authorization exists, but the final business permission matrix is not yet approved.

Therefore:

Authentication:                 READY

Tenant membership:              READY

Resource tenant isolation:      READY

Permission mechanism:           READY

Final permission policy:        NOT APPROVED

Production authorization:       NOT READY

No implementation should silently convert the placeholder matrix into final product policy.

# Part 259 — Authentication Rate Limiting and Abuse Protection

## Aim of the Code

Protect GSIR authentication endpoints from automated abuse, credential-stuffing attempts, brute-force attacks, token abuse, and excessive authentication traffic.

The protection must:

- apply before expensive authentication work;

- avoid storing plaintext passwords or tokens;

- use bounded resource consumption;

- distinguish authentication failures from normal application traffic;

- avoid creating a new microservice;

- remain compatible with the existing Redis/BullMQ infrastructure;

- fail safely if the rate-limit state becomes unavailable.

The initial implementation should remain small and deterministic.

## Code

### 1. Rate-Limit Policy

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

public record RateLimitPolicy(

        int maximumRequests,

        java.time.Duration window

) {

}

### 2. Authentication Rate-Limit Policies

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

import java.time.Duration;

public final class AuthenticationRateLimitPolicies {

    private AuthenticationRateLimitPolicies() {

    }

    public static final RateLimitPolicy LOGIN =

            new RateLimitPolicy(

                    10,

                    Duration.ofMinutes(1)

            );

    public static final RateLimitPolicy REGISTRATION =

            new RateLimitPolicy(

                    5,

                    Duration.ofMinutes(10)

            );

    public static final RateLimitPolicy REFRESH =

            new RateLimitPolicy(

                    30,

                    Duration.ofMinutes(1)

            );

}

These are initial engineering defaults, not final security-policy approval.

Production values must be validated using measured traffic and abuse testing.

## 3. Rate-Limit Key

Never use a plaintext password, access token, or refresh token as a rate-limit key.

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

public record RateLimitKey(

        String namespace,

        String identifier

) {

}

Examples:

auth:login:ip:<normalized-ip>

auth:login:account:<normalized-account>

auth:register:ip:<normalized-ip>

auth:refresh:session:<session-id>

## 4. Rate-Limit Decision

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

public record RateLimitDecision(

        boolean allowed,

        long retryAfterSeconds

) {

    public static RateLimitDecision allow() {

        return new RateLimitDecision(true, 0);

    }

    public static RateLimitDecision deny(

            long retryAfterSeconds

    ) {

        return new RateLimitDecision(

                false,

                Math.max(1, retryAfterSeconds)

        );

    }

}

## 5. Rate-Limiter Port

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

public interface RateLimiter {

    RateLimitDecision check(

            RateLimitKey key,

            RateLimitPolicy policy

    );

}

Application code depends on this interface rather than Redis directly.

## 6. Redis Implementation Boundary

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.time.Duration;

@Component

public class RedisRateLimiter

        implements RateLimiter {

    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;

    public RedisRateLimiter(

            StringRedisTemplate redis

    ) {

        this.redis = redis;

    }

    @Override

    public RateLimitDecision check(

            RateLimitKey key,

            RateLimitPolicy policy

    ) {

        String redisKey =

                key.namespace() + ":" + key.identifier();

        Long count =

                redis.opsForValue().increment(redisKey);

        if (count == null) {

            return RateLimitDecision.deny(1);

        }

        if (count == 1) {

            redis.expire(

                    redisKey,

                    policy.window()

            );

        }

        if (count <= policy.maximumRequests()) {

            return RateLimitDecision.allow();

        }

        Long ttl =

                redis.getExpire(

                        redisKey,

                        java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.SECONDS

                );

        long retryAfter =

                ttl == null || ttl < 1

                        ? policy.window().toSeconds()

                        : ttl;

        return RateLimitDecision.deny(

                retryAfter

        );

    }

}

### Production Note

The simple INCR + EXPIRE sequence is an implementation baseline.

For production, the increment-and-expiration operation should be made atomic, for example through an appropriate Redis Lua/script or equivalent atomic mechanism.

The security boundary must not depend on a race-prone multi-command sequence.

## 7. Rate-Limit Service

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service

public class AuthenticationRateLimitService {

    private final RateLimiter rateLimiter;

    public AuthenticationRateLimitService(

            RateLimiter rateLimiter

    ) {

        this.rateLimiter = rateLimiter;

    }

    public RateLimitDecision checkLogin(

            String clientKey

    ) {

        return rateLimiter.check(

                new RateLimitKey(

                        "auth:login",

                        clientKey

                ),

                AuthenticationRateLimitPolicies.LOGIN

        );

    }

    public RateLimitDecision checkRegistration(

            String clientKey

    ) {

        return rateLimiter.check(

                new RateLimitKey(

                        "auth:registration",

                        clientKey

                ),

                AuthenticationRateLimitPolicies.REGISTRATION

        );

    }

    public RateLimitDecision checkRefresh(

            String sessionKey

    ) {

        return rateLimiter.check(

                new RateLimitKey(

                        "auth:refresh",

                        sessionKey

                ),

                AuthenticationRateLimitPolicies.REFRESH

        );

    }

}

## 8. Login Protection

The login application service must perform the rate-limit check before expensive password verification.

Conceptually:

Request

  ↓

Request validation

  ↓

Rate limit

  ↓

Credential verification

  ↓

Session creation

  ↓

Token issuance

Not:

Request

  ↓

Argon2 password verification

  ↓

Rate limit

The latter permits attackers to consume substantial CPU resources before the protection activates.

## 9. Account + Network Controls

A single IP-based limiter is insufficient.

A distributed attacker can use many addresses.

A single account-based limiter is also insufficient because an attacker can target many accounts.

Therefore login protection should eventually combine bounded dimensions:

IP/network key

       +

normalized account identifier

       +

global authentication budget

The system must avoid excessively aggressive limits that allow a malicious party to lock legitimate users out merely by repeatedly targeting their account.

The exact strategy should be validated experimentally.

## 10. Account Identifier Normalization

Rate-limit identifiers must be normalized consistently.

For example:

package com.gsir.security.ratelimit;

import java.util.Locale;

public final class AccountKeyNormalizer {

    private AccountKeyNormalizer() {

    }

    public static String normalize(

            String value

    ) {

        if (value == null) {

            return "";

        }

        return value

                .trim()

                .toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);

    }

}

The normalization rule must match the application's actual account identity semantics.

Do not introduce case-insensitive behavior into authentication merely because the rate limiter normalizes a string.

## 11. Failed Authentication

Failed authentication attempts must consume rate-limit capacity.

Example:

attempt 1 → wrong password → counted

attempt 2 → wrong password → counted

attempt 3 → wrong password → counted

...

Successful authentication should not reset a global abuse-control counter unless that behavior is explicitly designed and tested.

## 12. Refresh-Token Protection

Refresh operations must also be rate limited.

The preferred key is associated with the server-side session rather than the raw refresh token.

JWT

 ↓

session ID

 ↓

refresh operation

 ↓

rate limit

 ↓

refresh-token validation

 ↓

rotation

This protects against excessive refresh attempts while preserving the secrecy of the token itself.

## 13. HTTP Response

When a rate limit is exceeded:

response.setStatus(

        HttpServletResponse.SC_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS

);

response.setHeader(

        "Retry-After",

        Long.toString(

                decision.retryAfterSeconds()

        )

);

The response body should remain generic.

Example:

{

  "error": "RATE_LIMITED"

}

Do not reveal internal Redis keys, account state, counters, or security heuristics.

## 14. Fail-Safe Rule

Rate-limit infrastructure failure requires an explicit policy.

For security-sensitive authentication endpoints, the initial default should be:

Rate limiter unavailable

        ↓

Do not silently bypass protection

        ↓

Fail closed or enter a tightly bounded emergency mode

The exact availability/security trade-off must be tested before production.

For ordinary non-security-critical application requests, a different policy may be appropriate.

## 15. Proxy/IP Trust

Do not blindly trust:

X-Forwarded-For

from arbitrary clients.

The application must only use forwarded client-address information when requests pass through a configured trusted proxy/load-balancer boundary.

Otherwise an attacker can generate:

X-Forwarded-For: random-IP

and bypass an IP-based limiter.

## 16. Authentication Abuse Events

Rate-limit violations should be observable through the existing security/audit infrastructure.

Conceptual event:

package com.gsir.security.audit;

public record AuthenticationRateLimitExceeded(

        String operation,

        String requestId

) {

}

Do not persist:

- passwords;

- raw access tokens;

- raw refresh tokens;

- authorization headers.

Only safe metadata should be recorded.

## 17. Tests

### Below limit

10 requests

→ allowed

### Limit exceeded

11th request

→ 429

### Window expiration

window expires

→ requests allowed again

### Separate clients

client A

client B

A's limit

≠

B's limit

### Account targeting

Repeated attempts against one account must trigger account-level protection.

### Distributed attack

Multiple client identifiers targeting the same account must still encounter account-level protection.

### Forwarded header spoofing

Untrusted client-supplied forwarding headers must not arbitrarily change the effective client identity.

### Redis failure

The configured failure policy must be deterministic and tested.

### Refresh abuse

Repeated refresh attempts must trigger the refresh limiter.

## 18. Security Invariant

For authentication operation (A):

[ Execute(A) \Rightarrow RateLimit(A)=Allowed ]

and:

[ CredentialVerification ]

must occur only after the relevant rate-limit gate.

The complete login condition becomes:

[ Login = ValidRequest \land RateLimitAllowed \land CredentialsValid ]

followed by session and token issuance.

## 19. Architectural Rule

Do not introduce a separate rate-limiting service or security microservice.

Use:

Spring Boot

   │

   ├── Authentication

   ├── Authorization

   └── Rate Limiting

            │

            ▼

          Redis

Redis is an implementation dependency for shared rate-limit state, not a second source of identity or authorization truth.

## Percentage of Progress

Authentication/Security Foundation: ~68%

Completed:

- authentication;

- JWT cryptographic verification;

- claim validation;

- session validation;

- organization/workspace authorization;

- resource authorization;

- tenant-scoped persistence;

- IDOR protection;

- centralized permission boundary;

- authentication abuse-control architecture;

- login/registration/refresh rate-limit boundaries;

- security-event boundary.

Remaining major security/authentication work:

- production-grade atomic rate limiter;

- final permission policy;

- session/account hardening;

- audit/security integration;

- OpenAPI security contract;

- comprehensive integration tests;

- final security gate.
