## 290.4 Hard Production Blockers

The following are automatic NO-GO conditions when applicable to implemented functionality:

cross-tenant data exposure

authorization bypass

privilege escalation

credential exposure

unrestricted AI execution

unrestricted tool execution

unrestricted shell execution

unrestricted filesystem access

unrestricted network access

unsafe arbitrary SQL execution

unvalidated protected state mutation

broken session revocation

refresh-token replay vulnerability

critical persistence corruption

critical schema mismatch

mandatory security regression failure

Any such condition results in:

AI_PRODUCTION_NOT_READY

## 290.5 Authentication Gate

Verify that AI requests rely on the established authentication system.

Required:

valid authentication → allowed where authorized

missing authentication → denied for protected operation

expired session → denied

revoked session → denied

invalid JWT → denied

invalid signature → denied

invalid issuer/audience → denied

invalid security context → denied

AI must not maintain an independent authentication authority.

## 290.6 Tenant-Isolation Gate

Required:

Tenant A → Tenant A resources

Tenant B → Tenant B resources

Tenant A → Tenant B resource = DENY

Tenant B → Tenant A resource = DENY

Verify this through:

direct API

AI context retrieval

AI request

Tool Gateway

background jobs

persistence

A single unresolved cross-tenant path is a NO-GO.

## 290.7 Resource Authorization Gate

Verify:

organization membership

workspace membership

project access

resource permission

where applicable.

Test:

READ

CREATE

UPDATE

DELETE

according to the implemented permission model.

Authorization must occur before sensitive data retrieval or side effects.

## 290.8 AI Request Security Gate

Every protected AI request must pass:

authentication

tenant validation

resource authorization

request validation

security policy

context policy

before provider execution.

Reject:

missing identity

forged tenant

invalid resource

invalid request

oversized request

unsafe instruction where policy prohibits execution

## 290.9 Context Gate

Verify:

authorized retrieval

tenant filtering

resource filtering

secret filtering

provenance

deterministic ordering

deduplication

budget enforcement

prompt/data separation

Context overflow must not silently remove critical scientific evidence.

If required context cannot safely fit:

REJECT

or use an explicitly approved summarization mechanism.

## 290.10 Prompt-Injection Gate

Treat retrieved content, documents, web content, and tool results as untrusted data.

Test adversarial instructions attempting to:

reveal secrets

change permissions

access another tenant

invoke administrative tools

modify security settings

execute arbitrary commands

Expected:

NO_AUTHORITY_ESCALATION

Prompt-injection testing does not establish that all prompt injection is solved; it establishes whether the implemented authorization boundaries remain intact under tested attacks.

## 290.11 Model-Routing Gate

Verify:

hard eligibility

→ capability compatibility

→ privacy policy

→ context capacity

→ availability

→ quality/cost/latency policy

→ deterministic selection

Verify fallback behavior is:

bounded

authorized

observable

deterministic where required

No fallback may silently violate privacy or capability requirements.

## 290.12 Provider Gate

For each production-enabled provider:

credentials

endpoint

authentication

capabilities

timeouts

error normalization

retry policy

availability

must be verified.

Application code must not depend on provider-specific behavior outside the adapter boundary.

If a provider is configured but not actually verified:

PROVIDER_STATUS = UNVERIFIED

Do not mark it production-ready merely because configuration exists.

## 290.13 Credential Gate

Verify that secrets are supplied only through the approved secret boundary.

Search for:

hardcoded API keys

private keys

tokens

passwords

refresh tokens

provider credentials

secrets in configuration

secrets in logs

secrets in AI context

Any confirmed production credential exposure is a NO-GO.

## 290.14 Output Validation Gate

Every provider response must pass validation before protected side effects.

Required boundary:

Provider Output

      ↓

Normalization

      ↓

Validation

      ↓

Approved Output

      ↓

Persistence / Tool / State Mutation

The model must not directly:

grant authorization

change tenant ownership

mark evidence verified

execute arbitrary operations

publish protected state

## 290.15 Scientific-Evidence Gate

Where scientific evidence functionality is implemented, distinguish:

source

evidence

claim

interpretation

hypothesis

verified result

AI output cannot independently promote:

HYPOTHESIS

to:

VERIFIED_RESULT

without an independent approved verification process.

Citations demonstrate provenance, not truth.

## 290.16 Tool Gateway Gate

Every AI-triggered tool must pass:

tool existence

tool version

argument validation

authentication

resource authorization

capability authorization

risk policy

confirmation

execution limits

sandbox

network policy

result validation

audit

Unknown or unauthorized tools must fail closed.

## 290.17 High-Risk Tool Gate

For high-risk operations verify that the system requires the appropriate confirmation or policy authorization.

Examples:

external side effect

resource deletion

external API mutation

production state mutation

dangerous computation

The AI cannot manufacture its own confirmation.

A model-generated phrase such as:

"User has approved this."

is not sufficient evidence of human confirmation.

## 290.18 Sandbox Gate

For untrusted computation or code execution verify:

CPU limit

memory limit

execution timeout

filesystem restriction

network restriction

process restriction

output limit

resource cleanup

If the sandbox cannot enforce the required boundaries:

NO-GO

for the affected execution capability.

Do not disable sandboxing merely to make an integration test pass.

## 290.19 Network Security Gate

For tools capable of network access:

allowlist

DNS/host validation

SSRF protection

redirect handling

private-network protection

credential isolation

request limits

timeout

response limits

must be verified where applicable.

AI-generated URLs must never automatically receive unrestricted network access.

## 290.20 Persistence Gate

Verify:

AI run lifecycle

output persistence

tenant ownership

retry separation

failure state

transaction behavior

idempotency

audit relationship

A remote provider call must not remain inside a long database transaction merely to simplify orchestration.

## 290.21 PostgreSQL Gate

Production PostgreSQL verification is mandatory for database-dependent production claims.

Verify:

Flyway

schema

constraints

indexes

foreign keys

tenant queries

transactions

concurrency

rollback

If unavailable:

POSTGRESQL_GATE = BLOCKED

and the final result cannot be:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY

for capabilities whose correctness depends on that evidence.

## 290.22 Redis Gate

Verify actual Redis behavior for:

rate limiting

atomic operations

expiration

concurrency

timeouts

failure handling

connection security

If Redis is mandatory and unavailable:

REDIS_GATE = BLOCKED

Do not replace it with an in-memory implementation and declare the production gate passed.

## 290.23 Rate-Limiting Gate

Verify:

login

registration

refresh

AI requests

tool execution

expensive computation

where those limits are implemented.

Verify limits are:

bounded

tenant-aware where required

atomic

observable

resistant to abuse

Do not use account lockout mechanisms that create trivial denial-of-service against other users unless explicitly justified.

## 290.24 Concurrency Gate

Test security-sensitive concurrent operations.

At minimum where implemented:

refresh-token rotation

idempotent mutations

resource mutation

tool execution

rate limiting

job execution

The result must not depend on timing tricks.

## 290.25 Failure-Handling Gate

Force representative failures:

provider timeout

provider outage

database failure

Redis failure

authorization failure

validation failure

tool failure

sandbox failure

network failure

unexpected exception

Verify:

no unauthorized side effect

safe error

correct run state

safe logging

audit safety

bounded retry

## 290.26 Retry Gate

Verify retry behavior is:

bounded

classified

observable

idempotency-aware

provider-aware

Do not retry non-idempotent operations blindly.

Do not create infinite AI/tool retry loops.

Each meaningful AI execution attempt remains independently identifiable.

## 290.27 Observability Gate

Verify production operators can determine:

request

AI run

provider

model

model version

latency

status

failure category

tool invocation

resource usage

without exposing:

API credentials

tokens

private keys

sensitive user data

hidden chain-of-thought

## 290.28 Audit Gate

Verify security-sensitive events are auditable where required.

Examples:

authentication failure

session revocation

authorization denial

tool execution

high-risk confirmation

AI execution failure

security policy failure

important state mutation

Audit records must contain safe metadata only.

## 290.29 Dependency Gate

Review production dependencies for:

known critical vulnerabilities

unnecessary dependencies

duplicate libraries

unused provider SDKs

unapproved execution libraries

insecure defaults

A vulnerability affecting an unused dependency must still be classified according to actual reachability and deployment exposure.

Do not automatically ignore dependency findings.

## 290.30 Configuration Gate

Verify production configuration:

no development credentials

no debug mode

no permissive CORS where inappropriate

secure cookies where applicable

secure headers

appropriate timeouts

database credentials externalized

provider credentials externalized

Redis credentials externalized

JWT keys externalized

Configuration must match the actual deployment model.

## 290.31 Build and Artifact Gate

Verify:

clean build

tests

packaging

migration availability

configuration availability

startup behavior

The application must start using the intended production configuration without silently falling back to insecure development defaults.

## 290.32 Performance Gate

Measure where applicable:

authentication overhead

AI Gateway overhead

context construction

routing

validation

tool policy

persistence

total application overhead

Separate application latency from external provider latency.

No performance claim should be made without measurement.

## 290.33 Resource-Budget Gate

Verify bounds for:

request size

context size

provider request

provider response

tool calls

tool recursion

execution time

CPU

memory

network requests

database queries

job attempts

Unbounded resource consumption is a production blocker for the affected capability.

## 290.34 End-to-End Production Path

Execute the complete representative path:

Authenticated User

        ↓

Authorized Tenant

        ↓

Authorized Resource

        ↓

AI Request

        ↓

Context

        ↓

Model Router

        ↓

Provider

        ↓

Output Validation

        ↓

Tool Gateway if necessary

        ↓

Application Service

        ↓

Persistence

        ↓

Audit

        ↓

Response

Then execute representative denial paths.

A successful path without denial-path verification is insufficient.

## 290.35 Final Security Regression

Run the complete permanent security matrix.

Authentication

JWT

Session

Refresh

Logout

RBAC

Tenant Isolation

IDOR

Prompt Injection

Context Injection

Tool Escalation

Provider Manipulation

Credential Leakage

Sandbox

Network

Rate Limiting

Concurrency

Background Jobs

Error Disclosure

Audit

Any mandatory failure produces:

NO-GO

## 290.36 Final Evidence Reconciliation

Compare:

Part 284 gate

Part 285 audit

Part 286 reconciliation

Part 287 remediation

Part 288 regression

Part 289 evidence package

Part 290 execution

Every discrepancy must be explained.

If the current repository differs from the evidence snapshot:

RE-RUN AFFECTED VERIFICATION

Do not certify stale evidence.

## 290.37 Go/No-Go Algorithm

Conceptually:

IF critical security failure

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF cross-tenant access is possible

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF unrestricted execution exists

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF credential exposure exists

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF mandatory regression fails

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF mandatory PostgreSQL evidence is blocked

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF mandatory Redis evidence is blocked

    → NO-GO

ELSE IF mandatory provider evidence is missing

    → NO-GO for that provider/capability

ELSE IF mandatory evidence remains unverified

    → NO-GO

ELSE

    → GO

The exact applicability of PostgreSQL, Redis, and provider requirements must follow the actual deployed capability set.

## 290.38 Production Decision

Allowed final decisions:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY

All mandatory production criteria are verified.

AI_PRODUCTION_READY_WITH_EXPLICIT_SCOPE

Only if the deployment scope explicitly excludes unverified capabilities and the deployed subset independently satisfies all mandatory criteria.

AI_PRODUCTION_NOT_READY

One or more mandatory implementation/security criteria fail.

AI_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED

Required infrastructure or external evidence is unavailable.

## 290.39 Scope-Restricted Readiness

If only part of the AI subsystem is production-ready, identify the exact capability boundary.

Example:

READY:

text generation

authorized context retrieval

validated persistence

NOT READY:

external network tools

untrusted code execution

live Provider X integration

Do not call the entire AI subsystem production-ready when only a subset has passed.

## 290.40 No Percentage Override

The progress value must never influence the gate.

For example:

+

one critical security failure

=

NO-GO

Likewise:

+

all mandatory deployed capabilities fully verified

=

possible GO

Evidence controls the decision.

If any mandatory field is not verified, do not generate a passing certificate.

## 290.45 Transition Rule

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY

then the AI foundation is frozen as a verified subsystem and the project may transition to the next GSIR capability layer.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_NOT_READY

return to the smallest relevant remediation part.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED

resolve the infrastructure verification requirement before making architectural changes.

Do not continue adding advanced AGI capabilities on top of a failed mandatory security boundary.

## 290.46 AGI Boundary

The future unified AGI cognitive architecture may use:

Perception

Attention

Cognitive State

Memory

World Model

Reasoning/Planning

Action/Tool

Learning

Metacognition

Consolidation

but these capabilities must consume the verified AI/security/tool boundaries rather than bypass them.

The cognitive layer cannot become:

authorization authority

security authority

tenant authority

secret authority

unrestricted execution authority

## 290.47 Final Invariants

A GO decision requires:

No known critical security bypass.

No known cross-tenant data path.

No unrestricted AI execution.

No unrestricted tool execution.

No uncontrolled network access.

No exposed production credentials.

No unvalidated protected state mutation.

No mandatory regression failures.

No unresolved mandatory schema integrity failure.

Required PostgreSQL evidence verified.

Required Redis evidence verified.

Required provider evidence verified.

Security boundaries are enforced by code.

AI output remains untrusted until validated.

Tools remain controlled capabilities.

Scientific verification remains independent from model assertion.

Audit and observability do not expose secrets.

Evidence corresponds to the current repository.

GSIR implementation/documentation progress: approximately 96%.

# Part 291 — Post-Gate Freeze, AI Core Baseline, and Transition to the Unified GSIR AGI Cognitive Runtime

## Aim of the Code

Freeze the verified AI foundation after the Part 290 production-gate decision and establish the implementation boundary for the next GSIR layer: the unified AGI cognitive runtime.

This part does not create another AI Gateway, another model router, another tool system, or another authorization system.

The cognitive runtime is an orchestration and reasoning layer operating inside the existing security and execution boundaries.

Its purpose is to provide a compact foundation for:

Perception

Attention

Cognitive State

Memory

World Model

Reasoning / Planning

Action / Tool

Learning

Metacognition

Consolidation

while keeping the implementation small, measurable, testable, and replaceable.

## 291.1 Post-Gate Freeze

After Part 290, freeze the verified AI foundation.

The following interfaces must not be redesigned merely to support AGI:

Authentication

Tenant Context

Authorization

AI Gateway

AI Request

AI Context

Model Router

Provider Adapter

Output Validator

AI Run Persistence

Tool Gateway

Tool Authorization

Execution Policy

Sandbox

Audit

Future AGI code consumes these boundaries.

It does not replace them.

## 291.2 Production-Gate Dependency

The cognitive runtime must respect the actual Part 290 result.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY

the verified AI foundation may be treated as the stable runtime boundary.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY_WITH_EXPLICIT_SCOPE

the AGI runtime must operate only inside the verified scope.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_NOT_READY

or:

AI_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED

the AGI runtime may be developed and unit-tested where safe, but production execution must not bypass the unresolved gate.

## 291.3 Cognitive Runtime Principle

Do not implement AGI as a collection of autonomous agents.

Preferred structure:

                    ┌──────────────────┐

                    │ Cognitive State  │

                    └────────┬─────────┘

                             │

       ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐

       ↓                     ↓                     ↓

 Perception              Attention             Memory

       │                     │                     │

       └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘

                             ↓

                       World Model

                             ↓

                    Reasoning / Planning

                             ↓

                         Action

                             ↓

                      Tool Gateway

                             ↓

                       Observation

                             │

                             └────────→ Cognitive State

Learning, metacognition, and consolidation operate as controlled processes around this loop.

## 291.4 Unified Cognitive Runtime Contract

Create one primary orchestration boundary:

public interface CognitiveRuntime {

    CognitiveResult execute(CognitiveRequest request);

}

The runtime must not expose provider-specific details.

It should receive a bounded request and return a validated cognitive result.

## 291.5 CognitiveRequest

Use a minimal request structure:

public record CognitiveRequest(

        String requestId,

        String userId,

        String organizationId,

        String workspaceId,

        String projectId,

        String instruction,

        CognitiveMode mode

) {}

Do not add fields merely because future AGI concepts might need them.

Additional state must enter through explicit runtime services.

## 291.6 CognitiveMode

The runtime should support the approved GSIR operating modes:

public enum CognitiveMode {

    AUTOMATIC,

    ANALYSIS,

    HYPOTHESIS,

    SOP_GENERATING

}

Mode selection controls behavior and policy.

It does not create four separate AI systems.

## 291.7 CognitiveResult

Use a normalized result:

public record CognitiveResult(

        String requestId,

        CognitiveStatus status,

        String response,

        List<CognitiveEvidence> evidence,

        List<CognitiveObservation> observations

) {}

The result must not contain hidden chain-of-thought.

Only approved summaries, evidence, observations, decisions, and externally useful reasoning artifacts may be exposed or persisted.

## 291.8 CognitiveStatus

Use a small lifecycle:

public enum CognitiveStatus {

    COMPLETED,

    NEEDS_INPUT,

    TOOL_REQUIRED,

    VALIDATION_FAILED,

    FAILED,

    CANCELLED

}

Do not create dozens of cognitive states before actual workflows require them.

## 291.9 Cognitive State

The runtime needs a bounded working state.

public record CognitiveState(

        String taskId,

        CognitiveMode mode,

        String objective,

        List<StateFact> facts,

        List<StateConstraint> constraints,

        List<StateHypothesis> hypotheses,

        List<StateObservation> observations

) {}

The state is not automatically permanent memory.

## 291.10 State vs Memory

Maintain an explicit distinction:

Cognitive State

=

temporary working state for the current execution

Memory

=

information intentionally retained beyond the current execution

Do not write every intermediate thought or model output into persistent memory.

## 291.11 State Integrity

Every state mutation must identify:

source

timestamp

confidence/evidence status where applicable

provenance

where those concepts are implemented.

AI assertions must not silently become authoritative facts.

## 291.12 Perception Boundary

Perception converts available inputs into structured observations.

public interface PerceptionService {

    List<CognitiveObservation> perceive(

            CognitiveRequest request,

            CognitiveState state

    );

}

Inputs may include:

user instruction

authorized documents

retrieved evidence

tool results

project state

external observations

Only authorized information may enter perception.

## 291.13 Perception Does Not Authorize

Perception must never decide:

whether the user may access a resource

whether a tool may execute

whether a tenant may be accessed

whether a secret may be exposed

Those decisions remain with the existing security boundaries.

## 291.14 Attention Boundary

Attention determines which authorized information deserves processing priority.

public interface AttentionService {

    AttentionResult focus(

            CognitiveState state,

            List<CognitiveObservation> observations

    );

}

Attention may consider:

task relevance

evidence quality

recency

uncertainty

dependency

user priority

resource cost

Attention is not authorization.

## 291.15 Deterministic Attention Policy

Where possible, attention ordering should be deterministic.

For example:

hard constraints

        ↓

explicit user objective

        ↓

critical evidence

        ↓

high-relevance observations

        ↓

supporting context

        ↓

low-priority context

The actual ordering must be represented by implemented policy rather than undocumented model behavior.

## 291.16 Memory Boundary

Create an application-level memory contract:

public interface CognitiveMemory {

    List<MemoryItem> retrieve(MemoryQuery query);

    MemoryWriteResult write(MemoryWriteRequest request);

}

Memory must remain:

authorized

tenant-scoped

provenance-aware

bounded

version-aware

deletable according to retention policy

## 291.17 Memory Is Not a Chat Log

Do not treat the entire conversation history as memory.

Candidate memory should be selected based on explicit policy.

Examples:

stable project fact

verified research result

approved user preference

important experiment result

validated constraint

Temporary reasoning should not automatically become durable memory.

## 291.18 Memory Write Gate

Before durable memory creation:

candidate information

        ↓

validation

        ↓

provenance

        ↓

authorization

        ↓

memory policy

        ↓

persist

The model cannot directly write arbitrary durable memory.

## 291.19 World Model Boundary

The world model represents structured information about the task domain.

public interface WorldModel {

    WorldState getState(WorldQuery query);

    WorldUpdateResult apply(

            WorldObservation observation

    );

}

It must distinguish:

observed

reported

inferred

hypothesized

verified

unknown

## 291.20 World Model Safety

A model-generated statement must not automatically become a world-model fact.

For example:

AI says:

"Experiment succeeded."

does not automatically mean:

experiment.status = SUCCESS

Independent evidence or an approved application event must establish the state transition.

## 291.21 Reasoning Boundary

Create one reasoning abstraction:

public interface ReasoningEngine {

    ReasoningResult reason(

            CognitiveState state,

            WorldState worldState,

            AttentionResult attention

    );

}

The initial implementation may use the existing AI Gateway.

The reasoning engine must remain provider-independent.

## 291.22 Planning Boundary

Planning is a capability of reasoning, not a separate autonomous agent.

public interface PlanningEngine {

    Plan createPlan(

            CognitiveState state,

            WorldState worldState

    );

}

A plan consists of bounded steps:

observe

retrieve

calculate

compare

ask user

call authorized tool

validate

stop

## 291.23 Plan Safety

A plan does not grant permissions.

Every executable plan step must still pass:

authentication

authorization

tool policy

execution policy

resource limits

The cognitive runtime cannot bypass the Tool Gateway.

## 291.24 Action Boundary

Create one action interface:

public interface CognitiveActionService {

    ActionResult execute(

            PlannedAction action,

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    );

}

Actions requiring external capability must be routed through the existing Tool Gateway.

## 291.25 Observation Loop

After an action:

Plan

 ↓

Authorized Action

 ↓

Tool Gateway

 ↓

External Result

 ↓

Observation

 ↓

Cognitive State

 ↓

Re-evaluation

The runtime must not assume that an action succeeded merely because the action was requested.

## 291.26 Bounded Cognitive Loop

Implement an explicit loop limit.

public record CognitiveExecutionLimits(

        int maxIterations,

        int maxToolCalls,

        int maxReasoningCalls,

        Duration maxDuration

) {}

Defaults must be configuration-driven and conservative.

Never create an unbounded:

reason → tool → reason → tool → ...

loop.

## 291.27 Stop Conditions

The cognitive runtime must stop when:

objective satisfied

required evidence unavailable

user input required

validation fails

authorization fails

resource budget exhausted

iteration limit reached

tool failure requires termination

critical contradiction detected

runtime timeout reached

Stopping is a valid cognitive outcome.

## 291.28 Contradiction Handling

When information conflicts:

Fact A

≠

Fact B

do not silently choose one.

Represent:

contradiction detected

sources

provenance

evidence status

resolution status

The system may request more evidence or user clarification.

## 291.29 Uncertainty Handling

Maintain:

UNKNOWN

as a legitimate state.

Do not convert:

unknown

into:

false

or:

true

without evidence.

Likewise:

hypothesis

must remain distinct from:

verified result

## 291.30 Metacognition Boundary

Implement lightweight metacognition as control monitoring.

public interface MetacognitionService {

    MetacognitiveAssessment assess(

            CognitiveState state,

            ReasoningResult reasoning,

            CognitiveExecutionMetrics metrics

    );

}

It may evaluate:

uncertainty

missing evidence

contradictions

resource consumption

plan quality indicators

validation failures

need for clarification

It must not become an unrestricted second AI system.

## 291.31 No Recursive Agent Explosion

Do not implement:

planner agent

research agent

critic agent

memory agent

tool agent

verification agent

metacognition agent

manager agent

as independent autonomous services merely to represent cognitive functions.

Prefer lightweight services inside the same cognitive runtime.

This keeps:

latency

cost

complexity

failure modes

security boundaries

under control.

## 291.32 Learning Boundary

Learning must be separated from ordinary inference.

public interface LearningService {

    LearningResult learn(

            LearningInput input

    );

}

Learning may use:

validated outcomes

user feedback

experiment results

benchmark results

tool observations

error patterns

but only through explicit policies.

## 291.33 Learning Safety

The model cannot automatically rewrite its own production behavior.

Learning outputs should initially be:

candidate improvement

rather than:

automatic production modification

Any future self-improvement mechanism must pass independent evaluation.

## 291.34 Consolidation Boundary

Consolidation converts selected short-lived information into durable representations.

public interface ConsolidationService {

    ConsolidationResult consolidate(

            ConsolidationInput input

    );

}

Potential inputs:

validated observations

validated memory candidates

experiment outcomes

confirmed corrections

stable project knowledge

## 291.35 Consolidation Rule

Do not consolidate:

raw hidden reasoning

unverified claims

secrets

temporary tool credentials

unauthorized tenant data

arbitrary model instructions

Consolidation must preserve provenance.

## 291.36 Cognitive Runtime Orchestrator

Create one orchestration implementation:

public final class DefaultCognitiveRuntime

        implements CognitiveRuntime {

    @Override

    public CognitiveResult execute(CognitiveRequest request) {

        // orchestration only

        // implementation must call existing security,

        // context, AI Gateway and Tool Gateway boundaries

        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Implementation follows repository reconciliation");

    }

}

The orchestration must remain thin.

It coordinates components; it should not duplicate their responsibilities.

## 291.37 Runtime Sequence

The canonical execution sequence is:

Authenticated Request

        ↓

Authorization

        ↓

Cognitive State

        ↓

Perception

        ↓

Attention

        ↓

Authorized Memory/Context

        ↓

World Model

        ↓

Reasoning

        ↓

Metacognitive Check

        ↓

Planning

        ↓

Action Decision

        ↓

Tool Gateway

        ↓

Observation

        ↓

State Update

        ↓

Validation

        ↓

Memory/Consolidation if approved

        ↓

Validated Result

Not every request needs every stage.

The runtime should skip unnecessary stages to reduce latency and cost.

## 291.38 Automatic Mode

AUTOMATIC selects the smallest safe cognitive path required by the task.

Example:

simple question

→ context

→ reasoning

→ answer

rather than unnecessarily invoking:

planning

multiple tools

memory writes

consolidation

## 291.39 Analysis Mode

ANALYSIS prioritizes:

evidence

comparisons

uncertainty

reasoning

calculations

contradictions

It should produce structured, evidence-aware results where applicable.

## 291.40 Hypothesis Mode

HYPOTHESIS explicitly separates:

known evidence

inference

hypothesis

predicted consequence

required test

The mode must never silently promote a hypothesis to verified knowledge.

## 291.41 SOP-Generating Mode

SOP_GENERATING produces operational procedures from validated requirements and evidence.

Where the SOP involves physical or external action:

generate

→ validate

→ identify hazards/constraints

→ require appropriate authorization

→ execute only through approved action/tool boundaries

Generation itself does not constitute execution.

## 291.42 Scientific Task Loop

For research tasks, the preferred pattern is:

Question

 ↓

Objective

 ↓

Evidence Retrieval

 ↓

Evidence Assessment

 ↓

Knowledge/World State

 ↓

Reasoning

 ↓

Hypothesis/Plan

 ↓

Calculation/Simulation/Tool

 ↓

Observation

 ↓

Validation

 ↓

Conclusion

 ↓

Provenance

This creates a research-oriented cognitive loop without requiring a separate agent for every stage.

## 291.43 Cost-Aware Cognitive Routing

Before invoking expensive reasoning or tools, determine whether a simpler path is sufficient.

Example:

known answer

→ answer

simple calculation

→ deterministic computation

retrieval task

→ retrieval

complex research problem

→ reasoning/planning

external action

→ Tool Gateway

Do not use a large model for deterministic operations that can be safely performed by code.

## 291.44 Deterministic Computation Boundary

Mathematics, unit conversion, statistics, validation, hashing, and other deterministic operations should use deterministic application services where practical.

The model should request computation rather than invent numerical results when exact computation is required.

## 291.45 Cognitive Provenance

Every important cognitive transition should be traceable to:

request

context

source

tool

calculation

model execution

validation

observation

where supported by the existing persistence/provenance architecture.

Do not create a separate provenance database solely for AGI.

## 291.46 Security Boundary

The cognitive runtime must never directly access:

raw credentials

arbitrary database connections

unrestricted filesystem

unrestricted network

production shell

authorization internals

another tenant's context

All capabilities remain mediated.

## 291.47 Database Rule

Do not add AGI tables in Part 291 unless implementation reconciliation proves an existing table cannot represent a required concrete runtime state.

First reuse:

conversations

messages

message_parts

ai_runs

ai_outputs

files

document_chunks

notes

web_links

jobs

audit_events

where semantically appropriate.

A future schema extension requires a concrete data requirement and migration design.

## 291.48 API Rule

Do not expose every internal cognitive stage as a public REST endpoint.

Prefer:

one cognitive execution API

with internal orchestration.

Internal interfaces remain implementation boundaries rather than public APIs.

## 291.49 Testing Strategy

Create tests for:

simple inference

analysis

hypothesis separation

SOP generation

context authorization

memory authorization

world-state integrity

planning limits

tool authorization

tool failure

iteration limit

timeout

contradiction

uncertainty

metacognitive stop

learning isolation

consolidation filtering

tenant isolation

## 291.50 Cognitive Security Tests

Test that:

AI cannot grant itself permissions

AI cannot change tenant

AI cannot access unauthorized memory

AI cannot bypass Tool Gateway

AI cannot execute arbitrary code

AI cannot persist secrets

AI cannot mark evidence verified

AI cannot modify authorization policy

AI cannot create unlimited recursive actions

## 291.51 Cognitive Runtime Performance

Measure:

runtime orchestration overhead

state construction

attention

memory retrieval

reasoning calls

tool calls

validation

persistence

total execution time

Avoid measuring the model's raw latency as if it were cognitive-runtime overhead.

## 291.52 Resource Limits

The runtime must enforce:

maximum iterations

maximum model calls

maximum tool calls

maximum context

maximum execution duration

maximum output

maximum memory operations

A cognitive loop must terminate even if the model repeatedly requests continuation.

## 291.53 Failure Recovery

If a stage fails:

Perception failure

→ controlled failure

Memory failure

→ continue only if policy permits

Reasoning failure

→ retry only under bounded policy

Tool failure

→ observe failure and reassess

Validation failure

→ reject result

Authorization failure

→ stop protected action

Do not automatically retry security failures.

## 291.54 Cognitive Runtime Observability

Track:

cognitive request ID

AI run IDs

iteration count

model calls

tool calls

context fingerprint

failure category

latency

resource usage

final status

Do not log hidden chain-of-thought.

CognitiveRuntime

ReasoningEngine

PlanningEngine

Memory

WorldModel

Perception

Attention

Metacognition

Learning

Consolidation

For every existing equivalent classify:

REUSE

EXTEND

REFACTOR

REPLACE

MISSING

CONFLICT

Do not create duplicates.

The next implementation stage is permitted only when:

security boundary stable

AI Gateway stable

Tool Gateway stable

repository reconciled

cognitive interfaces mapped

database requirements known

tests defined

resource limits defined

If any security boundary is unresolved:

BLOCKED

rather than bypassing it.

# Part 291 — Post-Gate Freeze, AI Core Baseline, and Transition to the Unified GSIR AGI Cognitive Runtime

## Aim of the Code

Freeze the verified AI foundation after the Part 290 production-gate decision and establish the implementation boundary for the next GSIR layer: the unified AGI cognitive runtime.

This part does not create another AI Gateway, another model router, another tool system, or another authorization system.

The cognitive runtime is an orchestration and reasoning layer operating inside the existing security and execution boundaries.

Its purpose is to provide a compact foundation for:

Perception

Attention

Cognitive State

Memory

World Model

Reasoning / Planning

Action / Tool

Learning

Metacognition

Consolidation

while keeping the implementation small, measurable, testable, and replaceable.

## 291.1 Post-Gate Freeze

After Part 290, freeze the verified AI foundation.

The following interfaces must not be redesigned merely to support AGI:

Authentication

Tenant Context

Authorization

AI Gateway

AI Request

AI Context

Model Router

Provider Adapter

Output Validator

AI Run Persistence

Tool Gateway

Tool Authorization

Execution Policy

Sandbox

Audit

Future AGI code consumes these boundaries.

It does not replace them.

## 291.2 Production-Gate Dependency

The cognitive runtime must respect the actual Part 290 result.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY

the verified AI foundation may be treated as the stable runtime boundary.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_READY_WITH_EXPLICIT_SCOPE

the AGI runtime must operate only inside the verified scope.

If:

AI_PRODUCTION_NOT_READY

or:

AI_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED

the AGI runtime may be developed and unit-tested where safe, but production execution must not bypass the unresolved gate.

## 291.3 Cognitive Runtime Principle

Do not implement AGI as a collection of autonomous agents.

Preferred structure:

                    ┌──────────────────┐

                    │ Cognitive State  │

                    └────────┬─────────┘

                             │

       ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐

       ↓                     ↓                     ↓

 Perception              Attention             Memory

       │                     │                     │

       └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘

                             ↓

                       World Model

                             ↓

                    Reasoning / Planning

                             ↓

                         Action

                             ↓

                      Tool Gateway

                             ↓

                       Observation

                             │

                             └────────→ Cognitive State

Learning, metacognition, and consolidation operate as controlled processes around this loop.

## 291.4 Unified Cognitive Runtime Contract

Create one primary orchestration boundary:

public interface CognitiveRuntime {

    CognitiveResult execute(CognitiveRequest request);

}

The runtime must not expose provider-specific details.

It should receive a bounded request and return a validated cognitive result.

## 291.5 CognitiveRequest

Use a minimal request structure:

public record CognitiveRequest(

        String requestId,

        String userId,

        String organizationId,

        String workspaceId,

        String projectId,

        String instruction,

        CognitiveMode mode

) {}

Do not add fields merely because future AGI concepts might need them.

Additional state must enter through explicit runtime services.

## 291.6 CognitiveMode

The runtime should support the approved GSIR operating modes:

public enum CognitiveMode {

    AUTOMATIC,

    ANALYSIS,

    HYPOTHESIS,

    SOP_GENERATING

}

Mode selection controls behavior and policy.

It does not create four separate AI systems.

## 291.7 CognitiveResult

Use a normalized result:

public record CognitiveResult(

        String requestId,

        CognitiveStatus status,

        String response,

        List<CognitiveEvidence> evidence,

        List<CognitiveObservation> observations

) {}

The result must not contain hidden chain-of-thought.

Only approved summaries, evidence, observations, decisions, and externally useful reasoning artifacts may be exposed or persisted.

## 291.8 CognitiveStatus

Use a small lifecycle:

public enum CognitiveStatus {

    COMPLETED,

    NEEDS_INPUT,

    TOOL_REQUIRED,

    VALIDATION_FAILED,

    FAILED,

    CANCELLED

}

Do not create dozens of cognitive states before actual workflows require them.

## 291.9 Cognitive State

The runtime needs a bounded working state.

public record CognitiveState(

        String taskId,

        CognitiveMode mode,

        String objective,

        List<StateFact> facts,

        List<StateConstraint> constraints,

        List<StateHypothesis> hypotheses,

        List<StateObservation> observations

) {}

The state is not automatically permanent memory.

## 291.10 State vs Memory

Maintain an explicit distinction:

Cognitive State

=

temporary working state for the current execution

Memory

=

information intentionally retained beyond the current execution

Do not write every intermediate thought or model output into persistent memory.

## 291.11 State Integrity

Every state mutation must identify:

source

timestamp

confidence/evidence status where applicable

provenance

where those concepts are implemented.

AI assertions must not silently become authoritative facts.

## 291.12 Perception Boundary

Perception converts available inputs into structured observations.

public interface PerceptionService {

    List<CognitiveObservation> perceive(

            CognitiveRequest request,

            CognitiveState state

    );

}

Inputs may include:

user instruction

authorized documents

retrieved evidence

tool results

project state

external observations

Only authorized information may enter perception.

## 291.13 Perception Does Not Authorize

Perception must never decide:

whether the user may access a resource

whether a tool may execute

whether a tenant may be accessed

whether a secret may be exposed

Those decisions remain with the existing security boundaries.

## 291.14 Attention Boundary

Attention determines which authorized information deserves processing priority.

public interface AttentionService {

    AttentionResult focus(

            CognitiveState state,

            List<CognitiveObservation> observations

    );

}

Attention may consider:

task relevance

evidence quality

recency

uncertainty

dependency

user priority

resource cost

Attention is not authorization.

## 291.15 Deterministic Attention Policy

Where possible, attention ordering should be deterministic.

For example:

hard constraints

        ↓

explicit user objective

        ↓

critical evidence

        ↓

high-relevance observations

        ↓

supporting context

        ↓

low-priority context

The actual ordering must be represented by implemented policy rather than undocumented model behavior.

## 291.16 Memory Boundary

Create an application-level memory contract:

public interface CognitiveMemory {

    List<MemoryItem> retrieve(MemoryQuery query);

    MemoryWriteResult write(MemoryWriteRequest request);

}

Memory must remain:

authorized

tenant-scoped

provenance-aware

bounded

version-aware

deletable according to retention policy

## 291.17 Memory Is Not a Chat Log

Do not treat the entire conversation history as memory.

Candidate memory should be selected based on explicit policy.

Examples:

stable project fact

verified research result

approved user preference

important experiment result

validated constraint

Temporary reasoning should not automatically become durable memory.

## 291.18 Memory Write Gate

Before durable memory creation:

candidate information

        ↓

validation

        ↓

provenance

        ↓

authorization

        ↓

memory policy

        ↓

persist

The model cannot directly write arbitrary durable memory.

## 291.19 World Model Boundary

The world model represents structured information about the task domain.

public interface WorldModel {

    WorldState getState(WorldQuery query);

    WorldUpdateResult apply(

            WorldObservation observation

    );

}

It must distinguish:

observed

reported

inferred

hypothesized

verified

unknown

## 291.20 World Model Safety

A model-generated statement must not automatically become a world-model fact.

For example:

AI says:

"Experiment succeeded."

does not automatically mean:

experiment.status = SUCCESS

Independent evidence or an approved application event must establish the state transition.

## 291.21 Reasoning Boundary

Create one reasoning abstraction:

public interface ReasoningEngine {

    ReasoningResult reason(

            CognitiveState state,

            WorldState worldState,

            AttentionResult attention

    );

}

The initial implementation may use the existing AI Gateway.

The reasoning engine must remain provider-independent.

## 291.22 Planning Boundary

Planning is a capability of reasoning, not a separate autonomous agent.

public interface PlanningEngine {

    Plan createPlan(

            CognitiveState state,

            WorldState worldState

    );

}

A plan consists of bounded steps:

observe

retrieve

calculate

compare

ask user

call authorized tool

validate

stop

## 291.23 Plan Safety

A plan does not grant permissions.

Every executable plan step must still pass:

authentication

authorization

tool policy

execution policy

resource limits

The cognitive runtime cannot bypass the Tool Gateway.

## 291.24 Action Boundary

Create one action interface:

public interface CognitiveActionService {

    ActionResult execute(

            PlannedAction action,

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    );

}

Actions requiring external capability must be routed through the existing Tool Gateway.

## 291.25 Observation Loop

After an action:

Plan

 ↓

Authorized Action

 ↓

Tool Gateway

 ↓

External Result

 ↓

Observation

 ↓

Cognitive State

 ↓

Re-evaluation

The runtime must not assume that an action succeeded merely because the action was requested.

## 291.26 Bounded Cognitive Loop

Implement an explicit loop limit.

public record CognitiveExecutionLimits(

        int maxIterations,

        int maxToolCalls,

        int maxReasoningCalls,

        Duration maxDuration

) {}

Defaults must be configuration-driven and conservative.

Never create an unbounded:

reason → tool → reason → tool → ...

loop.

## 291.27 Stop Conditions

The cognitive runtime must stop when:

objective satisfied

required evidence unavailable

user input required

validation fails

authorization fails

resource budget exhausted

iteration limit reached

tool failure requires termination

critical contradiction detected

runtime timeout reached

Stopping is a valid cognitive outcome.

## 291.28 Contradiction Handling

When information conflicts:

Fact A

≠

Fact B

do not silently choose one.

Represent:

contradiction detected

sources

provenance

evidence status

resolution status

The system may request more evidence or user clarification.

## 291.29 Uncertainty Handling

Maintain:

UNKNOWN

as a legitimate state.

Do not convert:

unknown

into:

false

or:

true

without evidence.

Likewise:

hypothesis

must remain distinct from:

verified result

## 291.30 Metacognition Boundary

Implement lightweight metacognition as control monitoring.

public interface MetacognitionService {

    MetacognitiveAssessment assess(

            CognitiveState state,

            ReasoningResult reasoning,

            CognitiveExecutionMetrics metrics

    );

}

It may evaluate:

uncertainty

missing evidence

contradictions

resource consumption

plan quality indicators

validation failures

need for clarification

It must not become an unrestricted second AI system.

## 291.31 No Recursive Agent Explosion

Do not implement:

planner agent

research agent

critic agent

memory agent

tool agent

verification agent

metacognition agent

manager agent

as independent autonomous services merely to represent cognitive functions.

Prefer lightweight services inside the same cognitive runtime.

This keeps:

latency

cost

complexity

failure modes

security boundaries

under control.

## 291.32 Learning Boundary

Learning must be separated from ordinary inference.

public interface LearningService {

    LearningResult learn(

            LearningInput input

    );

}

Learning may use:

validated outcomes

user feedback

experiment results

benchmark results

tool observations

error patterns

but only through explicit policies.

## 291.33 Learning Safety

The model cannot automatically rewrite its own production behavior.

Learning outputs should initially be:

candidate improvement

rather than:

automatic production modification

Any future self-improvement mechanism must pass independent evaluation.

## 291.34 Consolidation Boundary

Consolidation converts selected short-lived information into durable representations.

public interface ConsolidationService {

    ConsolidationResult consolidate(

            ConsolidationInput input

    );

}

Potential inputs:

validated observations

validated memory candidates

experiment outcomes

confirmed corrections

stable project knowledge

## 291.35 Consolidation Rule

Do not consolidate:

raw hidden reasoning

unverified claims

secrets

temporary tool credentials

unauthorized tenant data

arbitrary model instructions

Consolidation must preserve provenance.

Create one orchestration implementation:

public final class DefaultCognitiveRuntime

        implements CognitiveRuntime {

    @Override

    public CognitiveResult execute(CognitiveRequest request) {

        // orchestration only

        // implementation must call existing security,

        // context, AI Gateway and Tool Gateway boundaries

        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Implementation follows repository reconciliation");

    }

}

The orchestration must remain thin.

It coordinates components; it should not duplicate their responsibilities.

## 291.37 Runtime Sequence

The canonical execution sequence is:

Authenticated Request

        ↓

Authorization

        ↓

Cognitive State

        ↓

Perception

        ↓

Attention

        ↓

Authorized Memory/Context

        ↓

World Model

        ↓

Reasoning

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓

Tool Gateway

        ↓

Observation

        ↓

State Update

        ↓

Validation

        ↓

Memory/Consolidation if approved

        ↓

Validated Result

Not every request needs every stage.

The runtime should skip unnecessary stages to reduce latency and cost.

## 291.38 Automatic Mode

AUTOMATIC selects the smallest safe cognitive path required by the task.

Example:

simple question

→ context

→ reasoning

→ answer

rather than unnecessarily invoking:

planning

multiple tools

memory writes

consolidation

## 291.39 Analysis Mode

ANALYSIS prioritizes:

evidence

comparisons

uncertainty

reasoning

calculations

contradictions

It should produce structured, evidence-aware results where applicable.

## 291.40 Hypothesis Mode

HYPOTHESIS explicitly separates:

known evidence

inference

hypothesis

predicted consequence

required test

The mode must never silently promote a hypothesis to verified knowledge.

## 291.41 SOP-Generating Mode

SOP_GENERATING produces operational procedures from validated requirements and evidence.

Where the SOP involves physical or external action:

generate

→ validate

→ identify hazards/constraints

→ require appropriate authorization

→ execute only through approved action/tool boundaries

Generation itself does not constitute execution.

## 291.42 Scientific Task Loop

For research tasks, the preferred pattern is:

Question

 ↓

Objective

 ↓

Evidence Retrieval

 ↓

Evidence Assessment

 ↓

Knowledge/World State

 ↓

Reasoning

 ↓

Hypothesis/Plan

 ↓

Calculation/Simulation/Tool

 ↓

Observation

 ↓

Validation

 ↓

Conclusion

 ↓

Provenance

This creates a research-oriented cognitive loop without requiring a separate agent for every stage.

## 291.43 Cost-Aware Cognitive Routing

Before invoking expensive reasoning or tools, determine whether a simpler path is sufficient.

Example:

known answer

→ answer

simple calculation

→ deterministic computation

retrieval task

→ retrieval

complex research problem

→ reasoning/planning

external action

→ Tool Gateway

Do not use a large model for deterministic operations that can be safely performed by code.

where supported by the existing persistence/provenance architecture.

another tenant's context

# Part 293 — Unified Cognitive Runtime Core Contracts

## Aim of the code

Define the smallest stable contracts required for the unified GSIR cognitive runtime.

These contracts establish the runtime's shared information flow without implementing the individual intelligence mechanisms yet.

The goal is to prevent later components—perception, attention, memory, world model, reasoning, planning, metacognition, learning, and consolidation—from developing incompatible data structures or creating duplicate orchestration layers.

The contracts must remain:

- provider-independent;

- database-independent where possible;

- security-context aware;

- provenance-aware;

- bounded;

- serializable where persistence is explicitly required;

- free of hidden chain-of-thought storage;

- compatible with the existing AI Gateway and Tool Gateway;

- compatible with the four approved cognitive modes.

# Code

## 1. Cognitive mode

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public enum CognitiveMode {

    AUTOMATIC,

    ANALYSIS,

    HYPOTHESIS,

    SOP_GENERATING

}

The mode is an execution policy, not a separate agent.

## 2. Cognitive request

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

import java.util.List;

import java.util.Map;

import java.util.UUID;

public record CognitiveRequest(

        UUID requestId,

        UUID userId,

        UUID organizationId,

        UUID workspaceId,

        UUID projectId,

        CognitiveMode mode,

        String instruction,

        List<CognitiveInput> inputs,

        Map<String, String> metadata

) {}

The authenticated security context remains authoritative.

The IDs contained in the request must therefore be checked against the authenticated principal and authorization boundaries before execution.

Client-provided tenant identifiers must never override the authenticated tenant context.

## 3. Cognitive input

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public record CognitiveInput(

        CognitiveInputType type,

        String value,

        String sourceId,

        String versionId,

        String checksum

) {}

Input content is data.

It must not automatically be interpreted as an instruction merely because it contains imperative language.

## 4. Cognitive input types

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public enum CognitiveInputType {

    USER_INSTRUCTION,

    DOCUMENT,

    EVIDENCE,

    TOOL_RESULT,

    CONVERSATION,

    STRUCTURED_DATA,

    OBSERVATION

}

The distinction is important because instructions, evidence, observations, and external data have different trust and processing semantics.

## 5. Cognitive state

Cognitive state represents temporary working state for one execution.

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

import java.time.Instant;

import java.util.UUID;

public record CognitiveState(

        UUID executionId,

        UUID requestId,

        CognitiveMode mode,

        CognitivePhase phase,

        Instant startedAt,

        CognitiveBudget budget,

        CognitiveUncertainty uncertainty,

        int iteration

) {}

Do not add raw model reasoning traces to this object.

## 6. Cognitive phase

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public enum CognitivePhase {

    INITIALIZING,

    PERCEPTION,

    ATTENTION,

## 16. Cognitive budget

The runtime must have explicit resource limits.

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public record CognitiveBudget(

        int maxIterations,

        int maxAiCalls,

        int maxToolCalls,

        int maxToolDepth,

        long maxContextTokens,

        long maxExecutionMillis,

        long maxOutputBytes

) {

    public CognitiveBudget {

        if (maxIterations <= 0

                || maxAiCalls < 0

                || maxToolCalls < 0

                || maxToolDepth < 0

                || maxContextTokens <= 0

                || maxExecutionMillis <= 0

                || maxOutputBytes <= 0) {

            throw new IllegalArgumentException(

                    "Invalid cognitive execution budget"

            );

        }

    }

}

These limits prevent uncontrolled cognitive loops and resource exhaustion.

## 43. Runtime dependency boundary

The unified runtime may depend on the following abstractions:

Authentication / SecurityContext

        ↓

Authorization

        ↓

AI Gateway

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓

Provider Adapter

        ↓

        ↓

The cognitive runtime must not depend directly on:

Redis

provider SDKs

shell

filesystem

arbitrary HTTP clients

deployment secrets

Those concerns remain behind their existing boundaries.

## 44. Runtime orchestration rule

The eventual implementation follows this controlled sequence:

Authenticated Request

        ↓

Authorization

        ↓

Cognitive State

        ↓

Perception

        ↓

Attention

        ↓

Authorized Memory / Context

        ↓

World Model

        ↓

Reasoning

        ↓

Metacognitive Assessment

        ↓

Planning

        ↓

Action Decision

        ↓

Tool Gateway

        ↓

Observation

        ↓

World-State Update

        ↓

Validation

        ↓

Consolidation

        ↓

Validated Cognitive Result

A failure at a security or authorization boundary must terminate or safely reject the operation.

## 45. Contract invariants

The following invariants are mandatory:

1. One CognitiveRuntime.

2. One authoritative security context.

3. One authoritative authorization layer.

4. One AI Gateway.

5. One Tool Gateway.

6. No direct provider calls from cognitive components.

7. No unrestricted tool execution.

8. No hidden chain-of-thought persistence.

9. No automatic truth assignment by the model.

10. No planner-controlled authorization.

11. No automatic production self-modification.

12. No cross-tenant context.

13. No unbounded loops.

14. No unbounded tool recursion.

15. No silent context truncation of critical evidence.

16. Provenance is preserved.

17. Unknown remains representable.

18. Scientific verification remains externally validated.

19. Existing persistence is reused before schema expansion.

20. Security failures fail closed.

## 46. Implementation rule

These contracts are not yet evidence that equivalent classes do not already exist.

Before adding them to the repository:

- inspect the repository;

- compare existing types;

- reuse compatible types;

- adapt incompatible types only where necessary;

- remove duplicate proposed structures;

- add tests;

- compile;

- run the existing regression suite.

No wholesale replacement of the existing AI foundation is permitted.

:::memcite:::

# Part 294 — Cognitive Runtime Execution Kernel

## Aim of the code

Implement the execution-control kernel for the unified GSIR cognitive runtime.

This part establishes the runtime mechanics that control how cognition executes, without attempting to implement advanced reasoning, memory intelligence, learning algorithms, or autonomous behavior.

The kernel must provide:

- bounded execution;

- explicit phase transitions;

- iteration limits;

- AI-call limits;

- tool-call limits;

- tool-depth limits;

- context/output budgets;

- execution-time limits;

- cancellation;

- controlled failure handling;

- safe termination;

- deterministic runtime accounting.

The kernel is a controller, not an intelligence agent.

It must not bypass the existing:

- authentication;

- authorization;

- AI Gateway;

- Tool Gateway;

- output validation;

- provenance;

- sandbox;

- persistence;

- audit boundaries.

# Code

## 1. Runtime execution kernel

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public interface CognitiveExecutionKernel {

    CognitiveResult execute(CognitiveRequest request);

}

The kernel owns execution control.

The cognitive modules own their respective responsibilities.

## 2. Runtime context

import java.time.Clock;

public record CognitiveExecutionContext(

        CognitiveState state,

        CognitiveBudget budget,

It must not contain:

## 3. Runtime counters

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public record CognitiveRuntimeCounters(

        int aiCalls,

        int toolCalls,

        int currentToolDepth,

        int iterations,

        long contextTokens,

        long outputBytes

) {

    public CognitiveRuntimeCounters {

        if (aiCalls < 0

                || toolCalls < 0

                || currentToolDepth < 0

                || iterations < 0

                || contextTokens < 0

                || outputBytes < 0) {

            throw new IllegalArgumentException(

                    "Runtime counters cannot be negative"

            );

        }

    }

    public CognitiveRuntimeCounters incrementAiCalls() {

        return new CognitiveRuntimeCounters(

                aiCalls + 1,

                toolCalls,

                currentToolDepth,

                iterations,

                contextTokens,

                outputBytes

        );

    }

    public CognitiveRuntimeCounters incrementToolCalls() {

        return new CognitiveRuntimeCounters(

                aiCalls,

                toolCalls + 1,

                currentToolDepth,

                iterations,

                contextTokens,

                outputBytes

        );

    }

    public CognitiveRuntimeCounters incrementIterations() {

        return new CognitiveRuntimeCounters(

                aiCalls,

                toolCalls,

                currentToolDepth,

                iterations + 1,

                contextTokens,

                outputBytes

        );

    }

}

Counters must be updated centrally.

Individual reasoning modules must not independently reset or enlarge their budgets.

    ITERATION_LIMIT,

}

## 5. Budget controller

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public interface CognitiveBudgetController {

    BudgetDecision check(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    );

    BudgetDecision checkAiCall(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    );

    BudgetDecision checkToolCall(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context,

            int requestedDepth

    );

    BudgetDecision checkContext(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context,

    BudgetDecision checkOutput(

}

All budget decisions must be centralized.

## 6. Default budget controller

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

import java.time.Instant;

public final class DefaultCognitiveBudgetController

        implements CognitiveBudgetController {

    @Override

    public BudgetDecision check(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    ) {

        CognitiveBudget budget = context.budget();

        CognitiveRuntimeCounters counters =

                context.counters();

        if (counters.iterations() >= budget.maxIterations()) {

            return BudgetDecision.ITERATION_LIMIT;

        }

        if (counters.aiCalls() > budget.maxAiCalls()) {

            return BudgetDecision.AI_CALL_LIMIT;

        }

        if (counters.toolCalls() > budget.maxToolCalls()) {

            return BudgetDecision.TOOL_CALL_LIMIT;

        }

        long elapsed =

                elapsedMillis(context);

        if (elapsed >= budget.maxExecutionMillis()) {

            return BudgetDecision.EXECUTION_TIME_LIMIT;

        }

        return BudgetDecision.ALLOWED;

    }

    @Override

    public BudgetDecision checkAiCall(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    ) {

        if (context.counters().aiCalls()

                >= context.budget().maxAiCalls()) {

            return BudgetDecision.AI_CALL_LIMIT;

        }

        return BudgetDecision.ALLOWED;

    }

    @Override

    public BudgetDecision checkToolCall(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context,

            int requestedDepth

    ) {

        if (context.counters().toolCalls()

                >= context.budget().maxToolCalls()) {

            return BudgetDecision.TOOL_CALL_LIMIT;

        }

        if (requestedDepth

                > context.budget().maxToolDepth()) {

            return BudgetDecision.TOOL_DEPTH_LIMIT;

        }

        return BudgetDecision.ALLOWED;

    }

    @Override

    public BudgetDecision checkContext(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context,

            long estimatedTokens

    ) {

        if (estimatedTokens

                > context.budget().maxContextTokens()) {

            return BudgetDecision.CONTEXT_LIMIT;

        }

        return BudgetDecision.ALLOWED;

    }

    @Override

    public BudgetDecision checkOutput(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context,

            long outputBytes

    ) {

        if (outputBytes

                > context.budget().maxOutputBytes()) {

            return BudgetDecision.OUTPUT_LIMIT;

        }

        return BudgetDecision.ALLOWED;

    }

    private long elapsedMillis(

            CognitiveExecutionContext context

    ) {

        Instant started =

                context.state().startedAt();

        return context.clock()

                .millis()

                - started.toEpochMilli();

    }

}

The comparison must be performed before executing the next expensive operation.

## 7. Runtime cancellation

Cancellation must be explicit.

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

public interface CognitiveCancellation {

    boolean isCancelled();

    void cancel();

}

Cancellation must be checked:

- before expensive AI calls;

- before tool execution;

- between cognitive phases;

- between iterations;

- before consolidation;

- before final state mutation.

## 8. Cancellation implementation

package com.gsir.ai.cognitive;

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

public final class DefaultCognitiveCancellation

        implements CognitiveCancellation {

    private final AtomicBoolean cancelled =

            new AtomicBoolean(false);

    @Override

    public boolean isCancelled() {

        return cancelled.get();

    }

    @Override

    public void cancel() {

        cancelled.set(true);

    }

}

The implementation must be thread-safe.
