The most important implementation rule is:

A developer must always be able to identify exactly where a feature belongs, which file owns its business logic, which API exposes it, which repository persists it, which module consumes it, which tests verify it, and which external systems it depends on.

The backend must therefore be built as a controlled platform rather than a collection of rapidly accumulated files.

END OF PART 11

PART 12 — LOW-COST, HIGH-OUTPUT AI ROUTER, MODEL SELECTION, TOKEN OPTIMIZATION AND COMPUTE EFFICIENCY

12.1 PURPOSE

GSIR must achieve maximum useful output with minimum unnecessary token usage, processing, latency and infrastructure cost.

The system shall not use the largest or most expensive AI model for every request.

Instead, GSIR shall dynamically determine:

- What the user is asking.

- How difficult the task is.

- Whether AI reasoning is actually required.

- Whether retrieval is required.

- Whether a deterministic tool can solve the task.

- Whether a small model is sufficient.

- Whether a medium model is required.

- Whether a large reasoning model is justified.

- Whether a specialized scientific model is more appropriate.

- Whether a local/offline model can perform the task.

- Whether previous results can be reused.

- Whether the task can be processed asynchronously.

The objective is:

LOWEST RELIABLE COST + LOWEST NECESSARY TOKEN USAGE + LOWEST NECESSARY COMPUTE + LOW LATENCY + HIGH OUTPUT QUALITY + HIGH RELIABILITY

END OF 12.1

12.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

The AI Gateway must operate according to the following rule:

DO NOT ASK AN EXPENSIVE MODEL TO DO A CHEAP TASK.

Examples:

Simple arithmetic → calculator/tool

Database lookup → SQL/database tool

Exact file lookup → file search

Current scientific information → retrieval system

Simple classification → small model

Query rewriting → small/medium model

Document summarization → appropriate medium model

Complex scientific synthesis → advanced reasoning model

Large hypothesis investigation → advanced reasoning + retrieval + tools + verification

This architecture substantially reduces unnecessary inference cost.

END OF 12.2

12.3 AI ROUTER ARCHITECTURE

The routing pipeline shall be:

USER REQUEST ↓ AI GATEWAY ↓ REQUEST NORMALIZER ↓ INTENT CLASSIFIER ↓ COMPLEXITY ESTIMATOR ↓ TASK TYPE DETECTOR ↓ CONTEXT ANALYZER ↓ TOOL-REQUIREMENT DETECTOR ↓ MODEL ROUTER ↓ MODEL SELECTION ↓ EXECUTION ↓ QUALITY CHECK ↓ FALLBACK IF REQUIRED ↓ RESPONSE VALIDATION ↓ FINAL RESPONSE

The frontend must never directly select or call an external model provider.

All model requests must pass through the GSIR AI Gateway.

END OF 12.3

12.4 EXACT BACKEND FILE STRUCTURE

The AI routing subsystem shall use the following modular structure:

Backend/ └── app/ ├── ai/ │   ├── init.py │   ├── gateway.py │   ├── router.py │   ├── model_registry.py │   ├── model_selector.py │   ├── model_capability.py │   ├── complexity_estimator.py │   ├── token_budget.py │   ├── cost_estimator.py │   ├── context_manager.py │   ├── prompt_manager.py │   ├── response_manager.py │   ├── fallback_manager.py │   ├── streaming_manager.py │   ├── cache_manager.py │   ├── provider_manager.py │   └── usage_tracker.py │ ├── providers/ │   ├── init.py │   ├── base_provider.py │   ├── openai_provider.py │   ├── anthropic_provider.py │   ├── google_provider.py │   ├── open_source_provider.py │   └── local_provider.py │ ├── routing/ │   ├── init.py │   ├── route_policy.py │   ├── task_classifier.py │   ├── quality_policy.py │   ├── cost_policy.py │   └── escalation_policy.py │ └── services/ └── ai_service.py

No provider-specific logic shall be distributed throughout unrelated application modules.

END OF 12.4

12.5 MODEL REGISTRY

GSIR shall maintain a central model registry.

Each registered model must contain:

Model_id

Provider

Model_name

Model_version

Model_type

Context_window

Input_cost

Output_cost

Latency_profile

Reasoning_capability

Coding_capability

Mathematics_capability

Scientific_capability

Multimodal_capability

Tool_calling_support

Structured_output_support

Streaming_support

Local_available

Privacy_class

Reliability_score

Benchmark_score

Current_status

The model registry must be data-driven rather than hard-coded throughout the application.

END OF 12.5

12.6 MODEL CAPABILITY MATRIX

GSIR shall maintain a capability matrix.

Example:

TASK | REQUIRED CAPABILITY | PREFERRED MODEL CLASS

Simple chat | language | small

Classification | classification | small

Query rewrite | language | small

Extraction | structured extraction | small/medium

Summarization | language | medium

Coding | coding | coding-capable

Mathematics | mathematics | reasoning/tool-assisted

Scientific literature synthesis | research reasoning | advanced

Complex hypothesis generation | reasoning | advanced

Image interpretation | vision | multimodal

Large dataset analysis | tools + code | code-capable

Laboratory data analysis | scientific + code | specialized/advanced

The router shall select based on capability rather than model popularity.

END OF 12.6

12.7 TASK COMPLEXITY LEVELS

Every request shall receive a complexity score.

LEVEL 0 — DETERMINISTIC

Examples:

Arithmetic

Date conversion

Formatting

Simple validation

No LLM required.

LEVEL 1 — SIMPLE AI

Examples:

Basic question answering

Classification

Rewriting

Short summaries

Small model preferred.

LEVEL 2 — STANDARD AI

Examples:

Multi-step explanation

Document summarization

Normal coding assistance

Small/medium model.

LEVEL 3 — ADVANCED

Examples:

Multi-document reasoning

Complex programming

Technical analysis

Scientific comparison

Advanced model.

LEVEL 4 — DEEP RESEARCH

Examples:

Multidisciplinary research

Evidence synthesis

Hypothesis development

Conflicting literature analysis

Advanced reasoning model + retrieval + tools + verification.

LEVEL 5 — AUTONOMOUS SCIENTIFIC WORKFLOW

Examples:

Literature investigation

Dataset analysis

Code generation

Simulation

Experiment planning

Iterative validation

Research orchestrator + multiple specialized models/tools + verification.

END OF 12.7

12.8 MODEL ESCALATION

GSIR shall use progressive escalation.

Initial request ↓ Cheapest suitable model ↓ Quality evaluation ↓ Sufficient? ├── YES → return result └── NO ↓ Escalate ↓ More capable model ↓ Re-evaluate ↓ Return validated result

The system must not automatically begin every task with the most expensive model.

END OF 12.8

12.9 QUALITY-BASED ESCALATION

Escalation may occur when:

Confidence is low

Required evidence is missing

Tool calls fail

Reasoning complexity is high

Output violates schema

Citations fail validation

User requests deeper analysis

The critic identifies an error

Retrieved sources conflict

Code fails execution

Mathematical validation fails

The escalation decision must be recorded.

END OF 12.9

12.10 TOKEN BUDGET MANAGEMENT

Every request shall have a token budget.

The budget shall consider:

User input

System instructions

Conversation context

Project context

Retrieved documents

Tool results

Model output

Verification requirements

The system must not repeatedly send the entire conversation when only a small portion is required.

END OF 12.10

12.11 CONTEXT COMPRESSION

Long conversations shall be compressed using structured summaries.

Instead of repeatedly passing:

10,000 previous messages

The system should maintain:

Conversation summary

Active objectives

Important decisions

User preferences relevant to the project

Unresolved questions

Referenced files

Current task state

Original messages remain stored for retrieval but need not always be included in the model context.

END OF 12.11

12.12 HIERARCHICAL MEMORY

GSIR context shall use:

LEVEL 1 — Current turn

LEVEL 2 — Current conversation

LEVEL 3 — Project context

LEVEL 4 — User-approved long-term memory

LEVEL 5 — Organizational knowledge

LEVEL 6 — Scientific knowledge

Only relevant context should be injected into the model.

END OF 12.12

12.13 CONTEXT RELEVANCE FILTER

Before adding context, GSIR shall calculate relevance.

For every candidate context item:

RELEVANCE + RECENCY + IMPORTANCE + AUTHORIZATION + TASK MATCH

Only qualifying context should be passed to the model.

This prevents context overload and unnecessary token consumption.

END OF 12.13

12.14 PROMPT ARCHITECTURE

Prompts shall be modular.

The prompt manager shall assemble:

SYSTEM POLICY + TASK POLICY + USER REQUEST + RELEVANT CONTEXT + TOOLS + EVIDENCE + OUTPUT SCHEMA

Prompts must not be duplicated throughout the codebase.

END OF 12.14

12.15 PROMPT VERSIONING

Every production prompt must have:

Prompt_id

Version

Purpose

Model compatibility

Input schema

Output schema

Created_at

Updated_at

Test status

Changing a critical prompt must create a new version rather than silently replacing the old one.

END OF 12.15

12.16 STRUCTURED OUTPUT

AI responses should use structured schemas wherever possible.

Example:

{ “status”: “success”, “task_type”: “research”, “answer”: “…”, “evidence”: [], “citations”: [], “confidence”: 0.0, “warnings”: [], “next_actions”: [] }

This allows deterministic backend validation.

END OF 12.16

12.17 PROVIDER ABSTRACTION

All external and local models must implement the same internal provider interface.

Example conceptual interface:

Generate()

Stream()

Embed()

Count_tokens()

Health_check()

Supports_tools()

Supports_structured_output()

The rest of GSIR must not depend on provider-specific APIs.

END OF 12.17

12.18 PROVIDER ADAPTER ARCHITECTURE

The architecture shall be:

AI Gateway ↓ Provider Manager ↓ Provider Adapter ↓ External/Local Model

Examples:

OpenAI Adapter

Anthropic Adapter

Google Adapter

Open-Source Adapter

Local Model Adapter

New providers can therefore be added without rewriting the application.

END OF 12.18

12.19 OPEN-SOURCE MODEL INTEGRATION

GSIR must remain capable of integrating high-quality open-source models.

The system shall support:

Self-hosted inference

Private inference

Local inference

GPU inference

CPU inference where practical

Quantized models

Specialized scientific models

Coding models

Embedding models

Reranking models

The router shall compare quality, latency and cost before selecting them.

END OF 12.19

12.20 LOCAL/OFFLINE AI

GSIR shall support optional user-installed local AI.

Architecture:

GSIR APP ↓ LOCAL MODEL MANAGER ↓ INSTALLED MODEL ↓ LOCAL INFERENCE ENGINE

The user may choose local inference for suitable tasks.

Examples:

Offline chat

Summarization

Note processing

Document classification

Basic coding

Private local analysis

The local model must never be assumed to have the same capabilities as cloud models.

Capability detection must occur before routing.

END OF 12.20

12.21 MOBILE LOCAL AI

On supported devices, GSIR may use device-local models for lightweight tasks.

The system should consider:

RAM

Storage

CPU

GPU/NPU

Battery

Thermal state

Model size

The router should select a local model only when device resources are sufficient.

END OF 12.21

12.22 TOKEN OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES

GSIR shall implement:

- Context compression.

- Semantic context selection.

- Duplicate context removal.

- Retrieval deduplication.

- Prompt template reuse.

- Response-length control.

- Adaptive reasoning depth.

- Tool-first execution.

- Result caching.

- Streaming.

- Batch processing.

- Model escalation.

- Small-model preprocessing.

- Structured outputs.

- Asynchronous background processing.

END OF 12.22

12.23 DETERMINISTIC-FIRST COMPUTATION

Before using an LLM for a computational problem, GSIR should determine whether a deterministic tool is available.

Examples:

Mathematics → symbolic/numerical engine

SQL → database engine

Statistics → statistical library

Data transformation → data-processing engine

Unit conversion → deterministic conversion engine

Physics calculations → validated scientific computation library

This reduces hallucination and token consumption.

END OF 12.23

12.24 TOOL-FIRST ARCHITECTURE

The preferred sequence is:

QUESTION ↓ CAN A DETERMINISTIC TOOL SOLVE IT? ├── YES → TOOL └── NO ↓ CAN RETRIEVAL SOLVE IT? ├── YES → RETRIEVAL └── NO ↓ CAN SMALL MODEL SOLVE IT? ├── YES → SMALL MODEL └── NO ↓ MEDIUM/ADVANCED MODEL ↓ VERIFICATION

This becomes a central GSIR efficiency principle.

END OF 12.24

12.25 RESPONSE LENGTH CONTROL

The AI Gateway shall support:

CONCISE

BALANCED

DETAILED

DEEP RESEARCH

FULL RESEARCH REPORT

The selected response length must influence the generation budget.

A user asking a simple question should not consume the same resources as a scientific investigation.

END OF 12.25

12.26 STREAMING

AI responses shall support streaming.

Architecture:

Frontend ↓ API Gateway ↓ AI Gateway ↓ Provider Adapter ↓ Streaming Model ↓ Streaming Manager ↓ Frontend

Streaming must support:

Partial text

Structured events

Tool execution events

Research progress

Citations

Final completion status

The system must distinguish temporary streaming content from the final persisted answer.

END OF 12.26

12.27 FALLBACK ARCHITECTURE

If a selected provider fails:

Primary model ↓ Health check ↓ Failure ↓ Fallback policy ↓ Alternative suitable model/provider ↓ Retry ↓ Validation ↓ Response

Fallback must consider:

Capability

Cost

Privacy

Context requirements

Region

Latency

Current availability

A fallback model must not silently produce a materially lower-quality scientific answer without informing the appropriate system state.

END OF 12.27

12.28 RETRY POLICY

Retries must be controlled.

Retryable:

Temporary network failure

Provider timeout

Rate-limit response

Transient infrastructure error

Non-retryable:

Invalid request

Authorization failure

Unsupported capability

Policy rejection

Invalid schema caused by persistent configuration

Exponential backoff and retry limits must be implemented.

END OF 12.28

12.29 COST ESTIMATION

Before expensive operations, GSIR should estimate:

Expected input tokens

Expected output tokens

Model cost

Retrieval cost

Embedding cost

Compute cost

Expected latency

The system may choose a cheaper equivalent route when the expected quality remains within the task requirements.

END OF 12.29

12.30 COST-AWARE ROUTING

The router must optimize:

QUALITY / COST

Rather than:

QUALITY ALONE.

However, scientific reliability has priority over minimal cost.

The system must never select an unsafe or demonstrably inadequate model merely because it is cheaper.

END OF 12.30

12.31 CACHING ARCHITECTURE

AI caching shall contain:

Prompt Cache

Embedding Cache

Retrieval Cache

Tool Result Cache

Model Result Cache where appropriate

Research Result Cache

Caching must be disabled or isolated for sensitive operations where reuse could cause information leakage.

END OF 12.31

12.32 SEMANTIC CACHE

GSIR should detect semantically equivalent requests.

Example:

“What is the molecular mass of X?”

And

“How much does one mole of X weigh?”

May be treated as equivalent for appropriate deterministic or informational responses.

The semantic cache must not be used blindly for rapidly changing information.

END OF 12.32

12.33 BATCH PROCESSING

Background workloads should be batched.

Examples:

Document embeddings

Large document ingestion

Metadata extraction

Indexing

Evaluation

Benchmark generation

Non-urgent summaries

Batch processing improves infrastructure utilization and reduces cost.

END OF 12.33

12.34 PRIORITY QUEUES

AI requests shall be assigned priority.

P0 — system-critical

P1 — interactive user request

P2 — active research

P3 — background research

P4 — bulk processing

P5 — optimization/evaluation

Interactive workloads must not be blocked by background workloads.

END OF 12.34

12.35 CONCURRENCY CONTROL

The AI Gateway must enforce:

Per-user concurrency

Per-project concurrency

Organization concurrency

Provider concurrency

Model concurrency

Global concurrency

This protects the system from overload.

END OF 12.35

12.36 RATE LIMITING

Rate limits must operate at multiple levels:

User

IP/session

Organization

API key

Model

Provider

Endpoint

Background worker

Rate limiting must be configurable and observable.

END OF 12.36

12.37 REQUEST DEDUPLICATION

If identical requests arrive within a short controlled window, GSIR should optionally coalesce them.

Example:

100 identical document-processing requests

→ one processing operation

→ shared result for authorized requesters.

Authorization must be checked before sharing results.

END OF 12.37

12.38 MODEL HEALTH MONITORING

The model registry must continuously track:

Availability

Latency

Error rate

Timeout rate

Quality benchmark

Cost

Token throughput

Provider status

Fallback frequency

A degraded model can automatically be removed from preferred routing.

END OF 12.38

12.39 ROUTING POLICY ENGINE

Routing decisions must be policy-driven.

Example:

IF task = arithmetic THEN deterministic tool.

IF task = simple classification THEN small model.

IF task = current information THEN retrieval required.

IF task = deep scientific research THEN advanced research pipeline.

IF task = confidential project THEN approved private/local models only.

IF selected model fails THEN execute approved fallback.

Policies must be versioned and testable.

END OF 12.39

12.40 PRIVACY-AWARE ROUTING

The router must inspect data sensitivity.

Possible classifications:

PUBLIC

INTERNAL

CONFIDENTIAL

RESTRICTED

HIGHLY SENSITIVE

Sensitive data must only be routed to models/providers authorized for that classification.

Local/private inference should be preferred when required by policy.

END OF 12.40

12.41 SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ROUTING

Scientific research requests shall use a specialized route:

USER ↓ Research Intent ↓ Research Complexity ↓ Scientific Retrieval ↓ Evidence Validation ↓ Scientific Reasoning Model ↓ Critic ↓ Citation Validator ↓ Final Response

The system must not answer complex scientific questions solely from the model’s pretrained knowledge when current or source-specific evidence is required.

END OF 12.41

12.42 CODING ROUTING

Coding requests shall use:

QUESTION ↓ CODE TASK CLASSIFIER ↓ REPOSITORY CONTEXT ↓ RELEVANT FILE RETRIEVAL ↓ CODING MODEL ↓ CODE GENERATION ↓ STATIC ANALYSIS ↓ TEST EXECUTION ↓ ERROR FEEDBACK ↓ REPAIR ↓ TEST AGAIN ↓ FINAL PATCH

This prevents the coding model from blindly generating code without testing.

END OF 12.42

12.43 SELF-IMPROVEMENT CONNECTION

The AI router itself must be measurable and improvable.

The system shall record:

Routing decision

Selected model

Alternatives considered

Task complexity

Cost

Latency

Output quality

User feedback

Validation failures

Escalation frequency

Fallback frequency

The self-improvement system can analyze this data and propose improved routing policies.

Production routing policies must only change through controlled evaluation and deployment.

END OF 12.43

12.44 ROUTER LEARNING

The router may learn from historical performance.

Example:

Task class X

Model A: Quality = 0.92 Cost = high

Model B: Quality = 0.89 Cost = low

If the quality threshold is 0.88:

Model B may become preferred.

If the task requires scientific high-confidence reasoning:

Model A may remain preferred.

Routing is therefore optimization under constraints rather than simply selecting the strongest model.

END OF 12.44

12.45 QUALITY THRESHOLDS

Each task type must have a minimum quality threshold.

Example:

Simple formatting: moderate threshold.

Normal chat: standard threshold.

Coding: high threshold.

Scientific evidence synthesis: very high threshold.

High-impact scientific decisions: highest available validation requirements.

The exact numerical thresholds shall be determined through benchmarking rather than arbitrary assumptions.

END OF 12.45

12.46 OBSERVABILITY FILES

AI routing telemetry should be implemented through:

Backend/app/core/telemetry.py

And:

Backend/app/ai/usage_tracker.py

The system must record enough information to determine:

WHY A MODEL WAS SELECTED

WHAT IT COST

HOW LONG IT TOOK

WHETHER IT SUCCEEDED

WHETHER IT REQUIRED ESCALATION

WHETHER THE OUTPUT PASSED VALIDATION

12.49 FAILURE SAFETY

The AI Gateway must fail safely.

If no reliable model is available:

DO NOT FABRICATE A RESULT.

Return an appropriate unavailable/insufficient-capability state.

If the model produces invalid structured output:

Validate → repair or retry → escalate.

If scientific evidence is insufficient:

State insufficient evidence.

If a tool is unavailable:

Do not pretend the tool was executed.

12.50 TARGET ARCHITECTURE

The complete low-cost/high-output architecture shall be:

USER ↓ AI GATEWAY ↓ REQUEST CLASSIFIER ↓ COMPLEXITY ESTIMATOR ↓ SENSITIVITY CHECK ↓ TOOL-FIRST DECISION ↓ RETRIEVAL DECISION ↓ MODEL ROUTER ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ CHEAPEST SUITABLE ROUTE     │ │                             │ │ Deterministic Tool          │ │ Local Model                 │ │ Small Model                 │ │ Medium Model                │ │ Specialized Model           │ │ Advanced Reasoning Model    │ │ Research Pipeline           │ └─────────────────────────────┘ ↓ EXECUTION ↓ QUALITY VALIDATION ↓ ┌───────────────┐ │ PASS          │ │       OR      │ │ ESCALATE      │ └───────────────┘ ↓ FALLBACK IF NECESSARY ↓ FINAL VALIDATION ↓ RESPONSE ↓ USAGE/COST/QUALITY TELEMETRY ↓ EVALUATION ↓ SELF-IMPROVEMENT

PART 12 COMPLETED.

PART 13 — CONVERSATION STATE, MEMORY, CONTEXT ENGINE AND GPT-STYLE RESPONSE ARCHITECTURE

13.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall maintain a persistent, structured and intelligent conversation-state system rather than treating each message as an independent request.

The system must understand the difference between:

- Current user message.

- Current conversation.

- Open chat tab.

- Project context.

- Research session.

- User-approved memory.

- Uploaded files.

- Previous research results.

- Tool results.

- Laboratory context.

- AI model state.

- Temporary execution state.

The objective is to provide a GPT-quality conversational experience while preventing unnecessary context transmission, token waste, hallucination, context contamination and accidental mixing of unrelated projects.

END OF 13.1

13.2 CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall use:

PERSISTENCE WITHOUT CONTEXT OVERLOAD.

Everything important may be stored, but only information relevant to the current task should be supplied to the AI model.

The architecture shall separate:

STORAGE

from

ACTIVE MODEL CONTEXT.

A database may contain millions of records while the model receives only the smallest relevant context required for the current operation.

END OF 13.2

13.3 CONVERSATION HIERARCHY

The complete hierarchy shall be:

USER │ ├── Conversations │ ├── Chat 1 │ ├── Chat 2 │ └── Chat 3 │ ├── Projects │ ├── Project A │ │ ├── Chats │ │ ├── Notes │ │ ├── Files │ │ ├── Research │ │ ├── Experiments │ │ └── Knowledge │ │ │ └── Project B │ ├── Memory │ ├── Laboratory │ └── Account Preferences

Each conversation must have a clearly defined ownership and context boundary.

END OF 13.3

13.4 CHAT TAB STATE

Every browser-style chat tab shall maintain independent state.

Required fields:

chat_id

conversation_id

project_id

title

mode

model_id

status

created_at

updated_at

last_message_id

selected_files

selected_sources

selected_tools

temporary_context

draft_message

scroll_position where required

UI state

A closed tab must not automatically mean that the conversation is deleted.

END OF 13.4

13.5 CONVERSATION DATABASE TABLES

The database shall contain at minimum:

conversations

conversation_messages

conversation_tabs

conversation_context

conversation_summaries

conversation_metadata

conversation_participants

conversation_files

conversation_sources

conversation_tool_calls

conversation_events

conversation_exports

conversation_feedback

conversation_versions

These tables must be related through stable identifiers.

END OF 13.5

13.6 MESSAGE DATA MODEL

Each message shall contain structured metadata.

Example:

{ "message_id": "msg_xxx", "conversation_id": "conv_xxx", "role": "user", "content": "...", "content_type": "text", "created_at": "...", "model_id": null, "attachments": [], "tool_calls": [], "citations": [], "status": "completed" }

Assistant messages may additionally contain:

response_metadata

evidence

citations

confidence

tool_results

research_session_id

model_information

validation_status

The internal reasoning process must never be stored or exposed as hidden chain-of-thought merely for display to the user.

END OF 13.6

13.7 MESSAGE ROLES

GSIR shall support GPT-style message roles:

SYSTEM

DEVELOPER

USER

ASSISTANT

TOOL

RETRIEVED_CONTEXT

RESEARCH_RESULT

Each role must have a defined trust level.

Retrieved documents must never be treated as system instructions.

Tool output must be treated as data.

User content must not be allowed to override system-level security rules.

END OF 13.7

13.8 CONVERSATION STATE MACHINE

Every conversation shall have a controlled state.

Possible states:

CREATED

ACTIVE

WAITING_FOR_TOOL

WAITING_FOR_RESEARCH

WAITING_FOR_USER

GENERATING

VALIDATING

COMPLETED

FAILED

CANCELLED

ARCHIVED

The backend must update conversation state atomically.

END OF 13.8

13.9 MESSAGE PROCESSING PIPELINE

The message lifecycle shall be:

USER MESSAGE ↓ API GATEWAY ↓ AUTHENTICATION ↓ CONVERSATION VALIDATION ↓ STATE LOAD ↓ INTENT DETECTION ↓ CONTEXT RETRIEVAL ↓ RELEVANCE FILTER ↓ CONTEXT ASSEMBLY ↓ AI GATEWAY ↓ MODEL/TOOL EXECUTION ↓ VALIDATION ↓ RESPONSE FORMATTER ↓ MESSAGE PERSISTENCE ↓ CONVERSATION STATE UPDATE ↓ FRONTEND STREAM

END OF 13.9

13.10 EXACT BACKEND FILE STRUCTURE

The conversation-state subsystem shall use:

backend/ └── app/ ├── conversation/ │ ├── init.py │ ├── conversation_service.py │ ├── conversation_state.py │ ├── message_service.py │ ├── message_state.py │ ├── context_service.py │ ├── context_selector.py │ ├── context_builder.py │ ├── summary_service.py │ ├── memory_bridge.py │ ├── tab_service.py │ ├── history_service.py │ ├── export_service.py │ └── conversation_validator.py │ ├── models/ │ ├── conversation.py │ ├── message.py │ ├── conversation_tab.py │ ├── conversation_context.py │ └── conversation_summary.py │ └── schemas/ ├── conversation.py ├── message.py ├── context.py └── history.py

13.11 FRONTEND CONVERSATION ARCHITECTURE

The frontend shall contain:

frontend/ └── src/ ├── features/ │ └── conversation/ │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── ChatWindow │ │ ├── MessageList │ │ ├── MessageBubble │ │ ├── MessageComposer │ │ ├── ChatTabs │ │ ├── ContextIndicator │ │ ├── CitationList │ │ ├── ToolActivity │ │ ├── ResearchProgress │ │ └── ResponseActions │ │ │ ├── hooks/ │ │ ├── useConversation │ │ ├── useMessages │ │ ├── useChatTabs │ │ └── useStreamingResponse │ │ │ ├── state/ │ │ └── conversationStore │ │ │ └── services/ │ └── conversationApi │ └── core/ └── streaming/ └── streamClient

The frontend state must remain synchronized with backend state.

END OF 13.11

13.12 CONTEXT ENGINE

The context engine is responsible for determining what the AI needs to see.

It shall consider:

- Current message.

- Recent messages.

- Conversation summary.

- Active project.

- Relevant project documents.

- Relevant previous research.

- Relevant memory.

- Relevant laboratory information.

- Relevant tools.

- Retrieved scientific evidence.

It must not blindly send the complete history.

END OF 13.12

13.13 CONTEXT SELECTION

The context selector shall rank candidate context using:

semantic relevance

task relevance

recency

importance

explicit user reference

project association

conversation association

source reliability

permission

sensitivity

The highest-value context is selected until the available context budget is reached.

END OF 13.13

13.14 CONTEXT BUDGET

The system shall divide the model context budget into logical sections.

Example:

SYSTEM POLICY ↓ TASK INSTRUCTIONS ↓ CURRENT USER REQUEST ↓ RECENT CONVERSATION ↓ CONVERSATION SUMMARY ↓ PROJECT CONTEXT ↓ RELEVANT MEMORY ↓ RETRIEVED EVIDENCE ↓ TOOL INFORMATION ↓ OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS

The allocation must be dynamic.

Complex research requests may allocate more context to evidence.

Simple conversations may allocate more space to the current conversation.

END OF 13.14

13.15 CONTEXT COMPRESSION

Long conversations must be periodically summarized.

The summary should contain:

- current objective

- important decisions

- established facts

- unresolved questions

- important user instructions

- relevant files

- important tool results

- current project state

- research progress

The summary must not replace the original messages in storage.

Original messages remain available for retrieval.

END OF 13.15

13.16 SUMMARY GENERATION

Conversation summaries shall be generated using a controlled process:

MESSAGE HISTORY ↓ SUMMARY MODEL ↓ STRUCTURED SUMMARY ↓ SUMMARY VALIDATOR ↓ DATABASE ↓ VERSIONED SUMMARY

Important factual claims in summaries should remain traceable to the original messages.

END OF 13.16

13.17 SUMMARY VERSIONING

Every summary shall contain:

summary_id

conversation_id

version

created_at

source_message_range

summary_content

generated_by

validation_status

updated_at

This prevents silent corruption of long-term conversation context.

END OF 13.17

13.18 MEMORY SEPARATION

Conversation context and long-term memory must remain separate.

Conversation:

temporary and task-specific.

Memory:

persistent and user-approved.

Project knowledge:

persistent but project-specific.

Laboratory knowledge:

persistent but laboratory-specific.

Scientific knowledge:

global/shared only according to permissions and provenance.

The system must never treat all stored information as universal memory.

END OF 13.18

13.19 MEMORY WRITE POLICY

The AI must not automatically store every user statement as permanent memory.

Memory candidates must be evaluated.

Possible classifications:

TEMPORARY

CONVERSATION-SPECIFIC

PROJECT-SPECIFIC

USER MEMORY

ORGANIZATION KNOWLEDGE

SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE

The system should request or follow the appropriate user permission policy before persistent personal memory is created.

END OF 13.19

13.20 MEMORY RETRIEVAL

When the user asks a question, GSIR shall search memory only when relevant.

Example:

User asks about an active project.

Retrieve relevant project context.

User asks an unrelated general question.

Do not inject unrelated project information.

This reduces hallucination and unnecessary context.

END OF 13.20

13.21 PROJECT CONTEXT

When a conversation belongs to a project:

conversation ↓ project_id ↓ project knowledge ↓ project files ↓ project research ↓ project experiments ↓ project notes

The AI should prioritize project-specific information over generic information when the user asks a project-related question.

END OF 13.21

13.22 “USE PROJECT KNOWLEDGE” LOGIC

The interface shall support project-aware behavior.

If the user selects:

USE PROJECT KNOWLEDGE

the system retrieves relevant project information.

If the user does not select a project:

the system uses general context unless another explicit source is selected.

If the system determines that a project is clearly relevant, it may suggest using the project knowledge but must not silently mix unrelated projects.

END OF 13.22

13.23 FILE CONTEXT

Uploaded files shall be represented as references rather than blindly inserting entire files into prompts.

Flow:

FILE ↓ FILE METADATA ↓ INDEX ↓ SEARCH ↓ RELEVANT EXTRACTS ↓ CONTEXT ↓ MODEL

This dramatically reduces token usage.

END OF 13.23

13.24 CONVERSATION HISTORY SEARCH

History shall support:

keyword search

semantic search

date filtering

project filtering

source filtering

model filtering

conversation mode

favorites

tags

recent activity

The history service shall return only authorized conversations.

END OF 13.24

13.25 CHAT TAB ARCHITECTURE

The top browser-style tab system shall communicate with the conversation service.

Flow:

CREATE TAB ↓ CREATE/LOAD CONVERSATION ↓ TAB STATE ↓ CONVERSATION STATE ↓ MESSAGES ↓ AI RESPONSE ↓ PERSIST ↓ TAB UPDATE

Closing a tab should remove it from the active workspace but preserve the conversation unless the user explicitly deletes it.

END OF 13.25

13.26 MULTIPLE ACTIVE TABS

Each tab must maintain independent:

conversation_id

project_id

model

mode

draft

attachments

context selection

streaming state

The system must prevent messages from one tab from being sent into another conversation.

END OF 13.26

13.27 RESPONSE STREAMING STATE

During generation:

REQUESTED

QUEUED

PROCESSING

STREAMING

TOOL_EXECUTION

RESEARCHING

VALIDATING

COMPLETED

FAILED

The frontend should display appropriate progress without creating excessive notifications.

END OF 13.27

13.28 GPT-STYLE RESPONSE OBJECT

The internal response object shall follow a structured architecture.

Example:

{ "response_id": "resp_xxx", "request_id": "req_xxx", "conversation_id": "conv_xxx", "message_id": "msg_xxx", "status": "completed", "content": { "text": "..." }, "citations": [], "evidence": [], "tool_calls": [], "attachments": [], "confidence": null, "warnings": [], "usage": { "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0 }, "model": { "provider": "...", "model_id": "..." } }

The same response contract should be usable by web, desktop and mobile clients.

END OF 13.28

13.29 RESPONSE EVENTS

Streaming responses shall use typed events.

Possible events:

message.started

message.delta

tool.started

tool.progress

tool.completed

research.started

research.progress

citation.added

validation.started

validation.completed

message.completed

message.failed

This allows the frontend to render complex AI workflows without depending on provider-specific formats.

END OF 13.29

13.30 TOOL-CALL STATE

Every tool call shall have:

tool_call_id

request_id

conversation_id

tool_name

arguments

authorization_status

started_at

completed_at

status

result_reference

error

The actual result may be stored separately when large.

END OF 13.30

13.31 CONVERSATION ERROR RECOVERY

If an AI request fails:

- Preserve the user message.

- Preserve partial state where safe.

- Mark the request as failed.

- Record the failure.

- Retry if appropriate.

- Use fallback if appropriate.

- Allow the user to retry.

- Never duplicate the user's message accidentally.

END OF 13.31

13.32 IDEMPOTENCY

Every message submission shall have an idempotency key.

If the network sends the same request twice, the backend must detect the duplicate and prevent duplicate AI generations.

This is essential for mobile networks and unreliable connections.

END OF 13.32

13.33 CONCURRENT MESSAGE PROTECTION

If the user sends multiple messages quickly:

the backend must preserve ordering.

Each message shall have:

sequence_number

created_at

message_id

The conversation service shall guarantee deterministic ordering.

END OF 13.33

13.34 EDIT MESSAGE

Users should be able to edit a previous user message.

The architecture shall create a new conversation branch rather than silently destroying the previous state.

Example:

Conversation A │ ├── Message 1 ├── Message 2 │ └── Edited Message 2 ↓ New Branch

The original branch remains recoverable.

END OF 13.34

13.35 REGENERATE RESPONSE

When the user requests regeneration:

the system should create a new assistant response associated with the same user message.

It must preserve previous responses unless the user explicitly removes them.

This allows comparison between model responses.

END OF 13.35

13.36 RESPONSE EDITING

The user interface may allow response editing/copying/exporting.

However, edited user-visible content must be distinguished from the original AI-generated response in the database.

Required fields may include:

original_response

edited_response

edited_by

edited_at

This maintains provenance.

END OF 13.36

13.37 CHAT SEARCH AND AUTOCOMPLETE

The search box shall support:

conversation search

command search

project search

file search

knowledge search

recent queries

saved shortcuts

suggested actions

Autocomplete should use debouncing and asynchronous retrieval.

The UI must remain responsive while search suggestions are generated.

END OF 13.37

13.38 SHORTCUT SYSTEM

Shortcuts created by the user shall have:

shortcut_id

user_id

name

command

description

parameters

scope

created_at

updated_at

enabled

The shortcut engine must validate commands before execution.

A shortcut must never bypass security or authorization controls.

END OF 13.38

13.39 NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION

Conversation state changes must not generate excessive notifications.

Use:

inline status

streaming status

small temporary toast

persistent notification only for important events.

Examples:

“Saved”

“Research completed”

“Action requires approval”

“Model unavailable”

Auto-save operations must be deduplicated.

END OF 13.39

13.40 CROSS-DEVICE SYNCHRONIZATION

Because GSIR will operate on:

iOS

Android

Windows

macOS

web

and potentially additional platforms,

conversation state must be server-synchronized.

Flow:

DEVICE A ↓ GSIR API ↓ CENTRAL STATE ↓ DEVICE B

Offline changes must use controlled synchronization and conflict resolution.

END OF 13.40

13.41 OFFLINE CONVERSATION

When offline:

the client may allow:

- viewing cached conversations

- creating local notes

- drafting messages

- local AI

- local document processing

- local search where supported

When connectivity returns:

LOCAL STATE ↓ SYNC ENGINE ↓ CONFLICT DETECTION ↓ SERVER STATE ↓ MERGE ↓ CONFIRMED STATE

END OF 13.41

13.42 LOCAL AI CONNECTION

If the user has downloaded a compatible local AI model, the conversation engine may route suitable tasks locally.

The conversation state architecture remains unchanged.

Only the execution layer changes:

Conversation ↓ AI Router ↓ Local Model

or:

Conversation ↓ AI Router ↓ Cloud Model

This provides provider/model independence.

END OF 13.42

13.43 SECURITY BOUNDARIES

Conversation state must enforce:

USER A → only authorized USER A conversations.

PROJECT A → only authorized PROJECT A data.

ORGANIZATION A → only authorized ORGANIZATION A data.

LABORATORY A → only authorized laboratory information.

No context retrieval operation may bypass authorization.

Authorization must occur before context assembly.

END OF 13.43

13.44 CONTEXT INJECTION PROTECTION

Retrieved conversation messages, files, web content and scientific documents must be treated as untrusted data.

The context builder shall label data by origin.

Example:

CURRENT_USER_MESSAGE

TRUSTED_SYSTEM_POLICY

PROJECT_DATA

USER_FILE

EXTERNAL_SOURCE

TOOL_RESULT

This reduces the possibility that untrusted content becomes an instruction.

END OF 13.44

13.45 DATA RETENTION

The system shall support configurable retention for:

messages

attachments

tool results

temporary context

research sessions

logs

exports

deleted conversations

The retention policy must comply with account, organization and applicable legal requirements.

END OF 13.45

13.46 DELETION

When the user deletes a conversation, the system shall distinguish:

SOFT DELETE

from

PERMANENT DELETE.

Permanent deletion must remove or schedule removal of:

messages

attachments

context indexes

embeddings

cached representations

search indexes

derived records where legally and technically required.

Audit records required for security may follow separate retention policies.

END OF 13.46

13.47 EXPORT

Recommended formats:

JSON

Markdown

TXT

PDF

The export must preserve:

conversation order

timestamps

attachments/references

citations

sources

model information where appropriate

research metadata

The export system shall never expose internal secrets or security credentials.

END OF 13.47

13.48 PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION

The conversation system shall avoid loading an entire history into memory.

Use:

pagination

cursor-based retrieval

lazy loading

summaries

relevance retrieval

caching

streaming

incremental synchronization

database indexing

This is required for very large conversation histories.

END OF 13.48

13.49 LARGE-SCALE ARCHITECTURE

For the long-term target of approximately 1 crore concurrent queries/users, conversation services must remain horizontally scalable.

Use:

stateless API services

distributed caches

message queues

partitioned databases

read replicas

connection pooling

asynchronous workers

event-driven processing

distributed search

object storage

autoscaling

backpressure

The conversation service must not depend on a single server.

END OF 13.49

The system shall track:

context size

token usage

model latency

tool latency

fallbacks

END OF 13.50

Automated tests shall cover:

END OF 13.51

13.52 AI QUALITY TESTING

The context engine shall be tested for:

correct context selection

irrelevant context exclusion

memory contamination

project contamination

missing important context

incorrect summaries

The objective is to maximize relevant context rather than maximize context quantity.

END OF 13.52

13.53 SELF-IMPROVEMENT CONNECTION

Conversation telemetry may feed the GSIR self-improvement system.

The system can identify:

13.54 FINAL CONVERSATION ARCHITECTURE

The complete system shall operate as:

USER ↓ FRONTEND CHAT TAB ↓ API GATEWAY ↓ AUTHENTICATION ↓ CONVERSATION SERVICE ↓ LOAD CONVERSATION STATE ↓ LOAD CURRENT MESSAGE ↓ CONTEXT ENGINE ↓ ┌────────────────────────────┐ │ RELEVANT CONTEXT │ │ │ │ Recent Messages │ │ Conversation Summary │ │ Project Knowledge │ │ User Memory │ │ Files │ │ Research │ │ Laboratory Context │ │ Tool Results │ └────────────────────────────┘ ↓ CONTEXT VALIDATION ↓ AI GATEWAY ↓ MODEL ROUTER ↓ MODEL / LOCAL AI / TOOLS ↓ STREAMING RESPONSE ↓ VALIDATION ↓ CITATION/EVIDENCE PROCESSING ↓ MESSAGE PERSISTENCE ↓ CONVERSATION STATE UPDATE ↓ FRONTEND ↓ USER FEEDBACK ↓ EVALUATION ↓ SELF-IMPROVEMENT

13.55 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 13 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Multiple chat tabs work independently.

- Each conversation has persistent state.

- Messages are stored in correct order.

- Project context is isolated.

- User memory is separated from conversation state.

- Relevant context is retrieved automatically.

- Irrelevant context is excluded.

- Long conversations are summarized.

- Original messages remain recoverable.

- GPT-style structured message data is supported.

- Streaming responses work.

- Tool calls have persistent state.

- Duplicate requests are prevented.

- Failed requests can recover safely.

- Message editing creates controlled branches.

- Response regeneration works.

- History search works.

- Autocomplete works.

- Offline/local AI can integrate through the AI Gateway.

- Multi-device synchronization works.

- Authorization is enforced before context retrieval.

- Project and laboratory data cannot leak into unrelated conversations.

- Context injection defenses are implemented.

- Conversation exports work.

- Deletion works according to retention policy.

- Performance remains scalable.

- Token usage is minimized through selective context.

- Conversation quality is measurable.

- Context failures can be detected.

- The architecture can support future AI models, tools, research agents and scientific workflows without redesigning the conversation layer.

END OF PART 13

PART 14 — PROJECT WORKSPACE, RESEARCH PROJECT ARCHITECTURE, KNOWLEDGE ISOLATION AND PROJECT-CENTRIC AI

14.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall treat a PROJECT as the primary long-term workspace for scientific, engineering, technical, business, computational and research activities.

A project shall not be merely a folder containing chats.

A project shall be an intelligent, persistent research environment containing:

Project Identity │ ├── Conversations ├── Research Questions ├── Hypotheses ├── Literature ├── Sources ├── Files ├── Datasets ├── Code ├── Experiments ├── Experimental Results ├── Analysis ├── Models ├── Calculations ├── Notes ├── Tasks ├── Citations ├── Evidence ├── Decisions ├── Collaborators ├── Laboratory Context ├── Equipment ├── Suppliers ├── Research Timeline ├── Versions ├── Audit Trail └── AI Research Context

The project architecture shall allow GSIR to function as a persistent scientific research environment rather than a conventional chatbot.

END OF 14.1

14.2 PROJECT DESIGN PRINCIPLE

The fundamental rule shall be:

ONE PROJECT = ONE CONTROLLED KNOWLEDGE AND WORK CONTEXT.

Information belonging to Project A must not automatically enter Project B.

The AI may use:

Global scientific knowledge

plus

authorized project knowledge

plus

relevant conversation context

plus

authorized user memory

plus

authorized external information.

The system must explicitly distinguish these sources.

END OF 14.2

14.3 PROJECT TYPES

GSIR shall support extensible project types.

Initial types:

SCIENTIFIC_RESEARCH

BIOLOGY

CHEMISTRY

PHYSICS

ENGINEERING

CUSTOM

New project types shall be addable through configuration rather than requiring a complete architectural redesign.

END OF 14.3

14.16 PROJECT CONTEXT HIERARCHY

When the user asks a project-related question, context should be assembled in this order:

SYSTEM POLICY

↓

TASK INSTRUCTIONS

↓

CURRENT USER MESSAGE

↓

CURRENT CONVERSATION

↓

PROJECT ACTIVE CONTEXT

↓

PROJECT VERIFIED KNOWLEDGE

↓

PROJECT RESEARCH

↓

PROJECT FILES

↓

PROJECT DATASETS

↓

RELEVANT EXTERNAL SOURCES

↓

GENERAL MODEL KNOWLEDGE

14.17 VERIFIED PROJECT KNOWLEDGE

RETRIEVED

USER-PROVIDED

AI-GENERATED

COMPUTATIONALLY_VALIDATED

EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED

PEER-REVIEWED

HUMAN-APPROVED

REJECTED

This is essential for scientific reliability.

AI-generated information must never automatically become verified project knowledge.

Hypothesis → Experiment

14.66 AI PROJECT CONTEXT TESTS

The system must test that:

Project A information cannot leak into Project B.

Unrelated project files are excluded.

Relevant project knowledge is retrieved.

User-selected files are prioritized correctly.

Rejected findings are not presented as validated facts.

Old project information does not override newer verified information without appropriate version handling.

Conflicting sources remain identifiable.

Permission-restricted information is never supplied to unauthorized models/tools.

END OF 14.66

14.67 PROJECT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 14 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can create projects.

- Projects have persistent identifiers.

- Projects have controlled lifecycle states.

- Projects support multiple research domains.

- Projects support members and roles.

- Permissions are enforced server-side.

- Projects contain chats.

- Projects contain files.

- Projects contain datasets.

- Projects contain research questions.

- Projects contain hypotheses.

- Projects contain experiments.

- Projects contain results.

- Projects contain literature.

- Projects contain citations.

- Projects contain notes and tasks.

- Project context is isolated.

- Project knowledge is versioned.

- Knowledge has verification status.

- AI can retrieve relevant project context.

- AI does not blindly load all project data.

- Research questions connect to hypotheses.

- Hypotheses connect to evidence.

- Experiments connect to hypotheses.

- Experiments identify their data/code/environment.

- Dataset versions are preserved.

- Research decisions are traceable.

- Alternative research paths can be represented.

- Project timelines are available.

- Project events are auditable.

- Project deletion is controlled.

- Project data can scale to very large workloads.

- Project context can be cached and optimized.

- Project APIs are versioned.

- Frontend and backend use the same project identifiers and contracts.

- The architecture can accept future scientific modules without redesigning the project core.

END OF PART 14

PART 14 COMPLETED.

PART 15 — CONVERSATION, CHAT TABS, SEARCH, HISTORY, NOTES, NOTIFICATIONS AND PERSONAL WORKSPACE ARCHITECTURE

15.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a persistent, high-performance conversational workspace designed for scientific research, engineering, analysis, coding, general productivity and multi-step AI work.

The conversation system shall not be implemented as a basic chatbot message list.

It shall support:

Chat

Multiple tabs

Projects

Research context

AI model selection

AI operating modes

Files

Web research

Tool execution

Code

Notes

History

Search

Bookmarks/favorites

Notifications

Voice

Responses

Edits

Regeneration

Branching

Citations

Evidence

Feedback

Conversation memory

Conversation export

Conversation versioning

The architecture must allow the conversational system to evolve into the primary interaction layer of the GSIR research operating system.

END OF 15.1

15.2 CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Every conversation shall be treated as a structured stateful object.

The basic relationship shall be:

USER ↓ WORKSPACE ↓ PROJECT (OPTIONAL) ↓ CONVERSATION ↓ MESSAGE ↓ AI RESPONSE ↓ TOOLS / SOURCES / FILES / COMPUTATIONS ↓ VALIDATION ↓ FINAL RESPONSE

A conversation must therefore be capable of representing more than plain text.

END OF 15.2

15.3 CONVERSATION TYPES

Initial conversation types:

GENERAL_CHAT

RESEARCH_CHAT

PROJECT_CHAT

LITERATURE_REVIEW

DATA_ANALYSIS

CODING

DEBUGGING

EXPERIMENT_ANALYSIS

HYPOTHESIS_ANALYSIS

SCIENTIFIC_WRITING

WEB_RESEARCH

FILE_ANALYSIS

PLANNING

BRAINSTORMING

MODEL_EVALUATION

ENGINEERING

CUSTOM

The type shall influence default behavior but must not bypass authorization or validation.

END OF 15.3

15.4 CONVERSATION IDENTIFIER

Every conversation shall have:

conversation_id

Recommended format:

conv_<unique_identifier>

The identifier must remain stable even when the conversation title changes.

END OF 15.4

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ + │ Solved Problem × │ Number Systems × │ Research × │ … │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Each tab represents a conversation reference.

A tab shall maintain:

tab_id

conversation_id

position

active_state

opened_at

last_active_at

temporary_state

draft_message

scroll_position

selected_context

The tab itself should not duplicate the complete conversation database record.

END OF 15.7

15.8 TAB STATE VS SERVER STATE

Client state:

active tab

tab ordering

temporary draft

UI selection

temporary filters

scroll position

temporary model selection

Server state:

conversation

messages

attachments

project association

AI configuration

tool calls

sources

citations

memory

audit records

This separation prevents unnecessary synchronization traffic.

END OF 15.8

15.9 NEW CHAT

The top-bar + button shall support:

New Chat

New Project

New Note

New Workspace

Open Web Link

The frontend must send the appropriate action to the relevant subsystem rather than implementing independent duplicated logic.

END OF 15.9

15.10 CHAT CREATION FLOW

The flow shall be:

USER SELECTS NEW CHAT ↓ FRONTEND CREATES LOCAL TAB STATE ↓ CHAT CREATION REQUEST ↓ AUTHENTICATION ↓ AUTHORIZATION ↓ CONVERSATION SERVICE ↓ CONVERSATION RECORD ↓ CONVERSATION ID ↓ TAB SYNCHRONIZATION ↓ CHAT READY

If the product supports instant UI creation, the conversation may initially use an optimistic client state and synchronize with the backend.

END OF 15.10

15.11 MESSAGE ARCHITECTURE

A message shall not be stored as only:

role + text

It should contain structured metadata.

Minimum fields:

message_id

conversation_id

parent_message_id

role

content

content_type

status

sequence_number

created_at

updated_at

model_id

provider

request_id

response_id

metadata

15.12 MESSAGE ROLES

Supported roles:

USER

ASSISTANT

SYSTEM

TOOL

DEVELOPER

REVIEWER

The UI should normally display USER and ASSISTANT content.

Internal roles must remain controlled by the backend architecture.

END OF 15.12

15.13 MESSAGE CONTENT TYPES

Supported types:

TEXT

MARKDOWN

CODE

TABLE

IMAGE

FILE_REFERENCE

CITATION

STRUCTURED_DATA

TOOL_RESULT

ERROR

SYSTEM_EVENT

15.14 MESSAGE PARENTING

Messages should support:

parent_message_id

This enables:

branching

regeneration

editing

alternative responses

research reasoning paths

conversation forks

Example:

User Question │ ├── Assistant Response A │ └── Assistant Response B

The original conversation remains preserved.

END OF 15.14

15.15 MESSAGE STREAMING

AI responses should support streaming.

Flow:

USER SENDS MESSAGE ↓ API REQUEST ↓ AI GATEWAY ↓ MODEL ROUTER ↓ MODEL ↓ STREAM EVENT ↓ BACKEND STREAM ↓ FRONTEND ↓ INCREMENTAL RESPONSE RENDERING

Streaming must not require waiting for the complete model response before displaying content.

END OF 15.15

15.16 STREAM EVENT TYPES

The streaming protocol should support events such as:

message.started

content.delta

content.completed

citation.added

source.added

tool.started

tool.progress

tool.completed

validation.started

validation.completed

message.completed

message.failed

message.cancelled

The protocol must remain versioned.

END OF 15.16

15.17 RESPONSE ARCHITECTURE

AI responses shall be represented internally as structured response objects.

Conceptually:

{ "response_id": "...", "conversation_id": "...", "message_id": "...", "status": "completed", "content": [], "sources": [], "citations": [], "tool_calls": [], "validation": {}, "model": {}, "usage": {}, "metadata": {} }

The exact implementation shall follow the central API contract architecture.

END OF 15.17

15.18 GPT-LIKE RESPONSE EXPERIENCE

The visible response experience should support:

Markdown

Headings

Lists

Tables

Code blocks

Inline code

LaTeX/math

Images

Citations

Source references

Expandable details

Copy

Edit

Regenerate

Continue

Branch

Share

Save

Favorite

Feedback

The rendering system must be consistent across web, desktop and mobile.

END OF 15.18

15.19 EDIT MESSAGE

The user may edit a previous user message.

The system shall not silently overwrite the previous conversation state.

Instead:

Original Message ↓ Edit ↓ Create New Message Version ↓ Create Branch ↓ Generate New Response

Previous generated responses remain recoverable.

END OF 15.19

15.20 REGENERATE RESPONSE

Regenerate shall create a new response version.

Example:

Question │ ├── Response V1 ├── Response V2 └── Response V3

The system should record:

model version

configuration

timestamp

retrieval context

tool usage

validation status

This enables comparison.

END OF 15.20

15.21 CONTINUE RESPONSE

If a response is incomplete or intentionally stopped:

CONTINUE

shall allow the AI Gateway to resume using the appropriate conversation context.

It must not blindly duplicate the previous response.

END OF 15.21

15.22 RESPONSE FEEDBACK

The interface shall support:

Helpful

Not Helpful

Incorrect

Missing Evidence

Wrong Citation

Poor Reasoning

Code Error

Other

Feedback must not automatically modify production model behavior.

END OF 15.22

15.23 SEARCH INPUT

The main search/chat input shall support:

natural-language questions

commands

project queries

file questions

research requests

web searches

analysis requests

coding requests

tool requests

15.24 SEARCH/AUTOCOMPLETE

Autocomplete should support:

conversation history

commands

shortcuts

projects

files

recent searches

research questions

saved prompts

AI modes

available tools

KEYSTROKE ↓ LOCAL FILTER ↓ DEBOUNCE ↓ SERVER SEARCH IF REQUIRED ↓ RANK ↓ DISPLAY SUGGESTIONS

It should prioritize local results before network retrieval where possible.

The backend should use:

cached results

ranking

pagination

search_id

metadata

Search

Today

Projects

15.28 HISTORY SEARCH

conversation titles

message text

projects

notes

sources

files

research questions

hypotheses

datasets

15.29 HISTORY INDEXING

Possible architecture:

PostgreSQL metadata

search index

15.30 CONVERSATION FAVORITES

Users may mark:

conversation

message

source

note

15.31 NOTES CONNECTION

The Notes subsystem shall remain distinct from chat messages.

15.32 NOTE AUTOSAVE

Notes shall support draft autosave.

Autosave architecture:

USER EDIT ↓ DEBOUNCE ↓ LOCAL STATE ↓ AUTOSAVE REQUEST ↓ BACKEND ↓ VERSION CHECK ↓ SAVE ↓ SILENT SUCCESS

15.33 NOTIFICATION ARCHITECTURE

IN-APP NOTIFICATION

SYSTEM ALERT

SECURITY ALERT

TASK NOTIFICATION

RESEARCH NOTIFICATION

15.34 TOAST DEDUPLICATION

For repetitive events:

SAVE

AUTO_SAVE

INDEX_UPDATE

SYNC_COMPLETE

must become:

✓ Changes saved

The toast should disappear automatically after the configured duration.

END OF 15.34

15.35 IMPORTANT NOTIFICATIONS

Persistent notifications should be reserved for events such as:

security warning

failed experiment

important research result

failed backup

account action

permission change

critical system error

user-requested reminder

The notification system must support priority levels.

15.36 NOTIFICATION DATA MODEL

Minimum:

notification_id

user_id

project_id

type

title

message

status

created_at

read_at

expires_at

action_reference

metadata

15.37 CHAT ATTACHMENTS

Users shall be able to attach:

documents

PDFs

images

datasets

code

spreadsheets

text

scientific files

other supported formats.

15.38 FILE PROCESSING

Attachment flow:

UPLOAD ↓ VALIDATE ↓ MALWARE/SECURITY CHECK ↓ STORE ↓ EXTRACT METADATA ↓ EXTRACT CONTENT ↓ INDEX ↓ EMBED IF REQUIRED ↓ LINK TO MESSAGE ↓ AVAILABLE TO AI

The AI must not automatically trust every uploaded file.

END OF 15.38

15.39 WEB SEARCH CONNECTION

When web search is enabled:

USER QUERY ↓ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ↓ WEB SEARCH DECISION ↓ SEARCH ↓ SOURCE VALIDATION ↓ RETRIEVAL ↓ RANKING ↓ AI ANALYSIS ↓ CITATION ↓ RESPONSE

Web search must remain distinct from internal project knowledge.

END OF 15.39

15.40 PROJECT CONTEXT CONNECTION

If the conversation belongs to a project:

conversation.project_id

shall determine the default project context.

The AI context builder should retrieve:

project instructions

relevant research

relevant files

relevant sources

relevant datasets

relevant hypotheses

relevant experiments

relevant prior conversation context

Only relevant information should enter the model context.

END OF 15.40

15.41 CROSS-PROJECT CHAT

Cross-project analysis must be explicit.

Example:

Project A +

Project B

The user must have access to both.

The backend creates a controlled multi-project context.

No project data may leak into another project simply because the user has both projects open.

END OF 15.41

15.42 CONVERSATION MEMORY

Conversation memory has three levels:

SHORT-TERM

CURRENT MESSAGE CONTEXT

CONVERSATION MEMORY

PERSISTENT CONVERSATION SUMMARY

PROJECT MEMORY

PROJECT-LEVEL KNOWLEDGE

GLOBAL USER MEMORY

USER-LEVEL INFORMATION

These must remain logically separated.

END OF 15.42

15.43 CONTEXT WINDOW OPTIMIZATION

The system must not send the entire conversation to the model every time.

Use:

recent messages

conversation summary

relevant historical messages

retrieved project knowledge

selected files

relevant citations

The context builder shall dynamically select information.

END OF 15.43

15.44 CONVERSATION SUMMARIZATION

Long conversations should periodically generate structured summaries containing:

objective

important facts

decisions

open questions

assumptions

validated findings

rejected findings

pending tasks

important references

The summary must be versioned.

END OF 15.44

15.45 CONVERSATION COMPRESSION

Compression must preserve high-value information.

Low-value content:

repeated greetings

duplicate statements

redundant model explanations

temporary UI events

should not consume long-term context.

Scientific evidence, calculations, citations, decisions and user constraints must receive higher preservation priority.

END OF 15.45

15.46 CONVERSATION BRANCHING

Branching shall allow users to explore alternatives without destroying the original research path.

Example:

Research Question │ ├── Approach A │ └── Analysis │ ├── Approach B │ └── Analysis │ └── Approach C └── Analysis

Branches should preserve parent relationships.

END OF 15.46

15.47 CONVERSATION VERSIONING

Important state changes should be versionable.

Versioned objects may include:

messages

AI configuration

research context

generated code

analysis

responses

summaries

The system should be able to reconstruct relevant historical state.

END OF 15.47

15.48 CONVERSATION EXPORT

Supported formats may include:

JSON

Markdown

TXT

PDF

HTML

END OF 15.48

15.49 CONVERSATION IMPORT

Future versions may support importing:

previous GSIR conversations

supported AI conversation exports

research notes

structured datasets

/research

/code

/run

/note

/summarize

/cite

/compare

/validate

available

15.58 SECURITY BOUNDARY

Every conversation request must pass:

authorization

rate control

input validation

context authorization

tool authorization

output validation where applicable

audit logging

END OF 15.58

15.59 PROMPT INJECTION DEFENSE

Retrieved content must be treated as untrusted data.

A paper, webpage, uploaded file or tool result must not automatically become an instruction to the AI.

The system should distinguish:

SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS

USER INSTRUCTIONS

PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS

RETRIEVED DATA

TOOL OUTPUT

UNTRUSTED CONTENT

This is essential for scientific research environments.

END OF 15.59

15.60 RESPONSE RELIABILITY

For research responses, the system should distinguish:

MODEL KNOWLEDGE

RETRIEVED EVIDENCE

COMPUTED RESULT

USER-PROVIDED DATA

EXPERIMENTAL RESULT

INFERENCE

HYPOTHESIS

The UI should make these distinctions visible where useful.

END OF 15.60

15.61 HALLUCINATION REDUCTION

GSIR shall reduce hallucinations through:

retrieval

structured tools

source citations

database queries

calculation verification

code execution

cross-checking

critic models

uncertainty representation

source conflict detection

human review

The architecture must not claim absolute accuracy.

Scientific confidence must be evidence-based.

END OF 15.61

15.62 COST OPTIMIZATION

The conversation system shall minimize unnecessary model usage through:

local autocomplete

cached context

conversation summaries

semantic retrieval

prompt deduplication

model routing

small models for classification

larger models only for difficult reasoning

streaming

batch processing

asynchronous processing

cached tool results where valid

The AI Gateway defined in the central architecture shall control these decisions.

END OF 15.62

15.63 LARGE-SCALE QUERY ARCHITECTURE

The conversation subsystem must be designed for extremely high concurrency, including the previously specified target of up to 1 crore concurrent queries/workloads at system scale.

This shall not mean maintaining 1 crore active model generations on a single server.

The architecture must use:

stateless API servers

load balancing

distributed queues

partitioned workloads

autoscaling

model-serving pools

connection management

rate control

backpressure

caching

asynchronous workers

distributed observability

regional deployment where required

Capacity targets must be validated through load testing before being considered production guarantees.

END OF 15.63

15.64 CHAT DATABASE CONNECTION

The conversation system shall connect to:

users

projects

messages

files

models

AI requests

tool calls

sources

citations

memory

feedback

notifications

audit logs

The relationships must use stable IDs.

No subsystem should depend on UI labels as identifiers.

API

15.72 SECURITY TESTING

The conversation system must be tested for:

unauthorized conversation access

project leakage

cross-user data leakage

prompt injection

malicious files

tool abuse

session hijacking

message tampering

API replay

rate-limit bypass

model-provider credential exposure

sensitive data leakage

unsafe plugin execution

END OF 15.72

15.73 PERFORMANCE TESTING

Tests shall measure:

message latency

first-token latency

streaming latency

autocomplete latency

history search latency

conversation loading

large conversation loading

concurrent users

concurrent generations

file attachment performance

database throughput

cache effectiveness

failure recovery

The system must be benchmarked rather than assuming scalability.

END OF 15.73

15.74 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 15 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can create conversations.

- Conversations persist correctly.

- Browser-style chat tabs work.

- Multiple conversations can remain open.

- Tabs do not duplicate server data unnecessarily.

- Messages are structured records.

- Messages support branching.

- Messages support editing.

- Responses support regeneration.

- Responses support streaming.

- Citations can be attached.

- Sources can be attached.

- Files can be attached.

- Project context is supported.

- Conversation memory is separated from project memory.

- Long conversations can be summarized.

- Context is dynamically selected.

- Search works across conversation history.

- Autocomplete works efficiently.

- Search history is persisted.

- Notes can be created from conversations.

- Autosave does not generate notification spam.

- Notifications are deduplicated.

- Important notifications remain persistent.

- Voice input can be supported.

- Voice response can be enabled/disabled.

- Local AI can be integrated through a provider abstraction.

- Plugins can connect through controlled interfaces.

- Security boundaries are enforced server-side.

- Prompt injection defenses are implemented.

- Project isolation is tested.

- Cross-project access is explicit.

- Conversation exports work.

- Failure states are structured.

- Idempotency prevents duplicate operations.

- Requests are traceable.

- Performance is measured.

- High-concurrency architecture is load-tested.

- Frontend and backend contracts are synchronized.

- The subsystem can evolve without redesigning the core GSIR architecture.

END OF PART 15

16.1 PURPOSE

The system shall support:

PDFs

documents

spreadsheets

datasets

images

text files

code

research papers

experimental data

project documents

and other supported scientific file formats.

Files shall be usable by the AI only through controlled processing and retrieval.

PROCESSING QUEUE

↓

PROCESSING STATUS

END OF 16.7

16.8 SUPPORTED FILE VALIDATION

The backend shall validate:

file extension

MIME type

actual file signature

file size

encoding where applicable

structural validity

checksum

user/project permission

Unsupported files shall be rejected with a clear structured error.

END OF 16.8

16.9 FILE SECURITY

Uploaded files shall be treated as untrusted input.

The system shall protect against:

malicious files

embedded scripts

malformed documents

path traversal

dangerous archive contents

prompt injection contained inside documents

unauthorized file access

The security subsystem shall control the detailed scanning and isolation implementation.

END OF 16.9

16.10 OBJECT STORAGE

Large binary files should be stored in object storage rather than directly inside the primary relational database.

The database stores:

file metadata

ownership

relationships

storage reference

version

processing state

The object-storage layer stores the actual file.

END OF 16.10

16.11 FILE CHECKSUM

Every stored file shall have a checksum.

The checksum shall be used for:

integrity verification

duplicate detection

version identification

upload validation

processing verification

The checksum must not be treated as the file identifier.

END OF 16.11

16.12 DOCUMENT PROCESSING

After upload:

FILE

↓

FORMAT DETECTION

↓

PARSER SELECTION

↓

TEXT EXTRACTION

↓

STRUCTURE EXTRACTION

↓

METADATA EXTRACTION

↓

NORMALIZED DOCUMENT

The processing system shall preserve document structure where possible.

END OF 16.12

16.13 PDF PROCESSING

For PDFs, the system should extract where available:

title

authors

sections

paragraphs

tables

figures

captions

references

page numbers

equations

metadata

Text extraction must retain page references so that AI responses can cite the correct location.

END OF 16.13

16.14 IMAGE PROCESSING

Images may contain:

figures

graphs

experimental images

microscopy

diagrams

plots

screenshots

The processing pipeline may use appropriate vision/OCR systems when required.

The original image must remain available.

Extracted information must be marked as extracted information rather than original source text.

END OF 16.14

16.15 SPREADSHEET PROCESSING

Spreadsheet processing shall preserve:

sheet name

columns

rows

cell values

formulas where supported

data types

units where identifiable

metadata

The system must avoid converting scientific numeric data into ambiguous text.

END OF 16.15

16.16 DATASET PROCESSING

Datasets shall be handled through the dedicated dataset subsystem.

The file layer stores the underlying data.

The dataset layer stores:

schema

version

provenance

validation

analysis relationships

The two systems must remain connected through stable identifiers.

END OF 16.16

16.17 CODE FILES

Code files shall preserve:

language

filename

path

version

repository reference where applicable

commit reference where applicable

dependencies where available

The code must not be executed merely because it was uploaded.

Execution requires the controlled execution subsystem.

END OF 16.17

16.18 DOCUMENT NORMALIZATION

Different document formats shall be converted into a normalized internal representation.

Conceptually:

Document

├── Metadata ├── Sections ├── Blocks ├── Tables ├── Figures ├── References └── Source Locations

This allows retrieval to operate consistently across file types.

END OF 16.18

16.19 CHUNKING

Long documents shall be divided into retrieval units.

Chunking should respect:

section boundaries

paragraph boundaries

table boundaries

figure captions

semantic continuity

page information

Chunks should not be arbitrarily split when doing so destroys scientific meaning.

END OF 16.19

16.20 CHUNK METADATA

Each chunk shall retain:

chunk_id

file_id

file_version

document_section

page_number where available

position

text

content_type

checksum

embedding_reference where applicable

metadata

END OF 16.20

16.21 INDEXING

Processed content shall be indexed for efficient retrieval.

The system shall support:

keyword search

semantic search

metadata filtering

structured search

hybrid search

The AI must not depend exclusively on embeddings.

END OF 16.21

16.22 HYBRID RETRIEVAL

Retrieval flow:

USER QUERY

↓

QUERY ANALYSIS

↓

KEYWORD RETRIEVAL

SEMANTIC RETRIEVAL

METADATA FILTERING

↓

RESULT MERGING

↓

RANKING

↓

RELEVANCE FILTER

↓

CONTEXT BUILDER

END OF 16.22

16.23 EMBEDDINGS

Embeddings shall be generated only where useful.

They should support:

semantic retrieval

document similarity

research discovery

related evidence

The system should avoid unnecessary embedding generation to reduce storage and compute costs.

END OF 16.23

16.24 EMBEDDING VERSIONING

embedding_version

content_checksum

created_at

↓

PROJECT AUTHORIZATION

↓

FILE AUTHORIZATION

↓

RETRIEVAL

END OF 16.25

16.26 PROJECT FILE RETRIEVAL

For project conversations:

QUERY

↓

PROJECT ID

↓

AUTHORIZED FILES

↓

RELEVANCE SEARCH

↓

RANKING

↓

TOP EVIDENCE

↓

AI CONTEXT

The system must not send every project file to the model.

END OF 16.26

16.27 CONVERSATION FILE RETRIEVAL

file processing

authorization

format validation

END OF 16.27

16.28 SOURCE TRACEABILITY

Every retrieved chunk should be traceable to:

file_id

file_version

page/section where available

chunk_id

source metadata

END OF 16.28

16.29 DOCUMENT CITATIONS

AI-generated claims based on uploaded documents should be capable of referencing:

document

page

section

table

figure

or other available source location.

END OF 16.29

16.30 DUPLICATE FILE DETECTION

checksum

file metadata

UPLOADED

VALIDATING

SCANNING

STORED

PROCESSING

INDEXING

READY

PARTIALLY_READY

FAILED

DELETED

END OF 16.31

16.32 PROCESSING FAILURES

the error must be recorded

the user must receive a clear status

OCR

PDF extraction

embedding

large dataset processing

indexing

duplicate analysis

The upload request should not remain blocked unnecessarily.

END OF 16.33

16.34 PROCESSING QUEUE

Example:

UPLOAD

↓

FILE SERVICE

↓

PROCESSING QUEUE

↓

DOCUMENT WORKER

↓

INDEXING WORKER

↓

EMBEDDING WORKER

↓

READY

END OF 16.34

16.35 FILE SEARCH

The Files interface shall support:

filename search

content search

semantic search

project filtering

type filtering

date filtering

owner filtering

tag filtering

processing status

Search results must respect permissions.

END OF 16.35

16.36 FILE ORGANIZATION

All Files

Recent

Projects

Documents

Papers

Datasets

Code

Images

Experimental Data

Shared

Favorites

images

tables

code

metadata

16.41 FILE RETENTION

user deletion

project deletion

legal retention requirements

enterprise policies

research records

audit requirements

materials

parameters

results

conclusions

limitations

citations

entities

units

datasets

16.58 AI RELIABILITY TESTING

The system must verify that:

fabricated page numbers are not generated

AI context contains the intended document version

The system must preserve uncertainty when document extraction is incomplete.

END OF 16.58

16.59 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 16 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Files can be uploaded.

- File ownership is explicit.

- File IDs are stable.

- Metadata is stored separately from binary content.

- File versions are preserved.

- Files are validated.

- Files are security scanned.

- Files are stored securely.

- Checksums are generated.

- Documents are processed asynchronously.

- Document structure is preserved where possible.

- PDFs can retain page references.

- Images can be processed where supported.

- Spreadsheets preserve structured data.

- Datasets connect to the dataset subsystem.

- Code files connect to the code subsystem.

- Documents can be chunked.

- Chunks retain source references.

- Keyword search works.

- Semantic search works where enabled.

- Hybrid retrieval works.

- Retrieval respects permissions.

- Embeddings are versioned.

- Duplicate processing is minimized.

- Large documents use efficient retrieval.

- AI context uses relevant content rather than entire files.

- Citations can trace back to source locations where available.

- Processing failures are recoverable.

- File deletion is controlled.

- Project isolation is enforced.

- File processing is observable.

- The architecture can scale horizontally.

- File processing avoids unnecessary model and compute costs.

- The system is ready for integration with the research, experiment, dataset, AI and project subsystems.

END OF PART 16

PART 16 COMPLETED.

PART 17 — PROJECTS, WORKSPACES, RESEARCH CONTEXT AND KNOWLEDGE ORGANIZATION ARCHITECTURE

17.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall organize scientific work around persistent Projects and Workspaces rather than treating every AI conversation as an isolated chat.

A Project shall act as the primary container for a research objective and its associated:

Chats

Notes

Files

Datasets

Research questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Sources

Evidence

Tasks

AI context

Results

Research history

The Project architecture shall connect these components without duplicating the underlying data.

END OF 17.1

17.2 PROJECT HIERARCHY

The logical hierarchy shall be:

GSIR

↓

User

↓

Project

↓

Workspace

↓

Research Objects

Research Objects may include:

Chats

Notes

Files

Datasets

Questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Sources

Evidence

Tasks

Results

END OF 17.2

17.3 PROJECT

Every Project shall have:

Project_id

Owner_id

Name

Description

Status

Visibility

Created_at

Updated_at

Created_by

Updated_by

Metadata

The project_id shall be immutable.

END OF 17.3

17.4 PROJECT STATUS

The Project lifecycle shall support:

DRAFT

ACTIVE

PAUSED

COMPLETED

ARCHIVED

DELETED

Status changes must be recorded where auditability is required.

END OF 17.4

17.5 PROJECT CREATION FLOW

USER

↓

CREATE PROJECT

↓

VALIDATE PROJECT DATA

↓

CREATE PROJECT RECORD

↓

CREATE DEFAULT WORKSPACE

↓

INITIALIZE PROJECT CONTEXT

↓

PROJECT READY

END OF 17.5

17.6 PROJECT WORKSPACE

A Workspace is the active working environment inside a Project.

It shall provide access to:

Project AI

Chats

Files

Notes

Research

Datasets

Experiments

Sources

Tasks

Results

The Workspace shall use project_id as the primary context boundary.

Active_chat_id

Active_note_id

Active_file_id

Active_research_object

Selected_mode

Selected_model

Filters

Search_query

Temporary_ui_state

Temporary UI state must not be confused with permanent research data.

END OF 17.7

17.8 PROJECT CONTEXT

The AI shall be able to use Project context when the user explicitly works inside a Project.

Project context may contain:

Research objective

Research questions

Relevant files

Approved sources

Previous conclusions

Validated findings

Current hypotheses

Experimental information

Project terminology

The system shall retrieve only relevant information instead of sending the complete Project database to the model.

END OF 17.8

17.9 PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY

When the user asks:

“If we use project, use project knowledge; otherwise do not.”

The AI context system shall follow this rule.

Inside a Project:

USER QUERY

↓

PROJECT CONTEXT

↓

AUTHORIZED RETRIEVAL

↓

RELEVANT EVIDENCE

↓

AI RESPONSE

Outside a Project:

USER QUERY

↓

NORMAL AI CONTEXT

↓

AUTHORIZED GENERAL KNOWLEDGE/SEARCH

↓

AI RESPONSE

Project information must not automatically leak into unrelated conversations.

END OF 17.9

17.10 PROJECT CHAT

Every Project chat shall contain:

Chat_id

Project_id

Title

Mode

Model

Created_at

Updated_at

Messages

Attachments

Context_configuration

Metadata

Model

State

Last_activity

17.12 PROJECT NOTES

Personal Notes:

User-level

Private

General

Project-level

Research-related

Context-aware

↓

SEARCH

ANALYSIS

↓

↓

↓

↓

↓

Current information

Data

Calculation

Validation

↓

↓

17.29 WORKSPACE SEARCH

Chats

Notes

Files

Sources

Research questions

Hypotheses

Datasets

Experiments

Tasks

Results

END OF 17.29

17.30 PROJECT KNOWLEDGE INDEX

Project knowledge may be indexed using:

Metadata

Keyword indexes

Semantic indexes

Structured relationships

Knowledge graph relationships

17.31 PROJECT MEMORY

When inside a Project:

EXPLICIT CURRENT INPUT

DIRECTLY ATTACHED MATERIAL

RELEVANT PROJECT EVIDENCE

PROJECT MEMORY

GENERAL KNOWLEDGE

↓

↓

↓

RELEVANCE RETRIEVAL

↓

RANKING

↓

DEDUPLICATION

↓

CONTEXT BUDGETING

↓

AI CONTEXT

Recent activity

AI-generated summaries must not silently overwrite validated research records.

END OF 17.34

17.35 PROJECT ACTIVITY

Project activity may record:

Chat created

File added

Note updated

Dataset added

Question created

Hypothesis created

Experiment recorded

Result added

Task completed

This activity stream is separate from user notification spam.

END OF 17.35

17.36 PROJECT NOTIFICATIONS

Only important Project events should generate persistent notifications.

Routine operations such as repeated autosaves should use the lightweight notification/toast system defined previously.

END OF 17.36

17.37 PROJECT COLLABORATION

The architecture shall support future collaboration without changing the core Project model.

Potential access levels:

Administrator

Editor

Contributor

Viewer
