END OF 17.37

17.38 PROJECT SECURITY

Every Project API operation shall verify:

Authentication

Project membership

Authorization

Resource ownership/access

The Project ID supplied by a client must never be treated as proof of access.

END OF 17.38

17.39 CROSS-PROJECT ISOLATION

A query operating inside Project A must not retrieve private information from Project B.

Retrieval must apply Project-level authorization before context construction.

This rule applies to:

Files

Chats

Notes

Datasets

Experiments

Sources

Hypotheses

Results

Memory

END OF 17.39

The export should preserve relationships among:

Project

Chats

Notes

Files

Sources

Questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Datasets

Results

The export subsystem must preserve provenance.

END OF 17.40

17.41 PROJECT ARCHIVE

Archived Projects remain logically preserved but should not consume active workspace resources unnecessarily.

Archived Project data remains subject to authorization and retention policies.

END OF 17.41

17.42 PROJECT DELETION

Deletion shall require explicit authorization.

The system must distinguish:

Remove relationship

Archive Project

Soft delete

Permanent deletion

Deleting a Project must not automatically delete shared underlying files or resources unless the ownership rules explicitly permit it.

END OF 17.42

17.43 DATABASE TABLES

The Project subsystem shall contain at minimum:

Projects

Project_members

Project_workspaces

Project_chats

Project_notes

Project_questions

Project_hypotheses

Project_sources

Project_evidence

Project_tasks

Project_results

Project_activity

Project_settings

Project_context

Project_relationships

The underlying file, dataset, experiment and laboratory tables remain owned by their respective subsystems.

END OF 17.43

Users

↓

Projects

↓

Project_workspaces

↓

Project_relationships

↓

Research_objects

Research objects connect through stable IDs.

The database must avoid unnecessary duplication of complete objects.

17.55 PROJECT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 17 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Projects can be created.

- Projects have stable IDs.

- Project ownership is enforced.

- Workspaces can be created.

- Project chats are connected.

- Chat tabs can reference Project chats.

- Project Notes are supported.

- Project Files are linked without binary duplication.

- Datasets can be referenced.

- Research Questions are supported.

- Hypotheses can be connected to questions and evidence.

- Sources are traceable.

- Evidence retains provenance.

- Results retain research relationships.

- Project Tasks are supported.

- Project context is scope-controlled.

- Project memory is separated from global memory.

- Cross-project data leakage is prevented.

- Search works across authorized Project objects.

- Project AI uses relevant context instead of all Project data.

- All five AI modes work inside Project context.

- Laboratory information can be connected.

- Missing equipment can be represented accurately.

- Project activity is recorded.

- Routine autosave events do not create notification spam.

- Project permissions are enforced server-side.

- Project deletion is controlled.

- Project export preserves relationships.

29. Project operations are scalable

- Project architecture connects correctly to Files, AI, Research, Dataset, Experiment and Laboratory subsystems.

PART 18 — CHAT, CONVERSATION, MESSAGE, TAB AND RESPONSE WORKSPACE ARCHITECTURE

18.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a persistent, multi-tab, research-oriented conversation system that combines:

AI chat

research conversation

search

analysis

project context

file attachments

web research

structured AI responses

citations

reasoning status

editable responses

conversation history

and workspace operations.

The chat system shall be a core interface layer connected to the Project, File, Research, AI Gateway, Model Router, Memory, Search and Notification systems.

END OF 18.1

18.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

A conversation shall not be treated as only a sequence of text messages.

A conversation is a structured research interaction containing:

conversation identity

user messages

assistant responses

tool operations

sources

citations

attachments

selected model

selected mode

project context

memory references

response metadata

validation information

usage information

timestamps

The system must preserve enough metadata to reproduce and audit important research interactions.

END OF 18.2

18.3 CONVERSATION HIERARCHY

The hierarchy shall be:

USER

↓

PROJECT

↓

WORKSPACE

↓

CONVERSATION

↓

MESSAGE

↓

MESSAGE PARTS

↓

CONTENT / TOOL RESULTS / SOURCES

A conversation may exist outside a Project.

A Project conversation must always contain project_id.

END OF 18.3

18.4 CONVERSATION IDENTIFIER

Every conversation shall have:

conversation_id

Recommended format:

conv_<unique_identifier>

The identifier must remain immutable.

END OF 18.4

18.5 CONVERSATION METADATA

Minimum conversation metadata:

conversation_id

user_id

project_id

workspace_id

title

mode

model

status

created_at

updated_at

last_message_at

metadata

END OF 18.5

18.6 CONVERSATION STATUS

Supported states:

ACTIVE

ARCHIVED

DELETED

PROCESSING

ERROR

A deleted conversation must not be immediately physically removed if retention or audit requirements require preservation.

END OF 18.6

18.7 CONVERSATION CREATION

Flow:

USER SELECTS NEW CHAT

↓

CREATE CONVERSATION

↓

ASSIGN USER

↓

OPTIONALLY ASSIGN PROJECT

↓

INITIALIZE MODE

↓

INITIALIZE MODEL

↓

CREATE WORKSPACE STATE

↓

DISPLAY CHAT

END OF 18.7

18.8 CHAT TAB ARCHITECTURE

GSIR shall support browser-style conversation tabs.

Example:

[Solving Problem ×] [Number Systems ×] [Research Paper ×] [+]

Each open tab represents an active conversation reference.

Tabs must not duplicate the entire conversation.

END OF 18.8

18.9 TAB STATE

Each tab shall maintain:

tab_id

conversation_id

title

project_id

selected_mode

selected_model

draft_state

scroll_position where required

last_activity

temporary_state

The persistent conversation remains owned by the backend.

END OF 18.9

18.10 TAB OPERATIONS

The interface shall support:

new tab

open conversation

close tab

switch tab

reopen recent conversation

rename tab

duplicate conversation where explicitly requested

move conversation into Project where permitted

Closing a tab must not delete the conversation.

END OF 18.10

18.11 MULTI-TAB LIMIT

The frontend should avoid rendering every open conversation simultaneously.

Inactive tabs should use lightweight state.

Only the active conversation should maintain the complete interactive rendering state where practical.

END OF 18.11

18.12 MESSAGE IDENTIFIER

Every message shall have:

message_id

Recommended format:

msg_<unique_identifier>

The identifier must remain immutable.

END OF 18.12

18.13 MESSAGE TYPES

The system shall support at minimum:

USER

ASSISTANT

SYSTEM

TOOL

DEVELOPER

EVENT

ERROR

The UI shall normally expose USER and ASSISTANT messages while internal message types remain controlled by the backend.

END OF 18.13

18.14 MESSAGE STRUCTURE

A message shall contain:

message_id

conversation_id

role

content_parts

created_at

updated_at

status

model

mode

metadata

citations

attachments

tool_calls

usage

END OF 18.14

18.15 MESSAGE PARTS

A message should be represented as structured parts rather than one uncontrolled text string.

Possible parts:

TEXT

CODE

TABLE

IMAGE

FILE_REFERENCE

CITATION

TOOL_RESULT

EQUATION

WARNING

ERROR

Each part must have a defined type.

END OF 18.15

18.16 USER MESSAGE

A user message may contain:

text

files

images

voice input

references

selected Project

selected mode

selected model

additional actions

The backend shall normalize the request before sending it to the AI Gateway.

END OF 18.16

18.17 ASSISTANT RESPONSE

An assistant response may contain:

answer

structured sections

citations

source references

tables

code

calculations

warnings

uncertainty

tool results

follow-up suggestions

The response renderer must interpret structured response data rather than relying only on Markdown.

END OF 18.17

18.18 RESPONSE FORMAT

The internal AI response should follow a consistent structured format.

Conceptual structure:

{ "response_id": "...", "conversation_id": "...", "message_id": "...", "status": "completed", "content": [], "sources": [], "citations": [], "reasoning_metadata": {}, "validation": {}, "usage": {}, "warnings": [], "created_at": "..." }

Internal reasoning traces must not be exposed merely because internal reasoning metadata exists.

END OF 18.18

18.19 RESPONSE STATUS

Streaming responses shall support:

QUEUED

PROCESSING

STREAMING

VALIDATING

COMPLETED

PARTIAL

FAILED

CANCELLED

The frontend shall render the appropriate state.

END OF 18.19

18.20 STREAMING ARCHITECTURE

The response flow shall be:

USER MESSAGE

↓

CHAT API

↓

REQUEST VALIDATION

↓

PROJECT CONTEXT

↓

RETRIEVAL

↓

AI GATEWAY

↓

MODEL ROUTER

↓

MODEL

↓

STREAM

↓

RESPONSE ASSEMBLER

↓

VALIDATION

↓

FINAL RESPONSE

The frontend receives incremental response updates through the supported streaming transport.

END OF 18.20

18.21 STREAMING REQUIREMENTS

Streaming must support:

incremental text

structured content

tool status

source availability

errors

cancellation

completion

The frontend must not display incomplete structured information as final information.

END OF 18.21

18.22 RESPONSE CANCELLATION

The user shall be able to stop an active response.

Flow:

STOP

↓

CLIENT CANCEL REQUEST

↓

BACKEND CANCEL SIGNAL

↓

MODEL/TOOL CANCELLATION

↓

STREAM CLOSED

↓

MESSAGE STATUS = CANCELLED

Where cancellation is not technically possible for an underlying operation, the system shall stop downstream processing when safe.

END OF 18.22

18.23 RESPONSE EDITING

Users shall be able to edit their own previous messages where supported.

Editing a previous user message must create a new conversation branch or message version rather than silently destroying research history.

END OF 18.23

18.24 MESSAGE VERSIONING

Important conversation messages should support versions.

Example:

Message V1

↓

User edits

↓

Message V2

The system shall preserve the relationship between versions.

END OF 18.24

18.25 CONVERSATION BRANCHING

The system shall support future branching:

MESSAGE

↓

BRANCH

├── PATH A

└── PATH B

This allows researchers to explore different reasoning paths without losing the original conversation.

END OF 18.25

18.26 REGENERATE RESPONSE

The user may request:

Regenerate

Improve

Shorter

Longer

Simplify

Explain

Verify

Critique

The system must create a new response generation event rather than silently replacing the previous answer.

END OF 18.26

18.27 RESPONSE ACTIONS

Each assistant response may provide:

Copy

Edit

Regenerate

Verify

Save to Notes

Add to Project

Create Task

Create Hypothesis

Export

The actions shall call the appropriate subsystem instead of embedding business logic inside the chat UI.

END OF 18.27

18.28 RESPONSE CITATIONS

Scientific responses shall display citations where applicable.

A citation should connect to:

source_id

document_id or file_id

version

location

retrieved content

source metadata

The citation renderer must never invent a source.

END OF 18.28

18.29 SOURCE VALIDATION

Before displaying a citation as verified:

SOURCE

↓

SOURCE AVAILABLE?

↓

CONTENT RETRIEVED?

↓

REFERENCE VALID?

↓

LOCATION VALID?

↓

DISPLAY CITATION

If verification fails, the system must not represent the citation as verified.

END OF 18.29

18.30 AI RESPONSE RELIABILITY

The chat system shall distinguish:

SOURCE FACT

MODEL INFERENCE

CALCULATION

USER-PROVIDED INFORMATION

HYPOTHESIS

UNCERTAINTY

This distinction is particularly important for scientific research.

END OF 18.30

↓

PROJECT CONTEXT SERVICE

↓

↓

PROJECT MEMORY

↓

RESEARCH OBJECTS

↓

RELEVANT SOURCES

↓

CONTEXT BUILDER

↓

AI GATEWAY

↓

↓

↓

↓

18.80 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 18 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can create conversations.

- Conversations can exist inside or outside Projects.

- Conversations have stable IDs.

- Messages have stable IDs.

- Messages use structured message parts.

- Multiple browser-style chat tabs work.

- Closing a tab does not delete a conversation.

- Chat history works.

- History search works.

- Autocomplete works.

- Project context is correctly isolated.

- Files can be attached through the File subsystem.

- AI responses can stream.

- Streaming can be cancelled.

- Response failures are handled.

- Retry does not create unintended duplicate requests.

- Responses can be regenerated.

- Previous messages can be edited without destroying research history.

- Conversation branching is supported by the architecture.

- Citations are source-traceable.

- Unsupported citations are not presented as verified.

- Response types are structured.

- Tool calls are controlled.

- Tool results are distinguished from final conclusions.

- Long conversations use selective context.

- Conversation summaries do not replace original messages.

- Model and mode metadata are preserved.

- Usage and cost metadata can be recorded.

- Conversation export is supported.

- Conversation deletion is controlled.

- Security boundaries are enforced server-side.

- Chat operations are observable.

- Chat services can scale horizontally.

- Chat architecture connects correctly to Projects, Files, Retrieval, Memory, Search, AI Gateway, Model Router, Tools and Notifications.

- The complete workflow operates correctly under automated integration testing.

PART 19 — NOTES, PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE, RESEARCH NOTES AND NOTE-TO-AI INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE

19.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Notes system shall provide a persistent environment for creating, editing, organizing, searching and connecting notes with AI, Projects, research, files and knowledge.

Notes shall not be treated as simple text records.

The system must support:

Personal notes

Project notes

Research notes

Meeting notes

Experimental notes

Literature notes

AI-generated notes

Drafts

Auto-save

Version history

Search

Tags

Linking

Attachments

AI assistance

Conversion into knowledge

Connection to research questions

Connection to hypotheses

Connection to experiments

Export

The Notes system must remain separate from chat messages while allowing controlled relationships between them.

END OF 19.1

19.2 NOTE TYPES

Initial note types shall include:

PERSONAL

PROJECT

RESEARCH

LITERATURE

EXPERIMENT

MEETING

IDEA

DRAFT

AI_GENERATED

REFERENCE

CUSTOM

The architecture must permit additional note types later.

END OF 19.2

19.3 NOTE OWNERSHIP

Each note must have an explicit ownership scope.

Possible scopes:

USER

PROJECT

WORKSPACE

ORGANIZATION

The system must never infer ownership from the note title or folder name.

END OF 19.3

19.4 NOTE IDENTIFIER

Every note shall have:

Note_id

Recommended format:

Note_<unique_identifier>

The note identifier must remain stable throughout the note lifecycle.

END OF 19.4

19.5 NOTE DATABASE RECORD

Minimum fields:

Note_id

User_id

Workspace_id

Project_id

Title

Content

Content_format

Note_type

Status

Version

Created_at

Updated_at

Deleted_at

Metadata

END OF 19.5

19.6 NOTE STATUS

Supported states:

DRAFT

ACTIVE

ARCHIVED

DELETED

The system may introduce additional states when required.

END OF 19.6

19.7 NOTE CREATION FLOW

The user shall be able to create a note through:

New Note

The workflow shall be:

USER

↓

NEW NOTE

↓

CREATE LOCAL DRAFT

↓

ENTER TITLE/CONTENT

↓

AUTOSAVE

↓

BACKEND PERSISTENCE

↓

NOTE READY

END OF 19.7

19.8 NOTE EDITOR

The editor shall support:

Title

Body

Formatting

Links

Attachments

Tags

Project association

Research association

Save state

Version information

The editor must remain responsive during autosave.

END OF 19.8

19.9 AUTOSAVE

Autosave shall be implemented using controlled debouncing.

Flow:

USER EDITS

↓

WAIT FOR QUIET PERIOD

↓

SAVE REQUEST

↓

BACKEND VERSION CHECK

↓

PERSIST

↓

UPDATE LOCAL STATE

↓

SHOW LIGHTWEIGHT SAVED STATE

The system must not send a save request for every keystroke.

END OF 19.9

19.10 AUTOSAVE NOTIFICATION RULE

Autosave must not produce repeated persistent notifications.

Incorrect:

Note auto-saved

Note auto-saved

Note auto-saved

Note auto-saved

Correct:

✓ Changes saved

The saved indicator may remain inside the editor rather than appearing as a global notification.

END OF 19.10

19.11 NOTE VERSIONING

Important note changes must be versionable.

Example:

Note

├── Version 1

├── Version 2

├── Version 3

└── Current Version

Each version should record:

Version_id

Note_id

Version_number

Content

Created_by

Created_at

Change_summary where available

END OF 19.11

19.12 NOTE CONCURRENCY

If the same note is edited from multiple devices, the system must detect version conflicts.

Flow:

Device A

↓

Version 5

Device B

↓

Version 5

Device A saves

↓

Version 6

Device B attempts save

↓

Conflict detected

The system must not silently overwrite Version 6.

END OF 19.12

19.13 NOTE SEARCH

Users must be able to search:

Title

Content

Tags

Project

Note type

Date

Author

Research association

The search system must respect ownership and permissions.

END OF 19.13

19.14 NOTE TAGGING

Notes may contain:

Tags

Categories

Subjects

Research domains

Project tags

The tag system should use reusable identifiers rather than repeatedly storing identical text values.

END OF 19.14

Conversation

File

Research question

Hypothesis

Experiment

Dataset

Source

Task

Result

Knowledge item

AI Response

↓

Save as Note

↓

Create Note

↓

Store source conversation reference

↓

Save

A note may reference:

Conversation_id

Response_id

File_id

## PART 20 — PROJECTS, WORKSPACES AND RESEARCH PROJECT ARCHITECTURE

### 20.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Project system shall provide the primary organizational layer for scientific work.

A Project is not merely a folder for chats and files.

A Project shall provide an isolated research workspace containing the information, AI context, scientific records, documents, notes, sources, hypotheses, experiments, datasets, tasks and results associated with a specific research objective.

The Project system shall connect the frontend, backend, database, AI system and research architecture through explicit identifiers and permission boundaries.

END OF 20.1

### 20.2 PROJECT HIERARCHY

The core hierarchy shall be:

User

│

├── Workspaces

│   │

│   ├── Projects

│   │   ├── Chats

│   │   ├── Notes

│   │   ├── Files

│   │   ├── Sources

│   │   ├── Research Questions

│   │   ├── Hypotheses

│   │   ├── Experiments

│   │   ├── Datasets

│   │   ├── Results

│   │   └── Tasks

│   │

│   └── Shared Resources

│

└── Personal Resources

A Project must belong to exactly one primary Workspace.

END OF 20.2

### 20.3 WORKSPACE

A Workspace is the higher-level container for projects and collaboration.

A Workspace may represent:

- Individual research

- Laboratory

- Research group

- University department

- Company

- Organization

The architecture must allow additional Workspace types later.

END OF 20.3

### 20.4 PROJECT PURPOSE

Every Project should contain a defined research purpose.

Recommended fields:

project_name

project_description

research_domain

research_objective

status

start_date

target_date

owner

members

The objective is used as contextual information for project-aware AI operations.

END OF 20.4

### 20.5 PROJECT IDENTIFIER

Every Project shall have a stable:

project_id

Recommended format:

project_<unique_identifier>

The project_id must be used for all cross-module relationships.

END OF 20.5

### 20.6 WORKSPACE IDENTIFIER

Every Workspace shall have:

workspace_id

Recommended format:

workspace_<unique_identifier>

Every Project record must contain its workspace_id.

END OF 20.6

### 20.7 PROJECT DATABASE RECORD

Minimum Project fields:

project_id

workspace_id

owner_user_id

name

description

research_domain

research_objective

status

visibility

created_at

updated_at

archived_at

metadata

END OF 20.7

### 20.8 PROJECT STATUS

Initial Project states:

PLANNING

ACTIVE

PAUSED

COMPLETED

ARCHIVED

DELETED

The state transition must be controlled by backend business rules.

END OF 20.8

### 20.9 PROJECT CREATION FLOW

USER

↓

NEW PROJECT

↓

ENTER PROJECT INFORMATION

↓

VALIDATE

↓

CREATE WORKSPACE RELATIONSHIP

↓

CREATE PROJECT

↓

INITIALIZE PROJECT CONTEXT

↓

OPEN PROJECT

Project creation must not create unnecessary AI jobs or indexes synchronously.

END OF 20.9

### 20.10 PROJECT INITIALIZATION

After creation, GSIR should initialize:

Project metadata

Default project settings

Access permissions

AI context configuration

Search scope

Activity tracking

Empty research structure

No unnecessary model inference should occur during basic Project creation.

END OF 20.10

### 20.11 PROJECT STRUCTURE

The Project interface shall provide access to:

Overview

Chats

Notes

Files

Sources

Research Questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Datasets

Results

Tasks

Knowledge

Activity

Settings

The exact navigation may evolve while preserving the underlying module boundaries.

END OF 20.11

### 20.12 PROJECT OVERVIEW

The Project Overview shall provide a high-level view of:

Project objective

Current status

Recent activity

Research questions

Active hypotheses

Recent experiments

Important results

Pending tasks

Relevant sources

AI-generated project insights where explicitly enabled

The Overview must not replace the detailed research records.

END OF 20.12

### 20.13 PROJECT CHAT

Project Chat shall be connected to the Chat subsystem through:

project_id

conversation_id

workspace_id

The Project AI context may include authorized:

Project Notes

Project Files

Project Sources

Project Knowledge

Research records

The system must not automatically include unrelated personal data.

END OF 20.13

### 20.14 PROJECT NOTES

Project Notes shall use the Notes subsystem defined in Part 19.

Relationship:

Project

↓

project_id

↓

Notes

Notes remain independently stored and versioned.

END OF 20.14

### 20.15 PROJECT FILES

Project Files shall use the File subsystem.

Relationship:

Project

↓

project_id

↓

File records

↓

Object storage

The Project database must not duplicate the actual file binary.

END OF 20.15

### 20.16 PROJECT SOURCES

Sources may include:

Scientific papers

Books

Web sources

Datasets

Internal documents

Experimental records

Other references

Each source must maintain provenance.

END OF 20.16

### 20.17 RESEARCH QUESTIONS

A Project may contain multiple research questions.

Example:

Project

│

├── Research Question 1

├── Research Question 2

├── Research Question 3

└── Research Question 4

Each research question shall have a stable identifier.

END OF 20.17

### 20.18 RESEARCH QUESTION RECORD

Minimum fields:

research_question_id

project_id

title

question

description

status

priority

created_by

created_at

updated_at

metadata

END OF 20.18

### 20.19 RESEARCH QUESTION STATUS

Initial states:

OPEN

UNDER_RESEARCH

ANSWERED

REJECTED

REFINED

ARCHIVED

A research question may evolve without deleting its history.

END OF 20.19

### 20.20 HYPOTHESIS CONNECTION

Hypotheses shall reference the Project and, where applicable, a research question.

Project

↓

Research Question

↓

Hypothesis

The Hypothesis subsystem shall preserve its own validation and provenance records.

END OF 20.20

### 20.21 EXPERIMENT CONNECTION

Experiments shall reference:

project_id

research_question_id where applicable

hypothesis_id where applicable

experiment_id

This creates a traceable research chain.

END OF 20.21

### 20.22 DATASET CONNECTION

Datasets associated with a Project must have stable:

dataset_id

project_id

source information

provenance

version information

The Project system must reference datasets rather than duplicating dataset storage.

END OF 20.22

### 20.23 RESULT CONNECTION

Results shall be connected to their originating research entities where available.

Recommended chain:

Research Question

↓

Hypothesis

↓

Experiment

↓

Dataset

↓

Analysis

↓

Result

The architecture must permit branching and multiple experiments.

END OF 20.23

### 20.24 TASK CONNECTION

Tasks may be generated from:

Project planning

Research questions

Notes

Experiments

Results

AI suggestions

Users must be able to distinguish manually created tasks from AI-generated task candidates.

END OF 20.24

### 20.25 PROJECT KNOWLEDGE

Each Project may have a controlled knowledge layer containing approved project information.

Knowledge should be derived from:

validated sources

approved notes

validated results

project documents

approved scientific records

Knowledge status must remain distinguishable from unverified AI output.

END OF 20.25

### 20.26 PROJECT AI CONTEXT

The AI system shall use Project context through a controlled retrieval pipeline:

User Request

↓

Identify Project

↓

Authorization

↓

Determine Required Context

↓

Retrieve Relevant Project Data

↓

Rank Evidence

↓

Build AI Context

↓

AI Reasoning

↓

Response

The system must not send the entire Project database to the model.

END OF 20.26

### 20.27 PROJECT CONTEXT PRIORITY

When generating a Project response, the system should prioritize:

- Explicitly selected information

- Directly referenced records

- Project-approved knowledge

- Relevant project sources

- Relevant project notes

- Relevant research records

- Other permitted project context

Unrelated information must be excluded.

END OF 20.27

### 20.28 PROJECT MEMORY

Project memory is separate from global user memory.

Project memory may contain:

research decisions

project preferences

definitions

approved terminology

important constraints

project-specific assumptions

The memory subsystem must preserve provenance and allow deletion or correction.

END OF 20.28

### 20.29 PROJECT ISOLATION

Project data must be isolated logically.

A request for Project A must not retrieve Project B data unless explicit permissions allow it.

This applies to:

AI retrieval

search

autocomplete

files

notes

chat

datasets

sources

analytics

API responses

END OF 20.29

### 20.30 WORKSPACE MEMBERS

A Workspace may contain:

OWNER

ADMIN

RESEARCHER

SCIENTIST

MEMBER

VIEWER

CUSTOM ROLES

The permission system must be centralized rather than implemented independently inside every feature.

END OF 20.30

### 20.31 PROJECT MEMBERSHIP

Project access should be inherited from Workspace membership only when the Workspace policy permits it.

Project-specific membership may override or further restrict access.

END OF 20.31

### 20.32 PROJECT PERMISSIONS

At minimum:

PROJECT_VIEW

PROJECT_EDIT

PROJECT_MANAGE

PROJECT_SHARE

PROJECT_DELETE

PROJECT_EXPORT

PROJECT_AI_ACCESS

PROJECT_DATA_ACCESS

Permissions must be checked server-side.

END OF 20.32

### 20.33 PROJECT SHARING

Sharing shall support explicit access control.

Possible scopes:

Private

Workspace

Selected Users

Organization

The system must never expose a Project merely because its name or identifier is known.

END OF 20.33

### 20.34 PROJECT ACTIVITY

Project activity may record:

Project created

Member added

Chat created

Note created

File uploaded

Source added

Hypothesis created

Experiment created

Dataset uploaded

Result recorded

Task completed

Project settings changed

Activity records should contain:

activity_id

project_id

actor_id

event_type

target_type

target_id

created_at

metadata

END OF 20.34

### 20.35 PROJECT AUDITABILITY

Important research operations must remain traceable.

Examples:

Who created a hypothesis?

Who changed the hypothesis?

Which source was used?

Which dataset generated a result?

Which user approved project knowledge?

The Project architecture shall reference audit records rather than duplicating audit logic.

END OF 20.35

### 20.36 PROJECT ARCHIVE

Archiving a Project should make it inactive without immediately destroying its records.

Archived Projects may remain:

searchable to authorized users

exportable

restorable

read-only by default

END OF 20.36

### 20.37 PROJECT DELETION

Project deletion must use controlled deletion.

Recommended process:

DELETE REQUEST

↓

AUTHORIZATION

↓

CONFIRMATION

↓

SOFT DELETE

↓

RETENTION PERIOD

↓

PERMANENT DELETION

Referenced scientific records must follow their own retention and dependency rules.

END OF 20.37

### 20.38 PROJECT EXPORT

A Project export may contain:

Project metadata

Chats

Notes

Sources

Research questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Datasets metadata

Results

Tasks

Knowledge

Relationships

The export system must preserve identifiers and provenance.

END OF 20.38

### 20.39 PROJECT SEARCH

Project search shall support:

name

description

research domain

research objective

members

status

associated records

The search must respect authorization.

END OF 20.39

### 20.40 PROJECT AUTOCOMPLETE

When a user searches from the global interface:

User types

↓

Debounce

↓

Authorized project search

↓

Ranking

↓

Suggestions

Only Projects the user can access may appear.

END OF 20.40

### 20.41 PROJECT DASHBOARD PERFORMANCE

The Project Overview must not load every Project record simultaneously.

Use:

pagination

lazy loading

summary queries

cached aggregates

incremental loading

The initial Project page should load only information required for the first screen.

END OF 20.41

Minimum tables:

workspaces

workspace_members

workspace_roles

projects

project_members

project_settings

project_activity

research_questions

project_knowledge

project_memory

notes

files

chats

sources

datasets

results

tasks

### 20.46 PROJECT API

Primary endpoints:

POST   /api/v1/workspaces

GET    /api/v1/workspaces

GET    /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}

PATCH  /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}

POST   /api/v1/projects

GET    /api/v1/projects

GET    /api/v1/projects/{project_id}

PATCH  /api/v1/projects/{project_id}

DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}

GET    /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/activity

GET    /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/members

POST   /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/members

DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/members/{user_id}

GET    /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/research-questions

POST   /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/research-questions

PATCH  /api/v1/research-questions/{research_question_id}

DELETE /api/v1/research-questions/{research_question_id}

POST   /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/archive

POST   /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/restore

POST   /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/export

POST   /api/v1/projects/search

END OF 20.46

### 20.47 PROJECT API RESPONSE STRUCTURE

All Project API responses must follow the common GSIR API response architecture.

Successful response:

{

  "success": true,

  "data": {},

  "meta": {},

  "request_id": "..."

}

Error response:

{

  "success": false,

  "error": {

    "code": "...",

    "message": "...",

    "details": {}

  },

  "request_id": "..."

}

The exact global response contract defined by the Core API architecture remains authoritative.

END OF 20.47

### 20.48 PROJECT AI REQUEST

Project AI requests should carry explicit context.

Conceptual request:

{

  "project_id": "...",

  "conversation_id": "...",

  "message": "...",

  "context_mode": "project"

}

The backend must independently verify the user's authorization for the Project.

END OF 20.48

### 20.49 PROJECT AI RESPONSE PROVENANCE

AI responses generated from Project information should retain references to the underlying records when available.

Possible references:

note_id

file_id

source_id

research_question_id

hypothesis_id

experiment_id

dataset_id

result_id

The response layer must distinguish retrieved evidence from AI-generated reasoning.

END OF 20.49

### 20.50 PROJECT AI FAILURE HANDLING

If Project context cannot be retrieved:

The AI must not fabricate Project information.

The system should return a controlled response indicating that the required context could not be retrieved.

The request should be traceable through request_id.

END OF 20.50

### 20.51 PROJECT SECURITY

Project security must include:

authentication

authorization

workspace isolation

project isolation

object-level permission checks

secure file references

AI context authorization

audit logging

rate limiting

input validation

The frontend must never be considered the security boundary.

END OF 20.51

### 20.52 PROJECT DATA IN AI RETRIEVAL

The retrieval engine must apply permission filtering before ranking.

Correct:

Query

↓

Authorization Filter

↓

Eligible Project Records

↓

Retrieval

↓

Ranking

↓

AI Context

Incorrect:

Query

↓

Search All Data

↓

Retrieve

↓

Check Permission

Unauthorized information must never enter the AI context pipeline.

END OF 20.52

### 20.53 PROJECT OBSERVABILITY

Track:

project creation latency

project loading latency

search latency

context retrieval latency

permission failures

AI context failures

export failures

database errors

Project activity

Every important request should support distributed tracing through request_id and trace_id.

END OF 20.53

### 20.54 PROJECT TESTING

Tests must cover:

Workspace creation

Workspace permissions

Project creation

Project editing

Project deletion

Project restoration

Project archive

Project membership

Permission isolation

Research question creation

Project search

Project context retrieval

Project AI context

Project knowledge

Project memory

Project export

Cross-project isolation

Concurrent updates

API validation

Failure handling

END OF 20.54

### 20.55 PROJECT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 20 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can create Workspaces.

- Users can create Projects.

- Projects have stable IDs.

- Projects belong to Workspaces.

- Project membership is controlled.

- Project permissions are enforced server-side.

- Project navigation works correctly.

- Projects can contain Chats.

- Projects can contain Notes.

- Projects can contain Files.

- Projects can contain Sources.

- Projects can contain Research Questions.

- Projects can connect to Hypotheses.

- Projects can connect to Experiments.

- Projects can connect to Datasets.

- Projects can connect to Results.

- Projects can connect to Tasks.

- Project Knowledge is controlled.

- Project Memory is isolated from global memory.

- Project AI uses controlled context retrieval.

- Unauthorized records cannot enter AI context.

- Project search respects permissions.

- Project activity is traceable.

- Projects can be archived.

- Projects can be restored.

- Project deletion follows controlled lifecycle rules.

- Projects can be exported.

- Project APIs follow the common GSIR response architecture.

- Frontend and backend use the same Project identifiers.

- Project operations are observable.

- Project functionality is covered by automated tests.

- Project functionality integrates correctly with the Notes, Chat, Files, Research, AI, Knowledge and Task subsystems.

END OF PART 20

## PART 21 — CHAT, CONVERSATION TABS, MESSAGE ARCHITECTURE AND CONTEXT MANAGEMENT

### 21.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Chat system shall provide the primary interactive interface between the user and the GSIR AI system.

It shall support:

- Standard conversations

- Scientific research conversations

- Project conversations

- Multiple simultaneous conversation tabs

- Search

- AI modes

- Model selection

- File attachments

- Web research

- Scientific evidence retrieval

- AI reasoning

- Streaming responses

- Message editing

- Regeneration

- Branching

- Conversation history

- Conversation export

- Conversation memory

- Conversation-to-Project integration

- Conversation-to-Notes integration

The Chat subsystem must remain modular and must communicate with the AI Gateway rather than directly implementing model-provider logic.

END OF 21.1

### 21.2 CHAT ARCHITECTURE

The basic architecture shall be:

Frontend Chat

↓

Chat API

↓

Authentication / Authorization

↓

Conversation Service

↓

Context Manager

↓

AI Gateway

↓

Model Router

↓

Provider / Local Model

↓

Streaming Response

↓

Message Persistence

↓

Frontend

Scientific research requests may additionally use:

Research Request

↓

Research Orchestrator

↓

Search / Retrieval

↓

Evidence Validation

↓

Reasoning

↓

Scientific Response

END OF 21.2

### 21.3 CONVERSATION IDENTIFIER

Every conversation shall have a stable:

conversation_id

Recommended format:

conversation_<unique_identifier>

The identifier must remain unchanged throughout the conversation lifecycle.

END OF 21.3

### 21.4 MESSAGE IDENTIFIER

Every message shall have:

message_id

Recommended format:

message_<unique_identifier>

Every message must reference its conversation_id.

END OF 21.4

### 21.5 MESSAGE ROLES

The message architecture shall support:

SYSTEM

DEVELOPER

USER

ASSISTANT

TOOL

RESEARCH

The internal roles may not all be directly exposed to the user.

END OF 21.5

### 21.6 CONVERSATION RECORD

Minimum fields:

conversation_id

user_id

workspace_id

project_id

title

mode

model_id

status

created_at

updated_at

archived_at

metadata

END OF 21.6

### 21.7 MESSAGE RECORD

Minimum fields:

message_id

conversation_id

parent_message_id

role

content

content_format

status

model_id

created_at

updated_at

metadata

END OF 21.7

### 21.8 MESSAGE TREE

The architecture must support branching conversations.

Example:

User Message

     │

     └── AI Response A

           │

           ├── User Follow-up

           │

           └── Regenerated Response B

Therefore messages should support:

parent_message_id

This allows multiple response branches without destroying previous responses.

END OF 21.8

### 21.9 CHAT TAB ARCHITECTURE

The frontend shall support browser-like conversation tabs.

Example:

[ Solved Problem × ]

[ Number Systems × ]

[ Research Hypothesis × ]

[ New Chat + ]

Each tab must maintain:

conversation_id

title

selected model

selected mode

project_id

draft message

UI state

END OF 21.9

### 21.10 TAB STATE

Tab state should remain primarily client-side.

Example:

{

  "conversationId": "...",

  "title": "Research Hypothesis",

  "modelId": "...",

  "mode": "research",

  "projectId": "...",

  "draft": "..."

}

The backend remains authoritative for persisted conversation and message data.

END OF 21.10

### 21.11 NEW CHAT

New Chat flow:

NEW CHAT

↓

Create local conversation state

↓

User enters first message

↓

Create persistent conversation

↓

Persist message

↓

Send AI request

A completely empty tab does not need to create unnecessary database records immediately.

END OF 21.11

### 21.12 CHAT MODES

The Chat subsystem shall support a configurable mode architecture.

Initial modes:

AUTOMATIC

CHAT

ANALYSIS

RESEARCH

SCIENTIFIC

PROJECT

The mode determines orchestration behavior rather than merely changing the visual interface.

END OF 21.12

### 21.13 AUTOMATIC MODE

Automatic mode shall determine the appropriate execution strategy based on the request.

Conceptually:

User Request

↓

Intent Detection

↓

Complexity Assessment

↓

Required Tools

↓

Required Context

↓

Select Execution Strategy

Automatic mode must not unnecessarily invoke expensive tools or models.

END OF 21.13

### 21.14 CHAT MODE

Chat mode is intended for ordinary conversational requests.

It should minimize unnecessary:

web searches

retrieval

long reasoning chains

tool calls

expensive models

END OF 21.14

### 21.15 ANALYSIS MODE

Analysis mode should support deeper structured analysis.

Possible operations:

problem decomposition

comparison

reasoning

data interpretation

structured synthesis

The mode should use the AI Gateway and reasoning architecture defined elsewhere.

END OF 21.15

### 21.16 RESEARCH MODE

Research mode shall support:

question decomposition

web/source retrieval

source comparison

evidence extraction

citation tracking

conflict detection

synthesis

uncertainty identification

Research mode must not treat search results as automatically validated scientific facts.

END OF 21.16

### 21.17 SCIENTIFIC MODE

Scientific mode shall support the broader GSIR scientific workflow:

Question

↓

Research

↓

Evidence

↓

Analysis

↓

Hypothesis

↓

Prediction

↓

Validation Plan

↓

Conclusion

The scientific reasoning architecture shall remain separate from ordinary chat behavior.

END OF 21.17

### 21.18 PROJECT MODE

Project mode shall use the active Project context.

It may retrieve:

Project Notes

Project Files

Project Sources

Project Knowledge

Research Questions

Hypotheses

Experiments

Datasets

Results

The authorization layer must filter all retrieved information before AI context construction.

END OF 21.18

### 21.19 MESSAGE STATUS

Messages shall support:

PENDING

PROCESSING

STREAMING

COMPLETED

FAILED

CANCELLED

EDITED

DELETED

The frontend must display the appropriate state.

END OF 21.19

### 21.20 USER MESSAGE FLOW

USER

↓

Validate Input

↓

Create Message

↓

Persist Message

↓

Create AI Request

↓

Context Assembly

↓

AI Gateway

The user message must be persisted before or atomically with request processing so that failed AI execution does not lose the user's input.

END OF 21.20

### 21.21 AI RESPONSE FLOW

AI Request

↓

AI Gateway

↓

Model Router

↓

Provider

↓

Token Stream

↓

Response Parser

↓

Safety / Validation

↓

Message Persistence

↓

Frontend Stream

The final persisted response must represent the authoritative completed response state.

END OF 21.21

### 21.22 STREAMING

The Chat system shall support streaming AI responses.

The frontend should receive incremental response events rather than waiting for the complete response.

Example:

response.started

response.delta

response.delta

response.delta

tool.started

tool.completed

response.delta

response.completed

The exact event contract shall be defined by the global AI streaming architecture.

END OF 21.22

### 21.23 STREAM INTERRUPTION

If a connection is interrupted:

Frontend

↓

Reconnect

↓

Request stream state

↓

Resume or retrieve completed response

The system must avoid duplicating message content.

END OF 21.23

### 21.24 STOP GENERATION

The user shall be able to stop an active AI response.

Flow:

STOP

↓

Cancel Request

↓

Cancel Provider Generation Where Supported

↓

Persist Partial/Cancelled State

↓

Release Resources

END OF 21.24

### 21.25 MESSAGE EDITING

Users shall be able to edit previous user messages.

Editing must not silently overwrite the original research history.

Preferred behavior:

Original Message

↓

Edit

↓

Create New Branch

↓

Generate New Response

The original branch remains available.

END OF 21.25

### 21.26 RESPONSE REGENERATION

Regenerate shall create another response branch.

Original User Message

├── Response A

└── Response B

Previous responses must remain recoverable unless explicitly deleted.

END OF 21.26

### 21.27 MESSAGE ACTIONS

The interface may provide:

Copy

Edit

Regenerate

Retry

Stop

Save as Note

Add to Project

Create Task

Create Hypothesis

Share

Export

Report Problem

The availability of actions depends on message type and permissions.

END OF 21.27

### 21.28 RESPONSE CITATIONS

Research responses may contain structured source references.

The citation layer should maintain:

source_id

source_title

source_url where applicable

retrieval_timestamp

relevant passage/reference information

citation status

The citation system must not fabricate sources.

END OF 21.28

### 21.29 SOURCE TRACEABILITY

For research responses, the system should preserve the relationship:

Conversation

↓

Message

↓

Research Request

↓

Source Retrieval

↓

Evidence

↓

AI Response

This allows later auditing.

END OF 21.29

### 21.30 AI RESPONSE STRUCTURE

Internally, AI responses should use a structured representation rather than storing only an unstructured string.

Possible structure:

{

  "content": "...",

  "sections": [],

  "citations": [],

  "artifacts": [],

  "tool_results": [],

  "confidence": null,

  "warnings": [],

  "metadata": {}

}

The exact schema shall follow the global AI response contract.

END OF 21.30

### 21.31 CONTENT BLOCKS

The frontend should support message content blocks such as:

text

heading

code

table

citation

image

file

chart

equation

warning

source

tool result

research evidence

This allows scientific responses to be rendered correctly without treating every response as plain text.

END OF 21.31

### 21.32 CHAT SEARCH

Conversation search shall support:

conversation title

message content

project

date

mode

model

tags

source references

Search must respect user and Project permissions.

END OF 21.32

### 21.33 GLOBAL SEARCH

The global search system may search across:

Chats

Projects

Notes

Files

Sources

Research records

The search result must identify the object type.

Example:

Research Hypothesis

[Chat]

Experimental Observation

[Note]

Protein Structure Analysis

[Project]

END OF 21.33

### 21.34 CHAT HISTORY

History shall be grouped by:

Today

Yesterday

Last 7 Days

Earlier

The exact time grouping must use the user's configured timezone.

END OF 21.34

### 21.35 AUTO-RENAME

When enabled:

First meaningful user message

↓

Title generation

↓

Validate title

↓

Save conversation title

The title should not be regenerated unnecessarily after every message.

END OF 21.35

### 21.36 CHAT MEMORY

Conversation memory and long-term memory must remain separate.

Conversation context:

Current conversation

Project memory:

Current Project

User memory:

Authorized persistent user information

The system must not merge these scopes indiscriminately.

END OF 21.36

### 21.37 CONTEXT WINDOW MANAGEMENT

For long conversations:

Conversation

↓

Recent messages

+

Relevant older messages

+

Conversation summary

+

Explicit user-selected context

↓

Context Manager

↓

AI

The system must not send every historical message when unnecessary.

END OF 21.37

### 21.38 CONTEXT SUMMARIZATION

Long conversations may be summarized into internal conversation state.

The summary must remain distinguishable from original messages.

Important research evidence should retain source references and should not be reduced to unsupported summaries.

END OF 21.38

### 21.39 CONTEXT RETRIEVAL

Relevant previous conversation information may be retrieved using:

semantic relevance

keyword relevance

recency

explicit references

project association

message relationships

The authorization layer must execute before retrieval results enter the AI context.

END OF 21.39

### 21.40 FILE ATTACHMENTS

Chat messages may contain files.

Flow:

Attach File

↓

File Validation

↓

Upload

↓

Create File Reference

↓

Attach file_id to Message

↓

AI Processing if requested

The Chat database must store file references rather than duplicate binary files.

END OF 21.40

### 21.41 MULTIMODAL INPUT

The architecture should support:

text

documents

images

audio

structured data

future scientific data formats

The model capability registry must determine which model/provider can process each input type.

END OF 21.41

### 21.42 VOICE INPUT

Voice input flow:

Microphone

↓

Audio Capture

↓

Speech-to-Text

↓

User Confirmation / Edit

↓

Chat Message

The transcription should not automatically be treated as perfectly accurate.

END OF 21.42

### 21.43 VOICE OUTPUT

Voice response:

AI Response

↓

Text-to-Speech

↓

Audio Stream

↓

Frontend

Voice output should be optional according to user settings.

END OF 21.43

### 21.44 WEB SEARCH

When Web Search is enabled and required:

User Request

↓

Search Decision

↓

Query Generation

↓

Search

↓

Source Filtering

↓

Evidence Extraction

↓

Citation

↓

AI Context

Search must be performed only when required by the execution strategy.

END OF 21.44

### 21.45 TOOL CALLS

The Chat system may invoke tools through the centralized tool architecture.

Examples:

search

calculator

file analysis

database query

scientific analysis

laboratory integration

external plugin

Tools must be permission-controlled and independently validated.

END OF 21.45

### 21.46 TOOL RESULT HANDLING

Tool results must be represented separately from AI-generated text.

Tool Request

↓

Tool Execution

↓

Tool Result

↓

Validation

↓

Context

↓

AI

The model must not be allowed to falsely represent an unexecuted tool operation as completed.

END OF 21.46

### 21.47 CHAT PLUGINS

Plugins shall be accessed through the centralized Plugin architecture.

Chat may display:

available plugins

enabled plugins

connected plugins

plugin actions

Plugin results must identify their source.

END OF 21.47

### 21.48 OFFLINE AI

If the user has downloaded an approved local AI model:

Chat

↓

Model Capability Check

↓

Local Model Available?

├── Yes → Local Model

└── No → Remote AI Gateway

Offline mode must respect the model's capabilities and the user's selected privacy settings.

Cloud-only tools such as live Web Search cannot function without connectivity.

END OF 21.48

### 21.49 MODEL SELECTION

The frontend should not hard-code provider-specific logic.

It should send:

model_id

The backend Model Registry determines:

provider

capabilities

context capacity

cost class

availability

local/remote status

The Model Router makes the final execution decision.

END OF 21.49

### 21.50 COST-AWARE CHAT EXECUTION

Chat execution should avoid unnecessary expensive operations.

The system may use:

small models for classification

cached results

retrieval before generation

local models

streaming

prompt compression

context filtering

model routing

batch processing where appropriate

Expensive models should be reserved for requests requiring their capabilities.

END OF 21.50

### 21.51 ERROR HANDLING

Possible errors:

authentication failure

authorization failure

invalid request

model unavailable

provider timeout

rate limit

tool failure

network interruption

context retrieval failure

file processing failure

AI generation failure

The user should receive a useful controlled error without exposing internal secrets or infrastructure details.

END OF 21.51

### 21.52 RETRY POLICY

Retries must be controlled.

Transient failures may be retried.

Permanent failures should not be repeatedly retried.

Examples of potentially retryable failures:

network timeout

temporary provider error

temporary service unavailable

The retry system must use exponential backoff and retry limits.

END OF 21.52

### 21.53 IDEMPOTENCY

AI request submission should support idempotency.

Each generation request may include:

request_id

idempotency_key

This prevents duplicate AI generations when clients retry after network interruptions.

END OF 21.53

### 21.54 CHAT CONCURRENCY

Multiple conversations may execute simultaneously.

The system must isolate:

conversation state

request state

stream state

model state

tool state

A slow conversation must not block unrelated conversations.

END OF 21.54

### 21.55 SCALABILITY

The Chat architecture must be horizontally scalable.

Stateless API workers should handle requests while persistent state is stored in appropriate infrastructure.

Long-running AI operations should be handled through asynchronous job infrastructure where appropriate.

Streaming connections should be managed independently from database operations.

END OF 21.55

### 21.56 CHAT DATABASE TABLES

Minimum tables:

conversations

messages

message_branches

message_attachments

conversation_settings

conversation_participants

conversation_sources

conversation_tool_calls

conversation_exports

conversation_summaries

The exact database implementation must follow the global database architecture.

END OF 21.56

Primary endpoints:

### 21.60 CHAT API RESPONSE

Successful API responses shall follow the common GSIR contract:

{

  "success": true,

  "data": {},

  "meta": {},

  "request_id": "..."

}

Error responses:

{

  "success": false,

  "error": {

    "code": "...",

    "message": "...",

    "details": {}

  },

  "request_id": "..."

}

Streaming events shall use the dedicated streaming event contract.

END OF 21.60

### 21.61 CHAT FRONTEND STATE

Frontend state shall distinguish:

server state

local draft state

streaming state

tab state

UI state

The application must not treat all state as one global object.

END OF 21.61

### 21.62 CHAT CACHE

Frequently accessed conversation metadata may be cached.

Messages should use controlled caching and invalidation.

Streaming responses must update the active conversation state without corrupting cached historical data.

END OF 21.62

### 21.63 CHAT SECURITY

The Chat subsystem must enforce:

authentication

conversation ownership

Project authorization

Workspace authorization

message access control

file access control

tool permissions

plugin permissions

AI context permissions

rate limiting

input validation

audit logging where required

END OF 21.63

### 21.64 PROMPT-INJECTION PROTECTION

Messages, files, search results and tool outputs must be treated according to their source.

External content must not automatically become system instructions.

The architecture must separate:

system instructions

developer instructions

user instructions

retrieved data

tool results

untrusted external content

END OF 21.64

### 21.65 SENSITIVE DATA

The Chat subsystem must minimize exposure of sensitive information.

Logs must not unnecessarily contain:

passwords

authentication tokens

private credentials

full sensitive documents

secret API keys

The logging layer must support redaction.

END OF 21.65

### 21.66 CHAT OBSERVABILITY

Track:

request latency

time to first token

generation duration

token usage

model used

provider used

tool usage

retrieval latency

failure rate

stream interruptions

cancellation rate

The system must correlate operations using request_id and trace_id.

END OF 21.66

### 21.67 CHAT TESTING

Automated tests must cover:

conversation creation

message creation

message persistence

message editing

branching

regeneration

streaming

stream interruption

stop generation

context assembly

Project context

memory boundaries

file attachments

tool calls

search

history

model selection

offline model routing

authorization

prompt-injection handling

retry behavior

idempotency

concurrency

END OF 21.67

### 21.68 CHAT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 21 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can create conversations.

- Users can open multiple chat tabs.

- Each tab maintains independent state.

- Conversations have stable IDs.

- Messages have stable IDs.

- Messages support branching.

- Messages can be edited.

- Responses can be regenerated.

- Responses stream correctly.

- Generation can be stopped.

- Interrupted streams can recover safely.

- Chat history works.

- Chat search works.

- Project conversations work.

- Notes can be created from messages.

- Files can be attached.

- Models can be selected through model IDs.

- Chat modes work through the orchestration layer.

- Research mode can invoke the research architecture.

- Web Search can be controlled through settings and permissions.

- Tools use the centralized tool architecture.

- Plugin operations use the centralized plugin architecture.

- Offline models can be selected when available.

- Context is managed without unnecessarily loading complete histories.

- Conversation memory remains distinct from Project and user memory.

- Research citations remain traceable.

- Unauthorized data cannot enter AI context.

- Prompt injection from external content is isolated.

- API responses follow the common GSIR contract.

- Chat state is scalable and concurrency-safe.

- Failures are handled without data loss.

- Chat operations are observable.

- Automated tests cover the complete Chat lifecycle.

- Chat integrates correctly with AI Gateway, Model Router, Projects, Notes, Files, Search, Research, Memory, Tools and Plugins.

END OF PART 21

PART 21 COMPLETED.

## PART 22 — FILES, DOCUMENT INGESTION, DOCUMENT AI AND KNOWLEDGE EXTRACTION ARCHITECTURE

### 22.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR File and Document Intelligence system shall provide a secure, scalable and traceable system for uploading, storing, processing, analyzing, searching and connecting scientific documents and other research files.

The system shall support:

- PDF

- DOC/DOCX

- TXT

- Markdown

- CSV

- XLSX

- JSON

- Images

- Audio

- Video

- Scientific datasets

- Future scientific file formats

The File system shall remain responsible for file storage and metadata.

The Document AI system shall remain responsible for document understanding and extraction.

The Knowledge system shall remain responsible for validated knowledge.

The Research system shall remain responsible for scientific interpretation and research workflows.

These responsibilities must not be merged into one monolithic module.

END OF 22.1

### 22.2 CORE ARCHITECTURE

User

↓

Frontend File Upload

↓

Upload API

↓

Authentication

↓

Authorization

↓

File Validation

↓

Object Storage

↓

File Metadata Database

↓

Processing Queue

↓

Document Processing Pipeline

↓

Text / Structure / Metadata Extraction

↓

Chunking

↓

Indexing

↓

Retrieval

↓

AI / Research System

END OF 22.2

### 22.3 FILE IDENTIFIER

Every file shall have:

file_id

Recommended format:

file_<unique_identifier>

The file_id must remain stable throughout the file lifecycle.

END OF 22.3

### 22.4 FILE VERSION IDENTIFIER

Files that are replaced or updated shall support versioning.

Example:

file_id

├── version 1

├── version 2

├── version 3

└── current version

The original file must not be silently destroyed when versioning is enabled.

END OF 22.4

### 22.5 FILE METADATA

Minimum metadata:

file_id

owner_user_id

workspace_id

project_id

filename

mime_type

file_size

checksum

storage_reference

version

status

created_at

updated_at

metadata

The actual binary content must remain in object storage rather than inside the relational database.

END OF 22.5

### 22.6 FILE OWNERSHIP

Every file must have an explicit ownership scope:

USER

PROJECT

WORKSPACE

ORGANIZATION

Access must be evaluated through the centralized authorization system.

END OF 22.6

### 22.7 UPLOAD FLOW

USER SELECTS FILE

↓

Frontend validates basic properties

↓

Request upload authorization

↓

Backend validates permission

↓

Upload target generated

↓

File uploaded

↓

Checksum generated/verified

↓

File metadata created

↓

Processing job created

↓

Frontend receives processing status

END OF 22.7

### 22.8 FILE VALIDATION

The backend must validate:

filename

extension

MIME type

file size

checksum

upload ownership

workspace/project permissions

supported format

malware/security scanning status where implemented

The system must not trust a client-provided MIME type alone.

END OF 22.8

### 22.9 FILE STATUS

Initial states:

UPLOADING

UPLOADED

VALIDATING

PROCESSING

READY

FAILED

QUARANTINED

ARCHIVED

DELETED

END OF 22.9

### 22.10 ASYNCHRONOUS PROCESSING

Document processing must not block the normal API request.

Flow:

Upload

↓

Persist Metadata

↓

Queue Processing Job

↓

Return Upload Result

↓

Background Worker

↓

Process Document

This architecture permits horizontal scaling.

END OF 22.10

### 22.11 DOCUMENT PROCESSING PIPELINE

File

↓

Format Detection

↓

Security Validation

↓

Text Extraction

↓

Layout Analysis

↓

Table Extraction

↓

Image Extraction

↓

Metadata Extraction

↓

Section Detection

↓

Document Structure

↓

Chunking

↓

Indexing

Not every file type requires every stage.

END OF 22.11

### 22.12 PDF PROCESSING

PDF processing must distinguish:

text-based PDF

scanned PDF

mixed PDF

image-heavy PDF

The system should first attempt reliable text extraction.

If required, OCR may be invoked.

The system must preserve page references.

END OF 22.12

### 22.13 OCR

OCR shall be used when document text cannot be reliably extracted.

Flow:

PDF/Image

↓

Text Extraction Attempt

↓

Insufficient Text?

├── No → Continue

└── Yes → OCR

             ↓

        OCR Validation

             ↓

        Document Structure

OCR output must be marked as machine-extracted.

END OF 22.13

### 22.14 PAGE PROVENANCE

For documents such as scientific papers, extracted content should retain:

file_id

version_id

page_number

section

position where available

This enables citation back to the original document.

END OF 22.14

### 22.15 DOCUMENT STRUCTURE

The Document AI representation should recognize:

title

authors

abstract

keywords

headings

paragraphs

tables

figures

captions

equations

references

footnotes

appendices

page boundaries

The structure must be extensible.

END OF 22.15

### 22.16 DOCUMENT BLOCKS

The internal document representation should use typed blocks.

Example:

Document

├── Heading

├── Paragraph

├── Table

├── Figure

├── Caption

├── Equation

├── Reference

└── Page

Each block should retain its source location.

END OF 22.16

### 22.17 TABLE EXTRACTION

Tables must be stored separately from ordinary text where possible.

The system should preserve:

rows

columns

headers

cell values

units

source page

table identifier

Table extraction confidence may be recorded.

END OF 22.17

### 22.18 FIGURE HANDLING

Figures should retain:

figure_id

file_id

page_number

caption

image reference

surrounding text

Where supported, multimodal AI may analyze the figure.

The system must distinguish the original figure from AI interpretation.

END OF 22.18

### 22.19 EQUATION HANDLING

Scientific equations should not automatically be converted into plain prose.

Where possible, preserve:

original representation

rendered representation

LaTeX representation

page

section

equation identifier

END OF 22.19

### 22.20 METADATA EXTRACTION

The system may extract:

title

authors

DOI

journal

publication date

institution

keywords

document type

reference list

The extracted metadata must remain distinguishable from user-provided metadata.

END OF 22.20

### 22.21 DOCUMENT CHUNKING

Documents shall be divided into retrieval units.

Chunking should preferably respect semantic boundaries such as:

sections

paragraph groups

table units

figure descriptions

equation contexts

The system must avoid blindly splitting scientific concepts in the middle of a logical unit.

END OF 22.21

### 22.22 CHUNK IDENTIFIER

Every indexed chunk shall have:

chunk_id

Recommended format:

chunk_<unique_identifier>

Each chunk must reference:

file_id

file_version_id

document_id

source location

END OF 22.22

### 22.23 CHUNK METADATA

Minimum metadata:

chunk_id

file_id

version_id

page_number

section

content_type

text

position

token_count

created_at

metadata

END OF 22.23

### 22.24 SEARCH INDEX

Processed documents may be indexed for:

keyword search

semantic search

hybrid search

metadata filtering

citation retrieval

The system should use hybrid retrieval rather than relying exclusively on vector similarity.

END OF 22.24

### 22.25 RETRIEVAL FLOW

↓

Authorization Filter

↓

Search Scope

↓

Keyword Retrieval

+

↓

Candidate Fusion

↓

Ranking

↓

Evidence Selection

↓

AI Context

↓

The system may provide:

Results Summary

Limitations Summary

Paper B

+

Paper C

Differences

↓

↓

↓

Limitations

↓

### 22.29 DOCUMENT-TO-PROJECT CONNECTION

Project

↓

project_id

↓

File

↓

Document Processing

↓

selected source content

AI operation metadata where applicable

END OF 22.30

### 22.31 DOCUMENT-TO-RESEARCH CONNECTION

Documents may become research sources.

Relationship:

Document

↓

Source

↓

Research Question

↓

Evidence

↓

Analysis

END OF 22.31

### 22.32 DOCUMENT-TO-KNOWLEDGE CONNECTION

Document information may become a Knowledge Candidate.

Flow:

Document

↓

Extracted Evidence

↓

Knowledge Candidate

↓

Validation

↓

Approved Knowledge

Extraction alone must never imply scientific validation.

END OF 22.32

### 22.33 AI-GENERATED DOCUMENT ANALYSIS

Every AI-derived interpretation must remain distinguishable from source content.

Example:

SOURCE:

Original scientific paper

AI:

Interpretation of paper

VALIDATION:

User/system validation state

END OF 22.33

### 22.34 DOCUMENT CITATION

The system must support citations back to:

document

version

page

section

table

figure

equation

paragraph/block where available

This is essential for scientific reliability.

END OF 22.34

### 22.35 DOCUMENT PROVENANCE

Every extracted research fact should be traceable to its source where possible.

Example:

Claim

↓

Evidence

↓

Document

↓

Version

↓

Page

↓

Source

END OF 22.35

### 22.36 DOCUMENT VERSIONING

If a user uploads a new version of a document, the system should create a new version rather than silently replacing the previous source.

Previous citations must remain resolvable.

END OF 22.36

### 22.37 DUPLICATE DETECTION

The system should identify potential duplicate files using:

checksum

file metadata

content similarity

document identifiers such as DOI where applicable

Duplicate detection must not automatically delete files.

END OF 22.37

### 22.38 FILE PREVIEW

The frontend should support previews appropriate to file type.

For documents:

page navigation

zoom

search

text selection

citation reference

download/export where permitted

The preview must remain connected to the authoritative file version.

END OF 22.38

### 22.39 PROCESSING STATUS

The frontend should display:

Uploading

Processing

Extracting text

Analyzing structure

Indexing

Ready

Failed

The interface must not repeatedly create global notifications for routine processing stages.

END OF 22.39

### 22.40 PROCESSING RETRIES

Transient processing failures may be retried.

Permanent format or validation failures must produce a meaningful error.

Retry attempts must be bounded.

END OF 22.40

### 22.41 LARGE FILE PROCESSING

Large documents should be processed asynchronously.

The processing system should support:

streaming reads where possible

page-level processing

parallelizable extraction

incremental indexing

checkpointing

job retries

This prevents a single large document from blocking the processing system.

END OF 22.41

### 22.42 DOCUMENT PROCESSING QUEUE

Conceptual architecture:

Upload API

↓

Processing Queue

├── Text Extraction Worker

├── OCR Worker

├── Layout Worker

├── Table Worker

├── Metadata Worker

├── Chunk Worker

└── Index Worker

Workers must be independently scalable.

END OF 22.42

### 22.43 FILE STORAGE ARCHITECTURE

The binary storage layer should be separate from the relational database.

Conceptual:

Application

↓

File Service

↓

Object Storage

Database:

file_id

storage_reference

metadata

permissions

status

END OF 22.43

### 22.44 FILE ACCESS

Files must be accessed through authorization-controlled mechanisms.

The application must not expose unrestricted storage paths.

Temporary access URLs, where used, must be:

short-lived

scoped

authorized

END OF 22.44

### 22.45 SECURITY SCANNING

Uploaded files should pass applicable security checks before becoming available for processing.

Potentially unsafe files should be isolated from normal processing.

END OF 22.45

### 22.46 DATA RETENTION

File retention must follow:

user settings

Project policy

Workspace policy

organization policy

legal/administrative requirements where applicable

Deletion of metadata and deletion of binary content must be coordinated according to the retention policy.

END OF 22.46

### 22.47 FILE DELETE FLOW

Delete Request

↓

Authorization

↓

Soft Delete

↓

Retention Policy

↓

Remove Index

↓

Remove Storage Object

Referenced research records must retain appropriate provenance or deletion state.

END OF 22.47

### 22.48 FILE EXPORT

Export may provide:

original file

metadata

processed text

document structure

citations

analysis results

The original file must remain distinguishable from generated derivatives.

END OF 22.48

### 22.49 DOCUMENT AI COST OPTIMIZATION

To maximize output at low cost:

- Extract text deterministically before using AI.

- Use rules and parsers for straightforward metadata.

- Use OCR only when necessary.

- Use small models for classification.

- Use retrieval before generation.

- Cache processed documents.

- Avoid reprocessing unchanged files.

- Reuse existing embeddings/indexes.

- Use expensive multimodal models only when required.

- Process large files asynchronously.

END OF 22.49

### 22.50 DOCUMENT AI HALLUCINATION CONTROL

The system shall reduce hallucination through:

source-grounded retrieval

page-level provenance

citation requirements

structured extraction

evidence-first prompting

claim/evidence separation

uncertainty indicators

validation

source conflict detection

The AI must be allowed to state that evidence is insufficient.

END OF 22.50

### 22.51 DOCUMENT PROMPT-INJECTION PROTECTION

Documents must be treated as untrusted data.

Example:

Scientific Paper

↓

Extracted Content

↓

UNTRUSTED DOCUMENT DATA

↓

Context Isolation

↓

AI

Instructions contained inside a document must not override system or developer instructions.

END OF 22.51

### 22.52 DOCUMENT SEARCH SECURITY

Search must apply authorization before results are provided to the AI.

Incorrect:

Search Everything

↓

AI

↓

Permission Check

Correct:

User Query

↓

Permission Scope

↓

Search Authorized Documents

↓

Rank

↓

AI

END OF 22.52

versioning

PDF processing
