### 22.61 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 22 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Users can securely upload supported files.

- Files receive stable IDs.

- File metadata is persisted.

- Binary files are stored outside the relational database.

- File permissions are enforced server-side.

- Files can be associated with Projects.

- Files can be associated with Chats.

- Files can be associated with Notes.

- Files support controlled versioning.

- Documents are processed asynchronously.

- PDF text extraction works.

- OCR works where required.

- Document structure is preserved.

- Tables are represented separately where possible.

- Figures remain traceable.

- Equations remain traceable.

- Document metadata is extracted.

- Document chunks retain provenance.

- Search supports authorized document retrieval.

- Hybrid retrieval is supported.

- Document AI answers are grounded in retrieved evidence.

- Citations can point back to document locations.

- AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from source content.

- Documents cannot override system instructions.

- Unauthorized documents cannot enter AI context.

- Large files can be processed asynchronously.

- Processing failures are recoverable.

- File deletion follows retention rules.

- Document processing avoids unnecessary AI usage.

- File APIs follow the common GSIR response architecture.

- File operations are observable.

- Automated tests cover the complete file/document lifecycle.

- The subsystem integrates correctly with Chat, Projects, Notes, Search, Knowledge, Research and AI Gateway.

END OF PART 22

PART 22 COMPLETED.

## PART 23 — KNOWLEDGE GRAPH, SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE BASE AND EVIDENCE MANAGEMENT ARCHITECTURE

### 23.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Knowledge System shall transform validated information from research papers, uploaded documents, datasets, experiments, laboratory records, trusted web sources and user-created research material into a structured, traceable and continuously expandable scientific knowledge system.

The Knowledge System is not a simple vector database.

It shall combine:

- Structured entities

- Relationships

- Documents

- Evidence

- Claims

- Citations

- Scientific concepts

- Research findings

- Experimental observations

- Datasets

- Methods

- Materials

- Instruments

- Organizations

- Researchers

- Knowledge versions

- Confidence

- Provenance

The purpose is to allow GSIR to understand relationships between scientific information rather than treating every document as an isolated text source.

END OF 23.1

### 23.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR must distinguish between:

SOURCE

↓

EXTRACTED INFORMATION

↓

CLAIM

↓

EVIDENCE

↓

VALIDATION

↓

KNOWLEDGE

A statement extracted from a paper must not automatically become trusted knowledge.

END OF 23.2

### 23.3 KNOWLEDGE ARCHITECTURE

                         GSIR KNOWLEDGE SYSTEM

                                  │

          ┌───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐

          │                       │                        │

       Sources                 Claims                  Entities

          │                       │                        │

     Papers/Files          Scientific Statements     Molecules

     Websites              Findings                  Genes

     Datasets              Observations              Proteins

     Experiments           Hypotheses                Materials

          │                       │                        │

          └───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┘

                                  │

                              Evidence

                                  │

                           Validation Layer

                                  │

                         Knowledge Graph

                                  │

                         Retrieval System

                                  │

                              AI System

END OF 23.3

### 23.4 KNOWLEDGE OBJECT TYPES

The initial knowledge model shall support:

Source

Document

Claim

Evidence

Entity

Concept

Method

Experiment

Observation

Dataset

Finding

Hypothesis

Research Question

Citation

Relationship

Knowledge Record

The architecture must allow additional types in future.

END OF 23.4

### 23.5 SCIENTIFIC ENTITY TYPES

Examples:

Molecule

Chemical

Compound

Protein

Gene

RNA

DNA

Cell

Organism

Species

Tissue

Disease

Material

Polymer

Nanomaterial

Reaction

Pathway

Enzyme

Instrument

Technique

Method

Process

Property

Parameter

Unit

Organization

Researcher

Laboratory

Publication

Dataset

These are extensible categories rather than a fixed permanent list.

END OF 23.5

### 23.6 ENTITY IDENTIFIER

Every knowledge entity shall have a stable identifier.

Recommended format:

entity_<unique_identifier>

The identifier must remain stable even when the entity receives additional information.

END OF 23.6

### 23.7 ENTITY CANONICAL NAME

Every entity should have:

entity_id

entity_type

canonical_name

aliases

description

external_identifiers

metadata

created_at

updated_at

END OF 23.7

### 23.8 ENTITY ALIASES

Scientific entities frequently have multiple names.

Example:

Canonical:

Acetylsalicylic acid

Aliases:

Aspirin

2-acetoxybenzoic acid

ASA

The search system should recognize aliases while preserving one canonical entity where appropriate.

END OF 23.8

### 23.9 EXTERNAL IDENTIFIERS

Where applicable, entities may reference external identifiers such as:

DOI

CAS number

PubChem identifier

UniProt identifier

Gene identifiers

Taxonomic identifiers

Other recognized scientific identifiers

External identifiers must be stored as references and not treated as proof of scientific validity.

END OF 23.9

### 23.10 RELATIONSHIP MODEL

Knowledge relationships shall be represented explicitly.

Examples:

Compound

↓ inhibits

Enzyme

Gene

↓ encodes

Protein

Protein

↓ participates_in

Pathway

Material

↓ has_property

Property

Paper

↓ reports

Finding

Finding

↓ supported_by

Evidence

Experiment

↓ produces

Observation

END OF 23.10

### 23.11 RELATIONSHIP IDENTIFIER

Every relationship should have:

relationship_id

source_entity_id

relationship_type

target_entity_id

provenance

confidence

status

created_at

updated_at

END OF 23.11

### 23.12 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH

The primary conceptual graph is:

ENTITY

   │

   ├── RELATIONSHIP ──→ ENTITY

   │

   └── supported_by ──→ EVIDENCE

                              │

                              ↓

                           SOURCE

This graph allows GSIR to answer relationship-based questions rather than only similarity-based questions.

END OF 23.12

### 23.13 CLAIM MODEL

A scientific claim is a statement that can be supported, contradicted or remain uncertain.

Example:

Claim:

Compound X inhibits Enzyme Y.

Evidence:

Paper A, Page 7, Figure 3.

Status:

Supported

Confidence:

0.91

The confidence value must not be presented as an absolute scientific probability unless its statistical meaning is explicitly defined.

END OF 23.13

### 23.14 CLAIM IDENTIFIER

Every claim should receive:

claim_<unique_identifier>

A claim must retain its provenance.

END OF 23.14

### 23.15 CLAIM STATUS

Initial statuses:

EXTRACTED

UNVERIFIED

SUPPORTED

PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED

CONTRADICTED

UNCERTAIN

VALIDATED

REJECTED

SUPERSEDED

END OF 23.15

### 23.16 EVIDENCE MODEL

Evidence must be represented separately from claims.

Evidence may originate from:

- Research papers

- Experimental data

- Laboratory observations

- Datasets

- Official scientific databases

- Trusted web sources

- User-provided information

- Instrument outputs

END OF 23.16

### 23.17 EVIDENCE IDENTIFIER

Every evidence object shall have:

evidence_<unique_identifier>

END OF 23.17

### 23.18 EVIDENCE STRUCTURE

Minimum fields:

evidence_id

source_id

claim_id

evidence_type

content_reference

location

extraction_method

confidence

validation_status

created_at

END OF 23.18

### 23.19 SOURCE HIERARCHY

GSIR should distinguish source classes.

Example:

Primary Research

↓

Peer-Reviewed Literature

↓

Official Scientific Database

↓

Institutional/Technical Source

↓

Secondary Literature

↓

General Web Source

↓

User-Provided Unverified Information

This hierarchy must not automatically determine truth.

It is an input into evidence evaluation.

END OF 23.19

### 23.20 SOURCE QUALITY

Source quality may consider:

- provenance

- publication status

- recency

- methodological quality

- reproducibility

- citation information

- conflicts

- retraction status where available

- agreement with independent sources

GSIR must avoid reducing scientific quality to a single simplistic score.

END OF 23.20

### 23.21 CONTRADICTORY EVIDENCE

The knowledge system must support disagreement.

Example:

Claim A

├── Evidence 1 → supports

├── Evidence 2 → supports

├── Evidence 3 → contradicts

└── Evidence 4 → uncertain

The AI must not silently select only supporting evidence.

END OF 23.21

### 23.22 CONFLICT DETECTION

When sources disagree, GSIR should identify:

CONFLICT DETECTED

↓

Claims compared

↓

Evidence compared

↓

Methods compared

↓

Population/sample compared

↓

Conditions compared

↓

Publication dates compared

↓

Possible explanation

The system should present the disagreement to the user.

END OF 23.22

### 23.23 KNOWLEDGE VERSIONING

Knowledge records must support versioning.

Example:

Knowledge Record

├── Version 1

├── Version 2

├── Version 3

└── Current Version

Previous versions must remain traceable.

END OF 23.23

### 23.24 KNOWLEDGE PROVENANCE

Every important knowledge statement should answer:

Where did this information come from?

Which source supports it?

Which part of the source supports it?

When was it extracted?

Was it validated?

What evidence contradicts it?

END OF 23.24

### 23.25 KNOWLEDGE INGESTION PIPELINE

Source

↓

Ingestion

↓

Parsing

↓

Extraction

↓

Entity Recognition

↓

Relationship Extraction

↓

Claim Extraction

↓

Evidence Linking

↓

Normalization

↓

Deduplication

↓

Validation

↓

Knowledge Graph

↓

Search Index

END OF 23.25

### 23.26 ENTITY RECOGNITION

Document AI should identify scientific entities.

Example:

"The compound reduced expression of Gene X."

↓

Compound → Entity

Gene X → Entity

reduced expression → Relationship/Claim

The extracted entities must remain linked to the originating document.

END OF 23.26

### 23.27 ENTITY NORMALIZATION

Different mentions referring to the same scientific entity should be normalized when confidence is sufficient.

The system must not merge entities solely because their names look similar.

Potential ambiguity must remain unresolved until sufficient evidence exists.

END OF 23.27

### 23.28 ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION

Example:

"ATP"

may require contextual interpretation.

The system should use:

document context

scientific field

surrounding entities

definitions

external identifiers

to determine the intended meaning.

END OF 23.28

### 23.29 RELATIONSHIP EXTRACTION

Relationships should be extracted only when supported by source context.

The system must distinguish:

Explicit relationship

Inferred relationship

Hypothesized relationship

Unknown relationship

These must never be treated as equivalent.

END OF 23.29

### 23.30 INFERENCE LAYER

GSIR may derive new relationships through reasoning.

Example:

Fact A

+

Fact B

↓

Logical inference

↓

Candidate relationship

Derived knowledge must be marked as inferred rather than directly observed.

END OF 23.30

### 23.31 INFERENCE PROVENANCE

Every inference should retain:

input facts

reasoning method

rules/model used

timestamp

confidence/uncertainty

result

The system must allow the inference to be inspected.

END OF 23.31

### 23.32 HYPOTHESIS MODEL

GSIR shall support hypotheses as separate objects.

A hypothesis is not established knowledge.

Structure:

Hypothesis

↓

Supporting Evidence

↓

Contradicting Evidence

↓

Predictions

↓

Experimental Tests

↓

Result

END OF 23.32

### 23.33 RESEARCH QUESTION CONNECTION

Knowledge must connect to research questions.

Research Question

↓

Relevant Entities

↓

Existing Knowledge

↓

Evidence

↓

Knowledge Gaps

↓

Potential Hypotheses

END OF 23.33

### 23.34 KNOWLEDGE GAP DETECTION

GSIR may identify possible gaps by comparing:

existing claims

research questions

contradictory evidence

missing relationships

understudied entities

insufficient evidence

The system must label these as candidate gaps rather than guaranteed discoveries.

END OF 23.34

### 23.35 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH SEARCH

Users should be able to ask:

What is known about X?

What compounds interact with X?

Which papers support this relationship?

Which evidence contradicts it?

Which methods have been used?

What research gaps exist?

The system should combine graph retrieval with document retrieval.

END OF 23.35

### 23.36 GRAPH + VECTOR + KEYWORD ARCHITECTURE

GSIR should not depend on one retrieval method.

                 Query

                   │

       ┌───────────┼───────────┐

       ↓           ↓           ↓

   Keyword      Vector       Graph

   Search       Search       Search

       │           │           │

       └───────────┼───────────┘

                   ↓

              Result Fusion

                   ↓

                Ranking

                   ↓

                Evidence

END OF 23.36

### 23.37 RETRIEVAL RANKING

Ranking may consider:

semantic relevance

keyword relevance

graph relevance

source quality

evidence strength

recency

user/project context

authorization

document provenance

The ranking system must not hide important contradictory evidence merely because it has a lower similarity score.

END OF 23.37

### 23.38 KNOWLEDGE CONTEXT FOR AI

The AI system should receive structured context:

Question

↓

Relevant Entities

↓

Relevant Claims

↓

Relevant Evidence

↓

Source Documents

↓

Contradictions

↓

Uncertainty

↓

User/Project Context

↓

AI Reasoning

END OF 23.38

### 23.39 AI KNOWLEDGE RESPONSE

Scientific responses should preferably follow:

Answer

↓

Evidence

↓

Reasoning

↓

Uncertainty

↓

Sources

The exact presentation may depend on the user-selected response mode.

END OF 23.39

### 23.40 HALLUCINATION CONTROL

The Knowledge System must reduce hallucinations by:

- Retrieving evidence before generation.

- Linking claims to sources.

- Distinguishing facts from inference.

- Detecting contradictory evidence.

- Requiring citations for source-derived claims.

- Allowing insufficient-evidence responses.

- Preventing unsupported graph relationships from being treated as facts.

- Keeping AI-generated information separate from validated knowledge.

END OF 23.40

### 23.41 USER-CREATED KNOWLEDGE

Users may create:

claims

notes

hypotheses

observations

relationships

research conclusions

These must be labeled as user-created information.

They must not automatically become globally trusted knowledge.

END OF 23.41

### 23.42 PROJECT KNOWLEDGE

Every Project may maintain a private knowledge scope.

Project

├── Sources

├── Claims

├── Evidence

├── Entities

├── Hypotheses

├── Experiments

└── Findings

Project knowledge may be used by the project's AI context.

END OF 23.42

### 23.43 ORGANIZATIONAL KNOWLEDGE

Future GSIR organizations may maintain shared knowledge.

Access control must support:

USER

TEAM

PROJECT

ORGANIZATION

GLOBAL/PUBLIC

The scope must be explicit.

END OF 23.43

### 23.44 KNOWLEDGE ACCESS CONTROL

Every knowledge object must inherit or explicitly define an authorization scope.

The AI must never retrieve knowledge outside the current user's authorized scope.

END OF 23.44

### 23.45 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH SECURITY

Graph traversal must enforce permissions.

Incorrect:

User

↓

Graph

↓

Filter unauthorized results

Correct:

User

↓

Authorization Scope

↓

Graph Traversal

↓

Authorized Nodes/Edges

↓

Results

END OF 23.45

### 23.46 KNOWLEDGE API

Primary endpoints:

POST   /api/v1/knowledge/entities

GET    /api/v1/knowledge/entities/{entity_id}

PATCH  /api/v1/knowledge/entities/{entity_id}

POST   /api/v1/knowledge/claims

GET    /api/v1/knowledge/claims/{claim_id}

PATCH  /api/v1/knowledge/claims/{claim_id}

### 23.60 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 23 shall be considered implemented only when:

- Scientific entities can be represented.

- Entities have stable identifiers.

- Aliases are supported.

- External identifiers can be stored.

- Relationships are explicitly represented.

- Claims are separate from evidence.

- Evidence is separate from claims.

- Sources retain provenance.

- Claims have validation states.

- Contradictory evidence can be represented.

- Knowledge versions are supported.

- User knowledge is distinguishable from validated/global knowledge.

- Project knowledge is supported.

- Knowledge access control is enforced.

- Graph traversal respects permissions.

- Keyword retrieval is supported.

- Semantic retrieval is supported.

- Graph retrieval is supported.

- Hybrid retrieval is supported.

- AI context can contain structured knowledge.

- AI-generated inference is distinguishable from source evidence.

- Inferences retain provenance.

- Hypotheses remain separate from established knowledge.

- Research questions can connect to knowledge.

- Candidate knowledge gaps can be represented.

- Source conflicts can be detected and displayed.

- Knowledge can be incrementally updated.

- Source deletion does not corrupt unrelated provenance.

- Vector indexes are not treated as authoritative truth.

- The subsystem is horizontally scalable.

- The subsystem is observable.

- Automated tests cover the complete knowledge lifecycle.

- The subsystem integrates correctly with Files, Documents, Search, Projects, Research, AI Gateway, Chat and future Laboratory/Experiment systems.

## PART 24 — SCIENTIFIC DOCUMENT INTELLIGENCE, PAPER INGESTION, EXTRACTION, ANALYSIS AND RESEARCH-PAPER WORKFLOW

### 24.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a complete scientific-document intelligence system for discovering, importing, reading, understanding, extracting, comparing, validating, citing and continuously connecting research papers and other scientific documents to the GSIR Knowledge System.

The document system shall not behave as a basic PDF reader or document chatbot.

It shall convert scientific documents into structured, traceable research information while preserving the original document, exact evidence locations, document structure, citations, figures, tables, equations, numerical results and uncertainty.

This architecture is based on the principle that scientific AI requires both broad literature-level knowledge and fine-grained within-document understanding, with provenance connecting extracted claims to their evidential roots. 

END OF 24.1

The system shall support the complete workflow:

↓

STRUCTURE

↓

↓

END OF 24.2

### 24.80 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- Scientific documents can be uploaded.

- Document summaries can be generated.

- Literature gaps can be identified as candidate gaps.

- Documents can be searched hierarchically.

- Document chat is supported.

- Project document context is supported.

- Citations are validated before presentation.

- Document permissions are enforced.

- Document prompt injection is isolated.

- Document processing is asynchronous.

- Processing failures can be retried.

- Processing versions are auditable.

- Human review is supported.

- Document-derived knowledge connects to Part 23 Knowledge Architecture.

- Document retrieval connects to the AI Gateway.

- Document access connects to Projects.

- Document evidence can become Notes.

- Future laboratory data can enter the same architecture.

- Processing uses model escalation for cost efficiency.

- Extraction quality is measurable.

- Retrieval quality is measurable.

- AI grounding is measurable.

- Security testing is implemented.

- Performance testing is implemented.

- The complete document lifecycle is automated and observable.

END OF PART 24

PART 24 COMPLETED.

## PART 25 — SCIENTIFIC AGENT ORCHESTRATION, REASONING ENGINE AND AUTONOMOUS RESEARCH WORKFLOW

### 25.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall contain a modular Scientific Agent Orchestration System capable of coordinating specialized AI agents, scientific knowledge, research papers, mathematical reasoning, simulations, data analysis, experiments and, in future phases, laboratory instruments.

The system shall not depend on one general-purpose AI agent for every task.

Instead, GSIR shall use a controlled orchestration architecture in which specialized agents perform specific responsibilities while a central research orchestrator controls task decomposition, evidence requirements, tool permissions, validation, reasoning state, cost, execution order and final synthesis.

Recent scientific-agent research demonstrates the movement toward multi-agent systems that combine literature search, hypothesis generation, experimental planning, data analysis and iterative refinement. 

GSIR shall therefore be designed from the beginning as an extensible Scientific Operating System rather than as a chatbot with additional tools.

END OF 25.1

### 25.2 CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLE

The central principle shall be:

USER

↓

RESEARCH OBJECTIVE

↓

SCIENTIFIC ORCHESTRATOR

↓

TASK DECOMPOSITION

↓

SPECIALIZED AGENTS

↓

TOOLS + KNOWLEDGE + DATA

↓

EVIDENCE + REASONING

↓

VALIDATION

↓

SYNTHESIS

↓

USER

For physical laboratory execution:

USER

↓

RESEARCH OBJECTIVE

↓

SCIENTIFIC ORCHESTRATOR

↓

HYPOTHESIS

↓

EXPERIMENT DESIGN

↓

SAFETY VALIDATION

↓

HUMAN APPROVAL

↓

LAB ORCHESTRATOR

↓

INSTRUMENTS / ROBOTS

↓

MEASUREMENTS

↓

DATA ANALYSIS

↓

RESULT VALIDATION

↓

UPDATED KNOWLEDGE

↓

NEXT RESEARCH ACTION

The physical execution loop shall remain disabled unless the required laboratory permissions, safety controls and human-approval policies are satisfied.

END OF 25.2

### 25.3 WHY GSIR SHALL USE MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION

A single model has to simultaneously perform:

Research interpretation

Literature retrieval

Scientific reasoning

Mathematics

Planning

Coding

Data analysis

Critical evaluation

Citation

Tool selection

Safety checking

This creates unnecessary complexity and increases the probability of unsupported reasoning.

GSIR shall instead divide responsibilities.

Example:

Research Director Agent

        │

        ├── Literature Agent

        ├── Knowledge Agent

        ├── Hypothesis Agent

        ├── Experiment Agent

        ├── Mathematics Agent

        ├── Data Analysis Agent

        ├── Simulation Agent

        ├── Critical Review Agent

        ├── Evidence Agent

        ├── Safety Agent

        └── Synthesis Agent

Each agent shall have a clearly defined capability boundary.

END OF 25.3

### 25.4 AGENT HIERARCHY

GSIR shall use a hierarchical architecture.

LEVEL 0

User

LEVEL 1

Research Director

LEVEL 2

Domain/Task Managers

LEVEL 3

Specialized Scientific Agents

LEVEL 4

Tools and Computational Services

LEVEL 5

External Systems / Laboratory Equipment

Example:

Research Director

│

├── Chemistry Manager

│   ├── Literature Agent

│   ├── Reaction Analysis Agent

│   ├── Materials Agent

│   └── Chemistry Safety Agent

│

├── Biology Manager

│   ├── Literature Agent

│   ├── Molecular Biology Agent

│   ├── Bioinformatics Agent

│   └── Biology Safety Agent

│

└── Data Science Manager

    ├── Statistics Agent

    ├── ML Agent

    ├── Visualization Agent

    └── Validation Agent

The architecture must allow new domain managers to be added without modifying the core orchestration engine.

END OF 25.4

### 25.5 RESEARCH DIRECTOR AGENT

The Research Director Agent is responsible for coordinating a complete research task.

It shall:

Understand objective

Identify constraints

Determine required capabilities

Create research plan

Assign subtasks

Select agents

Select tools

Monitor execution

Detect conflicts

Request validation

Manage uncertainty

Request human approval when required

Synthesize results

Generate final research output

It shall not directly perform unrestricted laboratory actions.

END OF 25.5

### 25.15 LOW-COST REASONING STRATEGY

GSIR shall use progressive escalation.

Deterministic / cached solution

Stage 2

Retrieval + small model

↓ if insufficient

Stage 3

Specialized model






↓ if insufficient

Stage 4

High-capability reasoning model

↓ if uncertainty remains

Stage 5

Human review

This prevents expensive models from being used unnecessarily.

END OF 25.15

+

### 25.33 CRITICAL REVIEW AGENT

The Critical Review Agent shall challenge research outputs.

It should ask:

What evidence supports this?

What evidence contradicts it?

What assumptions were made?

What information is missing?

Could another explanation fit the data?

Was the method appropriate?

Is the sample sufficient?

Could measurement error explain the result?

Is the conclusion stronger than the evidence?

END OF 25.33

### 25.34 RED-TEAM RESEARCH AGENT

↓

↓

↓

Alternative Explanations

↓

Evidence Check

↓

Conclusion Revision

END OF 25.34

### 25.35 SCIENTIFIC CONSENSUS AGENT

Analysis B

Analysis C

      ↓

      ↓

Uncertainty

      ↓

### 25.36 RESEARCH MEMORY

+

+

## PART 26 — SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE FABRIC, EVIDENCE GRAPH, RESEARCH MEMORY AND PROVENANCE ARCHITECTURE

### 26.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall implement a unified Scientific Knowledge Fabric that connects scientific documents, papers, authors, institutions, datasets, experiments, measurements, hypotheses, methods, equations, claims, citations, results, instruments and user-created research knowledge.

The purpose is to prevent GSIR from behaving like a conventional vector-search chatbot.

The system shall instead maintain a continuously queryable representation of:

WHAT IS KNOWN

WHAT IS CLAIMED

WHO CLAIMED IT

WHERE IT WAS PUBLISHED

WHAT EVIDENCE SUPPORTS IT

WHAT EVIDENCE CONTRADICTS IT

HOW STRONG THE EVIDENCE IS

WHAT WAS EXPERIMENTALLY OBSERVED

WHAT GSIR INFERRED

WHAT REMAINS UNKNOWN

Recent scientific-agent research identifies scientific memory, verification and traceability as major limitations of current autonomous research systems. GSIR shall therefore treat provenance and verification as first-class architecture rather than adding them later. 

END OF 26.1

### 26.2 CORE ARCHITECTURE

The Scientific Knowledge Fabric shall use multiple complementary storage and reasoning mechanisms.

                    GSIR KNOWLEDGE FABRIC

                            │

       ┌────────────────────┼────────────────────┐

       │                    │                    │

   DOCUMENT STORE       KNOWLEDGE GRAPH      VECTOR INDEX

       │                    │                    │

 Papers                Entities              Embeddings

 PDFs                  Claims                Semantic Search

 Notes                 Relations             Similarity

 Datasets              Evidence              Retrieval

       │                    │                    │

       └────────────────────┼────────────────────┘

                            │

                    RESEARCH MEMORY

                            │

                  ┌─────────┴─────────┐

                  │                   │

             Evidence State      Research State

                  │                   │

                  └─────────┬─────────┘

                            │

                       AI REASONING

No single database technology shall be treated as the complete scientific knowledge layer.

END OF 26.2

### 26.3 KNOWLEDGE LAYERS

GSIR shall separate knowledge into the following layers:

Layer 1 — Raw Source

Layer 2 — Extracted Content

Layer 3 — Structured Facts

Layer 4 — Claims

Layer 5 — Evidence

Layer 6 — Relationships

Layer 7 — Research State

Layer 8 — Derived Knowledge

Layer 9 — Validated Knowledge

Layer 10 — User/Project Knowledge

Each layer must preserve its relationship with the previous layer.

END OF 26.3

### 26.4 RAW SOURCE LAYER

The Raw Source Layer contains immutable source material.

Examples:

Research Paper

PDF

Supplementary Material

Dataset

Experimental File

Instrument Export

Image

Spreadsheet

CSV

Notebook

Code Repository

Web Source

Patent

Technical Standard

Protocol

User Document

Raw sources shall be stored with integrity metadata.

Minimum metadata:

source_id

content_hash

mime_type

size

created_at

source_type

origin

owner

project_id

END OF 26.4

### 26.5 SOURCE IMMUTABILITY

Original scientific sources must never be silently overwritten.

If a document changes:

Original Version

      ↓

New Version

      ↓

Version Relationship

Both versions must remain identifiable.

This is essential for reproducibility.

END OF 26.5

### 26.6 DOCUMENT REPRESENTATION

Every scientific document shall have a structured representation.

Document

├── document_id

├── title

├── document_type

├── authors

├── organizations

├── publication

├── publication_date

├── identifiers

├── abstract

├── sections

├── references

├── extracted_entities

├── extracted_claims

├── embeddings

├── source_metadata

├── version

└── provenance

END OF 26.6

Examples:

PMID

ISBN

Internal GSIR ID

Identifiers shall not be replaced by GSIR-generated identifiers.

GSIR IDs shall provide internal linkage while external identifiers remain preserved.

END OF 26.7

### 26.8 DOCUMENT CHUNKING

Documents shall not be split into arbitrary fixed-size chunks only.

Chunking shall consider scientific structure.

Document

↓

↓

↓

↓

↓

Equation

↓

Table

↓

Figure

↓

Caption

The retrieval system should preserve structural relationships.

END OF 26.8

A retrieved chunk shall carry contextual metadata:

├── statistical_strength

├── independence

├── consistency

├── recency

├── directness

└── confidence

A single numerical confidence score shall not replace the underlying evidence attributes.

END OF 26.13

### 26.14 SUPPORTING AND CONTRADICTING EVIDENCE

The knowledge system shall explicitly represent both.

Claim A

│

├── SUPPORTS

│   ├── Evidence 1

│   └── Evidence 2

│

└── CONTRADICTS

    ├── Evidence 3

    └── Evidence 4

This is required for scientifically responsible reasoning.

END OF 26.14

The Knowledge Graph shall represent scientific entities and relationships.

   │

   │

   ├── SUPPORTED_BY → Paper A

   │

   │

REPLICATES

EXTENDS

IMPROVES

DEPENDS_ON

### 26.18 TEMPORAL KNOWLEDGE

Scientific knowledge changes.

GSIR shall therefore support temporal validity.

Example:

Claim A

Valid From: 2022

Status: Supported

New Evidence

2026

Claim A

Status: Re-evaluated

The system must not delete historical knowledge merely because newer evidence exists.

Current context

Temporary decisions

### 26.77 PART 26 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 26 shall be considered complete only when:

- Raw scientific sources are immutable and versioned.

- Documents have structured representations.

- Document structure is preserved during chunking.

- Scientific claims can be extracted.

- Claims have provenance.

- Claims can have supporting evidence.

- Claims can have contradicting evidence.

- Evidence quality is structured.

- Scientific entities are represented.

- Scientific relationships are represented.

- Knowledge is versioned.

- Knowledge has temporal state.

- Research memory is separated from global knowledge.

- User memory is separated from research memory.

- Project memory is isolated.

- Experiment memory is persistent.

- Failed approaches can be retained.

- Provenance is represented as a graph.

- AI-generated content has provenance.

- Human contributions have provenance.

- Answers can be traced to evidence.

- Citation validation exists.

- Hybrid retrieval exists.

- Vector retrieval exists.

- Graph retrieval exists.

- Metadata retrieval exists.

- Citation retrieval exists.

- Retrieval results can be fused and reranked.

- Multi-hop retrieval is supported.

- Conflicting scientific claims are preserved.

- Uncertainty is explicitly represented.

- Facts and inference are separated.

- Knowledge write gates exist.

- Entity resolution exists.

- Knowledge deduplication exists.

- Knowledge freshness is tracked.

- Global and project knowledge are separated.

- Tenant isolation is enforced.

- PostgreSQL is the transactional source of truth for core metadata.

- Large source files use object storage.

- Vector indexing is separate from transactional storage.

- Graph storage is separately abstracted.

- Search infrastructure is separately abstracted.

- Memory modules are modular.

- Provenance modules are modular.

- Retrieval modules are modular.

- Frontend evidence navigation exists.

- Research graph visualization is supported by the architecture.

- Reproducibility packages are supported.

- Scientific audit trails are maintained.

- Context construction is dynamic.

- Full databases are never blindly injected into model context.

- Evidence-grounded generation is implemented.

- Hallucination reduction is architectural.

- Scientific answer validation exists.

- Future AI Scientist systems can consume the Knowledge Fabric.

- Future laboratory systems can consume the same scientific state.

- The entire knowledge layer remains replaceable and extensible.

END OF PART 26

## PART 27 — SCIENTIFIC DATA ENGINE, DATASET MANAGEMENT, EXPERIMENTAL DATA PIPELINE AND COMPUTATIONAL WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

### 27.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a unified scientific data engine capable of receiving, storing, validating, transforming, analyzing, versioning and connecting scientific data with research questions, experiments, instruments, AI reasoning and final results.

The data engine shall support both:

UNSTRUCTURED DATA

+

SEMI-STRUCTURED DATA

+

STRUCTURED DATA

+

TIME-SERIES DATA

+

SCIENTIFIC MEASUREMENTS

+

EXPERIMENTAL DATA

+

INSTRUMENT DATA

+

COMPUTATIONAL RESULTS

+

AI-GENERATED DERIVED DATA

The architecture shall be designed from the beginning for future laboratory equipment connectivity and large-scale scientific computing.

Scientific reproducibility requires the ability to preserve the relationship between data, software, execution environment, parameters and generated results. GSIR shall therefore treat data provenance and computational workflow metadata as fundamental data rather than optional logging. 

END OF 27.1

### 27.2 DATA ENGINE PRINCIPLE

The GSIR data engine shall follow this fundamental rule:

RAW DATA MUST NEVER BE DESTROYED BY PROCESSING.

Instead:

Raw Data

    ↓

Validated Data

    ↓

Processed Data

    ↓

Analyzed Data

    ↓

Derived Result

    ↓

Scientific Conclusion

Each stage shall remain traceable to its input.

END OF 27.2

### 27.3 DATA OBJECT MODEL

Every important scientific data object shall have a unique internal identity.

├── data_id

├── dataset_id

├── organization_id

├── provenance_id

├── validation_status

└── access_policy

END OF 27.3

             ↓

          Step 2 ───── Input B

             ↓

          Step 3

          ↙    ↘

     Result A   Result B

+

+

### 27.93 DISASTER RECOVERY

The system shall define:

RPO — Recovery Point Objective

RTO — Recovery Time Objective

Critical research data shall receive stronger recovery guarantees than temporary cache data.

END OF 27.93

### 27.94 DATA COST OPTIMIZATION

To maintain high output at low cost:

Cold Storage

Compression

Deduplication

Chunked Processing

Caching

Incremental Processing

Materialized Results

Columnar Formats

Lazy Loading

Resource-aware Scheduling

shall be used where appropriate.

END OF 27.94

### 27.95 AVOIDING UNNECESSARY AI COST

The data engine shall perform deterministic operations without an LLM whenever possible.

Examples:

Unit Conversion → Deterministic Engine

Filtering → Database

Sorting → Database

Aggregation → Database

Validation → Schema Engine

Statistics → Scientific Library

File Parsing → Parser

Duplicate Detection → Hashing / Algorithms

AI shall be used where reasoning or semantic interpretation is actually required.

END OF 27.95

### 27.96 DATA ENGINE AND 1-CRORE QUERY REQUIREMENT

The target architecture for extremely high request volume shall not mean that one server processes one crore queries.

The architecture shall scale horizontally:

Global Load Balancer

        ↓

API Gateway

        ↓

Multiple API Instances

        ↓

Cache / Query Router

        ↓

Distributed Services

        ↓

Databases / Search / Workers

Read-heavy operations shall use caching and replicas.

Heavy analytical operations shall be moved to asynchronous workers.

END OF 27.96

### 27.97 QUERY CLASSIFICATION

Every data request shall be classified:

FAST_READ

SEARCH

ANALYTICAL

LONG_RUNNING

STREAMING

BATCH

EXPORT

AI_RESEARCH

The router shall send each request to the appropriate execution path.

END OF 27.97

### 27.98 FAST PATH

Simple requests should use:

Cache

↓

Read Replica

↓

Minimal Service Logic

without invoking AI or heavy processing.

END OF 27.98

### 27.99 HEAVY PATH

Complex scientific computation shall use:

API

↓

Job Creation

↓

Queue

↓

Worker

↓

Workflow

↓

Result Store

↓

Notification

The API returns a job identifier rather than waiting indefinitely.

END OF 27.99

### 27.100 DATA ENGINE SUCCESS CRITERIA

Part 27 shall be considered complete only when:

- Scientific data has a unified object model.

- Datasets have explicit metadata.

- Dataset schemas are versioned.

- Data contracts are defined.

- Incoming data is validated.

- Invalid data is quarantined.

- Data integrity is checked.

- Raw data is preserved.

- Large files use object storage.

- Large datasets support streaming and partitioned processing.

- Scientific workflows are represented explicitly.

- Workflow tasks have states.

- Workflow retries are controlled.

- Workflow checkpoints exist.

- Workflow execution environments are recorded.

- Computational provenance is captured.

- Data lineage is maintained.

- Dataset branching is supported.

- Dataset snapshots are supported.

- Instruments can eventually connect through adapters.

- Instrument data has a canonical representation.

- Units are machine-readable.

- Calibration can be represented.

- Samples have persistent identities.

- Sample lineage is maintained.

- Time-series data is supported.

- Streaming data architecture exists.

- Event-driven processing exists.

- Backpressure exists.

- Dead-letter handling exists.

- Data retention is configurable.

- Data access control exists.

- Data classification exists.

- AI cannot directly access unrestricted data.

- AI data queries are validated.

- Analysis runs through controlled tools.

- Computational execution can be sandboxed.

- Analysis results have provenance.

- Visualizations are reproducible objects.

- A searchable data catalog exists.

- Natural-language data queries can be translated into structured queries.

- Query execution is permission-controlled.

- Query caching is supported.

- Data modules are separated from AI modules.

- Workflow modules are independently scalable.

- Instrument modules are independent.

- Sample management is independent.

- Data APIs are versioned.

- Data processing is horizontally scalable.

- API servers remain stateless where possible.

- Long-running jobs do not block API servers.

- Workers are independently scalable.

- Indexes remain synchronized with dataset versions.

- Data observability exists.

- Data errors are structured.

- Data audit trails exist.

- FAIR principles are supported.

- Research software metadata and provenance are preserved.

- Data and software versions remain coupled.

- Workflows can be reused.

- AI Scientist can access the Data Engine through controlled tools.

- Future laboratory equipment can connect through the Instrument Gateway.

- AI cannot directly perform unrestricted physical operations.

- Human approval can be required for sensitive operations.

- Data security controls are enforced.

- Data corruption testing exists.

- Failure recovery is tested.

- Backup restoration is tested.

- Disaster recovery is defined.

- Data processing is cost optimized.

- Deterministic operations do not unnecessarily consume LLM resources.

- The architecture can scale horizontally toward extremely high query volumes.

- Fast and heavy query paths are separated.

- The entire data architecture remains modular and replaceable.

END OF PART 27

MASTER DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT

## PART 28 — LABORATORY INTELLIGENCE, EQUIPMENT REGISTRY, INSTRUMENT CONNECTIVITY AND LAB-AWARE RESEARCH ARCHITECTURE

### 28.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a laboratory intelligence layer that connects a user's real laboratory capabilities with the research, AI, data, experiment and knowledge systems.

The laboratory system shall allow GSIR to understand:

- Laboratory type

- Laboratory capability

- Available equipment

- Instrument specifications

- Instrument condition

- Calibration status

- Available techniques

- Available materials

- Existing data systems

- Staff capabilities

- Technical support

- Permissions

- Safety requirements

- Supplier information

- Data generated by instruments

The system shall use this information when preparing research plans, SOP-related workflows, experiment designs, equipment requirements and data-analysis workflows.

END OF 28.1

### 28.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall know the difference between:

WHAT THE RESEARCH REQUIRES

and

WHAT THE LABORATORY ACTUALLY HAS

The system shall never assume that an instrument, chemical, technique, staff capability or facility exists merely because it is commonly used for a particular experiment.

The laboratory registry shall be the authoritative source for known laboratory capabilities.

END OF 28.2

### 28.3 LABORATORY ARCHITECTURE

USER

↓

LABORATORY PROFILE

↓

CAPABILITY REGISTRY

↓

EQUIPMENT REGISTRY

↓

INSTRUMENT STATUS

↓

TECHNIQUE REGISTRY

↓

↓

↓

↓

EXPERIMENT / SOP / RESEARCH PLAN

END OF 28.3

### 28.4 LABORATORY HIERARCHY

↓

Laboratory

↓

Facility / Room

↓

Equipment

↓

Instrument

↓

↓

Measurement

↓

Dataset

↓

Every physical resource must have a clear ownership and location relationship.

END OF 28.4

            │   ├── useInstrument

            │   ├── useTechniques

            │   └── useLabFeasibility

            │

            ├── state/

            │   └── laboratoryStore

            │

            └── services/

                └── laboratoryApi

### 28.61 AI FEASIBILITY RESPONSE

When a user asks:

“Can my laboratory perform this experiment?”

the response should be structured as:

RESEARCH REQUIREMENT

REQUIRED TECHNIQUE

REQUIRED EQUIPMENT

AVAILABLE EQUIPMENT

MISSING EQUIPMENT

EQUIPMENT WITH UNKNOWN STATUS

AVAILABLE ALTERNATIVES

EXTERNAL FACILITY REQUIREMENT

DATA REQUIREMENTS

STAFF/EXPERTISE REQUIREMENTS

FEASIBILITY STATUS

LIMITATIONS

END OF 28.61

### 28.62 AI RESOURCE RESPONSE

When a user asks:

“What equipment do I need?”

GSIR shall provide:

Required Equipment

Purpose

Required Capability

Available in Lab

Alternative

External Requirement

Status

Source/Reason

It must not fabricate equipment specifications.

END OF 28.62

The Research Agent shall use the laboratory state while planning experiments.

Research Agent

↓

Research Requirement

↓

Laboratory Capability Query

↓

Available Resources

↓

Experiment Plan

Instrument

↓

Measurement

↓

Dataset

↓

Experiment

↓

Result

↓

Evidence

↓

Knowledge

The resulting knowledge must retain the complete provenance chain.

END OF 28.64

### 28.65 DATA ENGINE CONNECTION

Laboratory measurements shall enter the Data Engine.

Instrument

↓

Instrument Adapter

↓

Data Validation

↓

Dataset

↓

Data Engine

↓

Analysis

The laboratory module must not implement its own independent scientific data-processing platform.

END OF 28.65

### 28.66 AI GATEWAY CONNECTION

Laboratory Question

↓

Research Context

↓

Laboratory Context

↓

↓

Model Router

↓

Agent

↓

Response

### 28.67 SECURITY

The Laboratory subsystem must enforce:

Authentication

Authorization

Equipment Permissions

Data Permissions

Project Permissions

Instrument Permissions

Command Validation

Safety Policies

Audit Logging

Tenant Isolation

END OF 28.67

### 28.68 PHYSICAL ACTION SAFETY

AI-generated physical actions shall never be executed solely because an AI model produced them.

Required process:

AI Proposal

↓

Capability Check

↓

Parameter Validation

↓

Safety Validation

↓

Permission

↓

Human Approval if Required

↓

Controlled Execution

↓

Result Validation

END OF 28.68

### 28.69 FAILURE HANDLING

The laboratory system shall handle:

Instrument Offline

Connection Failure

Unexpected Measurement

Calibration Expired

Maintenance Required

Invalid Command

Permission Failure

Data Validation Failure

Partial Data

Instrument Error

Worker Failure

Failure must be recorded and must not be hidden from the research state.

END OF 28.69

### 28.70 OBSERVABILITY

Track:

Instrument Availability

Connection Errors

Command Count

Command Failures

Measurement Rate

Data Validation Failures

Calibration Status

Maintenance Status

Experiment State

Data Ingestion Latency

Sensitive instrument data must be handled according to its classification.

END OF 28.70

### 28.71 TESTING

Testing shall include:

Laboratory Creation

Equipment Registration

Equipment Status

Capability Mapping

Technique Mapping

Feasibility Analysis

Permission Checks

Calibration

Maintenance

Instrument Connectivity

Measurement Ingestion

Data Validation

Sample Tracking

Experiment Association

Command Validation

Approval

Abort

Failure Recovery

Audit

Physical equipment integrations must also be tested in a controlled test environment before production operation.

END OF 28.71

### 28.72 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 28 shall be considered complete only when:

- Laboratories can be registered.

- Laboratory types are supported.

- Laboratory capabilities can be recorded.

- Equipment can be registered.

- Equipment has stable identifiers.

- Equipment status can be tracked.

- Equipment capabilities can be represented.

- Calibration status can be recorded.

- Maintenance status can be recorded.

- Techniques can be registered.

- Techniques can map to equipment capabilities.

- Research requirements can be compared with laboratory capability.

- Missing equipment can be identified.

- Unknown equipment status remains unknown.

- Alternative equipment can be represented.

- Alternative techniques can be represented.

- External-facility requirements can be represented.

- Staff capabilities can be represented where required.

- Laboratory permissions are explicit.

- SOP workflows can use laboratory context.

- Laboratory data can enter the Data Engine.

- Instruments can eventually connect through adapters.

- Measurements have canonical representations.

- Raw instrument data is preserved.

- Instrument data retains provenance.

- Samples can be tracked.

- Sample lineage can be represented.

- Experiments connect to laboratory resources.

- AI can query laboratory capability through controlled tools.

- AI cannot directly access laboratory databases.

- AI cannot directly issue unrestricted hardware commands.

- Physical commands pass validation.

- Safety and permission checks exist.

- Human approval can be required.

- Executed hardware actions are auditable.

- Laboratory state is versioned or event-tracked.

- Equipment availability can be represented.

- Future instrument streaming is supported by the architecture.

- Laboratory and equipment data are permission-controlled.

- Laboratory functionality integrates correctly with Research, Projects, AI, Data, Knowledge, Experiments, Samples and Suppliers.

END OF PART 28

GSIR — GLOBAL SCIENTIFIC INTELLIGENT RESEARCH

MASTER DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT

PART 29 — SCIENTIFIC DATA PLATFORM, DATA INGESTION, DATA NORMALIZATION, DATA LINEAGE, DATASET MANAGEMENT AND RESEARCH DATA LIFECYCLE

29.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide a unified scientific data platform capable of receiving, storing, validating, transforming, indexing, analyzing and tracing data generated by:

Laboratory instruments

Connected equipment

Experiments

Samples

Manual data entry

Uploaded files

Research projects

External datasets

APIs

Computational pipelines

AI-generated analysis

Simulation systems

The data architecture shall be designed around scientific reproducibility, interoperability, provenance and controlled reuse.

Scientific research data should be designed to be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR), with persistent identifiers, rich metadata, controlled access and provenance. 

END OF 29.1

29.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall never treat a scientific file as merely an uploaded file.

Every research dataset shall be treated as a scientific object with:

Identity

Metadata

Source

Provenance

Schema

Version

Ownership

Permissions

Quality

Relationships

Processing History

END OF 29.2

29.3 SCIENTIFIC DATA LIFECYCLE

DATA SOURCE

↓

INGESTION

↓

RAW DATA

↓

METADATA EXTRACTION

↓

SCHEMA DETECTION

↓

VALIDATION

↓

NORMALIZATION

↓

DATASET REGISTRATION

↓

VERSIONING

↓

PROCESSING

↓

ANALYSIS

↓

RESULTS

↓

KNOWLEDGE

↓

REUSE / EXPORT / PUBLICATION

Every stage must be traceable.

END OF 29.3

29.4 DATA SOURCES

GSIR shall support:

Instrument Data

Sensor Data

CSV

TSV

JSON

XML

Parquet

Excel

Text

Scientific Documents

API Responses

Simulation Outputs

Manual Measurements

AI/ML Outputs

The architecture shall allow additional formats through modular adapters.

END OF 29.4

Created_at

Checksum

Format

Size

29.6 DATA INGESTION ARCHITECTURE

↓

Ingestion Gateway

↓

Source Adapter

↓

↓

↓

↓

↓

↓

END OF 29.6

29.7 INGESTION GATEWAY

The ingestion gateway shall be responsible for:

Authentication

Authorization

Upload Validation

Protocol Validation

File Identification

Checksum Generation

Rate Limiting

Size Limits

Virus/Malware Scanning

Duplicate Detection

Queue Submission

Audit Logging

It must not perform heavy scientific processing synchronously.

END OF 29.7

29.8 LARGE DATA INGESTION

Large scientific files must use asynchronous ingestion.

Client

↓

Upload Session

↓

Chunk Upload

↓

Object Storage

↓

Checksum Verification

↓

Ingestion Job

↓

Processing Queue

The API server must not keep large files in application memory.

Upload_id

Total_chunks

Uploaded_at

29.10 RAW DATA PRESERVATION

Original scientific data shall be preserved.

Raw Data

    ↓

Immutable / Protected Storage

    ↓

Processing Copies

Processing must never silently overwrite the original source.

END OF 29.10

29.11 RAW DATA STORAGE

Object storage shall be used for large binary or file-based scientific data.

The database shall store metadata and references rather than embedding large scientific files directly into relational tables.

END OF 29.11

29.13 DATASET IDENTIFIERS

├── Version 2

└── Current Version

When data enters GSIR:

Input

↓

Format Detection

↓

Schema Detection

↓

Known Schema?

├── YES → Validate

29.19 UNIT-AWARE DATA

Measurements must preserve units.

Example:

Value = 25

Unit = °C

Parameter = temperature

Must not be stored merely as:

Temperature = 25

The unit is part of the scientific meaning.

Example:

Input:

Normalized:

1 L

↓

↓

Relationship Validation

↓

Scientific Consistency Checks

29.22 VALIDATION STATES

PENDING

VALID

VALID_WITH_WARNINGS

INVALID

QUARANTINED

REJECTED

END OF 29.22

29.23 QUARANTINE

Incoming Data

↓

Validation

↓

Problem Detected

↓

Quarantine

↓

Review

├── Correct

├── Accept With Warning

└── Reject

29.24 DATA QUALITY

Every dataset shall have quality metadata.

Example:

Consistency

29.25 DATA QUALITY SCORE

A quality score may be calculated internally, but it must never be presented as absolute scientific truth.

The system should expose the reasons behind a quality assessment.

Example:

Quality: WARNING

Reasons:

- 4.2% missing measurements

- Calibration record unavailable

- 12 values outside expected range

END OF 29.25

29.26 MISSING VALUES

Missing values must remain distinguishable from:

ZERO

NOT APPLICABLE

NOT MEASURED

UNKNOWN

FAILED MEASUREMENT

WITHHELD

The system must not convert missing values to zero automatically.

END OF 29.26

    ↓

29.34 DATA LINEAGE

Every derived result must answer:

Where did this data come from?

Which instrument produced it?

Which sample was used?

Which experiment produced it?

Which processing pipeline modified it?

Which code version processed it?

Which model analyzed it?

Which user initiated it?

END OF 29.34

29.35 SCIENTIFIC TRACE

GSIR shall preserve three interconnected traces:

SAMPLE TRACE

+

INSTRUMENT TRACE

+

DECISION TRACE

These shall connect to the experiment and dataset lineage.

This extends ordinary file provenance into an experiment-level history of samples, instrument state and research decisions. Recent research has proposed recording such synchronized traces for autonomous experimentation and reproducibility. 

END OF 29.35

29.36 SAMPLE TRACE

Sample Created

↓

Sample Prepared

↓

Sample Modified

↓

↓

Sample Stored

↓

↓

Error

↓

Dataset Identification

29.50 AI HALLUCINATION REDUCTION

The AI must not infer unsupported measurements.

For every scientific result, GSIR should distinguish:

OBSERVED

CALCULATED

INFERRED

HYPOTHESIZED

UNKNOWN

Example:

Observed:

Instrument measured 25.4 °C.

Calculated:

Mean temperature = 25.1 °C.

Inferred:

The trend may indicate stabilization.

Unknown:

Cause of stabilization has not been established.

END OF 29.50

29.51 AI SOURCE REQUIREMENT

When the answer depends on laboratory data, the AI should cite the corresponding dataset, experiment or measurement object internally.

The user-facing response should allow the user to inspect the supporting data.

Cold data in cheaper storage

Model routing

Local processing where appropriate

29.85 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Part 29 shall be considered complete only when:

Data sources can be registered.

Large files can be uploaded asynchronously.

Checksums can verify integrity.

Raw data is preserved.

Instrument lineage can be maintained.

Decision traces can be maintained.

Dataset exports are supported.

Machine-readable representations are supported.

AI receives controlled dataset context.

AI cannot directly access the database.

AI analysis executes in a controlled environment.

AI-generated analytical results retain provenance.

Raw, processed and derived datasets remain distinguishable.

Object storage is used for large scientific files.

Relational storage is used for authoritative metadata.

Search indexing is separated from authoritative storage.

Time-series storage can support continuous instrument data.

Events can notify downstream systems.

Project relationships are maintained.

Experiment relationships are maintained.

Knowledge relationships are maintained.

Offline AI can work with locally available data under permission.

Plugins use controlled data APIs.

Data encryption is supported.

Tenant isolation is enforced.

Audit records exist.

Backup and restoration are tested.

Large-data performance is tested.

Failure recovery is tested.

Data lifecycle is traceable from source to final result.

The architecture supports future autonomous laboratory workflows without redesigning the core data model.

END OF PART 29

PART 29 COMPLETED.

## PART 30 — SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE GRAPH, ONTOLOGY, SEMANTIC LAYER AND KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION ARCHITECTURE

### 30.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall contain a dedicated Scientific Knowledge Layer that converts validated research information into structured, connected and machine-understandable knowledge.

The Knowledge Layer shall connect:

Users

Projects

Research Questions

Documents

Datasets

Experiments

Samples

Measurements

Instruments

Methods

Materials

Chemicals

Results

Claims

Evidence

AI Analyses

Research Papers

Sources

Laboratories

Suppliers

Models

Workflows

The purpose is to allow GSIR to understand relationships between scientific objects instead of treating every object as an isolated record.

The architecture shall follow principles of findability, interoperability, provenance and reuse, while keeping the authoritative source records in the underlying data platform.

END OF 30.1

### 30.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

The Knowledge Layer must not become a second uncontrolled database.

The authoritative hierarchy shall be:

SOURCE DATA

↓

VALIDATED DATA

↓

AUTHORITATIVE DATABASE RECORD

↓

KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION

↓

AI CONTEXT

The Knowledge Graph represents relationships and meaning.

It does not replace the primary database.

END OF 30.2

### 30.3 KNOWLEDGE ARCHITECTURE

                    GSIR KNOWLEDGE LAYER

                           │

          ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐

          │                │                │

       Entities        Relationships      Evidence

          │                │                │

          └────────────────┼────────────────┘

                           │

                    Semantic Layer

                           │

                  Knowledge Graph

                           │

                  Reasoning Engine

                           │

                    AI Context

END OF 30.3

### 30.4 KNOWLEDGE OBJECT

Every important scientific object shall have a unique identity.

Example:

Entity

├── entity_id

├── entity_type

├── canonical_name

├── description

├── source_reference

├── metadata

├── provenance

├── confidence

├── status

├── created_at

└── updated_at

END OF 30.4

### 30.5 ENTITY TYPES

Initial GSIR entity types shall include:

USER

ORGANIZATION

LABORATORY

PROJECT

RESEARCH_QUESTION

EXPERIMENT

SAMPLE

SPECIMEN

MATERIAL

CHEMICAL

COMPOUND

GENE

PROTEIN

CELL

ORGANISM

DISEASE

METHOD

PROTOCOL

INSTRUMENT

MEASUREMENT

DATASET

DOCUMENT

PAPER

SOURCE

CLAIM

EVIDENCE

RESULT

ANALYSIS

MODEL

WORKFLOW

PLUGIN

SUPPLIER

PRODUCT

LOCATION

The registry shall remain extensible.

END OF 30.5

### 30.6 ENTITY IDENTITY

Each entity shall have:

entity_id

entity_type

canonical_name

aliases

external_ids

source_ids

version

status

External identifiers may reference recognized scientific databases or other authoritative systems.

END OF 30.6

### 30.7 CANONICAL ENTITY

Multiple names referring to the same concept should resolve to a canonical entity when sufficient evidence exists.

Example:

Acetylsalicylic acid

Aspirin

2-acetyloxybenzoic acid

may resolve to one canonical chemical entity.

The system must not merge entities solely because their names appear similar.

END OF 30.7

### 30.8 ENTITY RESOLUTION

Entity resolution shall follow:

Candidate Detection

↓

Normalization

↓

Identifier Matching

↓

Context Comparison

↓

Evidence Evaluation

↓

Confidence Calculation

↓

Accept / Review / Reject

Low-confidence matches must remain unresolved or require review.

END OF 30.8

### 30.9 RELATIONSHIP MODEL

Knowledge shall be represented using explicit relationships.

Example:

Experiment

    └── uses → Instrument

Experiment

    └── uses → Sample

Experiment

    └── follows → Protocol

Experiment

    └── produces → Dataset

Dataset

    └── supports → Result

Result

    └── supports → Claim

END OF 30.9

### 30.10 RELATIONSHIP STRUCTURE

Every relationship shall contain:

relationship_id

source_entity_id

relationship_type

target_entity_id

confidence

source_reference

provenance

created_at

valid_from

valid_until

status

END OF 30.10

### 30.11 RELATIONSHIP TYPES

Initial relationship types shall include:

USES

CONTAINS

PART_OF

DERIVED_FROM

GENERATED

MEASURED_BY

MEASURED_ON

PERFORMED_BY

LOCATED_IN

BELONGS_TO

USES_METHOD

USES_PROTOCOL

SUPPORTS

CONTRADICTS

CITES

REFERENCES

RELATED_TO

DEPENDS_ON

CAUSES

CORRELATES_WITH

PREDICTS

VALIDATES

INVALIDATES

REPRODUCES

EXTENDS

DERIVED_FROM

Relationship types shall be controlled through the ontology registry.

END OF 30.11

### 30.12 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH EXAMPLE

Sample S001

    ↓ used_in

Experiment E001

    ↓ follows

Protocol P001

    ↓ uses

Instrument I001

    ↓ generates

Dataset D001

    ↓ analyzed_by

Analysis A001

    ↓ produces

Result R001

    ↓ supports

Claim C001

    ↓ referenced_by

Paper P001

This creates a traceable scientific chain.

END OF 30.12

### 30.13 EVIDENCE-CENTRIC KNOWLEDGE

GSIR shall distinguish a claim from the evidence supporting the claim.

CLAIM

↓

SUPPORTED_BY

↓

EVIDENCE

↓

SOURCE

A claim must not be treated as established merely because it exists in the Knowledge Graph.

END OF 30.13

### 30.14 CLAIM OBJECT

A claim shall contain:

claim_id

statement

claim_type

status

confidence

created_by

source_reference

evidence_ids

contradiction_ids

created_at

updated_at

END OF 30.14

### 30.15 CLAIM STATUS

Possible statuses:

PROPOSED

SUPPORTED

PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED

CONTRADICTED

UNVERIFIED

REJECTED

SUPERSEDED

END OF 30.15

### 30.16 EVIDENCE OBJECT

Evidence shall contain:

evidence_id

evidence_type

source_id

dataset_id

experiment_id

measurement_id

location

content_reference

quality_status

confidence

created_at

END OF 30.16

### 30.17 EVIDENCE TYPES

OBSERVATION

MEASUREMENT

EXPERIMENTAL_RESULT

DATASET

STATISTICAL_RESULT

COMPUTATIONAL_RESULT

DOCUMENT

PUBLISHED_SOURCE

REVIEWED_SOURCE

USER_ASSERTION

AI_GENERATED_HYPOTHESIS

AI-generated hypotheses shall never automatically receive the same evidentiary status as experimentally observed data.

END OF 30.17

### 30.18 KNOWLEDGE CONFIDENCE

GSIR shall maintain confidence as metadata rather than converting uncertainty into false certainty.

Confidence may consider:

Source Quality

Evidence Quantity

Evidence Quality

Agreement

Contradiction

Recency

Reproducibility

Method Quality

Data Quality

Entity Resolution Confidence

END OF 30.18

### 30.19 CONFIDENCE IS NOT TRUTH

The system must never interpret:

confidence = 0.95

as:

scientific truth = 95%

Confidence is an assessment of the reliability of the specific system-generated representation.

END OF 30.19

### 30.20 TEMPORAL KNOWLEDGE

Scientific knowledge changes over time.

Relationships shall therefore support temporal validity.

Example:

Claim

↓

valid_from

valid_until

A newer study may supersede an older interpretation without deleting the historical record.

END OF 30.20

### 30.21 KNOWLEDGE VERSIONING

The Knowledge Graph shall support:

Entity Version

Relationship Version

Ontology Version

Evidence Version

Claim Version

Historical knowledge must remain auditable.

END OF 30.21

### 30.22 ONTOLOGY

GSIR shall maintain an ontology layer defining:

Concepts

Entity Types

Relationships

Properties

Constraints

Controlled Vocabulary

Synonyms

Hierarchies

Domains

Ranges

END OF 30.22

### 30.23 ONTOLOGY HIERARCHY

Example:

Scientific Object

│

├── Biological Object

│   ├── Organism

│   ├── Cell

│   ├── Gene

│   └── Protein

│

├── Chemical Object

│   ├── Compound

│   ├── Experiment

    ├── Laboratory

    ├── Instrument

    └── Supplier

### 30.24 CONTROLLED VOCABULARIES

GSIR shall use controlled vocabularies where appropriate.

Examples:

Units

Experimental Methods

Instrument Types

Sample Types

Research Domains

Laboratory Types

Data Types

Evidence Types

Relationship Types

Free-text values may remain available where controlled vocabulary cannot adequately represent the concept.

END OF 30.24

### 30.25 SYNONYMS

The semantic system shall support:

Canonical Term

Aliases

Abbreviations

Alternative Spellings

Scientific Names

Common Names

Historical Names

Example:

Canonical:

Deoxyribonucleic acid

Aliases:

DNA

Desoxyribonucleic acid

END OF 30.25

### 30.26 SEMANTIC NORMALIZATION

User input:

"DNA sequencing"

may be normalized into concepts such as:

DNA

Sequencing

Genomic Analysis

The original user wording must remain available.

END OF 30.26

### 30.27 KNOWLEDGE EXTRACTION

GSIR shall extract candidate knowledge from:

Documents

Research Papers

Datasets

Experiments

Notes

Conversations

Reports

External Sources

Extraction shall produce candidates rather than silently modifying authoritative knowledge.

END OF 30.27

### 30.28 EXTRACTION PIPELINE

Source

↓

Document/Data Parser

↓

Entity Extraction

↓

Relationship Extraction

↓

Claim Extraction

↓

Evidence Linking

↓

Entity Resolution

↓

Validation

↓

Knowledge Candidate

↓

Approval / Automatic Acceptance According to Policy

↓

Knowledge Graph

END OF 30.28

### 30.29 AI KNOWLEDGE EXTRACTION

The AI may propose:

Entities

Relationships

Claims

Keywords

Methods

Research Topics

Potential Connections

Each AI-generated object must retain:

model_id

model_version

source_reference

execution_id

confidence

created_at

END OF 30.29

### 30.30 HALLUCINATION CONTROL

The Knowledge Layer shall never allow an AI model to create an apparently factual relationship without provenance.

Incorrect:

Chemical A

→ causes

Disease B

without evidence.

Correct:

Candidate Relationship

Chemical A

→ may be associated with

Disease B

Evidence:

Source X

Status:

UNVERIFIED

END OF 30.30

### 30.31 KNOWLEDGE VALIDATION

Knowledge candidates shall be validated through:

Schema Validation

Ontology Validation

Identifier Validation

Source Validation

Relationship Validation

Evidence Validation

Conflict Detection

END OF 30.31

### 30.32 CONFLICT DETECTION

The system must detect contradictory knowledge.

Example:

Study A:

Treatment X increases outcome Y.

Study B:

Treatment X does not increase outcome Y.

The system must not silently choose one.

Instead:

Conflict

├── Evidence A

├── Evidence B

└── Resolution Status

END OF 30.32

### 30.33 KNOWLEDGE RECONCILIATION

Possible states:

UNRESOLVED

PARTIALLY_RECONCILED

RECONCILED

REJECTED

REQUIRES_EXPERT_REVIEW

END OF 30.33

### 30.34 SOURCE PRIORITY

Source quality may be evaluated according to configurable policies.

The system must not use a single universal ranking for every scientific domain.

Priority can consider:

Source Type

Peer Review

Publication Quality

Method Transparency

Evidence Quality

Recency

Reproducibility

Domain Authority

Citation Context

END OF 30.34

### 30.35 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH SEARCH

Users shall be able to search:

Entity

Relationship

Claim

Evidence

Source

Experiment

Dataset

Project

Example:

"What experiments used this compound?"

"What datasets support this claim?"

"Which instruments produced these measurements?"

"What research connects these two concepts?"

END OF 30.35

### 30.36 SEMANTIC SEARCH

Semantic search shall combine:

Keyword Search

+

Vector Search

+

Metadata Search

+

Knowledge Graph Search

+

Relationship Traversal

No single retrieval mechanism shall be treated as sufficient for all queries.

END OF 30.36

### 30.37 GRAPH RETRIEVAL

For an AI question:

User Question

↓

Intent

↓

Entity Identification

↓

Graph Retrieval

↓

Evidence Retrieval

↓

Source Retrieval

↓

Context Assembly

↓

Reasoning

END OF 30.37

### 30.38 GRAPH TRAVERSAL LIMITS

The AI must not automatically traverse an unlimited graph.

Use:

Maximum Hops

Maximum Entities

Maximum Evidence Items

Maximum Token Budget

Relevance Threshold

Permission Boundary

END OF 30.38

### 30.39 PERMISSION-AWARE GRAPH

Knowledge retrieval must respect permissions.

If:

then the Knowledge Layer must not expose a private relationship that reveals sensitive information from Dataset D.

Permission checks must occur before context assembly.

END OF 30.39

### 30.40 TENANT ISOLATION

For multi-tenant deployments:

Organization A

    ↓

Projects

    ↓

Datasets

    ↓

Knowledge

must remain isolated from:

Organization B

unless explicit sharing permissions exist.

├── Experiments

├── Samples

├── Methods

├── Results

├── Claims

└── Evidence

END OF 30.41

### 30.42 PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE

Users may maintain personal knowledge references.

However:

Personal Memory

≠

Scientific Authority

Personal knowledge may influence personalization but cannot override authoritative scientific evidence.
