45.100 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

The GSIR Research Orchestration Layer shall function as the execution control plane for long-running scientific intelligence.

It shall ensure that complex research is not implemented as one uncontrolled AI conversation.

Instead, every substantial research operation shall become a structured, observable and recoverable workflow composed of:

Workflows

+

Tasks

+

Dependencies

+

Agents

+

AI Models

+

Tools

+

Evidence

+

Verification

+

Queues

+

Workers

+

Checkpoints

+

Budgets

+

Approvals

+

Auditing.

This architecture allows GSIR to execute simple research tasks efficiently while also supporting extremely complex, multi-agent, long-running scientific research programs.

46.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Scientific Research Layer shall provide the complete domain architecture for converting a research question into a structured, evidence-backed and reproducible scientific investigation.

The system shall support:

1. Research projects.

2. Research questions.

3. Research objectives.

4. Hypotheses.

5. Literature investigation.

6. Evidence collection.

7. Evidence evaluation.

8. Experiment design.

9. Dataset management.

10. Experimental execution.

11. Result analysis.

12. Statistical analysis.

13. Verification.

14. Scientific conclusions.

15. Uncertainty tracking.

16. Provenance.

17. Reproducibility.

18. Research versioning.

19. Collaboration.

20. Publication-ready outputs.

46.99 PRODUCTION READINESS GATE

The scientific research layer shall not be considered production-ready until:

Research projects are versioned.

Questions are structured.

Objectives are traceable.

Hypotheses are versioned.

Evidence is explicitly linked to claims.

Contradictory evidence is preserved.

Literature sources are traceable.

Datasets are versioned.

Dataset lineage is preserved.

Experiments are reproducible.

Analysis is reproducible.

Results are validated.

Conclusions are evidence-linked.

Provenance is recorded.

Research snapshots are supported.

Collaboration controls exist.

Reviews are supported.

Publication traceability exists.

AI-generated research outputs are clearly controlled.

Security and audit controls are implemented.

END OF 46.99

46.100 COMPLETE SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ARCHITECTURE

The complete GSIR scientific research lifecycle shall be:

RESEARCH PROJECT ↓ RESEARCH QUESTION ↓ OBJECTIVES ↓ BACKGROUND KNOWLEDGE ↓ LITERATURE SEARCH ↓ SOURCE EVALUATION ↓ EVIDENCE EXTRACTION ↓ HYPOTHESIS GENERATION ↓ HYPOTHESIS VALIDATION ↓ EXPERIMENT DESIGN ↓ EXPERIMENT APPROVAL ↓ DATASET SELECTION ↓ EXPERIMENT EXECUTION ↓ RAW RESULTS ↓ ANALYSIS ↓ STATISTICAL / COMPUTATIONAL VALIDATION ↓ RESULTS ↓ INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ↓ CLAIM–EVIDENCE MAPPING ↓ CONCLUSION ↓ PROVENANCE ↓ REPRODUCIBILITY CHECK ↓ RESEARCH REVIEW ↓ PUBLICATION ↓ VERIFIED KNOWLEDGE UPDATE

END OF 46.100

46.101 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall treat scientific research as a versioned, evidence-linked and reproducible computational process.

No major scientific conclusion shall exist independently from its supporting evidence, data, analysis or experimental provenance.

Every important research result shall answer:

What question was investigated?

What hypothesis was tested?

What evidence was used?

What data was analyzed?

What experiment was performed?

What method was used?

What result was obtained?

How was the result verified?

What uncertainty remains?

Which conclusion follows?

Can another researcher reproduce the result?

This architecture establishes the foundation required for GSIR to operate as a scientific research operating system rather than only an AI research assistant.

PART 47 — COMPLETE SCIENTIFIC DATA PLATFORM, DATA LINEAGE, DATA CATALOG, DATA QUALITY, COMPUTATIONAL ARTIFACTS AND FAIR/REPRODUCIBLE DATA ARCHITECTURE

47.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Scientific Data Platform shall provide the controlled infrastructure for storing, describing, validating, transforming, analyzing, discovering and reusing scientific data and computational research artifacts.

The architecture shall support:

- Raw scientific data.

- Processed data.

- Derived datasets.

- Experimental measurements.

- Instrument output.

- Research documents.

- Computational results.

- Analysis scripts.

- Notebooks.

- Models.

- Workflow definitions.

- Metadata.

- Provenance.

- Data lineage.

- Data quality.

- Dataset versioning.

- Data catalogs.

- Data access policies.

- Reproducibility.

- Scientific collaboration.

- AI-assisted data analysis.

- Large-scale data processing.

GSIR shall treat datasets, analytical pipelines, software, workflows and research outputs as connected research objects rather than isolated files. FAIR principles emphasize findability, accessibility, interoperability and reusability, including for the algorithms, tools and workflows used to produce research outputs. 

END OF 47.1

47.2 SCIENTIFIC DATA PRINCIPLE

The central data lifecycle shall be:

DATA GENERATION

↓

DATA INGESTION

↓

DATA VALIDATION

↓

RAW DATA PRESERVATION

↓

METADATA

↓

DATA CATALOG

↓

PROCESSING

↓

DERIVED DATA

↓

ANALYSIS

↓

RESULTS

↓

VERIFICATION

↓

PUBLICATION / REUSE

Every derived object shall remain connected to its source.

END OF 47.2

47.3 DATA ARCHITECTURE

GSIR shall separate five major data layers:

RAW DATA

↓

CURATED DATA

↓

ANALYTICAL DATA

↓

RESULT DATA

↓

PUBLISHED / SHARED DATA

Raw data must remain immutable.

Curated data may contain validated cleaning and normalization.

Analytical data contains data prepared for analysis.

Result data contains outputs derived from analysis.

Published/shared data contains explicitly released artifacts.

PART 48 — COMPLETE SCIENTIFIC WORKFLOW ORCHESTRATION, RESEARCH STATE, DAG EXECUTION, AGENT COORDINATION, CHECKPOINTING, RECOVERY AND LONG-RUNNING RESEARCH ARCHITECTURE

48.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Scientific Workflow Orchestration Layer shall provide the execution backbone for long-running scientific research.

It shall convert structured research intent into controlled, executable and observable workflows while preserving research state, provenance, evidence, failures, intermediate results and recovery information.

The architecture shall support:

- Research workflow definition.

- Workflow planning.

- Workflow DAG generation.

- Workflow validation.

- Task scheduling.

- Agent coordination.

- Tool execution.

- Scientific computation.

- Human approval gates.

- Parallel execution.

- Dependency management.

- Checkpointing.

- Failure recovery.

- Retry policies.

- Branching.

- Resumption.

- Cancellation.

- Resource management.

- Cost control.

- Provenance.

- Long-running autonomous research.

- Reproducible execution.

The workflow layer shall separate semantic research intent from deterministic execution wherever practical. This allows AI to assist with interpretation and planning while validated workflow structures control execution. Recent scientific workflow research similarly emphasizes separating natural-language intent from validated executable workflow specifications. 

END OF 48.1

48.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall treat a research workflow as a persistent computational object.

The workflow shall not exist only inside an AI conversation.

48.9 DAG MODEL

Research workflows shall use a Directed Acyclic Graph where appropriate.

Task A

├──→ Task B ──→ Task D

└──→ Task C ──→ Task D

Task D cannot execute until its required dependencies complete successfully or satisfy their defined dependency conditions.

Missing tasks

48.98 PRODUCTION READINESS GATE

The workflow layer shall not be production-ready until:

- Workflow definitions are versioned.

- Workflow specifications are validated.

- DAGs are validated.

- Dependencies are enforced.

- Tasks execute through controlled executors.

- Workers are isolated from API processes.

- Queues are durable.

- Checkpoints are durable.

- Recovery is implemented.

- Retry policies are implemented.

- Idempotency is enforced where required.

- Resource limits exist.

- Budget limits exist.

- Approval gates exist.

- Agent capabilities are registered.

- Tool permissions are enforced.

- Research state persists independently of sessions.

- Workflow provenance is complete.

- Failed branches remain visible.

- Long-running execution is resumable.

- Workflow execution is observable.

- Security policies are enforced.

- Reproducibility metadata is preserved.

- Comprehensive failure testing is implemented.

48.100 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall not treat AI research as a single prompt followed by a single answer.

The system shall treat research as a persistent, versioned, observable and recoverable workflow.

The fundamental execution model shall be:

INTENT

↓

PLAN

↓

SPECIFICATION

↓

VALIDATION

↓

EXECUTION

↓

OBSERVATION

↓

STATE UPDATE

↓

VERIFICATION

↓

DECISION

↓

NEXT ACTION

The Research State shall remain independent from any individual model, session or agent.

The Workflow Engine shall remain independent from scientific domain logic.

The Agent Layer shall remain independent from workflow persistence.

The Data Platform shall remain independent from AI interpretation.

The Provenance Layer shall connect all of them.

This separation creates the foundation required for GSIR to evolve from an AI research assistant into a long-running AI Scientist and Scientific Research Operating System capable of planning, executing, monitoring, recovering, verifying and continuing complex research.

PART 50 — SCIENTIFIC EVALUATION, VALIDATION, BENCHMARKING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE ARCHITECTURE

50.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Evaluation, Validation, Benchmarking and Quality Assurance Layer shall determine whether research outputs, AI decisions, analyses, experiments, workflows, evidence chains and scientific conclusions are reliable enough for their intended use.

The system shall not treat successful execution as proof of scientific correctness.

A workflow can execute successfully while producing:

Incorrect Results

Invalid Assumptions

Unsupported Claims

Data Leakage

Statistical Errors

Model Failures

Reproducibility Failures

Citation Errors

Tool Errors

Therefore GSIR shall maintain a dedicated scientific evaluation architecture.

END OF 50.1

50.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall separate:

EXECUTION

from

VALIDATION

from

EVALUATION

from

ACCEPTANCE

The architecture shall follow:

Research Task

↓

Execution

↓

Output

↓

Validation

↓

Evaluation

↓

Quality Assessment

↓

Human / Policy Gate

↓

Accepted Result

END OF 50.2

50.3 QUALITY ASSURANCE LAYERS

GSIR shall evaluate research at multiple levels:

Level 1 — Data Quality

Level 2 — Computational Correctness

Level 3 — Methodological Validity

Level 4 — Statistical Validity

Level 5 — Model Quality

Level 6 — Evidence Quality

Level 7 — Reproducibility

Level 8 — Scientific Claim Validity

Level 9 — Research Integrity

END OF 50.3

50.5 VALIDATION VERSUS EVALUATION

Validation shall answer:

"Is this output valid according to a defined rule?"

Evaluation shall answer:

"How good is this output relative to a defined criterion?"

Example:

Validation:

Schema is valid.

Evaluation:

Scientific prediction accuracy is 94%.

Both mechanisms shall be retained.

50.99 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall never confuse:

"the system produced an answer"

with:

"the system produced a scientifically reliable result."

Execution establishes that a computation occurred.

Validation establishes that defined conditions were satisfied.

Evaluation establishes quality relative to defined criteria.

Benchmarking establishes comparative performance.

Reproducibility establishes whether the result can be reconstructed.

Evidence validation establishes whether claims are supported.

Human review establishes acceptance where automated evaluation is insufficient.

The complete GSIR quality chain shall therefore be:

EXECUTE

↓

VALIDATE

↓

EVALUATE

↓

COMPARE

↓

VERIFY

↓

REVIEW

↓

ACCEPT

↓

PUBLISH / USE

Every accepted scientific result shall retain its evaluation history and provenance.

END OF PART 50

PART 51 — REPRODUCIBILITY, REPEATABILITY, REPLICATION AND EXPERIMENT PACKAGING ARCHITECTURE

51.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Reproducibility Architecture shall ensure that research results can be reconstructed, repeated, independently verified and, where appropriate, replicated.

Every important research result shall preserve sufficient information to determine:

What was executed

Which data were used

Which code was used

Which models were used

Which parameters were used

Which environment was used

Which tools were used

Which evidence was used

Which outputs were produced

Which evaluation was performed

END OF 51.1

51.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall distinguish:

REPEATABILITY

REPRODUCIBILITY

REPLICABILITY

Repeatability concerns repeated execution under substantially the same conditions.

Reproducibility concerns obtaining consistent results when the documented computational method is re-executed under appropriately controlled variations.

Replicability concerns whether independent researchers or implementations can reach consistent scientific conclusions.

END OF 51.2

51.99 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall treat reproducibility as a built-in property of the research execution system, not as documentation added after research is complete.

Every important experiment shall be capable of answering:

What happened?

Why did it happen?

With which inputs?

Using which code?

Using which model?

Using which environment?

Using which configuration?

Can it be executed again?

Did it produce the same result?

If not, why?

Does the scientific conclusion remain valid?

The complete reproducibility chain shall therefore be:

CAPTURE

↓

PACKAGE

↓

VERIFY

↓

RE-EXECUTE

↓

COMPARE

↓

REPLICATE

↓

ASSESS

↓

PRESERVE

END OF PART 51

PART 52 — SECURITY, PRIVACY, DATA PROTECTION AND TRUST ARCHITECTURE

52.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Security, Privacy, Data Protection and Trust Architecture shall protect research data, scientific knowledge, user information, credentials, models, tools, workflows, experiments, evidence, provenance and system infrastructure from unauthorized access, modification, disclosure, destruction and misuse.

Security shall be integrated into the architecture rather than added after implementation.

The system shall apply security controls throughout:

Identity

↓

Authentication

↓

Authorization

↓

Data Access

↓

Tool Execution

↓

AI Execution

↓

Research Workflow

↓

Storage

↓

Audit

↓

Export

END OF 52.1

52.2 CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall follow:

VERIFY

BEFORE

TRUST

No user, agent, service, tool, model or workflow shall automatically receive access merely because it exists inside the GSIR system.

END OF 52.2

PART 53 — OBSERVABILITY, MONITORING, LOGGING, TRACING AND SYSTEM HEALTH ARCHITECTURE

53.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Observability Architecture shall provide complete visibility into system behavior, research execution, AI activity, workflows, tools, infrastructure, performance, failures and resource consumption.

Observability shall allow GSIR to determine:

What happened?

Where did it happen?

When did it happen?

Why did it happen?

Which component caused it?

Which user or agent initiated it?

What resources were consumed?

What was the final result?

END OF 53.1

GSIR shall treat observability as a core system capability.

LOGS

METRICS

TRACES

SYSTEM OBSERVABILITY

56.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR frontend shall provide the primary human interaction layer for the complete Scientific Research Operating System.

The frontend must not behave as a collection of disconnected screens.

It shall function as one integrated application in which:

Navigation

+

Workspace

+

AI Chat

+

Projects

+

Research

+

Files

+

Notes

+

History

+

Laboratory

+

Suppliers

+

Account

+

Settings

+

Notifications

operate through a shared application architecture.

The frontend shall consume backend APIs through defined contracts and shall never access the database directly.

END OF 56.1

↓

Request A

solve

↓

Cancel / supersede A

↓

Request B

Only the latest applicable result should update the suggestion UI.

56.140 OPTIMISTIC UPDATE RULE

Optimistic updates may be used when:

Action is reversible

Failure is recoverable

Rollback is reliable

Security is unaffected

Otherwise use pessimistic update behavior.

END OF 56.140

56.141 FRONTEND HIGH-CONCURRENCY STRATEGY

The frontend must not generate excessive backend traffic.

Use:

Request Deduplication

Debouncing

Caching

Batching

Pagination

Lazy Loading

Visibility-Based Updates

WebSocket Updates

This is essential for large-scale GSIR operation.

END OF 56.141

56.142 ONE-CRORE-QUERY COMPATIBILITY

The frontend architecture shall reduce avoidable traffic.

It shall not:

Poll aggressively

Refetch identical data

Send request per keystroke

Reload complete conversations unnecessarily

Load complete projects for every screen

Instead:

Cache

+

Incremental Fetch

+

Streaming

+

Subscriptions

+

Pagination

+

Request Cancellation

END OF 56.142

56.154 FRONTEND QUALITY PRINCIPLE

State

+

+

Loading

+

+

END OF 56.154

56.155 FRONTEND PRODUCTION READINESS GATE

The frontend shall not be considered production-ready until:

- Application shell is implemented.

- Navigation is functional.

- Routing is functional.

- Authentication state is functional.

- Chat tabs are functional.

- Chat streaming is functional.

- Chat actions are functional.

- Search and autocomplete are functional.

- History is functional.

- Notifications are deduplicated.

- Projects are functional.

- Project context is functional.

- Notes are functional.

- Autosave works reliably.

- Profile is functional.

- Laboratory interface is functional.

- Supplier interface is functional.

- Settings are functional.

- Dark mode is functional.

- Timezone handling is functional.

- Accessibility controls are functional.

- File workflows are functional.

- Research workflows are functional.

- Real-time updates work.

- Reconnection works.

- Error boundaries work.

- API contracts are validated.

- Security controls are respected.

- Performance is tested.

- E2E workflows pass.

- Mobile/responsive behavior works.

- No direct database access exists.

- No provider credentials exist in frontend code.

- Frontend telemetry is controlled.

- Large-scale request behavior is optimized.

END OF 56.155

56.156 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

The GSIR frontend shall function as an integrated scientific workspace rather than a collection of ordinary web pages.

The user experience shall follow:

ENTER GSIR

↓

SELECT WORKSPACE

↓

SELECT PROJECT / CONTEXT

↓

CHAT / RESEARCH / DATA / NOTES

↓

EXECUTE ACTION

↓

RECEIVE REAL-TIME STATE

↓

VIEW EVIDENCE / RESULTS

↓

EDIT / REVIEW / VERIFY

↓

SAVE

↓

CONTINUE WORK

The frontend shall remain lightweight, responsive and modular while the backend remains responsible for authoritative business logic, AI execution, research orchestration, security, persistence and scientific validation.

The final frontend architecture shall therefore provide a stable human interface to the larger GSIR system:

USER

↓

GSIR FRONTEND

↓

APPLICATION STATE

↓

API CONTRACT

↓

GSIR BACKEND

↓

AI / RESEARCH / DATA / WORKFLOW / DATABASE

↓

VERIFIED RESULT

↓

GSIR FRONTEND

↓

USER

PART 57 — FRONTEND DESIGN SYSTEM, UI COMPONENT STANDARD, ACCESSIBILITY, RESPONSIVE DESIGN AND VISUAL CONSISTENCY

57.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR frontend shall use one centralized design system so that every page, feature and workflow follows the same visual, interaction and accessibility standards.

The design system shall control:

Typography

Colors

Spacing

Sizing

Borders

Elevation

Icons

Buttons

Forms

Cards

Tables

Dialogs

Drawers

Navigation

Notifications

Loading States

Error States

Responsive Behavior

Accessibility

Motion

No major feature shall independently invent its own visual system.

END OF 57.1

END OF 57.74

57.75 CHAT STREAMING ANIMATION

Streaming responses may use subtle activity indicators.

The interface shall prioritize readable streamed content over animation.

END OF 57.75

57.76 DESIGN SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION

Every reusable component shall document:

Purpose

Props

States

Variants

Accessibility

Responsive Behavior

Usage Rules

Restrictions

END OF 57.76

57.77 COMPONENT STORY / PREVIEW SYSTEM

A component preview environment shall be maintained where practical.

It shall allow developers to inspect:

Default

Loading

Error

Disabled

Dark Theme

Mobile

Desktop

Accessibility

states independently.

END OF 57.77

57.78 DESIGN SYSTEM TESTING

The design system shall be tested independently from feature workflows.

Tests shall verify:

Visual Consistency

Interaction

Keyboard Access

Screen Reader Semantics

Theme Support

Responsive Behavior

END OF 57.78

57.79 VISUAL REGRESSION

Critical shared components shall have visual regression coverage.

Examples:

Navigation

Buttons

Dialogs

Forms

Tables

Chat Messages

Research Results

Cards

Settings

END OF 57.79

57.80 ACCESSIBILITY TEST AUTOMATION

Automated accessibility checks shall run during development and CI.

They shall supplement, not replace, manual accessibility testing.

END OF 57.80

57.81 DESIGN TOKEN GOVERNANCE

Only the design-system layer shall define global visual tokens.

Feature-specific values may exist only when they have a legitimate domain-specific purpose.

END OF 57.81

57.82 COMPONENT NAMING

Component names shall be descriptive and consistent.

Examples:

AppShell

Sidebar

TopBar

ChatComposer

MessageList

ProjectCard

NoteEditor

ResearchTimeline

SourceCard

FileUploader

NotificationPanel

END OF 57.82

57.83 COMPONENT OWNERSHIP

Shared components belong in:

frontend/src/components/

Feature components belong in:

frontend/src/features/<feature>/components/

A component shall be promoted to shared scope only when reuse is justified.

END OF 57.83

57.84 DOMAIN COMPONENT RULE

Domain components may contain domain presentation logic but shall not directly access the database.

All persistent data access shall pass through feature API services and application state.

END OF 57.84

57.85 DESIGN SYSTEM DEPENDENCY RULE

Feature components may depend on shared UI components.

Shared UI components shall not depend on feature-specific components.

Correct:

Feature

↓

Shared UI

Incorrect:

Shared UI

↓

Feature

END OF 57.85

57.86 ACCESSIBILITY-FIRST DEVELOPMENT

Accessibility shall be considered during component design rather than added after implementation.

Every new interactive component shall define:

Keyboard Behavior

Focus Behavior

Screen Reader Name

Disabled State

Error State

Mobile Behavior

END OF 57.86

57.87 INTERNATIONALIZATION

The frontend shall support centralized translation resources.

User-facing text shall not be scattered as uncontrolled hardcoded strings.

Translation architecture shall support:

Language

Region

Pluralization

Date Formatting

Number Formatting

Units

END OF 57.87

57.88 SCIENTIFIC LOCALIZATION

Scientific interfaces shall preserve:

Scientific Symbols

Units

Decimal Precision

Scientific Notation

Chemical Formula Formatting

during localization.

END OF 57.88

57.89 DATE AND TIME DISPLAY

Date/time rendering shall respect:

User Timezone

Locale

Application Preference

Backend Timestamp

The original server timestamp shall remain authoritative.

END OF 57.89

57.90 NUMBER FORMATTING

Numeric display shall distinguish:

Integer

Decimal

Percentage

Currency

Scientific Notation

Measurement

Uncertainty

Ratio

Formatting must not change the underlying numerical value.

END OF 57.90

57.91 UNIT DISPLAY

Scientific units shall be rendered separately from numeric values where practical.

Example:

25.4

mm

rather than treating the complete value as arbitrary text.

END OF 57.91

57.92 PRECISION DISPLAY

The frontend shall not silently change scientific precision.

If the backend provides:

1.2300

the UI shall preserve meaningful precision unless the user explicitly chooses a display transformation.

END OF 57.92

57.93 DATA EXPORT UI

Export controls shall provide:

Format

Scope

Filters

Include Metadata

Confirm

Progress

Download

END OF 57.93

57.94 EXPORT FORMATS

Depending on the feature, supported formats may include:

CSV

JSON

PDF

DOCX

XLSX

Plain Text

The backend shall perform authoritative export generation.

END OF 57.94

57.95 PRINT LAYOUT

Research reports, notes and scientific documents shall support print-friendly layouts where required.

Navigation and interactive controls should be removed from print output.

END OF 57.95

57.96 USER FEEDBACK

The frontend may provide feedback controls for:

Helpful

Not Helpful

Bug Report

Suggestion

Incorrect Information

Missing Source

Feedback shall be associated with the relevant object when possible.

END OF 57.96

57.97 FEEDBACK SAFETY

Feedback must not accidentally expose:

Authentication Tokens

Provider Credentials

Private System Data

Internal Secrets

Hidden Application Metadata

END OF 57.97

57.98 FRONTEND DESIGN REVIEW

Every major feature shall pass a design review covering:

Consistency

Accessibility

Responsive Behavior

Loading

Empty

Error

Success

Security

Performance

END OF 57.98

57.99 DESIGN SYSTEM COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR design system shall be considered complete only when:

1. Tokens are centralized.

2. Themes are centralized.

3. Typography is standardized.

4. Spacing is standardized.

5. Buttons are standardized.

6. Forms are standardized.

7. Dialogs are standardized.

8. Drawers are standardized.

9. Notifications are standardized.

10. Tables are standardized.

11. Loading states are standardized.

12. Empty states are standardized.

13. Error states are standardized.

14. AI response components are standardized.

15. Research components are standardized.

16. File components are standardized.

17. Responsive rules are standardized.

18. Accessibility rules are standardized.

19. Internationalization is supported.

20. Scientific number and unit formatting is standardized.

21. Visual regression coverage exists for critical components.

22. Shared component documentation exists.

23. Design-system tests pass.

24. Dark and light themes work.

25. Mobile, tablet and desktop layouts work.

END OF 57.99

57.100 FINAL DESIGN SYSTEM PRINCIPLE

The GSIR interface shall provide one coherent visual language across the entire platform.

The user shall be able to move from:

Chat

↓

Project

↓

Research

↓

Files

↓

Notes

↓

Experiments

↓

Results

↓

Account

↓

Settings

without encountering unrelated interaction patterns.

The design system shall therefore provide:

Consistency

+

Accessibility

+

Scientific Precision

+

Responsiveness

+

Performance

+

Security

+

Usability

as one unified frontend standard.

END OF PART 57

PART 57 COMPLETED.

GSIR — GLOBAL SCIENTIFIC INTELLIGENT RESEARCH

MASTER DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT

PART 58 — FRONTEND APPLICATION ARCHITECTURE, ROUTING, STATE MANAGEMENT AND MODULE ORGANIZATION

58.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR frontend shall use a modular architecture that separates application structure, feature logic, shared components, state management, API communication and domain-specific functionality.

The frontend architecture shall be designed for:

Scalability

Maintainability

Performance

Security

Testability

Reusability

Accessibility

Feature Isolation

END OF 58.1

58.2 FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE MODEL

The frontend shall follow:

Application Shell

↓

Routing

↓

Pages

↓

Features

↓

Components

↓

State

↓

API Services

↓

Backend APIs

Shared utilities and design-system components shall be available to appropriate layers without creating circular dependencies.

END OF 58.2

58.3 FRONTEND SOURCE DIRECTORY

The primary frontend structure shall be:

frontend/

├── src/

│   ├── app/

│   ├── assets/

│   ├── components/

│   ├── config/

│   ├── features/

│   ├── hooks/

│   ├── layouts/

│   ├── lib/

│   ├── pages/

│   ├── routes/

│   ├── services/

│   ├── state/

│   ├── theme/

│   ├── types/

│   ├── utils/

│   └── main.tsx

│

├── public/

├── tests/

├── package.json

├── tsconfig.json

└── vite.config.ts

END OF 58.3

58.4 APPLICATION ENTRY POINT

The frontend entry point shall initialize:

React Application

↓

Global Configuration

↓

Theme

↓

Error Boundary

↓

Authentication Context

↓

State Providers

↓

Router

↓

Application Shell

The entry point shall remain lightweight.

END OF 58.4

58.5 APP DIRECTORY

frontend/src/app/

shall contain application-level initialization and providers.

Example:

app/

├── App.tsx

├── providers.tsx

├── error-boundary.tsx

├── app-config.ts

└── initialization.ts

END OF 58.5

58.6 APPLICATION PROVIDERS

Global providers shall be centralized.

Possible providers include:

ThemeProvider

AuthProvider

QueryProvider

NotificationProvider

ModalProvider

AccessibilityProvider

Only genuinely global concerns shall become providers.

END OF 58.6

58.7 ROUTING DIRECTORY

frontend/src/routes/

shall contain route definitions.

Example:

routes/

├── index.tsx

├── public.routes.tsx

├── auth.routes.tsx

├── app.routes.tsx

├── project.routes.tsx

└── admin.routes.tsx

END OF 58.7

58.8 ROUTE HIERARCHY

The route hierarchy shall follow application context.

/

├── authentication

├── dashboard

├── projects

│   └── :projectId

│       ├── chat

│       ├── research

│       ├── files

│       ├── notes

│       ├── sources

│       ├── experiments

│       ├── tasks

│       ├── knowledge

│       ├── activity

│       └── settings

├── account

└── administration

END OF 58.8

58.9 ROUTE PROTECTION

Protected routes shall require appropriate authentication.

Authorization shall also be enforced by the backend.

Frontend route protection is a user-experience mechanism and shall never be treated as the primary security boundary.

END OF 58.9

58.10 AUTHENTICATION FLOW

The frontend authentication flow shall be:

User

↓

Login

↓

Authentication Provider

↓

Session / Token

↓

Frontend Auth State

↓

Protected Application

The frontend shall not store sensitive credentials unnecessarily.

END OF 58.10

58.11 SESSION INITIALIZATION

At application startup:

Initialize

↓

Check Existing Session

↓

Validate Session

↓

Load User Context

↓

Load Permissions

↓

Load Application

Failure shall result in a controlled authentication state rather than an application crash.

END OF 58.11

58.12 AUTHORIZATION UI

The frontend may hide or disable controls based on permissions.

However, every protected backend operation shall independently validate authorization.

END OF 58.12

58.13 LAYOUT ARCHITECTURE

GSIR shall use reusable layouts.

layouts/

├── PublicLayout.tsx

├── AuthLayout.tsx

├── AppLayout.tsx

├── ProjectLayout.tsx

├── ResearchLayout.tsx

└── AdminLayout.tsx

END OF 58.13

58.14 APP SHELL

The main application shell shall provide:

Sidebar

Top Navigation

Main Content

Notification Layer

Modal Layer

Command Layer

The shell shall remain independent of individual feature implementations.

END OF 58.14

58.15 PROJECT SHELL

The project shell shall provide:

Project Header

Project Navigation

Main Workspace

Optional Context Panel

Project-specific features shall render inside the project shell.

END OF 58.15

58.16 FEATURE ARCHITECTURE

Every major capability shall be implemented as a feature module.

Example:

features/

├── auth/

├── chat/

├── research/

├── projects/

├── files/

├── notes/

├── sources/

├── experiments/

├── knowledge/

├── tasks/

├── notifications/

├── settings/

└── administration/

END OF 58.16

58.17 FEATURE INTERNAL STRUCTURE

A feature may use:

features/research/

├── components/

├── hooks/

├── pages/

├── services/

├── state/

├── types/

├── utils/

└── index.ts

Feature-specific implementation should remain inside the feature directory.

END OF 58.17

58.18 FEATURE BOUNDARIES

Features shall communicate through defined interfaces.

A feature shall not directly manipulate another feature's internal state.

Correct:

Feature A

↓

Public Feature API

↓

Feature B

Incorrect:

Feature A

↓

Feature B internal state

END OF 58.18

58.19 SHARED COMPONENTS

Shared reusable UI components shall remain in:

frontend/src/components/

Examples:

Button

Input

Dialog

Table

Dropdown

Tabs

Tooltip

Pagination

FilePreview

StatusBadge

END OF 58.19

58.20 SHARED COMPONENT RULE

A shared component shall not contain business logic belonging to one feature.

For example, a generic table shall not contain research-specific database logic.

END OF 58.20

58.21 PAGE COMPONENTS

Pages shall compose:

Layout

+

Feature Components

+

Feature State

+

Navigation

Pages should not contain large amounts of reusable business logic.

END OF 58.21

58.22 HOOK ARCHITECTURE

Reusable React hooks shall be placed in:

frontend/src/hooks/

Feature-specific hooks shall remain inside their feature.

Examples:

useAuth

useDebounce

useKeyboardShortcut

useMediaQuery

usePermissions

useNotification

END OF 58.22

58.23 API SERVICE ARCHITECTURE

Frontend API communication shall be centralized.

frontend/src/services/

may contain:

api-client.ts

auth.service.ts

project.service.ts

research.service.ts

file.service.ts

note.service.ts

experiment.service.ts

user.service.ts

END OF 58.23

58.24 API CLIENT

A centralized API client shall handle:

Base URL

Authentication

Headers

Serialization

Deserialization

Timeouts

Retries Where Appropriate

Error Normalization

Request Identification

END OF 58.24

58.25 API SERVICE RULE

Components shall not directly construct raw HTTP requests throughout the application.

Preferred:

Component

↓

Hook / Feature Service

↓

API Service

↓

API Client

↓

Backend

END OF 58.25

58.26 REQUEST STATE

Asynchronous requests shall expose appropriate states:

Idle

Loading

Success

Error

Cancelled

Long-running operations may additionally expose:

Queued

Processing

Progress

Completed

END OF 58.26

58.27 SERVER STATE

Server-owned data shall be treated separately from local UI state.

Server state includes:

Projects

Messages

Research Runs

Files

Sources

Experiments

Tasks

Notifications

User Profile

END OF 58.27

58.28 LOCAL UI STATE

Local state includes:

Modal Open

Selected Tab

Dropdown Open

Temporary Form Input

Panel Width

UI Preferences

Local UI state should not be unnecessarily persisted to the backend.

END OF 58.28

58.29 GLOBAL STATE

Global application state shall contain only information that genuinely requires cross-feature access.

Examples:

Authenticated User

Theme

Global Notifications

Application Preferences

Active Workspace

Permission Context

END OF 58.29

58.30 STATE MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLE

State ownership shall follow:

Most Local Appropriate Owner

↓

Feature State

↓

Shared State

↓

Global State

State shall not become global merely for convenience.

END OF 58.30

58.31 SERVER CACHE

Frequently accessed server data may use a client-side server-state cache.

The cache shall support:

Fetching

Caching

Invalidation

Refetching

Mutation Updates

Optimistic Updates Where Safe

END OF 58.31

58.32 CACHE INVALIDATION

After mutations, affected cached resources shall be invalidated or updated.

Example:

Create Project

↓

Project List Cache

↓

Invalidate / Update

↓

Project List Refresh

END OF 58.32

58.33 OPTIMISTIC UI

Optimistic updates may be used for low-risk operations.

They shall not be used where temporary incorrect state could cause:

Data Loss

Security Issues

Scientific Misinterpretation

Financial Consequences

Irreversible Actions

END OF 58.33

58.34 FORM STATE

Forms shall maintain controlled state for:

Values

Validation

Dirty State

Submitting State

Errors

Success

Reset

END OF 58.34

58.35 AUTOSAVE

Autosave may be supported for appropriate resources such as:

Notes

Draft Research

Documents

Prompts

Project Descriptions

Autosave shall clearly indicate:

Saving

Saved

Save Failed

Offline / Pending

END OF 58.35

58.36 DRAFT STATE

Draft content shall remain distinguishable from finalized content.

Example:

Draft

↓

Review

↓

Verified

↓

Published

END OF 58.36

58.37 URL STATE

State that users may reasonably expect to preserve or share shall be represented in the URL where appropriate.

Examples:

Selected Project

Selected Research Run

Tab

Filter

Search Query

Pagination

Sensitive information shall never be placed in URLs.

END OF 58.37

58.38 SEARCH STATE

Search interfaces shall support controlled state synchronization.

Search Input

↓

Debounce

↓

Query

↓

Server Request

↓

Results

Search requests shall be cancellable where practical.

END OF 58.38

58.39 PAGINATION STATE

Large datasets shall use server-side pagination or controlled incremental loading.

The frontend shall not load massive datasets unnecessarily.

END OF 58.39

58.40 INFINITE SCROLL

Infinite scrolling may be used for:

Chat History

Activity

Notifications

Search Results

It shall preserve accessibility and navigation.

END OF 58.40

58.41 CHAT FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

The chat feature shall separate:

Conversation State

Message Rendering

Composer State

Streaming State

Tool Events

Attachments

Citations

Error Handling

END OF 58.41

58.42 CHAT MESSAGE STREAMING

Streaming shall follow:

User Message

↓

Request Created

↓

AI Processing

↓

Stream Events

↓

Partial Message

↓

Completed Message

The frontend shall safely handle interrupted streams.

END OF 58.42

58.43 STREAM EVENT HANDLING

Streaming events may include:

Message Started

Token / Content Delta

Tool Started

Tool Progress

Tool Completed

Citation

Artifact

Warning

Error

Message Completed

Unknown event types shall not crash the interface.

END OF 58.43

58.44 CHAT RECONNECTION

If a streaming connection is interrupted:

Detect Interruption

↓

Preserve Existing Content

↓

Display Connection State

↓

Attempt Recovery Where Supported

↓

Finalize Or Mark Interrupted

END OF 58.44

58.45 RESEARCH FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

Research shall be represented as a workflow rather than a single request.

Question

↓

Research Plan

↓

Search

↓

Evidence Collection

↓

Analysis

↓

Verification

↓

Synthesis

↓

Final Result

END OF 58.45

58.46 RESEARCH RUN STATE

The frontend shall maintain a research run state containing:

Run ID

Question

Status

Progress

Current Stage

Sources

Evidence

Findings

Errors

Final Output

END OF 58.46

58.47 RESEARCH LIVE UPDATES

Long-running research shall support live status updates where available.

The frontend shall not require full-page refreshes to observe progress.

END OF 58.47

58.48 FILE FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

The file feature shall separate:

Upload

File Listing

File Metadata

Preview

Processing Status

Download

Deletion

Search

Indexing Status

END OF 58.48

58.49 FILE UPLOAD QUEUE

Multiple uploads shall be represented as a queue.

Queued

↓

Uploading

↓

Processing

↓

Completed

Failures shall be individually retryable where possible.

END OF 58.49

58.50 NOTES FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

The notes feature shall separate:

Note List

Note Editor

Note Viewer

Autosave

Version History

AI Assistance

Search

Links

END OF 58.50

58.51 EXPERIMENT FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

Experiment interfaces shall separate:

Experiment Definition

Inputs

Parameters

Execution

Live Status

Measurements

Results

Analysis

Provenance

END OF 58.51

58.52 KNOWLEDGE FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE

Knowledge interfaces shall support:

Entities

Relationships

Documents

Sources

Collections

Search

Graph Views

Evidence

The frontend shall not assume that visual graph representation is always the preferred view.

END OF 58.52

58.53 NOTIFICATION STATE

Notifications shall support:

Unread

Read

Archived

Dismissed

Action Required

Real-time notifications shall update the UI without requiring manual refresh where supported.

END OF 58.53

58.54 ERROR BOUNDARIES

Major application areas shall use error boundaries.

A failure in one feature shall not unnecessarily terminate the entire application.

Example:

Application

├── Sidebar

├── Chat

├── Research

│   └── Error Boundary

├── Files

└── Notes

END OF 58.54

58.55 FRONTEND ERROR NORMALIZATION

Backend errors shall be converted into a consistent frontend error model.

Example:

{

  code,

  message,

  category,

  retryable,

  requestId

}

END OF 58.55

58.56 RETRY POLICY

Automatic retries shall be used only for appropriate transient failures.

The frontend shall not repeatedly retry:

Authentication Failures

Authorization Failures

Validation Errors

Destructive Operation Failures

END OF 58.56

58.57 OFFLINE STATE

Where offline behavior is supported, the frontend shall clearly distinguish:

Online

Offline

Reconnecting

Pending Sync

Sync Failed

END OF 58.57

58.58 SYNCHRONIZATION

Offline or delayed synchronization shall use explicit conflict handling.

The frontend shall never silently overwrite newer server data.

END OF 58.58

58.59 PERFORMANCE ARCHITECTURE

The frontend shall minimize:

Initial JavaScript

Unnecessary Rendering

Large Bundle Dependencies

Repeated API Requests

Large DOM Trees

Unnecessary State Updates

END OF 58.59

58.60 CODE SPLITTING

Large features shall be loaded lazily where practical.

Example:

Application Shell

↓

Core Features

↓

Lazy Feature Module

Research, administration and advanced visualization modules may be candidates for lazy loading.

END OF 58.60

58.61 ROUTE-LEVEL LAZY LOADING

Major routes may use route-level code splitting.

This shall reduce initial application load without harming navigation performance.

END OF 58.61

58.62 COMPONENT MEMOIZATION

Memoization shall be used only where it produces measurable benefit.

The application shall avoid unnecessary optimization complexity.

END OF 58.62

58.63 LARGE LIST RENDERING

Large lists shall use virtualization where necessary.

Potential candidates:

Messages

Files

Research Results

Activity

Notifications

Dataset Rows

END OF 58.63

58.64 IMAGE OPTIMIZATION

Images shall use appropriate:

Dimensions

Compression

Lazy Loading

Responsive Sources

Alternative Text

END OF 58.64

58.65 FRONTEND SECURITY

The frontend shall follow:

No Secrets in Source

No Provider API Keys in Browser

No Trust in Client Authorization

Safe Rendering

Input Validation

Secure Authentication

Safe File Handling

END OF 58.65

58.66 XSS PROTECTION

User-generated content shall be safely rendered.

HTML insertion shall be avoided unless explicitly required and safely sanitized.

Markdown rendering shall use a controlled renderer.

END OF 58.66

58.67 SENSITIVE DATA

Sensitive data shall not unnecessarily remain in:

Local Storage

Session Storage

URLs

Console Logs

Analytics Events

Error Messages

Client Cache

END OF 58.67

58.68 FRONTEND LOGGING

Frontend logs shall be structured and environment-aware.

Production logging shall avoid exposing:

Tokens

Passwords

Private Documents

Private Messages

Secrets

Sensitive Scientific Data

END OF 58.68

58.69 TELEMETRY

Telemetry shall capture useful operational information such as:

Performance

Errors

Feature Usage

Request Failures

Frontend Crashes

Telemetry collection shall respect privacy and configured consent requirements.

END OF 58.69

58.70 FRONTEND TEST STRUCTURE

Tests shall be organized into:

Unit Tests

Component Tests

Feature Tests

Integration Tests

Accessibility Tests

End-to-End Tests

Visual Regression Tests

END OF 58.70

58.71 UNIT TESTS

Unit tests shall cover:

Utilities

Hooks

Formatters

Validators

State Logic

Pure Functions

END OF 58.71

58.72 COMPONENT TESTS

Component tests shall verify:

Rendering

Interaction

States

Accessibility

Error Handling

END OF 58.72

58.73 FEATURE TESTS

Feature tests shall verify complete feature behavior without requiring the entire application.

Examples:

Create Project

Upload File

Run Research

Save Note

Start Experiment

Search Knowledge

END OF 58.73

58.74 END-TO-END TESTS

Critical user journeys shall be tested from the browser.

Examples:

Login

Create Project

Start Chat

Upload Document

Run Research

Review Sources

Create Experiment

Export Result

END OF 58.74

58.75 FRONTEND CONTRACT TESTING

Frontend API types and backend API contracts shall remain synchronized.

Breaking API changes shall be detected before production deployment.

END OF 58.75

58.76 TYPE SAFETY

The frontend shall use strict TypeScript configuration.

Shared API models shall have explicit types.

Avoid uncontrolled use of:

any

END OF 58.76

58.77 FRONTEND CONFIGURATION

Environment-specific configuration shall be centralized.

Examples:

API Base URL

WebSocket URL

Feature Flags

Environment Name

Telemetry Configuration

Secrets shall not be included in public frontend configuration.

END OF 58.77

58.78 FEATURE FLAGS

Feature flags shall support controlled rollout.

Example:

Disabled

↓

Internal

↓

Beta

↓

Limited Release

↓

General Availability

END OF 58.78

58.79 FEATURE FLAG SAFETY

Feature flags shall not be treated as authorization controls.

Security-sensitive access must be enforced by the backend.

END OF 58.79

58.80 FRONTEND DEPENDENCY MANAGEMENT

Dependencies shall be:

Version Controlled

Audited

Updated

Reviewed

Removed When Unnecessary

Unused dependencies shall not remain indefinitely.

END OF 58.80

58.81 FRONTEND BUILD PIPELINE

The build pipeline shall execute:

Install

↓

Type Check

↓

Lint

↓

Unit Tests

↓

Component Tests

↓

Build

↓

Integration / E2E Tests

↓

Security Checks

↓

Artifact Generation

END OF 58.81

58.82 FRONTEND DEPLOYMENT

Frontend deployment shall use immutable versioned builds where practical.

A deployment shall be traceable to:

Git Commit

Build ID

Environment

Release Version

END OF 58.82

58.83 FRONTEND ROLLBACK

A previous stable frontend build shall be deployable quickly.

Rollback shall not require rebuilding the application from source during an incident.

END OF 58.83

58.84 FRONTEND OBSERVABILITY

Frontend observability shall monitor:

Page Load

API Latency

JavaScript Errors

Render Failures

Streaming Failures

Upload Failures

Route Failures

END OF 58.84

58.85 ACCESSIBILITY GATE

A feature shall not be considered production-ready if critical accessibility requirements fail.

The release process shall include accessibility validation.

END OF 58.85

58.86 RESPONSIVE GATE

Every major feature shall be validated at:

Mobile

Tablet

Desktop

58.88 FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR frontend architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Application initialization is centralized.

- Routing is modular.

- Authentication is isolated.

- Authorization-aware UI is implemented.

- Layouts are reusable.

- Features are isolated.

- Shared components are centralized.

- API access is centralized.

- Server state is separated from local state.

- Global state is minimized.

- Chat streaming is supported.

- Research workflows are supported.

- File workflows are supported.

- Notes workflows are supported.

- Experiment workflows are supported.

- Knowledge workflows are supported.

- Error boundaries exist.

- Error normalization exists.

- Offline behavior is defined where required.

- Performance optimization is implemented.

- Security controls are implemented.

- Accessibility controls are implemented.

- Testing layers are implemented.

- Type safety is enforced.

- Build and deployment pipelines are defined.

- Observability is implemented.

- Rollback is supported.

Pages

↓

↓

PART 59 — BACKEND API ARCHITECTURE, REQUEST FLOW, API CONTRACTS AND SERVICE COMMUNICATION

59.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR backend API layer shall provide a controlled interface between the frontend, AI systems, research engines, data services, authentication systems, file processing systems and external integrations.

The API architecture shall provide:

Security

Consistency

Validation

Versioning

Observability

Scalability

Reliability

Traceability

The API layer shall prevent frontend clients from directly accessing internal databases, model providers or protected infrastructure.

END OF 59.1

59.2 API ARCHITECTURE

The request architecture shall follow:

Frontend

↓

API Gateway / Application Entry

↓

Authentication

↓

Authorization

↓

Request Validation

↓

Application Service

↓

Domain Service

↓

Repository / External Service

↓

Database / AI / Storage / External API

Responses shall travel back through the appropriate service boundaries before reaching the client.

END OF 59.2

59.3 BACKEND API DIRECTORY

The backend shall maintain a dedicated API layer:

backend/

└── app/

    ├── api/

    │   ├── routes/

    │   ├── dependencies/

    │   ├── middleware/

    │   ├── schemas/

    │   ├── errors/

    │   └── versioning/

    │

    ├── services/

    ├── domains/

    ├── repositories/

    ├── models/

    ├── ai/

    ├── research/

    ├── files/

    ├── security/

    ├── tasks/

    └── main.py

END OF 59.3

59.4 API ROUTES

API route modules shall be separated by domain.

Example:

api/routes/

auth.py

users.py

projects.py

chat.py

research.py

files.py

notes.py

sources.py

experiments.py

knowledge.py

tasks.py

notifications.py

settings.py

admin.py

health.py

A route module shall remain focused on HTTP/API concerns.

END OF 59.4

59.5 ROUTE RESPONSIBILITY

A route handler shall primarily perform:

Request Parsing

↓

Authentication Context

↓

Authorization

↓

Validation

↓

Service Invocation

↓

Response Construction

Business logic shall not be duplicated inside route handlers.

END OF 59.5

59.6 API VERSIONING

The API shall support explicit versioning.

Example:

/api/v1/...

Future incompatible changes shall be introduced through a new API version rather than silently changing existing contracts.

END OF 59.6

59.7 API CONTRACT

Every API endpoint shall define:

HTTP Method

Path

Authentication Requirement

Authorization Requirement

Request Schema

Response Schema

Error Schema

Status Codes

Idempotency Behavior

Rate Limit

Where applicable, pagination and filtering rules shall also be documented.

END OF 59.7

59.8 HTTP METHODS

The API shall use HTTP methods according to semantic purpose:

GET

→ Retrieve

POST

→ Create / Execute Action

PUT

→ Replace

PATCH

→ Partial Update

DELETE

→ Remove

The implementation shall avoid using POST for ordinary retrieval merely for convenience.

END OF 59.8

59.9 RESOURCE NAMING

Resource paths shall use predictable naming.

Example:

/projects

/projects/{project_id}

/projects/{project_id}/files

/projects/{project_id}/notes

/projects/{project_id}/research-runs

/projects/{project_id}/experiments

Names shall remain consistent across the platform.

END OF 59.9

59.10 ACTION ENDPOINTS

Operations that represent commands rather than ordinary CRUD may use explicit action endpoints.

Example:

/research-runs/{run_id}/cancel

/research-runs/{run_id}/verify

/files/{file_id}/retry

/experiments/{experiment_id}/execute

Action endpoints shall have clearly defined state transitions.

END OF 59.10

59.11 REQUEST VALIDATION

Every externally supplied request shall be validated before entering business logic.

Validation shall cover:

Type

Format

Length

Range

Required Fields

Allowed Values

Relationships

Authorization Context

Validation shall occur server-side even when the frontend performs equivalent validation.

END OF 59.11

59.12 INPUT SANITIZATION

User-controlled data shall be treated as untrusted.

The backend shall safely process:

Text

Markdown

HTML

Files

URLs

Metadata

Search Queries

Filters

Identifiers

AI Prompts

No user input shall be assumed safe merely because it originated from the GSIR frontend.

END OF 59.12

59.13 AUTHENTICATION MIDDLEWARE

Protected API requests shall pass through authentication middleware.

The middleware shall establish:

User ID

Session

Authentication Method

Token Context

Session Validity

Invalid authentication shall terminate the request before protected business logic executes.

END OF 59.13

59.14 AUTHORIZATION MIDDLEWARE

Authorization shall evaluate:

User

Role

Permission

Organization

Project

Resource Ownership

Resource State

Authorization shall be enforced for every protected resource.

END OF 59.14

59.15 RESOURCE-LEVEL AUTHORIZATION

A user may have permission to access one project but not another.

Therefore:

Authenticated

≠

Authorized

Resource-level authorization shall be performed after authentication and before sensitive resource access.

END OF 59.15

59.16 API DEPENDENCIES

Reusable API dependencies shall provide:

Current User

Database Session

Project Context

Permission Context

Request Context

Rate Limit Context

Correlation ID

This avoids repeating infrastructure logic across route modules.

END OF 59.16

59.17 SERVICE LAYER

Routes shall call application services.

Example:

POST /projects

↓

ProjectRoute

↓

ProjectService

↓

ProjectRepository

↓

Database

The service layer shall contain application orchestration logic.

END OF 59.17

59.18 DOMAIN SERVICE

Domain services shall contain domain-specific operations.

Example:

ResearchService

ExperimentService

KnowledgeService

FileProcessingService

ProjectService

Domain services shall not depend on HTTP-specific implementation details.

END OF 59.18

59.19 REPOSITORY LAYER

Repositories shall isolate persistence operations.

Example:

ProjectService

↓

ProjectRepository

↓

Database

This prevents database queries from being scattered throughout API handlers.

END OF 59.19

59.20 DATABASE ACCESS

The API shall never expose raw database access to clients.

The backend shall control:

Queries

Transactions

Filtering

Authorization

Data Transformation

Pagination

before returning data.

END OF 59.20

59.21 RESPONSE SCHEMAS

API responses shall use explicit schemas.

Responses shall not automatically expose entire database models.

Example:

Database Model

↓

Internal Object

↓

Response Schema

↓

API Client

This prevents accidental exposure of internal fields.

END OF 59.21

59.22 RESPONSE ENVELOPE

Where appropriate, GSIR APIs shall use a consistent response structure.

Example:

{

  "data": {...},

  "meta": {...}

}

Error responses shall use a separate standardized error structure.

END OF 59.22

59.23 ERROR RESPONSE

A standardized error may contain:

{

  "error": {

    "code": "...",

    "message": "...",

    "details": {},

    "request_id": "..."

  }

}

Sensitive internal stack traces shall never be returned to clients.

END OF 59.23

59.24 ERROR CATEGORIES

GSIR shall define categories such as:

AUTHENTICATION_ERROR

AUTHORIZATION_ERROR

VALIDATION_ERROR

NOT_FOUND

CONFLICT

RATE_LIMITED

DEPENDENCY_ERROR

PROCESSING_ERROR

INTERNAL_ERROR

Clients shall use error codes rather than fragile message-string matching.

END OF 59.24

59.25 HTTP STATUS CODES

The API shall use appropriate status codes.

Examples:

200

Successful retrieval/update

201

Resource created

202

Accepted asynchronous operation

204

Successful operation with no body

400

Invalid request

401

Unauthenticated

403

Unauthorized

404

Resource not found

409

Conflict

422

Validation failure

429

Rate limited

500

Internal server error

502/503

Dependency/service failure

END OF 59.25

59.26 ASYNCHRONOUS OPERATIONS

Long-running operations shall not keep ordinary HTTP requests open unnecessarily.

Examples:

Research

Document Processing

Embedding

Large Export

Experiment Execution

Model Evaluation

The API shall create an operation or job and return its identifier.

59.27 JOB CREATION FLOW

POST /research-runs

↓

Validate

↓

Authorize

↓

Create Research Run

↓

Queue Job

↓

Return Run ID

↓

Frontend Observes Status

The worker performs the long-running operation independently.

59.28 JOB STATUS API

Long-running resources shall expose status.

Example:

GET /research-runs/{run_id}

QUEUED

RUNNING

PAUSED

COMPLETED

FAILED

CANCELLED

Additional domain-specific states may be defined.

END OF 59.28

59.29 JOB CANCELLATION

Cancellable operations shall support cancellation.

Cancellation shall be explicit and idempotent.

The system shall distinguish:

Cancel Requested

↓

Cancellation Processing

↓

Cancelled

from a job that has already completed.

END OF 59.29

59.30 API IDEMPOTENCY

Operations that create expensive or irreversible resources shall support idempotency where appropriate.

Example:

Client

↓

Idempotency Key

↓

API

↓

Operation

Repeated requests with the same valid idempotency key shall not unintentionally create duplicate operations.

END OF 59.30

59.31 REQUEST IDENTIFICATION

Every request shall have a correlation/request identifier.

Example:

Request

↓

request_id

↓

Logs

↓

Services

↓

Workers

↓

External Calls

This allows one operation to be traced across the system.

END OF 59.31

59.32 DISTRIBUTED TRACE CONTEXT

Where distributed tracing is implemented, trace context shall propagate through:

API

↓

Service

↓

Queue

↓

Worker

↓

External Provider

The trace shall never contain sensitive user content unnecessarily.

END OF 59.32

59.33 RATE LIMITING

Research

File Processing

Search

Exports

END OF 59.33

59.34 QUOTA MANAGEMENT

Storage

External Searches

Experiment Execution

59.36 PAGINATION RESPONSE

    "page_size": 25,

  }

59.38 SORTING

Ranking

59.51 DEPENDENCY HEALTH

Database

Cache

Queue

Object Storage

59.52 API TIMEOUTS

Every external or internal network call shall have an appropriate timeout.

Timeout

Healthy

↓

Failure Threshold

↓

Open

↓

Recovery Wait

↓

↓

Healthy / Open

↓

↓

↓

↓

before execution.

↓

Validation

↓

Endpoint Usage

Rate Limits

OR

↓

OR

↓

↓

59.84 API ARCHITECTURE COMPLETION CRITERIA

The API architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Routes are modular.

- API versioning exists.

- Authentication is centralized.

- Authorization is enforced.

- Input validation is centralized.

- Services own application logic.

- Repositories own persistence access.

- Response schemas are explicit.

- Errors are standardized.

- Long-running work is asynchronous.

- Idempotency is supported where required.

- Request tracing exists.

- Rate limits exist.

- Quotas are enforceable.

- Pagination is standardized.

- Search and filtering are controlled.

- AI providers are abstracted.

- Research tools are controlled.

- File processing is asynchronous.

- Webhooks are verified.

- Security headers and CORS are controlled.

- Audit events exist.

- Logging and metrics exist.

- API contracts are tested.

- Security testing exists.

- Deployment and rollback are defined.

- API documentation is maintained.

- Backward compatibility and deprecation are governed.

END OF 59.84

59.85 FINAL API PRINCIPLE

The GSIR API shall act as the controlled execution boundary of the entire platform.

Every important operation shall pass through explicit:

Identity

↓

Permission

↓

Validation

↓

Business Logic

↓

Resource Access

↓

Execution

↓

Observation

↓

Response

This architecture shall allow GSIR to integrate frontend applications, AI models, research agents, databases, files, experiments and external services without allowing any individual client or provider to bypass the platform's security, governance and domain boundaries.

END OF 59.85

PART 60 — BACKEND SERVICE LAYER, DOMAIN MODULES AND INTERNAL SERVICE COMMUNICATION

60.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR service layer shall contain the application and domain logic that operates between the API layer and the underlying infrastructure.

The service architecture shall ensure that:

API Layer

↓

Application Services

↓

Domain Services

↓

Repositories / Infrastructure

remains clearly separated.

The service layer shall prevent HTTP handlers from becoming the location of business logic and shall keep domain behavior independent from frontend implementation details.

60.2 SERVICE ARCHITECTURE

The backend shall use the following logical flow:

Client

↓

API

↓

Application Service

↓

Domain Service

↓

Repository / Adapter

↓

Infrastructure

This separation allows the API contract and infrastructure implementation to evolve without unnecessarily changing domain behavior.

END OF 60.2

The backend shall organize services by responsibility.

backend/app/services/

├── auth_service.py

├── user_service.py

├── project_service.py

├── chat_service.py

├── research_service.py

├── file_service.py

├── document_service.py

├── note_service.py

├── source_service.py

├── experiment_service.py

├── knowledge_service.py

├── task_service.py

├── notification_service.py

└── audit_service.py

END OF 60.3

60.4 DOMAIN DIRECTORY

Domain-specific logic shall be organized under:

backend/app/domains/

├── auth/

├── projects/

├── conversations/

├── research/

├── documents/

├── knowledge/

├── experiments/

├── tasks/

└── administration/

Each domain shall expose controlled interfaces rather than allowing unrestricted cross-domain access.

END OF 60.4

60.5 APPLICATION SERVICE

Application services shall coordinate complete use cases.

Example:

Create Research Run

↓

Validate Request

↓

Check Permission

↓

Create Run

↓

Create Job

↓

Queue Execution

↓

Return Run

Application services shall coordinate the operation without embedding low-level infrastructure details.

END OF 60.5

60.6 DOMAIN SERVICE

Domain services shall contain rules that represent GSIR business behavior.

Examples include:

Research Planning

Evidence Verification

Experiment Validation

Knowledge Relationship Validation

Project Permission Rules

Document Processing Decisions

Domain services shall remain independent of HTTP request objects.

END OF 60.6

60.7 SERVICE DEPENDENCY DIRECTION

Dependencies shall generally point inward toward domain logic.

API

↓

Application

↓

Domain

↓

Infrastructure

END OF 60.7

Example:

ResearchService

↓

SearchProvider Interface

↓

WebSearchAdapter

ProjectRepository

create()

get_by_id()

list_for_user()

update()

archive()

Create Project

↓

Validate

↓

Database Transaction

├── Create Project

├── Create Membership

└── Create Audit Event

↓

Commit

Research Run

CREATED

↓

QUEUED

↓

RUNNING

↓

↓

Project Permissions

↓

↓

↓

Attributes

↓

↓

↓

↓

60.25 EXPERIMENT SERVICE

Parameter Validation

Execution State

Results

↓

Validate Definition

↓

Validate Inputs

↓

Validate Parameters

↓

Validate Permissions

↓

Validate Resources

↓

Create Execution

60.27 TASK SERVICE

Embedding

AI Evaluation

END OF 60.27

60.28 TASK STATE

The common task lifecycle shall be:

↓

QUEUED

↓

↓

COMPLETED

RUNNING

↓

RUNNING

↓

↓

CANCELLED

60.29 TASK RETRY

Maximum Retries

Failure Reason

END OF 60.29

60.30 NOTIFICATION SERVICE

The notification service shall provide a common mechanism for:

Task Completion

Research Completion

Processing Failure

Permission Changes

Important User Events

END OF 60.30

60.31 AUDIT SERVICE

Security-sensitive operations shall generate audit records through a dedicated audit service.

Result

Relevant Metadata

END OF 60.31

60.32 QUOTA SERVICE

The quota service shall manage resource consumption.

Potential quota dimensions:

Research Operations

Search Requests

Storage

File Processing

Experiment Runtime

API Requests

END OF 60.32

60.33 USAGE SERVICE

Usage accounting shall be separate from business operations.

Example:

AI Execution

↓

Usage Event

↓

Usage Service

↓

Accounting / Analytics

This prevents usage tracking from becoming tightly coupled to every domain implementation.

END OF 60.33

60.34 AI SERVICE BOUNDARY

AI functionality shall be exposed through a controlled backend service.

Application Service

↓

AI Orchestrator

↓

Model Router

↓

Provider Adapter

↓

Model Provider

The application shall not depend directly on one provider's API format.

END OF 60.34

60.35 MODEL ROUTER

The model router shall select an appropriate model based on:

Task Type

Required Quality

Context Size

Latency Requirement

Cost Budget

Availability

Privacy Requirement

Model Capability

END OF 60.35

60.36 MODEL ADAPTER

Every provider adapter shall translate between GSIR's internal model interface and the provider-specific API.

GSIR Model Request

↓

Provider Adapter

↓

Provider Request

↓

Provider Response

↓

Normalized GSIR Response

Provider-specific structures shall not leak into the rest of the application.

END OF 60.36

60.37 AI EXECUTION RECORD

Every important AI execution shall produce an internal execution record containing appropriate metadata.

Possible fields:

Execution ID

Task

Model

Provider

Status

Latency

END OF 60.37

60.38 AI FAILURE HANDLING

AI failures shall be classified.

Transient Provider Failure

Permanent Provider Failure

Rate Limit

Context Limit

Validation Error

Safety / Policy Rejection

Timeout

Unavailable Model

The service layer shall determine whether fallback or retry is appropriate.

END OF 60.38

60.39 SERVICE-TO-SERVICE COMMUNICATION

Internal services shall communicate through explicit interfaces.

Communication may use:

Direct Function Calls

Internal HTTP

RPC

Message Queue

Event Bus

The mechanism shall be selected according to latency, reliability and coupling requirements.

END OF 60.39

60.40 SYNCHRONOUS COMMUNICATION

Synchronous communication shall be used when an immediate result is required.

Example:

ProjectService

↓

PermissionService

↓

Result

Timeouts shall always be defined for network-based synchronous communication.

END OF 60.40

60.41 ASYNCHRONOUS COMMUNICATION

Asynchronous communication shall be used for operations such as:

Research

Document Processing

Embedding

Experiment Execution

Large Exports

Evaluation

The caller shall receive an operation identifier rather than waiting indefinitely.

END OF 60.41

60.42 EVENT-DRIVEN COMMUNICATION

Domain events may be emitted for important state changes.

Examples:

ProjectCreated

FileUploaded

FileProcessed

ResearchStarted

ResearchCompleted

ExperimentCompleted

KnowledgeUpdated

Events shall contain stable identifiers and sufficient metadata for consumers.

END OF 60.42

60.43 EVENT CONSUMERS

Consumers shall process events independently.

Example:

ResearchCompleted

├── Notification Service

├── Usage Service

├── Audit Service

└── Analytics Service

The research service shall not need to directly call every consumer.

END OF 60.43

60.44 EVENT IDEMPOTENCY

Event consumers shall be idempotent where duplicate delivery is possible.

A consumer shall safely recognize that an event has already been processed.

END OF 60.44

60.45 EVENT ORDERING

Where ordering matters, events shall contain appropriate sequence information.

Consumers shall not assume global ordering unless the messaging infrastructure explicitly guarantees it.

END OF 60.45

60.46 DEAD-LETTER HANDLING

Events that repeatedly fail shall be moved to a controlled dead-letter mechanism.

Event

↓

Consumer

↓

Failure

↓

Retry

↓

Failure

↓

Dead Letter

Dead-letter events shall be observable and recoverable.

END OF 60.46

60.47 SERVICE TIMEOUTS

Each service dependency shall define an appropriate timeout.

Timeouts shall prevent:

Thread Exhaustion

Worker Exhaustion

Connection Pool Exhaustion

Cascading Failure

from propagating throughout the system.

END OF 60.47

60.48 CIRCUIT BREAKERS

Critical external dependencies may use circuit breakers.

The service shall temporarily stop calling a failing dependency and allow controlled recovery attempts.

END OF 60.48

60.49 BULKHEAD ISOLATION

High-cost operations shall be isolated from normal API workloads.

For example:

Normal API Workers

≠

Research Workers

≠

Document Processing Workers

≠

Experiment Workers

This prevents one workload from exhausting all system resources.

END OF 60.49

60.50 RESOURCE LIMITS

Every expensive service shall enforce limits.

Examples:

Maximum File Size

Maximum Research Duration

Maximum Experiment Runtime

Maximum Search Results

Maximum AI Context

Maximum Concurrent Jobs

Limits shall be configurable rather than hard-coded throughout the application.

END OF 60.50

60.51 SERVICE CACHING

Caching may be applied to stable or expensive data.

Suitable candidates include:

Configuration

Public Metadata

Repeated Knowledge Queries

Model Metadata

Permission Metadata

Frequently Used Reference Data

Sensitive user-specific data shall have carefully controlled cache scope.

END OF 60.51

60.52 CACHE INVALIDATION

Services modifying cached resources shall invalidate or update affected cache entries.

Cache invalidation shall be part of the resource lifecycle rather than an afterthought.

END OF 60.52

60.53 SERVICE SECURITY

Every service shall assume that upstream inputs may be invalid or malicious.

Security shall include:

Authentication Context

Authorization

Validation

Resource Isolation

Input Sanitization

Rate Limits

Auditability

Internal services shall not automatically trust one another merely because they operate inside the same network.

END OF 60.53

60.54 TENANT ISOLATION

If GSIR supports multiple organizations or tenants, service methods shall carry appropriate tenant context.

Request

↓

Tenant Context

↓

Authorization

↓

Service

↓

Repository

Queries shall prevent cross-tenant data access.

END OF 60.54

60.55 SERVICE OBSERVABILITY

Every important service operation shall be measurable.

Metrics shall include:

Invocation Count

Latency

Success Rate

Failure Rate

Dependency Latency

Retry Count

Queue Delay

Long-running operations shall additionally expose progress where possible.

END OF 60.55

60.56 SERVICE LOGGING

Service logs shall contain:

Request ID

Trace ID

Operation

Resource ID

Status

Duration

Error Code

Logs shall avoid storing sensitive scientific, user or authentication data unless explicitly required.

END OF 60.56

60.57 SERVICE TESTING

Services shall be tested independently from HTTP where possible.

Tests shall verify:

Business Rules

State Transitions

Authorization

Error Handling

Transaction Behavior

Dependency Failures

Retry Behavior

This allows domain logic to be tested without starting the complete application.

END OF 60.57

60.58 SERVICE CONTRACT TESTING

Service interfaces shall have contract tests where multiple implementations or independent consumers exist.

The purpose is to ensure that implementations continue to satisfy the expected interface.

END OF 60.58

60.59 SERVICE INTEGRATION TESTING

Integration tests shall verify combinations such as:

ResearchService

+

TaskService

+

Repository

+

Queue

and:

FileService

+

Storage

+

DocumentProcessing

+

TaskService

END OF 60.59

60.60 FAILURE INJECTION

Critical services shall be tested against controlled failures.

Examples:

Database Unavailable

Queue Unavailable

AI Provider Timeout

Storage Failure

Search Provider Failure

Network Timeout

Duplicate Event

The expected recovery behavior shall be defined for each case.

END OF 60.60

60.61 SERVICE DEPLOYMENT

Services shall be deployable with:

Configuration Validation

Health Checks

Dependency Checks

Migration Compatibility

Observability

Rollback Support

Deployment shall not depend on manual intervention for ordinary operations.

END OF 60.61

60.62 SERVICE SCALING

Services shall scale according to workload.

Example:

API

→ Scale by Request Load

Research Workers

→ Scale by Research Queue

Document Workers

→ Scale by Processing Queue

Experiment Workers

→ Scale by Execution Queue

Different workloads shall not be forced to scale identically.

END OF 60.62

60.63 COST CONTROL

Service architecture shall minimize unnecessary infrastructure consumption.

The system shall prefer:

Asynchronous Processing

Caching

Batching

Reuse

Efficient Queries

Appropriate Model Selection

Resource Limits

over uncontrolled scaling.

END OF 60.63

60.64 SERVICE MODULARITY

A service shall be split only when the separation provides a meaningful architectural benefit.

GSIR shall avoid creating excessive microservices merely for theoretical scalability.

END OF 60.64

60.65 MODULAR MONOLITH PRINCIPLE

The initial GSIR backend may remain a modular monolith while preserving strong domain boundaries.

One Deployment

├── Project Domain

├── Research Domain

├── Document Domain

├── Knowledge Domain

├── Experiment Domain

└── AI Domain

Individual domains may later be extracted into independent services if scale, reliability, ownership or deployment requirements justify it.

END OF 60.65

60.66 SERVICE EXTRACTION CRITERIA

A domain should be extracted only when there is a demonstrated need such as:

Independent Scaling

Independent Deployment

Resource Isolation

Different Reliability Requirements

Different Ownership

Strong Domain Boundary

Infrastructure Requirements

Code size alone shall not be sufficient justification.

END OF 60.66

60.67 INTERNAL API RULE

Internal services shall communicate through stable interfaces.

The database shall not become an uncontrolled communication mechanism between domains.

One domain shall not directly modify another domain's tables merely to avoid creating a service interface.

END OF 60.67

60.68 DOMAIN OWNERSHIP

Each major domain shall have clear ownership of its rules and primary data.

Example:

Research Domain

→ Research Lifecycle

Document Domain

→ Document Processing

Experiment Domain

→ Experiment Lifecycle

Knowledge Domain

→ Knowledge Objects

Cross-domain operations shall use defined service or event boundaries.

END OF 60.68

60.69 SERVICE ARCHITECTURE COMPLETION CRITERIA

The service architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Application services are separated from API routes.

- Domain services contain domain behavior.

- Repository access is isolated.

- Service dependencies are explicit.

- Long-running work is asynchronous.

- Tasks have explicit states.

- Events are supported where appropriate.

- Event processing is idempotent.

- Dead-letter handling exists.

- Timeouts are defined.

- Retry policies are defined.

- Expensive workloads are isolated.

- Resource limits exist.

- Tenant isolation is enforced where required.

- AI provider access is abstracted.

- Research execution is isolated.

- Document processing is isolated.

- Experiment execution is isolated.

- Usage and quota services exist.

- Audit events are supported.

- Service observability exists.

- Service-level testing exists.

- Failure scenarios are tested.

- Scaling strategies are defined.

- Cost-control mechanisms are implemented.

- Domain boundaries are documented.

- Service extraction criteria are defined.

END OF 60.69

60.70 FINAL SERVICE ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall use a domain-centered service architecture rather than allowing application behavior to become distributed randomly across API routes, database queries, background workers and external providers.

The intended architecture is:

API

↓

Application Services

↓

Domain Services

↓

Repositories / Adapters

↓

Infrastructure

              ↘

               Events

                 ↓

        Independent Consumers

This structure shall allow GSIR to begin as a cost-efficient modular backend while preserving the architectural boundaries required for future large-scale deployment.

END OF 60.70

PART 61 — DATABASE ARCHITECTURE, DATA MODEL, STORAGE STRATEGY AND DATA ACCESS DESIGN

61.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR database architecture shall provide a reliable, scalable and secure foundation for storing application data, research data, scientific knowledge, provenance, user information, task state and system metadata.

The database architecture shall prioritize:

Data Integrity

Consistency

Security

Traceability

Scalability

Performance

Recoverability

Maintainability

The database shall remain an internal infrastructure component and shall never be exposed directly to frontend clients.

END OF 61.1

61.2 DATABASE ARCHITECTURE

The logical data architecture shall follow:

Frontend

↓

API

↓

Application Service

↓

Domain Service

↓

Repository

↓

Database

Other storage systems may be used alongside the primary database:

Database

├── Relational Data

├── Search Index

├── Vector Index

├── Object Storage

├── Cache

└── Event / Job Storage

END OF 61.2

61.3 PRIMARY DATABASE

GSIR shall use a relational database as the authoritative transactional store for core application data.

The relational database shall contain data requiring:

Transactions

Relationships

Constraints

Consistency

Authorization

Auditability

Structured Queries

The exact database engine shall be selected according to deployment, scale, operational and compatibility requirements.

END OF 61.3

61.4 DATABASE RESPONSIBILITY

The primary database shall own authoritative records such as:

Users

Organizations

Projects

Conversations

Messages

Files Metadata

Research Runs

Sources

Evidence

Experiments

Tasks

Notifications

Audit Records

Configuration

Large binary files shall not normally be stored directly inside relational tables.

END OF 61.4

61.5 DATA STORAGE MODEL

GSIR shall use multiple storage mechanisms according to data characteristics.

Relational Database

→ Transactional Data

Object Storage

→ Files and Large Artifacts

Search Index

→ Full-Text Retrieval

Vector Store

→ Embeddings and Semantic Retrieval

Cache

→ Temporary / Frequently Accessed Data

Queue

→ Asynchronous Work

No single storage technology shall be forced to perform every workload.

END OF 61.5

61.6 DATABASE SCHEMA ORGANIZATION

The schema shall be organized around GSIR domains.

Logical groups may include:

Identity

Projects

Conversations

Documents

Research

Knowledge

Experiments

Tasks

Notifications

Administration

Audit

Physical schema organization may vary according to the selected database engine.

END OF 61.6

61.7 IDENTITY DATA

User

Organization

Membership

Role

Permission

Session

Authentication Identity

Identity records shall contain only the information necessary for platform functionality.

A user record may contain:

User ID

Status

Updated At

↓

↓

User

shall establish the relationship.

↓

↓

↓

↓

├── Execution 1
