75.96 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT

The GSIR Scientific Knowledge Graph Engine shall enforce:

EVERY IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE OBJECT MUST HAVE AN IDENTITY.

EVERY IMPORTANT CLAIM MUST HAVE TRACEABLE EVIDENCE.

EVERY IMPORTANT RELATIONSHIP MUST HAVE PROVENANCE.

SOURCE STATEMENTS MUST REMAIN DISTINGUISHABLE FROM GSIR CONCLUSIONS.

CONTRADICTORY KNOWLEDGE MUST BE PRESERVED, NOT SILENTLY DELETED.

UNKNOWN MUST REMAIN DIFFERENT FROM FALSE.

CORRELATION MUST REMAIN DIFFERENT FROM CAUSATION.

INFERENCE MUST REMAIN DIFFERENT FROM DIRECT OBSERVATION.

EVERY IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE STATE MUST BE VERSIONED.

EVERY RETRACTION MUST PROPAGATE THROUGH IMPACT ANALYSIS.

EVERY AI-GENERATED CONCLUSION MUST BE TRACEABLE TO ITS EVIDENCE.

EVERY SCIENTIFIC ANSWER MUST BE CAPABLE OF TRACING BACK TO ITS SOURCES.

The resulting GSIR knowledge layer shall provide the foundation for evidence-grounded scientific reasoning, contradiction analysis, multi-hop discovery, provenance-aware AI, research memory, hypothesis generation, and eventually autonomous scientific investigation. Its design shall preserve the distinction between source information, extracted evidence, validated claims, and inferred knowledge rather than collapsing them into a single undifferentiated graph. 

END OF PART 75.

PART 76 — SCIENTIFIC DATA GOVERNANCE, SECURITY, ACCESS CONTROL, PRIVACY AND COMPLIANCE ARCHITECTURE

76.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Data Governance Architecture shall define how scientific data, research objects, knowledge, files, experiments, workflows, AI inputs, AI outputs, metadata, and provenance are controlled throughout their complete lifecycle.

The governance system shall ensure:

Security

Privacy

Ownership

Access Control

Data Quality

Provenance

Retention

Compliance

Interoperability

Scientific Integrity

FAIR principles emphasize that research objects should be findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable, while sensitive data may require authentication and authorization and still retain rich metadata. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/sdata201618))

76.97 GOVERNANCE COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR governance architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Data ownership is defined.

- Data stewardship is defined.

- Classification exists.

- Classification metadata exists.

- Classification propagation exists.

- Sensitive-data policies exist.

- Privacy-by-design requirements exist.

- Data minimization exists.

- Authentication is centralized.

- Authorization is enforced.

- Role-based access is supported.

- Attribute-based access is supported where required.

- Resource-level authorization exists.

- Field-level protection exists where required.

- Service-to-service authorization exists.

- Least privilege is enforced.

- AI access is governed.

- AI data routing is policy-controlled.

- Redaction is supported.

- Pseudonymization is supported where required.

- Consent management exists where required.

- Purpose limitation is enforced.

- External sharing is controlled.

- Export control exists.

- Tenant isolation exists where required.

- Data residency rules are supported.

- Retention policies exist.

- Legal holds are supported.

- Archiving exists.

- Deletion workflows exist.

- Dependency-aware deletion exists.

- Backup governance exists.

- Provenance is preserved.

- Data quality governance exists.

- Policy engine exists.

- Policy versioning exists.

- Governance exceptions are controlled.

- Security incidents are tracked.

- Audit records are protected.

- Access reviews exist.

- Stale access is removed.

- Autonomous research is governed.

- Laboratory operations are governed.

- External APIs are governed.

- RAG access is governed.

- Knowledge graph access is governed.

- Memory access is governed.

- AI training-data eligibility is governed.

- Policy simulation exists.

- Governance monitoring exists.

- Governance metrics exist.

- Fail-secure behavior exists for high-risk operations.

END OF 76.97

76.98 FINAL GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLE

The GSIR governance system shall ensure that access to scientific information is determined by policy rather than convenience.

The complete decision path shall be:

WHO

↓

WANTS TO DO WHAT

↓

TO WHICH RESOURCE

↓

FOR WHAT PURPOSE

↓

UNDER WHICH CLASSIFICATION

↓

UNDER WHICH POLICY

↓

WITH WHICH PERMISSION

↓

IN WHICH ENVIRONMENT

↓

WITH WHICH DATA

↓

UNDER WHICH AUDIT REQUIREMENTS

Only when all applicable controls permit the operation shall execution proceed.

END OF 76.98

76.99 FINAL DATA GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENT

GSIR shall preserve the following fundamental rules:

NO UNAUTHORIZED DATA ACCESS.

NO UNCONTROLLED DATA SHARING.

NO UNTRACKED SENSITIVE DATA PROCESSING.

NO UNGOVERNED AI ACCESS.

NO SILENT POLICY OVERRIDES.

NO UNEXPLAINED DATA DELETION.

NO LOSS OF PROVENANCE.

NO CROSS-TENANT DATA LEAKAGE.

NO TRUST BASED ONLY ON NETWORK LOCATION.

NO AI AGENT WITH UNBOUNDED AUTHORITY.

The governance architecture shall operate across the full research lifecycle:

COLLECT

↓

CLASSIFY

↓

STORE

↓

PROCESS

↓

ANALYZE

↓

SHARE

↓

PUBLISH

↓

ARCHIVE

↓

DELETE / RETAIN

At every stage, the system shall preserve appropriate security, privacy, ownership, provenance, licensing, access and scientific-integrity controls.

END OF 76.99

76.100 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE

The GSIR governance layer shall become a cross-cutting control system for the complete platform.

                         GSIR PLATFORM

          ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐

       DATA                  AI               RESEARCH

The final GSIR architecture shall therefore make governance a foundational capability rather than an administrative layer added after implementation.

Every significant scientific resource and every significant AI operation shall remain subject to explicit rules for identity, authorization, classification, privacy, provenance, retention, sharing, scientific integrity and accountability.

PART 76 COMPLETED.

PART 77 — GSIR TRUST, PROVENANCE INTEGRITY, REPRODUCIBILITY AND RESEARCH ASSURANCE ARCHITECTURE

77.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Research Assurance Layer shall ensure that scientific results, data transformations, AI operations, models, workflows, experiments, evidence and knowledge can be independently inspected, reproduced, verified and trusted.

Scientific data governance increasingly requires lifecycle controls spanning stakeholders, processes and governance elements, while provenance integrity is particularly important for scientific workflows and AI systems.

77.95 ASSURANCE COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR assurance architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Every critical research object has an identity.

- Every important artifact has integrity verification.

- Every critical transformation has provenance.

- Every reproducibility-sensitive execution captures its environment.

- Models have versioned lineage.

- Software dependencies are recorded.

- AI operations have execution provenance.

- Retrieval context can be traced where required.

- Claims have evidence chains.

- Results have computational lineage.

- Reproduction can be executed independently.

- Reproduction failures can be diagnosed.

- Trust can be revoked.

- Downstream impact can be calculated.

- Verification status is explicit.

- Human and automated verification are distinguished.

- Assurance policies are versioned.

- Critical failures stop trust-sensitive operations.

- Audit packages can be generated.

- Assurance records are themselves protected.

77.97 FINAL RESEARCH ASSURANCE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall never treat a scientific result as trustworthy merely because an AI model, researcher, workflow or database produced it.

Trust shall be established through evidence:

IDENTITY

+

PROVENANCE

+

INTEGRITY

+

EXECUTION CONTEXT

+

VALIDATION

+

REPRODUCIBILITY

+

ATTESTATION

This architecture makes provenance and verification operational rather than documentary, which is particularly important as scientific systems increasingly combine data-intensive computing, AI models, automated workflows and multi-stage research pipelines. 

END OF PART 77

PART 78 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC WORKFLOW ORCHESTRATION AND EXECUTION ARCHITECTURE

78.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Workflow Orchestration Layer shall provide the execution infrastructure for scientific workflows, AI workflows, data-processing pipelines, experiments, simulations, evaluations and autonomous research tasks.

The architecture shall capture the complete computational process, including data, code, parameters, environment, workflow and execution state, because these elements are fundamental to reproducible computational research.

78.99 WORKFLOW COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR workflow architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Workflows are versioned.

- Workflow graphs are validated.

- Dependencies are explicit.

- Parameters are recorded.

- Inputs and outputs are typed.

- Execution plans are generated.

- Resource-aware scheduling exists.

- Parallel execution exists.

- Worker capabilities are tracked.

- Execution states are explicit.

- Step states are explicit.

- Sandboxed execution exists.

- AI tool execution is controlled.

- External API execution is controlled.

- Model execution is traceable.

- Human approval gates are supported.

- Retry policies exist.

- Idempotency is supported.

- Checkpointing exists.

- Recovery exists.

- Cancellation exists.

- Timeouts exist.

- Structured execution events exist.

- Monitoring exists.

- Cost tracking exists.

- Cost budgets exist.

- Multi-tenant isolation exists where required.

- Workflow provenance is automatic.

- Execution environments are captured.

- Intermediate artifacts can be retained.

- Workflow cloning exists.

- Workflow templates exist.

- Parameter sweeps are supported.

- Optimization workflows are supported.

- Subworkflows are supported.

- Dependency impact analysis exists.

- Revalidation is supported.

- Reproduction is supported.

- Governance is enforced.

- Assurance is connected.

- AI workflow creation is controlled.

- Self-improvement workflows are isolated and evaluated.

- Worker failures can be recovered.

- Execution reports can be generated.

- Complete workflow provenance can be queried.

END OF 78.99

78.100 FINAL WORKFLOW PRINCIPLE

The GSIR workflow engine shall transform scientific intent into controlled, observable, reproducible execution.

SCIENTIFIC INTENT

        ↓

WORKFLOW

        ↓

VALIDATION

        ↓

PLAN

        ↓

SCHEDULE

        ↓

EXECUTE

        ↓

OBSERVE

        ↓

VALIDATE

        ↓

PROVENANCE

        ↓

ASSURE

        ↓

SCIENTIFIC RESULT

The workflow system shall therefore function as the execution backbone connecting GSIR's data, AI, experiments, tools, governance, provenance, assurance and research-intelligence layers.

PART 79 — GSIR RESEARCH RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, COMPUTE ORCHESTRATION AND RESOURCE OPTIMIZATION ARCHITECTURE

79.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Resource Management Architecture shall control the computational, storage, AI, network, laboratory and execution resources required by research workflows.

The resource system shall ensure:

Availability

Cost Control

Performance

Isolation

Scalability

Observability

Modern scientific platforms increasingly combine heterogeneous compute, data, workflow and AI resources, making centralized resource governance important for reliable execution.

79.97 RESOURCE COMPLETION CRITERIA

- All major resource types are represented.

- A central resource registry exists.

- Resource capabilities are discoverable.

- Resource health is monitored.

- Resource capacity is measurable.

- CPU scheduling exists.

- GPU scheduling exists.

- Storage allocation exists.

- AI resources are represented.

- Laboratory resources are represented.

- Task requirements are structured.

- Resource matching exists.

- Scheduling exists.

- Fair-share allocation exists.

- Priority scheduling exists.

- Reservations exist.

- Resource locking exists where required.

- Resource leases exist where required.

- Timeouts exist.

- Preemption exists where supported.

- Data locality is considered.

- Data residency is enforced.

- Privacy-aware scheduling exists.

- AI fallback exists.

- GPU sharing is controlled where supported.

- Quotas exist.

- Budgets exist.

- Cost accounting exists.

- Usage accounting exists.

- Cost forecasting exists.

- Laboratory reservation is integrated.

- Resource migration is supported where possible.

- Workload isolation exists.

- Autoscaling is supported where available.

- Resource policies are enforced.

- Agent resource access is bounded.

- Resource observability exists.

- Resource events exist.

- Failure recovery exists.

- Resource quarantine exists.

- Computational sandboxing exists.

- Network restrictions exist.

- Secret isolation exists.

- Data isolation exists.

- Resource cleanup exists.

- Leak detection exists.

- Capacity forecasting exists.

- Scheduler simulation exists.

- Resource-policy testing exists.

- Resource chaos testing exists.

- Resource APIs exist.

Every execution shall operate within explicit:

PART 79 COMPLETED.

PART 80 — GSIR DATA AND KNOWLEDGE PROVENANCE, LINEAGE AND RESEARCH TRACEABILITY ARCHITECTURE

80.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Provenance Architecture shall provide a complete, machine-readable record of how research data, knowledge, analyses, models, decisions and results are produced.

The system shall capture not only the final result, but also the chain of inputs, transformations, workflows, tools, parameters and environments responsible for producing that result. This approach is central to computational reproducibility and is used by established scientific workflow systems. 

END OF 80.1

80.100 FINAL PROVENANCE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall treat provenance as a first-class research infrastructure rather than an after-the-fact log.

Every important scientific result should have a machine-traceable path back to the data, code, models, workflows, parameters, tools, environments and decisions that produced it.

RESULT

  ↓

WHAT PRODUCED IT?

  ↓

HOW WAS IT PRODUCED?

  ↓

WITH WHICH DATA?

  ↓

WITH WHICH CODE?

  ↓

WITH WHICH MODEL?

  ↓

WITH WHICH PARAMETERS?

  ↓

IN WHICH ENVIRONMENT?

  ↓

VALIDATED HOW?

  ↓

CAN IT BE REPRODUCED?

This provenance layer shall become the connective tissue between GSIR's workflow engine, resource infrastructure, knowledge system, AI reasoning architecture, experimentation system, governance layer and research-assurance system.

END OF PART 80

PART 81 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC DATA FABRIC, DATA LIFECYCLE AND INTELLIGENT DATA ORCHESTRATION ARCHITECTURE

81.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Data Fabric shall provide the unified data-management layer connecting research data, documents, datasets, experimental measurements, computational outputs, AI-generated artifacts, metadata, knowledge objects and external data sources.

Identity

Version

Lineage

Access Control

Quality

Context

Provenance

Reproducibility

Modern scientific workflow architectures increasingly treat data management, provenance, resource allocation and workflow execution as interconnected layers rather than isolated subsystems.

81.98 DATA FABRIC COMPLETION CRITERIA

The architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Multiple scientific data types are supported.

- External sources can be connected.

- Data ingestion is controlled.

- Data identity exists.

- Integrity verification exists.

- Data versioning exists.

- Snapshots exist.

- Schemas are represented.

- Schema validation exists.

- Data quality validation exists.

- Data quarantine exists.

- Data classification exists.

- Access control exists.

- Project isolation exists.

- Encryption requirements are enforced.

- Multi-tier storage exists.

- Data lifecycle management exists.

- Retention policies exist.

- Controlled deletion exists.

- Dependency checks exist.

- Data catalog exists.

- Semantic discovery exists.

- Metadata indexing exists.

- Multimodal data is supported.

- AI retrieval is controlled.

- Retrieval provenance exists.

- Data federation exists.

- Data locality is supported.

- Large-data transfer is supported.

- Transfer verification exists.

- Caching exists.

- Cache invalidation exists.

- Raw data preservation exists.

- Derived-data lineage exists.

- Reproducible transformation metadata exists.

- Workflow integration exists.

- Resource-scheduler integration exists.

- Knowledge-graph integration exists.

- Research-object integration exists.

- Data quality gates exist.

- Data release controls exist.

- Data export/import tracking exists.

- Connector security exists.

- Data monitoring exists.

- Data events exist.

- Audit records exist.

- AI-agent data access is governed.

- Data minimization is supported.

- Purpose binding is supported where required.

- Data residency is enforced.

- Synchronization is controlled.

- Conflict detection exists.

- Consistency models are explicit.

- Backup exists.

- Restoration exists.

- Disaster recovery exists.

- RPO/RTO policies exist for critical data.

- Data APIs exist.

- Data database entities exist.

- Data provenance connects the complete lifecycle.

81.100 FINAL ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT

The GSIR Data Fabric shall become the authoritative data-management backbone connecting the research platform's workflows, AI systems, experiments, resource infrastructure, knowledge graph, provenance system and assurance architecture.

       └────────────────────┼────────────────────┘

                            ▼

                       TRUSTED RESULT

The architecture shall allow GSIR to move scientific information efficiently across heterogeneous storage, compute, AI and experimental environments while maintaining identity, integrity, lineage, governance and reproducibility throughout the complete research lifecycle. This separation of data management from higher-level AI and workflow orchestration also supports modular evolution and interoperability with existing scientific workflow systems.

PART 82 — GSIR DISTRIBUTED AND FEDERATED RESEARCH EXECUTION ARCHITECTURE

82.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Distributed Research Execution Architecture shall allow research workloads, AI services, datasets, computational resources, scientific instruments and workflows to operate across multiple execution environments while maintaining a single logical research system.

The architecture shall support:

Local

On-Premise

Cloud

HPC

GPU Clusters

Edge

Laboratory

Remote Facilities

Federated Research Sites

Modern scientific-workflow architectures increasingly require coordination across heterogeneous Edge, Cloud and HPC environments while preserving reproducibility, provenance, security and local autonomy.

16. Distributed execution state exists.

18. Federated events exist.

20. Site failure handling exists.

21. Remote checkpoints exist.

22. Artifact integrity verification exists.

23. Federated provenance exists.

24. Federated knowledge relationships exist.

25. Facility agents are supported.

26. Agent authorization is enforced.

27. Zero-trust principles are implemented.

28. Local policies can reject requests.

29. Federated scheduling exists.

30. Two-level scheduling exists.

31. Federated queues are supported.

32. Distributed experiments are supported.

33. Instrument authorization exists.

34. Federated analytics are supported.

35. Federated model evaluation is supported.

36. Protocol versioning exists.

37. Conflict resolution exists.

38. Network partition recovery exists.

39. Federation chaos testing exists.

40. Federation security testing exists.

41. Federation performance monitoring exists.

42. Federation cost controls exist.

43. Resource optimization spans sites.

44. Workflow integration exists.

48. Self-improvement experiments remain controlled.

PART 83 — GSIR DATA LINEAGE, PROVENANCE AND RESEARCH TRACEABILITY ARCHITECTURE

83.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Data Lineage and Provenance Architecture shall maintain a complete, machine-readable history of how research data, models, code, workflows, experiments and results are created, transformed, evaluated and reused.

The architecture shall make it possible to answer:

Where did this result come from?

Which data produced it?

Which version of the data was used?

Which code executed?

Which model was used?

Which parameters were applied?

Which workflow generated it?

Who initiated it?

When did it happen?

What transformations occurred?

What evidence supports the result?

END OF 83.1

  ↓

  ↓

Every transition shall be traceable.

83.98 COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR provenance architecture shall be considered complete when:

- Research objects have provenance identities.

- Data lineage is captured.

- Workflow lineage is captured.

- Execution lineage is captured.

- Code lineage is captured.

- Model lineage is captured.

- Experiment lineage is captured.

- Tool lineage is captured.

- Artifact lineage is captured.

- Parameter lineage is captured.

- Environment lineage is captured.

- Version-aware lineage exists.

- Forward lineage queries exist.

- Backward lineage queries exist.

- Impact analysis exists.

- Provenance events are append-oriented.

- Integrity verification exists.

- Provenance completeness is measured.

- Reproducibility information is connected.

- Human actions are traceable.

- AI actions are traceable.

- AI and human actions are distinguishable.

- Sensitive lineage is protected.

- Access control exists.

- Lineage visualization exists.

- Lineage filtering exists.

- Provenance reports exist.

- Reproduction reports exist.

- Audit reports exist.

- External provenance can be classified.

- Imported provenance is distinguished from verified provenance.

- Lineage anomalies can be detected.

- Temporal consistency is checked.

- Reconstructed lineage is clearly labeled.

- No false certainty is presented.

- Provenance integrates with validation.

- Provenance integrates with assurance.

- Provenance integrates with governance.

- Provenance integrates with the knowledge graph.

- Provenance integrates with research search.

- Provenance integrates with research memory.

- Provenance scales to high-volume execution.

- Provenance events can survive temporary service failure.

- Event replay is idempotent.

- Critical provenance is backed up.

- Disaster recovery preserves research history.

END OF PART 83,

PART 85 — GSIR RESEARCH KNOWLEDGE GRAPH AND KNOWLEDGE CONTINUITY ARCHITECTURE

85.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Knowledge Graph shall connect research knowledge across documents, papers, datasets, experiments, hypotheses, methods, models, results, claims, citations, projects and AI interactions.

Knowledge-centric architecture is increasingly recognized as a foundation for research operating systems because it preserves continuity across fragmented research workflows. 

END OF 85.1

GSIR shall not treat uploaded files as isolated objects.

   ↓

   ↓

Research Knowledge Graph

   ↓

Reasoning

85.46 KNOWLEDGE GRAPH DATABASE

PART 88 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC DATA GOVERNANCE, FAIR DATA AND RESEARCH DATA MANAGEMENT ARCHITECTURE

88.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Scientific Data Governance Architecture shall control how research data is created, imported, classified, validated, stored, discovered, accessed, processed, shared, cited, preserved and reused.

GSIR shall follow FAIR principles—Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable—while enforcing security, privacy, provenance and research-specific governance. FAIR principles apply not only to datasets but also to algorithms, tools and workflows.

PART 90 — GSIR RESEARCH DATA LIFECYCLE AND DATA GOVERNANCE ARCHITECTURE

The GSIR Research Data Lifecycle Architecture shall manage scientific data from creation or acquisition through processing, analysis, sharing, preservation, reuse and controlled disposal.

90.100 FINAL DATA PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall treat scientific data as a governed research asset rather than merely as files.

Every important dataset shall remain connected to its:

SOURCE

+

OWNER

+

VERSION

+

QUALITY

+

WORKFLOW

+

PARAMETERS

+

PROVENANCE

+

RESULTS

+

RESEARCH CONTEXT

This creates a continuous data lineage from acquisition to scientific conclusion and supports traceability, reproducibility, quality assessment and reuse.

END OF PART 90

PART 91 — GSIR RESEARCH KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT AND KNOWLEDGE GRAPH ARCHITECTURE

91.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Knowledge Management Architecture shall convert disconnected research information into a connected, searchable, traceable and machine-actionable research knowledge system.

The system shall connect:

Papers

Datasets

Documents

Experiments

Protocols

Samples

Methods

Models

Researchers

Projects

Workflows

Results

Claims

Publications

AI Conversations

The architecture shall support both human researchers and computational agents. FAIR principles specifically emphasize making research resources discoverable and usable by machines as well as humans.

PART 92 — GSIR RESEARCH REPRODUCIBILITY, PROVENANCE AND RESULT TRACEABILITY ARCHITECTURE

92.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Reproducibility Architecture shall ensure that scientific results can be traced back to the complete chain of data, methods, code, models, parameters, environments, workflows and decisions used to produce them.

Current research-reproducibility guidance emphasizes transparent methods, data, code, workflows and computational environments as core requirements.

END OF 92.1

92.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

Every important GSIR result shall answer:

What was produced?

Why was it produced?

Which data was used?

Which method was used?

Which code was executed?

Which model was used?

Which parameters were used?

Which environment was used?

Who performed or approved it?

When was it performed?

Can it be reproduced?

END OF 92.2

92.24 REPRODUCIBILITY LEVELS

GSIR shall distinguish:

LEVEL 0 — Undocumented

LEVEL 1 — Documented

LEVEL 2 — Traceable

LEVEL 3 — Re-executable

LEVEL 4 — Reproducible

LEVEL 5 — Independently Verifiable

END OF 92.24

92.25 LEVEL 0 — UNDOCUMENTED

The result lacks sufficient information for meaningful reconstruction.

END OF 92.25

92.26 LEVEL 1 — DOCUMENTED

The method and major inputs are described but execution cannot necessarily be reconstructed.

END OF 92.26

92.27 LEVEL 2 — TRACEABLE

Data, workflow and execution lineage are available.

END OF 92.27

92.28 LEVEL 3 — RE-EXECUTABLE

The system has sufficient technical assets to execute the workflow again.

END OF 92.28

92.29 LEVEL 4 — REPRODUCIBLE

Re-execution produces equivalent results within defined scientific tolerances.

END OF 92.29

92.30 LEVEL 5 — INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE

An authorized independent researcher can inspect the evidence and independently verify the result.

END OF 92.30

92.99 COMPLETION CRITERIA

The GSIR Reproducibility Architecture shall be considered complete when:

1. Research provenance is captured.

2. Data lineage is maintained.

3. Workflow lineage is maintained.

4. Code versions are recorded.

5. Model versions are recorded.

6. Parameters are recorded.

7. Execution environments are recorded.

8. Execution manifests exist.

9. Artifact integrity hashes exist.

10. Workflow signatures are supported.

11. Reproducibility levels are defined.

12. Re-execution is supported.

13. Result comparison is supported.

14. Numerical tolerance is supported.

 

15. AI provenance is supported.

 

16. External API provenance is supported.

 

17. Changing data can be snapshotted.

 

18. Irreproducible components are identified.

 

19. Conditional reproducibility is supported.

 

20. Provenance is queryable.

 

21. Backward tracing is supported.

 

22. Forward tracing is supported.

 

23. Impact analysis is supported.

 

24. Dependency invalidation is supported.

 

25. Provenance quality can be measured.

 

26. Reproducibility reports can be generated.

 

27. Research objects can be versioned.

 

28. Publication snapshots can be created.

 

29. Claim-to-evidence relationships can be maintained.

 

30. AI-generated claims can be traced.

 

31. Workflow provenance is automatic.

 

32. Resource provenance is captured.

 

33. Experiment provenance is captured.

 

34. Transformation provenance is captured.

 

35. Model-training provenance is captured.

 

36. Visualization provenance is captured.

 

37. Report-generation provenance is captured.

 

38. Human decisions can be recorded.

 

39. Approval events are traceable.

 

40. Provenance access control exists.

 

41. Provenance recovery is supported.

 

42. Reproducibility testing exists.

 

43. Reproducibility regression detection exists.

 

44. Reproducibility status is visible.

 

45. Provenance APIs exist.

 

 

END OF 92.99

 

92.100 FINAL REPRODUCIBILITY PRINCIPLE

 

GSIR shall treat reproducibility as a system property rather than a documentation task.

 `DATA + CODE + MODEL + PARAMETERS + ENVIRONMENT + WORKFLOW + EXECUTION + PROVENANCE + VALIDATION = REPRODUCIBLE RESEARCH ` 

The objective is not merely to preserve files. GSIR shall preserve the complete evidence chain required to understand, trace, reconstruct, validate and independently examine scientific results.

 

END OF PART 92

PART 93 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC PROVENANCE, LINEAGE AND REPRODUCIBILITY ARCHITECTURE

93.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Provenance Architecture shall automatically record the complete origin, transformation, execution and dependency history of research objects.

Scientific workflow systems can improve reproducibility by automatically connecting results to the computational processes that produced them.

93.90 FINAL PROVENANCE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall not merely store scientific results.

It shall preserve the path by which those results came into existence.

  ↑

ANALYSIS

  ↑

WORKFLOW

  ↑

PARAMETERS

  ↑

CODE / MODEL

  ↑

DATA

  ↑

EXPERIMENT

  ↑

SOURCE

This makes provenance a foundational infrastructure layer connecting GSIR's workflows, knowledge system, AI system, experiments, documents, datasets, results and publications.

PART 94 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE GRAPH AND RESEARCH RELATIONSHIP ARCHITECTURE

94.1 PURPOSE

The GSIR Scientific Knowledge Graph shall connect research entities, concepts, evidence, documents, datasets, experiments, models, workflows, people, projects and results into a continuously queryable research relationship system.

The architecture shall make scientific knowledge machine-readable, discoverable, traceable and reusable. FAIR principles explicitly support applying these concepts beyond datasets to workflows and other research objects.

This follows the important FAIR principle that research data, algorithms and workflows should be treated as interconnected research objects and made findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable where appropriate. 

### One Core Rule

Do not create a separate database for every feature.

Use one integrated GSIR data architecture:

                    GSIR CORE

                       │

        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐

        ↓              ↓              ↓

     IDENTITY       RESEARCH       KNOWLEDGE

        │              │              │

        └──────────────┼──────────────┘

                       ↓

                    WORKFLOW

                       ↓

              ┌────────┴────────┐

              ↓                 ↓

             AI             EXPERIMENT

              │                 │

              └────────┬────────┘

                       ↓

                    ANALYSIS

                       ↓

                   RESULTS

                       ↓

                  PUBLICATION

                       ↓

                 PROVENANCE

### Final Storage Decision

PostgreSQL = authoritative structured system of record.

Object Storage = original files, documents, datasets, large artifacts.

Redis = cache, sessions, queues and temporary state.

Vector Search = embeddings and semantic retrieval.

Search Engine = hybrid/full-text search when PostgreSQL search is insufficient.

Knowledge Graph = introduced when relationship/graph workloads justify it, not as a duplicate database for ordinary records.

### Final Data Relationship Rule

Everything important must connect through common IDs:

Organization

    ↓

Workspace

    ↓

Project

    ↓

Research Question

    ↓

Experiment / Workflow

    ↓

Data

    ↓

Analysis

    ↓

Result

    ↓

Evidence

    ↓

Report

    ↓

Publication

And simultaneously:

EVERY OBJECT

     ↓

VERSION

     ↓

PROVENANCE

     ↓

USER / AI / TOOL

     ↓

TIMESTAMP

This prevents the architecture from becoming a collection of disconnected applications.

### Final Task Decision

GSIR should use one unified task system, not separate task tables for AI tasks, research tasks, workflow tasks, document tasks, etc.

Task

├── Research Task

├── AI Task

├── Workflow Task

├── Analysis Task

├── Document Task

├── Experiment Task

└── System Task

The task type determines behavior; the underlying task infrastructure remains shared.

### Final AI Decision

Do not create unnecessary independent agents.

Use:

GSIR AI CORE

      ↓

Reasoning / Planning

      ↓

Tools

      ↓

Knowledge

      ↓

Workflow

      ↓

Specialized capabilities

Specialized agents should only exist when a capability genuinely requires independent planning, permissions, lifecycle or execution.

### Final Principle

From this point forward, all remaining GSIR parts should reference this master architecture instead of inventing new foundational data structures.

That means:

No duplicate User system.
No duplicate Project system.
No duplicate File system.
No duplicate Task system.
No duplicate AI conversation system.
No duplicate Workflow system.
No duplicate Experiment system.
No duplicate Provenance system.
No duplicate Resource system.

The architecture becomes one connected GSIR Research Operating System, rather than dozens of separate applications.

#  MODEL ORCHESTRATION AND INTELLIGENT MODEL ROUTING changes ask approval

## 85.1 Purpose

GSIR shall support multiple AI models through one unified model orchestration layer.

The system must not depend permanently on a single model or provider. GSIR shall automatically select the most suitable model based on task requirements, quality, latency, cost, context size, availability, privacy, and resource limits.

## 85.2 Model Architecture

GSIR AI Request

      ↓

AI Gateway

      ↓

Task Classification

      ↓

Model Router

      ↓

Model Selection

      ↓

Provider Adapter

      ↓

AI Model

      ↓

Response Validation

      ↓

Final Response

The application must communicate with the AI Gateway, not directly with individual model providers.

## 85.3 Provider Abstraction

Backend structure:

src/ai/

├── ai.module.ts

├── gateway/

│   ├── ai.gateway.ts

│   └── ai-request.service.ts

├── router/

│   ├── model-router.service.ts

│   ├── routing-policy.service.ts

│   └── model-selector.service.ts

├── providers/

│   ├── openai/

│   ├── anthropic/

│   ├── google/

│   ├── deepseek/

│   ├── ollama/

│   └── openrouter/

├── models/

│   ├── model-registry.service.ts

│   └── model-capability.service.ts

└── validation/

    └── ai-response-validator.service.ts

All providers must implement the same internal interface.

## 85.4 Model Registry

GSIR shall maintain a model registry containing:

Model

├── model_id

├── provider

├── capability

├── context_limit

├── reasoning_level

├── latency_profile

├── cost_profile

├── tool_support

├── vision_support

├── embedding_support

├── availability

├── reliability_score

└── version

The registry allows GSIR to choose models using actual capabilities rather than hard-coded names.

## 85.5 Task-Based Routing

Different tasks require different models.

Examples:

Simple classification

→ Small/fast model

Document summarization

→ Efficient long-context model

Complex scientific reasoning

→ High-reasoning model

Coding

→ Code-specialized model

Vision/document analysis

→ Vision-capable model

Embedding generation

→ Embedding model

Local/private processing

→ Local model

GSIR shall avoid using an expensive model when a smaller model can produce an equivalent acceptable result.

## 85.6 Intelligent Routing Factors

Model selection shall consider:

Task Type

+

Required Quality

+

Context Length

+

Reasoning Complexity

+

Latency Requirement

+

Cost Budget

+

Privacy Requirement

+

Tool Requirements

+

Model Availability

+

Historical Reliability

Conceptually:

Model Score =

Quality

+ Capability Match

+ Reliability

+ Availability

- Cost

- Latency

- Risk

Weights shall be configurable by GSIR administrators.

## 85.7 Tiered Model Strategy

GSIR shall support model tiers:

Tier 0 — Local / Tiny Model

        ↓

Tier 1 — Small Efficient Model

        ↓

Tier 2 — General High-Quality Model

        ↓

Tier 3 — Advanced Reasoning Model

GSIR should normally begin with the lowest-cost model capable of completing the task.

Escalation occurs only when necessary.

Small Model

    ↓

Validation

    ↓

Pass → Finish

    ↓

Fail/Low Confidence

    ↓

Larger Model

    ↓

Validation

This reduces token consumption and operating cost.

## 85.8 Model Fallback

A model failure must not automatically become an application failure.

Fallback sequence:

Primary Model

     ↓

Timeout/Error

     ↓

Secondary Model

     ↓

Timeout/Error

     ↓

Tertiary Model

     ↓

Safe Failure Response

Fallback rules shall consider:

- provider outage,

- timeout,

- rate limits,

- invalid response,

- context limitations,

- tool incompatibility,

- safety/policy restrictions.

## 85.9 Model Reliability Tracking

GSIR shall continuously measure model performance.

Metrics include:

success_rate

error_rate

latency

token_usage

cost

validation_failure_rate

tool_success_rate

user_feedback_score

hallucination_detection_rate

These metrics shall influence future routing decisions.

A model that historically performs poorly for a specific task should automatically receive a lower routing priority for that task.

## 85.10 Cost Optimization

GSIR shall implement cost-aware inference.

The router should optimize:

Required Quality

      ↓

Minimum Computational Cost

Possible techniques:

small-model-first

context compression

prompt optimization

retrieval filtering

response length control

result caching

batch processing

local inference

model escalation only when needed

Repeated identical or equivalent requests should reuse cached results where correctness permits.

## 85.11 Privacy-Aware Routing

Some data must not leave the user's approved environment.

Routing policies may specify:

Public Data

→ External Models Allowed

Sensitive Organization Data

→ Approved Providers Only

Private Research Data

→ Approved Private/Local Models

Restricted Data

→ Local Processing Only

The router must evaluate privacy policy before sending context to a provider.

## 85.12 Context-Aware Routing

Before selecting a model, GSIR shall calculate the request's context requirements.

Input

  ↓

Token Estimation

  ↓

Required Context

  ↓

Available Model Context

  ↓

Context Fit

If the context is too large, GSIR may:

compress context

→ summarize

→ retrieve relevant sections

→ process in chunks

→ use long-context model

## 85.13 Model Ensemble

For high-value tasks GSIR may use multiple models.

Example:

Model A → Answer

Model B → Independent Answer

Model C → Verification

        ↓

Consensus / Validator

        ↓

Final Result

Ensembles should be used selectively because they increase computational cost.

They are particularly useful for:

- critical scientific analysis,

- difficult reasoning,

- conflicting evidence,

- high-value reports,

- validation of generated conclusions.

## 85.14 Model Versioning

Every AI response must record sufficient model metadata for reproducibility.

model_id

provider

model_version

routing_policy_version

prompt_version

retrieval_version

timestamp

temperature/configuration

This allows GSIR to reproduce and audit historical outputs.

## 85.15 Model Evaluation Pipeline

New models shall not immediately become production defaults.

New Model

    ↓

Capability Test

    ↓

Benchmark

    ↓

Cost Test

    ↓

Latency Test

    ↓

Safety Test

    ↓

Regression Test

    ↓

Limited Deployment

    ↓

Production Evaluation

    ↓

Routing Approval

## 85.16 Core Principle

GSIR's AI architecture shall follow:

ONE AI INTERFACE

        ↓

MULTIPLE MODELS

        ↓

INTELLIGENT ROUTING

        ↓

VALIDATED OUTPUT

The user should not need to understand which model was selected.

GSIR shall select the appropriate model automatically while preserving transparency, reproducibility, privacy, performance, reliability, and cost efficiency.

PART 95 — GSIR RESEARCH STATE, CONTINUOUS RESEARCH CONTEXT AND LONG-RUNNING RESEARCH EXECUTION ARCHITECTURE

95.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall maintain a persistent Research State representing the current state of a research investigation across projects, knowledge, workflows, experiments, AI operations, evidence, tasks and results.

The Research State shall prevent GSIR from treating each AI interaction as an isolated request. Modern research-OS proposals similarly emphasize persistent research state, knowledge continuity, model independence and lifecycle coherence.

GSIR shall treat the research investigation itself as the persistent unit of continuity.

AI models, agents, workflows, tools, documents and experiments are components that operate on the research state; they are not substitutes for it.

Research-Centric

Stateful

Traceable

Recoverable

Scalable

# PART 97 — GSIR RESEARCH REPRODUCIBILITY, ARTIFACT PACKAGING AND EXECUTION REPLAY ARCHITECTURE

## 97.1 Purpose

GSIR shall provide a unified reproducibility and replay capability for research workflows, experiments, analyses, AI operations, and computational results.

Every reproducible research execution shall preserve the required inputs, workflow definition, parameters, software/model versions, execution environment, resources, outputs, validation information, and existing provenance references.

The system shall allow researchers to:

- Re-run previous research executions.

- Reproduce computational results.

- Compare original and reproduced executions.

- Identify differences and divergence points.

- Package research artifacts for sharing or archiving.

- Validate whether a result is reproducible.

- Continue research from a previous execution state.

Workflow provenance and execution-environment information are important for reliable replay and reproducibility.

## 97.2 Architecture

Research / Experiment / Workflow

              │

              ▼

      Execution Orchestrator

              │

              ▼

      Reproducibility Capture

              │

      ┌───────┼────────┐

      ▼       ▼        ▼

   Inputs   Environment  Configuration

      │       │        │

      └───────┼────────┘

              ▼

       Execution Manifest

              │

              ▼

        Artifact Package

              │

              ▼

       Reproduction Run

              │

              ▼

      Result Comparison

              │

       ┌──────┴──────┐

       ▼             ▼

   Reproduced     Diverged

       │             │

       └──────┬──────┘

              ▼

       Research State

## 97.3 Reproducibility Levels

GSIR shall distinguish reproducibility levels rather than treating every successful re-run as identical.

### Level 1 — Execution Repeatability

The same workflow is executed again using the same inputs and configuration.

### Level 2 — Computational Reproducibility

The same computational method produces equivalent results using the captured software, dependencies, models, parameters, and environment.

### Level 3 — Experimental Reproducibility

The same experimental methodology is repeated with controlled conditions and comparable resources.

### Level 4 — Research Replication

An independent researcher or system reproduces the research process using the documented methodology and available artifacts.

The system shall record which level was tested.

## 97.4 Reproducibility Manifest

Every eligible execution shall be capable of generating a reproducibility manifest.

ReproducibilityManifest

├── manifest_id

├── execution_id

├── project_id

├── workflow_version

├── workflow_signature

├── input_artifacts

├── input_hashes

├── parameters

├── configuration

├── software_versions

├── dependency_versions

├── model_versions

├── prompt_versions

├── tool_versions

├── environment

├── compute_resources

├── random_seeds

├── execution_timestamp

├── output_artifacts

├── output_hashes

├── validation_rules

├── provenance_reference

└── manifest_signature

The manifest shall reference existing GSIR entities rather than creating duplicate versions of those entities.

## 97.5 Immutable Research Artifacts

Artifacts required for reproduction shall be versioned and content-addressable where practical.

Examples include:

- Source datasets.

- Dataset versions.

- Workflow definitions.

- Code.

- Configuration.

- Parameters.

- AI model versions.

- Prompt versions.

- Tool versions.

- Generated intermediate files.

- Final results.

- Reports.

- Analysis outputs.

- Execution logs.

An artifact shall not be silently replaced after it has been referenced by a completed execution.

## 97.6 Artifact Package

GSIR shall support packaging the complete reproducibility context of an execution.

ResearchArtifactPackage

├── manifest

├── workflow

├── configuration

├── input references

├── input metadata

├── code references

├── dependency metadata

├── model metadata

├── execution environment

├── execution logs

├── provenance references

├── output artifacts

├── validation results

└── reproduction instructions

The package shall use references to large existing files instead of unnecessarily duplicating large datasets.

Where appropriate, GSIR may use interoperable research-object packaging approaches for workflow execution artifacts.

## 97.7 Execution Replay

GSIR shall provide replay from a completed execution.

Original Execution

       │

       ▼

Load Manifest

       │

       ▼

Resolve Versions

       │

       ▼

Resolve Inputs

       │

       ▼

Prepare Environment

       │

       ▼

Recreate Execution

       │

       ▼

Run Workflow

       │

       ▼

Capture Results

       │

       ▼

Compare

Replay shall create a new execution, never modify the original execution.

## 97.8 Deterministic and Non-Deterministic Execution

GSIR shall identify whether an execution is deterministic.

### Deterministic

The same inputs, environment, parameters, and execution path should produce equivalent outputs.

### Non-Deterministic

Outputs may vary because of:

- Randomness.

- AI model sampling.

- External services.

- Dynamic datasets.

- Hardware differences.

- Network-dependent resources.

- Time-dependent information.

- Floating-point differences.

- Parallel execution behavior.

For non-deterministic executions, GSIR shall use configurable equivalence rules instead of requiring byte-for-byte equality.

## 97.9 Result Comparison

GSIR shall compare original and reproduced executions using multiple comparison strategies.

Comparison

├── Artifact Hash Comparison

├── Structural Comparison

├── Numerical Comparison

├── Statistical Comparison

├── Semantic Comparison

├── Workflow Comparison

├── Provenance Comparison

└── Environment Comparison

The comparison engine shall identify:

- Matching artifacts.

- Changed artifacts.

- Missing artifacts.

- Changed parameters.

- Changed workflow nodes.

- Changed model versions.

- Changed software versions.

- Environment differences.

- Output differences.

- First known divergence point.

Workflow signatures and structured reproducibility tests can make these comparisons more systematic and efficient.

## 97.10 Reproduction Result

Each replay shall produce a reproduction result.

ReproductionResult

├── reproduction_id

├── original_execution_id

├── reproduction_execution_id

├── reproducibility_level

├── status

├── comparison_summary

├── matched_artifacts

├── changed_artifacts

├── divergence_points

├── output_comparison

├── environment_comparison

├── provenance_comparison

├── validation_result

├── confidence

└── created_at

Possible statuses:

REPRODUCED

PARTIALLY_REPRODUCED

DIVERGED

FAILED

BLOCKED

NOT_COMPARABLE

## 97.11 Divergence Detection

GSIR shall detect the earliest meaningful divergence in a replay.

Input

  ↓

Workflow

  ↓

Task 1 ✓

  ↓

Task 2 ✓

  ↓

Task 3 ✗

  ↓

Task 4 not executed

The system shall identify Task 3 as the first known divergence and expose the relevant:

- Inputs.

- Parameters.

- Environment.

- Model/tool versions.

- Logs.

- Intermediate artifacts.

- Errors.

- Provenance links.

This shall help researchers determine why two apparently identical executions produced different results.

## 97.12 AI Reproducibility

AI-assisted research shall capture the AI execution context required for later inspection and replay.

This includes:

- Provider.

- Model.

- Model version.

- Prompt version.

- System configuration.

- Tool configuration.

- Retrieval context references.

- Knowledge references.

- Temperature and sampling parameters where applicable.

- Structured tool calls.

- Input/output artifact references.

- AI execution identifiers.

For inherently non-deterministic AI models, GSIR shall distinguish exact replay from controlled replay.

Controlled replay verifies that the same model, instructions, context, tools, and constraints produce an equivalent research outcome rather than requiring identical generated tokens.

## 97.13 Environment Capture

The reproducibility system shall capture relevant execution-environment information.

Environment

├── Operating System

├── Runtime

├── Language Version

├── Framework Versions

├── Package Versions

├── Container Image

├── Hardware

├── GPU

├── Driver Versions

├── Memory

├── CPU

├── Environment Variables

└── External Dependencies

Secrets shall never be stored directly inside reproducibility manifests.

Secret references may be recorded where necessary, subject to authorization and security policies.

## 97.14 Reproducibility Validation

GSIR shall validate a replay before marking it reproducible.

Validation may include:

- Input integrity.

- Workflow signature.

- Artifact integrity.

- Environment compatibility.

- Parameter equivalence.

- Model/version compatibility.

- Output comparison.

- Statistical equivalence.

- Provenance completeness.

- Required dependency availability.

The final result shall clearly state what was reproduced and what could not be reproduced.

## 97.15 Database Integration

GSIR shall reuse the existing research, execution, artifact, provenance, experiment, task, AI, and resource entities.

Only reproducibility-specific records shall be introduced where required.

Suggested entities:

reproducibility_manifests

reproduction_runs

reproduction_results

artifact_packages

artifact_package_items

execution_comparisons

These records shall reference existing:

projects

workflows

workflow_versions

workflow_runs

workflow_tasks

experiments

datasets

dataset_versions

ai_runs

models

model_versions

files

artifacts

provenance

resources

No duplicate workflow, task, experiment, AI, or provenance systems shall be created.

## 97.16 Backend Architecture

The reproducibility capability shall integrate with the existing orchestration architecture.

## 97.17 Integration with Orchestration

The reproducibility layer shall not execute workflows independently.

Reproducibility Service

        │

        ▼

Execution Orchestrator

        │

        ▼

Execution Engine

Replay requests shall be converted into controlled executions through the existing orchestration layer.

This guarantees that normal execution and replay use the same task scheduling, dependency management, resource management, security, logging, and state-update mechanisms.

## 97.18 Research State Integration

After replay completion:

Original Research State

        │

        ▼

Replay Execution

        │

        ▼

Validation

        │

        ▼

Comparison

        │

        ▼

Research State Update

The original research state shall remain immutable for historical accuracy.

The reproduced execution becomes a new research event and may update the current research state according to validation and authorization rules.

## 97.19 Reproducibility Certificate

GSIR may generate a reproducibility certificate for successfully validated executions.

ReproducibilityCertificate

├── certificate_id

├── execution_id

├── reproducibility_level

├── workflow_signature

├── artifact_signature

├── validation_summary

├── comparison_summary

├── provenance_reference

├── generated_at

└── certificate_signature

The certificate shall never claim scientific correctness merely because an execution was reproduced.

It shall only certify the scope of reproducibility that GSIR actually verified.

## 97.20 Security

Reproduction shall follow existing GSIR security architecture.

Requirements:

- Tenant isolation.

- Project authorization.

- Artifact access control.

- Model/provider authorization.

- Resource authorization.

- Secret protection.

- Signed artifacts where required.

- Immutable audit records.

- No unauthorized execution.

- No automatic access to restricted datasets.

- No secret leakage through manifests or logs.

A replay shall inherit the authorization requirements of the original research context while still requiring current authorization.

## 97.21 Performance and Cost

Reproduction shall avoid unnecessary computation.

GSIR shall support:

- Artifact reuse.

- Cached dependency resolution.

- Incremental replay.

- Partial workflow replay.

- Replay from checkpoints.

- Selective node execution.

- Existing artifact reuse.

- Environment reuse where safe.

- Resource-aware scheduling.

A researcher shall be able to request:

Full Replay

Partial Replay

Replay From Checkpoint

Replay Specific Node

Compare Only

Validate Only

## 97.22 Final Architecture Rule

GSIR shall maintain:

ONE Research State

ONE Task System

ONE Workflow Orchestrator

ONE Execution Engine

ONE Provenance System

ONE Artifact/Knowledge Architecture

ONE Reproducibility Layer

The reproducibility layer shall build upon existing GSIR systems rather than creating parallel research execution, provenance, workflow, artifact, or AI infrastructures.

The objective is to make every important GSIR research execution inspectable, replayable, comparable, verifiable, and reusable without unnecessarily duplicating data or computation.

PART 98 — GSIR RESEARCH DATA INTEGRITY, VALIDATION AND QUALITY CONTROL ARCHITECTURE

98.1 Purpose

GSIR shall provide one unified research data integrity and quality-control layer for validating data, documents, datasets, experiment measurements, AI-generated outputs, analytical results, and research artifacts.

The system shall ensure that research data remains:

- Accurate.

- Complete.

- Consistent.

- Traceable.

- Validated.

- Versioned.

- Protected from unauthorized modification.

- Suitable for its intended research purpose.

GSIR shall follow the principle that research data and associated research objects should be findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable while retaining appropriate provenance and validation information.

---

98.2 Architecture

Research Data / Artifact

          │

          ▼

   Ingestion Layer

          │

          ▼

   Schema Validation

          │

          ▼

   Data Quality Engine

          │

    ┌─────┼─────┐

    ▼     ▼     ▼

 Completeness Accuracy Consistency

    │     │     │

    └─────┼─────┘

          ▼

   Integrity Validation

          │

          ▼

   Provenance Recording

          │

          ▼

 Research Data Store

          │

          ▼

 Knowledge / Analysis / Experiment

---

98.3 Data Quality Dimensions

GSIR shall evaluate research data across configurable quality dimensions.

Completeness

Checks whether required information is present.

Accuracy

Checks whether values satisfy known correctness rules.

Consistency

Checks whether related records agree with one another.

Validity

Checks whether values conform to defined schemas, types, ranges, and scientific constraints.

Uniqueness

Detects unintended duplicate records or artifacts.

Timeliness

Determines whether information is sufficiently current for the research task.

Integrity

Determines whether data has been modified unexpectedly or corrupted.

Traceability

Determines whether the origin and transformation history can be established.

---

98.4 Validation Layers

GSIR shall use multiple validation levels.

Level 1 — Format Validation

Level 2 — Schema Validation

Level 3 — Structural Validation

Level 4 — Data Quality Validation

Level 5 — Domain Validation

Level 6 — Cross-Entity Validation

Level 7 — Research Integrity Validation

A dataset may pass lower-level validation while failing a higher-level scientific validation.

---

98.5 Validation Rules

Validation rules shall be reusable and versioned.

ValidationRule

├── rule_id

├── name

├── description

├── rule_type

├── expression

├── severity

├── applicable_entity

├── applicable_version

├── domain

├── enabled

├── created_by

└── version

Rule types may include:

REQUIRED

TYPE

RANGE

PATTERN

ENUMERATION

RELATIONSHIP

UNIQUENESS

STATISTICAL

DOMAIN

CROSS_RECORD

CROSS_ENTITY

CUSTOM

---

98.6 Validation Severity

Each validation failure shall have a severity.

INFO

WARNING

ERROR

CRITICAL

Critical failures may block downstream execution.

Warnings may allow execution while clearly reporting the risk.

---

98.7 Data Quality Result

Each validation operation shall generate a quality result.

DataQualityResult

├── validation_run_id

├── entity_id

├── entity_version

├── status

├── score

├── passed_rules

├── failed_rules

├── warnings

├── errors

├── critical_errors

├── quality_dimensions

├── provenance_reference

└── created_at

Possible statuses:

PASSED

PASSED_WITH_WARNINGS

FAILED

BLOCKED

NOT_VALIDATED

---

98.8 Integrity Verification

GSIR shall support integrity verification using content hashes and existing artifact/version mechanisms.

Artifact

   │

   ▼

Content

   │

   ▼

Hash

   │

   ▼

Stored Integrity Reference

   │

   ▼

Later Verification

If the calculated hash differs from the recorded integrity value, GSIR shall mark the artifact as potentially modified or corrupted.

Integrity verification shall not replace authorization, access control, or audit logging.

---

98.9 Version Integrity

Every important research object shall retain its version relationship.

Dataset v1

    │

    ├── Dataset v2

    │

    └── Dataset v3

A new version shall not silently overwrite the historical version used by an experiment, analysis, workflow, or publication.

---

98.10 Data Lineage Integration

The quality layer shall use the existing GSIR provenance and lineage architecture.

Source Data

    ↓

Transformation

    ↓

Processed Data

    ↓

Analysis

    ↓

Result

    ↓

Report

    ↓

Publication

Each quality decision shall reference the affected research object and its existing provenance information.

No duplicate lineage system shall be created.

---

98.11 Cross-Entity Validation

GSIR shall validate relationships between research entities.

Examples:

Experiment → Dataset

Experiment → Protocol

Analysis → Dataset Version

Result → Analysis Run

Report → Results

Publication → References

AI Result → Evidence

The system shall detect conditions such as:

- Analysis using an unavailable dataset version.

- Result referencing a deleted artifact.

- Experiment referencing an invalid protocol version.

- Publication referencing an incomplete result.

- AI-generated claim without required evidence.

- Workflow execution using incompatible input versions.

---

98.12 Scientific Domain Validation

Domain-specific validation shall be supported without changing the core architecture.

Examples:

Biology

├── Sample constraints

├── Measurement ranges

└── Experimental conditions

Chemistry

├── Units

├── Concentrations

└── Reaction constraints

Physics

├── Units

├── Physical ranges

└── Measurement uncertainty

Data Science

├── Dataset schema

├── Statistical constraints

└── Model evaluation

Domain rules shall be plugins or configuration-driven extensions rather than separate validation architectures.

---

98.13 Measurement Validation

Experimental measurements shall support:

- Units.

- Precision.

- Significant figures.

- Expected ranges.

- Instrument references.

- Calibration references.

- Measurement uncertainty.

- Replicate relationships.

- Missing-value handling.

- Outlier flags.

GSIR shall distinguish between:

Invalid Measurement

Questionable Measurement

Valid Measurement

Unverified Measurement

A questionable measurement shall not automatically be deleted.

---

98.14 Dataset Quality Profiling

When a dataset enters GSIR, the quality engine may generate a profile.

Dataset Profile

├── Row Count

├── Column Count

├── Missing Values

├── Duplicate Values

├── Unique Values

├── Data Types

├── Value Ranges

├── Outliers

├── Invalid Values

├── Distribution Summary

├── Unit Information

└── Quality Score

The profile shall become part of the dataset's research context.

---

98.15 AI Output Validation

AI-generated research outputs shall be treated as potentially unverified research artifacts.

GSIR shall support validation of:

- Claims.

- Citations.

- References.

- Extracted values.

- Calculations.

- Generated tables.

- Generated code.

- Generated hypotheses.

- Scientific statements.

- Evidence relationships.

AI output shall not automatically become authoritative research data merely because an AI model generated it.

---

98.16 Evidence Validation

Where a research claim requires evidence, GSIR shall be able to verify that:

Claim

  ↓

Evidence

  ↓

Source

  ↓

Source Version

  ↓

Provenance

The system shall identify:

- Missing evidence.

- Weak evidence.

- Conflicting evidence.

- Outdated evidence.

- Unsupported claims.

- Evidence-source mismatch.

---

98.17 Automated Quality Gates

Quality validation shall integrate with the existing workflow orchestration layer.

Workflow Task

     │

     ▼

Quality Gate

     │

 ┌───┼────┐

 ▼   ▼    ▼

Pass Warn Block

 │    │     │

 └────┼─────┘

      ▼

Next Execution Step

A workflow may define whether a validation failure:

- Stops execution.

- Requires human approval.

- Allows execution with warning.

- Automatically retries.

- Routes to correction.

---

98.18 Human Review

Certain quality decisions shall support human review.

Validation Failure

       │

       ▼

Human Review

       │

 ┌─────┼─────┐

 ▼     ▼     ▼

Accept Reject Correct

Human decisions shall be recorded with:

- Reviewer.

- Timestamp.

- Decision.

- Reason.

- Related validation result.

---

98.19 Quality Score

GSIR may calculate a configurable quality score.

The score shall never replace detailed validation results.

Quality Score

      │

      ├── Completeness

      ├── Accuracy

      ├── Consistency

      ├── Validity

      ├── Integrity

      └── Traceability

Different research domains may use different weighting rules.

---

98.20 Quality-Aware Research Execution

The orchestration system shall be able to use quality information when selecting execution paths.

Research Input

      │

      ▼

Quality Check

      │

      ├── High Quality → Execute

      │

      ├── Warning → Execute With Warning

      │

      └── Critical → Block / Review

This prevents known-invalid data from silently entering downstream research processes.

---

98.21 Storage and Database Integration

GSIR shall reuse existing data, artifact, version, provenance, experiment, workflow, and execution entities.

Quality-specific entities may include:

validation_rules

validation_rule_versions

validation_runs

validation_results

data_quality_profiles

quality_issues

quality_reviews

These records shall reference existing research objects.

No separate database for data quality shall be created.

---

98.23 Performance

Validation shall be optimized for large research datasets.

GSIR shall support:

- Streaming validation.

- Batch validation.

- Incremental validation.

- Parallel validation.

- Cached validation results.

- Partition-level validation.

- Sampling for large datasets where scientifically appropriate.

- Background validation jobs.

- Revalidation only when dependencies change.

Large validation operations shall use the existing BullMQ/background execution architecture.

---

98.24 Security

The quality system shall follow existing GSIR security controls.

Requirements:

- Tenant isolation.

- Role-based access.

- Project-level authorization.

- Restricted dataset protection.

- Immutable validation history.

- Secure artifact access.

- No secret exposure.

- Audit logging.

- Protected validation-rule modification.

- Authorized human review.

---

98.25 Final Architecture Rule

GSIR shall maintain:

ONE Data Architecture

ONE Versioning System

ONE Provenance System

ONE Artifact System

ONE Validation Engine

ONE Quality-Control Layer

The quality layer shall validate existing GSIR research objects rather than creating duplicate data stores.

The objective is to ensure that research data entering GSIR is validated, traceable, integrity-protected, quality-aware, and safe for downstream research execution.

PART 99 — GSIR RESEARCH DATA GOVERNANCE, METADATA AND LIFECYCLE ARCHITECTURE

99.1 Purpose

GSIR shall provide one unified research data governance layer controlling how research data and research artifacts are described, classified, accessed, used, retained, shared, archived, and reused.

The governance layer shall ensure that research data remains understandable and reusable throughout its lifecycle while respecting organizational, legal, privacy, security, licensing, and scientific requirements.

FAIR principles emphasize persistent identification, rich metadata, standardized access, interoperability, provenance, and reuse.

---

99.2 Architecture

Research Data / Artifact

          │

          ▼

   Data Registration

          │

          ▼

 Metadata & Classification

          │

          ▼

 Governance Policies

          │

    ┌─────┼─────┐

    ▼     ▼     ▼

 Access  Usage  Retention

    │     │     │

    └─────┼─────┘

          ▼

 Research Data Lifecycle

          │

   ┌──────┼──────┐

   ▼      ▼      ▼

 Active  Shared  Archived

          │

          ▼

      Reuse / Disposal

---

99.3 Data Governance Principles

GSIR shall follow:

Governance by Design

Privacy by Design

Security by Design

FAIR by Design

Provenance by Design

Versioning by Design

Machine-Readable Metadata

Least Privilege

Explicit Authorization

Lifecycle Management

Governance shall be integrated into the existing GSIR architecture rather than implemented as an independent data platform.

---

99.4 Research Data Classification

Every governed research object shall support classification.

PUBLIC

INTERNAL

CONFIDENTIAL

RESTRICTED

SENSITIVE

Organizations may define additional classifications through configuration.

Classification shall influence:

- Access.

- Sharing.

- Export.

- AI usage.

- External integrations.

- Retention.

- Archiving.

- Publication.

---

99.5 Research Data Categories

GSIR shall classify research objects by their role.

Raw Data

Processed Data

Derived Data

Experimental Data

Observational Data

Reference Data

Training Data

Validation Data

Analysis Data

AI-Generated Data

Research Artifacts

Published Data

Archived Data

Classification and category shall remain separate concepts.

---

99.6 Metadata Architecture

Metadata shall describe the meaning, origin, structure, quality, ownership, lifecycle, and permitted use of a research object.

Research Object

├── Identity Metadata

├── Scientific Metadata

├── Structural Metadata

├── Provenance Metadata

├── Quality Metadata

├── Governance Metadata

├── Access Metadata

├── License Metadata

├── Lifecycle Metadata

└── Technical Metadata

Metadata should be sufficient for another researcher to understand and appropriately reuse the associated data.

---

99.7 Core Metadata

GSIR shall support common metadata fields such as:

object_id

object_type

title

description

creator

owner

organization

workspace

project

created_at

updated_at

version

status

classification

source

license

access_policy

retention_policy

quality_status

provenance_reference

parent_object

related_objects

Domain-specific metadata shall extend the common structure rather than replace it.

---

99.8 Machine-Readable Metadata

GSIR metadata shall be machine-readable wherever practical.

Supported representations may include:

JSON

JSON-LD

CSV Metadata

RDF-compatible representations

Domain-specific schemas

The exact representation shall depend on the integration and research domain.

The objective is to allow both humans and machines to discover, interpret, validate, and reuse research objects.

---

99.9 Metadata Standards

GSIR shall prefer existing recognized metadata standards when an appropriate standard exists.

GSIR Core Metadata

        │

        ├── General Metadata Standards

        ├── Domain Standards

        ├── Organization Standards

        └── Project-Specific Extensions

GSIR shall not invent a new standard when an established community standard already satisfies the requirement.

Metadata standards vary by discipline, so the architecture shall support domain-specific standards while maintaining a common core.

---

99.10 Metadata Profiles

A metadata profile shall define the metadata required for a specific research object.

Examples:

Dataset Profile

Experiment Profile

Sample Profile

Instrument Profile

Protocol Profile

Analysis Profile

AI Run Profile

Publication Profile

Research Artifact Profile

A profile may specify:

- Required fields.

- Optional fields.

- Controlled vocabularies.

- Validation rules.

- Units.

- Identifier requirements.

- Governance requirements.

---

99.11 Metadata Validation

Metadata shall pass validation before an object reaches a required lifecycle stage.

Object

  │

  ▼

Metadata Validation

  │

  ├── Complete → Continue

  │

  ├── Warning → Continue / Review

  │

  └── Invalid → Block

Metadata validation shall reuse the validation architecture defined in Part 98.

No second validation engine shall be created.

---

99.12 Ownership and Stewardship

GSIR shall distinguish between:

Creator

Owner

Data Steward

Custodian

Researcher

Reviewer

Publisher

These roles may belong to different users or organizations.

The system shall record responsibility for important research objects throughout their lifecycle.

---

99.13 Data Governance Metadata

Governance metadata shall describe rules affecting the use of research data.

Examples:

Access Restrictions

Sharing Restrictions

Usage Restrictions

Consent Requirements

License

Retention Period

Deletion Policy

Export Restrictions

AI Usage Permission

External Processing Permission

Publication Restrictions

Governance metadata can improve machine-readable interpretation of authorization, linkage, sharing, and usage requirements.

---

99.14 AI Data Governance

GSIR shall explicitly govern whether research data may be processed by AI systems.

Each governed object may specify:

AI_PROCESSING_ALLOWED

AI_PROCESSING_RESTRICTED

AI_PROCESSING_PROHIBITED

Additional controls may specify:

Internal Models Only

Approved Providers Only

No External Provider

No Training Usage

No Persistent Storage

Human Approval Required

The AI layer shall check these policies before sending data to an AI provider.

---

99.15 External Sharing

Before research data is shared externally, GSIR shall evaluate:

Classification

Access Policy

License

Consent

Retention Rules

Organization Policy

Project Policy

Export Restrictions

Destination

Recipient Authorization

The sharing operation shall be recorded in the existing audit and provenance systems.

---

99.16 Data Lifecycle

Every governed research object shall follow a lifecycle.

REGISTERED

    ↓

ACTIVE

    ↓

PROCESSED

    ↓

VALIDATED

    ↓

SHARED / USED

    ↓

ARCHIVED

    ↓

RETAINED / DISPOSED

Not every object must pass every state.

Lifecycle transitions shall be policy-controlled.

---

99.17 Retention

GSIR shall support configurable retention policies.

RetentionPolicy

├── policy_id

├── object_type

├── classification

├── retention_period

├── archive_action

├── deletion_action

├── legal_hold_behavior

└── approval_requirement

Retention policies shall never automatically delete an object that is under legal hold, active research dependency, or another protected state.

---

99.18 Archiving

Archived research objects shall remain discoverable through metadata where permitted.

Active Object

     │

     ▼

Archive Preparation

     │

     ▼

Integrity Check

     │

     ▼

Metadata Preservation

     │

     ▼

Archive

Archiving shall preserve sufficient information to identify the object, its version, provenance, and applicable governance restrictions.

---

99.19 Deletion and Disposal

Deletion shall be controlled and auditable.

Before deletion GSIR shall check:

- Active dependencies.

- Research state.

- Experiments.

- Workflows.

- Publications.

- Provenance.

- Legal holds.

- Retention requirements.

- Organizational policy.

Where complete deletion is prohibited or impractical, GSIR shall support controlled deactivation or restricted archival instead.

---

99.20 Data Dependency Protection

GSIR shall identify objects that depend on a dataset or artifact.

Dataset

  │

  ├── Experiment

  ├── Analysis

  ├── AI Run

  ├── Report

  └── Publication

A governance action affecting the dataset shall evaluate these dependencies before proceeding.

---

99.21 Persistent Identification

Important research objects shall receive stable identifiers.

Organization

   ↓

Workspace

   ↓

Project

   ↓

Research Object

   ↓

Object Version

Identifiers shall remain stable across supported lifecycle operations.

Where external publication or repository integration requires persistent identifiers such as DOIs, GSIR shall store the external identifier and its relationship to the internal GSIR identifier.

FAIR guidance specifically recommends globally unique and persistent identifiers for research objects.

---

99.22 Interoperability

GSIR shall provide controlled data exchange through:

REST API

JSON

CSV

Standard File Formats

Metadata Export

Research Object Export

External Repository Connectors

Exported objects shall include appropriate metadata and provenance references where permitted.

The architecture shall support future interoperability standards without making any single external standard mandatory for the entire platform.

---

99.23 Governance-Aware Search

Search shall respect governance policies.

Search Request

      │

      ▼

Authorization

      │

      ▼

Classification Check

      │

      ▼

Policy Filtering

      │

      ▼

Search / Retrieval

A user shall never receive restricted metadata or content merely because the search engine can technically locate it.

---

99.24 Governance-Aware Knowledge Retrieval

The knowledge system shall apply access controls before returning information to:

- Users.

- AI models.

- Agents.

- Workflows.

- External integrations.

This prevents unauthorized research information from entering AI context or generated responses.

---

99.25 Governance and Provenance

Governance actions shall connect to existing provenance and audit systems.

Data Object

    │

    ▼

Governance Decision

    │

    ├── Who

    ├── What

    ├── Why

    ├── When

    └── Under Which Policy

The governance layer shall not create a second audit or provenance architecture.

---

99.26 Database Integration

GSIR shall reuse existing research-object, version, organization, workspace, project, user, access-control, provenance, artifact, and audit entities.

Governance-specific entities may include:

data_classifications

metadata_profiles

metadata_records

governance_policies

governance_policy_versions

retention_policies

data_holds

sharing_policies

These entities shall reference existing GSIR objects.

99.29 Performance

GSIR shall support:

- Policy caching.

- Metadata indexing.

- Permission caching.

- Background metadata enrichment.

Governance policies themselves shall be protected from unauthorized modification.

---

99.31 Final Architecture Rule

GSIR shall maintain:

ONE Research Data Architecture

ONE Metadata Architecture

ONE Governance Layer

ONE Policy Engine

ONE Lifecycle System

ONE Provenance System

ONE Validation System

ONE Access-Control System

The governance architecture shall make GSIR research data understandable, controlled, discoverable, interoperable, reusable, secure, and traceable throughout its complete lifecycle.

PART 100 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC AI EVALUATION, BENCHMARKING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE ARCHITECTURE

100.1 PURPOSE

GSIR shall provide one unified evaluation architecture for measuring the quality, reliability, safety, efficiency, reproducibility and scientific usefulness of AI models, agents, workflows and research outputs.

The evaluation system shall prevent GSIR from selecting or trusting an AI system based on a single score.

Modern AI-agent evaluation increasingly requires assessment of capability, cost, safety, robustness, process quality and reproducibility rather than only final-answer accuracy.

END OF 100.1

100.2 CORE PRINCIPLE

GSIR shall evaluate:

MODEL

+

AI RUN

+

AGENT

+

WORKFLOW

+

TOOL USE

+

RESEARCH RESULT

using a common evaluation architecture.

The evaluation layer shall remain separate from production execution.

END OF 100.2

PART 101 — GSIR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH MONITORING, DRIFT DETECTION AND CONTINUOUS ASSURANCE ARCHITECTURE

101.1 Purpose

GSIR shall provide one unified monitoring and continuous-assurance layer for detecting changes in research data, AI behavior, model performance, workflows, resources, knowledge, and system reliability.

The objective is to detect important changes before they silently reduce research quality, reliability, safety, reproducibility, or efficiency.

GSIR shall monitor the complete research lifecycle rather than monitoring only infrastructure metrics.

- Predictive models.

- Scientific classification.

- Time-dependent research.

- Dynamic experimental systems.

Concept drift shall remain distinct from simple data-distribution changes.
